const SCROLLBACK: u64 = 2000

# The screen is one text per row, each exactly `cols` characters, so a
# write rebuilds one row (O(cols)) and a scroll moves rows, not cells.
fn blank_row(n: u64) -> text
    var s = ""
    for _ in 0..n
        s = s + " "
    return s

fn blank_screen(r: u64, c: u64) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for _ in 0..r
        o.push(blank_row(c))
    return o

# row with the cells x0..=x1 replaced by c (one character each)
fn put(row: text, x0: u64, x1: u64, c: text) -> text
    let cs = row.chars()
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..cs.len()
        if (i as u64) >= x0 and (i as u64) <= x1
            o = o + copy(c)
        else
            o = o + copy(cs[i])
    return o

# row cut or padded to n characters
fn fit(row: text, n: u64) -> text
    let cs = row.chars()
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..n
        if (i as usize) < cs.len()
            o = o + copy(cs[i as usize])
        else
            o = o + " "
    return o

fn num(p: text, dflt: u64) -> u64
    if p == "" or not p.isdigit() or p.len_bytes() > 6
        return dflt
    let v = p.toint() as u64
    if v == 0
        return dflt
    return v

fn rtrim(r: text) -> text
    let cs = r.chars()
    var n = cs.len()
    while n > 0 and cs[n - 1] == " " bound 1048576
        n -= 1
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..n
        o = o + copy(cs[i])
    return o

state Term
    next: u64 = 0
    id: u64 = 0
    opening: bool = false
    opened: bool = false
    closed: bool = false
    shown: u64 = 0
    lines: u64 = 0
    rows: u64 = 24
    cols: u64 = 80
    commands: u64 = 0
    last_command: text = ""
    screen: List[text] = blank_screen(24, 80)
    crow: u64 = 0
    ccol: u64 = 0
    esc: u64 = 0
    csi: text = ""
    sb: Map[u64, bool] = {}
    sb_head: u64 = 0
    sb_tail: u64 = 0
    pending: text = ""

step Term on Tick
    if closed
        pass
    elif not opening
        opening = true
        next += 1
        emit PtyOpen(req: next, argv: ["/bin/sh"], rows: rows, cols: cols)
    elif opened
        next += 1
        emit PtyRead(req: next, id: id, max: 65536)

step Term on Input(data: d)
    if opened and not closed
        commands += 1
        last_command = copy(d)
        next += 1
        emit PtyWrite(req: next, id: id, data: d)
    elif not closed
        # typed before the PTY opened: kept and written once it is open
        commands += 1
        last_command = copy(d)
        pending = pending + d

step Term on Resize(rows: r, cols: c)
    # keep the overlapping top-left part of the screen
    var ns: List[text] = []
    for y in 0..r
        if y < rows
            ns.push(fit(copy(screen[y as usize]), c))
        else
            ns.push(blank_row(c))
    screen = ns
    if crow >= r
        crow = r - 1
    if ccol >= c
        ccol = c - 1
    rows = r
    cols = c
    if opened and not closed
        next += 1
        emit PtyResize(req: next, id: id, rows: r, cols: c)

step Term on Interrupt
    if opened and not closed
        next += 1
        emit PtyWrite(req: next, id: id, data: "\u{3}")

step Term on PtyResizeDone(req: _r, status: _s, data: _d, err: _e)
    pass

step Term on PtyOpenDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: e)
    if s == "delivered"
        id = d.or(0)
        opened = true
        if rows != 24 or cols != 80
            # resized while the PTY was opening
            next += 1
            emit PtyResize(req: next, id: id, rows: rows, cols: cols)
        if pending != ""
            next += 1
            emit PtyWrite(req: next, id: id, data: copy(pending))
            pending = ""
    else
        closed = true
        emit Display(data: "terminal: " + e + "\n")
        emit Exit(code: 1)

step Term on PtyWriteDone(req: _r, status: _s, data: _d, err: _e)
    pass

step Term on PtyReadDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        let out = d.or("")
        if out.len_bytes() > 0
            shown += out.len_bytes() as u64
            for c in copy(out).chars()
                if c == "\n"
                    lines += 1
                if esc == 1
                    if c == "["
                        esc = 2
                        csi = ""
                    else
                        esc = 0
                elif esc == 2
                    if c.isdigit() or c == ";" or c == "?"
                        csi = csi + c
                    else
                        esc = 0
                        let ps = copy(csi).split(";")
                        let p0 = num(copy(ps[0]).strip(), 1)
                        if c == "A"
                            crow = crow - p0.min(crow)
                        elif c == "B"
                            crow = (crow + p0).min(rows - 1)
                        elif c == "C"
                            ccol = (ccol + p0).min(cols - 1)
                        elif c == "D"
                            ccol = ccol - p0.min(ccol)
                        elif c == "H" or c == "f"
                            var p1: u64 = 1
                            if ps.len() > 1
                                p1 = num(copy(ps[1]), 1)
                            crow = (p0 - 1).min(rows - 1)
                            ccol = (p1 - 1).min(cols - 1)
                        elif c == "J"
                            let mode = num(copy(csi), 0)
                            for y in 0..rows
                                if mode == 2 or (mode == 0 and y > crow) or (mode == 1 and y < crow)
                                    screen[y as usize] = blank_row(cols)
                            if mode == 0
                                screen[crow as usize] = put(copy(screen[crow as usize]), ccol, cols, " ")
                            elif mode == 1
                                screen[crow as usize] = put(copy(screen[crow as usize]), 0, ccol, " ")
                        elif c == "K"
                            let mode = num(copy(csi), 0)
                            if mode == 2
                                screen[crow as usize] = blank_row(cols)
                            elif mode == 0
                                screen[crow as usize] = put(copy(screen[crow as usize]), ccol, cols, " ")
                            elif mode == 1
                                screen[crow as usize] = put(copy(screen[crow as usize]), 0, ccol, " ")
                elif c == "\u{1b}"
                    esc = 1
                elif c == "\r"
                    ccol = 0
                elif c == "\u{8}"
                    if ccol > 0
                        ccol -= 1
                elif c == "\t"
                    ccol = ((ccol / 8 + 1) * 8).min(cols - 1)
                elif c == "\n" or ccol >= cols
                    if c != "\n"
                        ccol = 0
                    if crow + 1 < rows
                        crow += 1
                    else
                        # scroll: the top row goes to the scrollback
                        sb[sb_tail] = rtrim(copy(screen[0]))
                        sb_tail += 1
                        if sb_tail - sb_head > SCROLLBACK
                            let _ = sb.remove(sb_head)
                            sb_head += 1
                        var ns: List[text] = []
                        for y in 1..rows
                            ns.push(copy(screen[y as usize]))
                        ns.push(blank_row(cols))
                        screen = ns
                    if c != "\n"
                        screen[crow as usize] = put(copy(screen[crow as usize]), ccol, ccol, copy(c))
                        ccol += 1
                elif c >= " "
                    screen[crow as usize] = put(copy(screen[crow as usize]), ccol, ccol, copy(c))
                    ccol += 1
            emit Display(data: out)
    else
        closed = true
        next += 1
        emit PtyClose(req: next, id: id)

step Term on PtyCloseDone(req: _r, status: _s, data: d, err: _e)
    emit Exit(code: d.or(0))

# The visible screen, one Display per row (trailing blanks trimmed), then
# the cursor.
step Term on Screen
    for y in 0..rows
        emit Display(data: rtrim(copy(screen[y as usize])) + "\n")
    emit Display(data: "cursor " + (crow + 1).tostr() + ";" + (ccol + 1).tostr() + "\n")

# Scrollback lines start..start+count (0 is the oldest kept line).
step Term on History(start: f, count: n)
    var i = sb_head + f
    while i < sb_tail and i < sb_head + f + n bound 2000
        emit Display(data: (sb.get(i) catch "") + "\n")
        i += 1

module col

# Collections (survey M6) beyond the built-in List and Map: deque, binary
# heap, ordered map and ordered set (sorted vectors, canonical key order),
# and a hash map with fixed hashing (FNV-1a 32, no seed) whose iteration
# order is insertion order. Every operation is deterministic: no seeds, no
# addresses, no host input. Containers are generic structs used through
# &mut / & functions (rce 0.1.3 resolves generic fields that way).

# ---------------- Deque ----------------
# Two stacks: front holds the front elements reversed. Amortized O(1).

pub struct Deque[T]
front: List[T]
back: List[T]

pub fn dq_len[T](d: &Deque[T]) -> usize = d.front.len() + d.back.len()

pub fn dq_push_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T], x: T)
d.back.push(x)

pub fn dq_push_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T], x: T)
d.front.push(x)

fn dq_spill_to_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T])
# move the older half of back to front, keeping the rest in back
let n = d.back.len()
let k = (n + 1) / 2
var rest: List[T] = []
var i: usize = k
while i < n bound 16777216
rest.push(copy(d.back[i]))
i += 1
var j = k
while j > 0 bound 16777216
j -= 1
d.front.push(copy(d.back[j]))
d.back = rest

fn dq_spill_to_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T])
let n = d.front.len()
let k = (n + 1) / 2
var rest: List[T] = []
var i: usize = k
while i < n bound 16777216
rest.push(copy(d.front[i]))
i += 1
var j = k
while j > 0 bound 16777216
j -= 1
d.back.push(copy(d.front[j]))
d.front = rest

pub fn dq_pop_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T]) -> T?
if d.front.len() == 0
dq_spill_to_front(d)
if d.front.len() == 0

# ---------------- Deque ----------------
# Two stacks: front holds the front elements reversed. Amortized O(1).

pub struct Deque[T]
    front: List[T]
    back: List[T]

pub fn dq_len[T](d: &Deque[T]) -> usize = d.front.len() + d.back.len()

pub fn dq_push_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T], x: T)
    d.back.push(x)

pub fn dq_push_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T], x: T)
    d.front.push(x)

fn dq_spill_to_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T])
    # move the older half of back to front, keeping the rest in back
    let n = d.back.len()
    let k = (n + 1) / 2
    var rest: List[T] = []
    var i: usize = k
    while i < n bound 16777216
        rest.push(copy(d.back[i]))
        i += 1
    var j = k
    while j > 0 bound 16777216
        j -= 1
        d.front.push(copy(d.back[j]))
    d.back = rest

fn dq_spill_to_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T])
    let n = d.front.len()
    let k = (n + 1) / 2
    var rest: List[T] = []
    var i: usize = k
    while i < n bound 16777216
        rest.push(copy(d.front[i]))
        i += 1
    var j = k
    while j > 0 bound 16777216
        j -= 1
        d.back.push(copy(d.front[j]))
    d.front = rest

pub fn dq_pop_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T]) -> T?
    if d.front.len() == 0
        dq_spill_to_front(d)
    if d.front.len() == 0
        return none
    let x = copy(d.front[d.front.len() - 1])
    let _ = d.front.pop()
    return some(x)

pub fn dq_pop_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T]) -> T?
    if d.back.len() == 0
        dq_spill_to_back(d)
    if d.back.len() == 0
        return none
    let x = copy(d.back[d.back.len() - 1])
    let _ = d.back.pop()
    return some(x)

    if i < d.front.len()
        return copy(d.front[d.front.len() - 1 - i])
    return copy(d.back[i - d.front.len()])

    var o: List[T] = []
    var i = d.front.len()
    while i > 0 bound 16777216
        i -= 1
        o.push(copy(d.front[i]))
    for x in d.back

    return o

# ---------------- Binary min-heap ----------------
# heap_pop returns the least element; among equal elements the order is
# fixed by the algorithm (deterministic, not stable).

pub fn heap_push[T: Ord](h: &mut List[T], x: T)
    h.push(x)
    var i = h.len() - 1
    while i > 0 bound 64
        let p = (i - 1) / 2
        if h[i] < h[p]
            let t = copy(h[i])
            h[i] = copy(h[p])
            h[p] = t
            i = p
        else
            i = 0

pub fn heap_peek[T: Ord](h: &[T]) -> T? = if h.len() == 0 then none else some(copy(h[0]))

pub fn heap_pop[T: Ord](h: &mut List[T]) -> T?
    if h.len() == 0
        return none
    let top = copy(h[0])
    let last = copy(h[h.len() - 1])
    let _ = h.pop()
    let n = h.len()
    if n == 0
        return some(top)
    h[0] = last
    var i: usize = 0
    var go = true
    while go bound 64
        let l = 2 * i + 1
        let r = l + 1
        var m = i
        if l < n and h[l] < h[m]
            m = l
        if r < n and h[r] < h[m]
            m = r
        if m == i
            go = false
        else
            let t = copy(h[i])
            h[i] = copy(h[m])
            h[m] = t
            i = m
    return some(top)

# ---------------- Ordered map or set ----------------
# Sorted vectors: lookup O(log n), insert/remove O(n), iteration in
# ascending key order (the canonical order the survey requires).

pub struct OrdMap[K, V]
    keys: List[K]
    vals: List[V]

# First index whose key is >= k.
pub fn lower_bound[K: Ord + Eq](xs: &[K], k: &K) -> usize
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = xs.len()
    while lo < hi bound 64
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if xs[mid] < k
            lo = mid + 1
        else
            hi = mid
    return lo

fn insert_at[T](xs: &mut List[T], i: usize, x: T)
    xs.push(x)
    var j = xs.len() - 1
    while j > i bound 16777216
        let t = copy(xs[j])
        xs[j] = copy(xs[j - 1])
        xs[j - 1] = t
        j -= 1

fn remove_at[T](xs: &mut List[T], i: usize)
    var j = i
    while j + 1 < xs.len() bound 16777216
        xs[j] = copy(xs[j + 1])
        j += 1
    let _ = xs.pop()

pub fn om_insert[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &mut OrdMap[K, V], k: K, v: V)
    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, &k)
    if i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] == k
        m.vals[i] = v
    else
        insert_at(&mut m.keys, i, k)
        insert_at(&mut m.vals, i, v)

pub fn om_get[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &OrdMap[K, V], k: &K) -> V?
    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, k)
    if i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] == k
        return some(copy(m.vals[i]))
    return none

pub fn om_contains[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &OrdMap[K, V], k: &K) -> bool
    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, k)
    return i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] == k

pub fn om_remove[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &mut OrdMap[K, V], k: &K) -> bool
    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, k)
    if i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] == k
        remove_at(&mut m.keys, i)
        remove_at(&mut m.vals, i)
        return true
    return false

# generic struct's field types on direct access outside generic code.)

pub fn om_range[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &OrdMap[K, V], lo: &K, hi: &K) -> List[K]
    var o: List[K] = []
    var i = lower_bound(&m.keys, lo)
    while i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] < hi bound 16777216
        o.push(copy(m.keys[i]))
        i += 1

    let i = lower_bound(s, k)

    let i = lower_bound(s, k)

    var o: List[K] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    var j: usize = 0
    while i < a.len() or j < b.len() bound 33554432
        if j >= b.len() or (i < a.len() and a[i] < b[j])
            o.push(copy(a[i]))
            i += 1
        elif i >= a.len() or b[j] < a[i]

            j += 1
        else
            o.push(copy(a[i]))
            i += 1
            j += 1
    return o

        if a[i] < b[j]
            i += 1
        elif b[j] < a[i]
            j += 1
        else
            o.push(copy(a[i]))
            i += 1

# ---------------- Fixed-hash map (text keys) ----------------
# FNV-1a 32-bit (no seed), open addressing with linear probing over a
# power-of-two table, load <= 1/2. Entries live in insertion order in
# keys/vals; slots hold entry index + 1 (0 empty). Removal compacts the
# entries and rebuilds the slots, so iteration order is always insertion
# order of the live keys.

pub fn fnv1a32(s: &text) -> i64
    var h: i64 = 2166136261
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        h = ((h ^ (s[i] as i64)) * 16777619) & 4294967295
        i += 1
    return h

pub struct HMap[V]
    keys: List[text]
    vals: List[V]
    slots: List[i64]

fn hm_rebuild[V](m: &mut HMap[V], cap: usize)
    var sl: List[i64] = []
    for _i in 0..cap
        sl.push(0)
    var e: usize = 0
    while e < m.keys.len() bound 16777216
        var p = (fnv1a32(&m.keys[e]) as usize) & (cap - 1)
        while sl[p] != 0 bound 16777216
            p = (p + 1) & (cap - 1)
        sl[p] = (e + 1) as i64
        e += 1
    m.slots = sl

fn hm_find[V](m: &HMap[V], k: &text) -> i64
    let cap = m.slots.len()
    if cap == 0
        return -1
    var p = (fnv1a32(k) as usize) & (cap - 1)
    while m.slots[p] != 0 bound 16777216
        let e = (m.slots[p] - 1) as usize
        if m.keys[e] == k
            return e as i64
        p = (p + 1) & (cap - 1)
    return -1

pub fn hm_len[V](m: &HMap[V]) -> usize = m.keys.len()

pub fn hm_get[V](m: &HMap[V], k: &text) -> V?
    let e = hm_find(m, k)
    if e < 0
        return none
    return some(copy(m.vals[e as usize]))

pub fn hm_contains[V](m: &HMap[V], k: &text) -> bool = hm_find(m, k) >= 0

pub fn hm_insert[V](m: &mut HMap[V], k: text, v: V)
    let e = hm_find(m, &k)
    if e >= 0
        m.vals[e as usize] = v
        return
    m.keys.push(k)
    m.vals.push(v)
    if 2 * m.keys.len() > m.slots.len()
        var cap: usize = 8
        while cap < 2 * m.keys.len() bound 40
            cap = cap * 2
        hm_rebuild(m, cap)
    else
        let cap = m.slots.len()
        var p = (fnv1a32(&m.keys[m.keys.len() - 1]) as usize) & (cap - 1)
        while m.slots[p] != 0 bound 16777216
            p = (p + 1) & (cap - 1)
        m.slots[p] = m.keys.len() as i64

pub fn hm_remove[V](m: &mut HMap[V], k: &text) -> bool
    let e = hm_find(m, k)
    if e < 0
        return false
    remove_at(&mut m.keys, e as usize)
    remove_at(&mut m.vals, e as usize)
    let cap = m.slots.len()
    hm_rebuild(m, cap)
    return true

pub fn hm_keys[V](m: &HMap[V]) -> List[text] = copy(m.keys)

module col

# Collections (survey M6) beyond the built-in List and Map: deque, binary
# heap, ordered map and ordered set (sorted vectors, canonical key order),
# and a hash map with fixed hashing (FNV-1a 32, no seed) whose iteration
# order is insertion order. Every operation is deterministic: no seeds, no
# addresses, no host input. Containers are generic structs used through
# &mut / & functions (rce 0.1.3 resolves generic fields that way).

# ---------------- Deque ----------------
# Two stacks: front holds the front elements reversed. Amortized O(1).

pub struct Deque[T]
    front: List[T]
    back: List[T]

pub fn dq_len[T](d: &Deque[T]) -> usize = d.front.len() + d.back.len()

pub fn dq_push_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T], x: T)
    d.back.push(x)

pub fn dq_push_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T], x: T)
    d.front.push(x)

fn dq_spill_to_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T])
    # move the older half of back to front, keeping the rest in back
    let n = d.back.len()
    let k = (n + 1) / 2
    var rest: List[T] = []
    var i: usize = k
    while i < n bound 16777216
        rest.push(copy(d.back[i]))
        i += 1
    var j = k
    while j > 0 bound 16777216
        j -= 1
        d.front.push(copy(d.back[j]))
    d.back = rest

fn dq_spill_to_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T])
    let n = d.front.len()
    let k = (n + 1) / 2
    var rest: List[T] = []
    var i: usize = k
    while i < n bound 16777216
        rest.push(copy(d.front[i]))
        i += 1
    var j = k
    while j > 0 bound 16777216
        j -= 1
        d.back.push(copy(d.front[j]))
    d.front = rest

pub fn dq_pop_front[T](d: &mut Deque[T]) -> T?
    if d.front.len() == 0
        dq_spill_to_front(d)
    if d.front.len() == 0
        return none
    let x = copy(d.front[d.front.len() - 1])
    let _ = d.front.pop()
    return some(x)

pub fn dq_pop_back[T](d: &mut Deque[T]) -> T?
    if d.back.len() == 0
        dq_spill_to_back(d)
    if d.back.len() == 0
        return none
    let x = copy(d.back[d.back.len() - 1])
    let _ = d.back.pop()
    return some(x)

# Element i from the front (0-based); traps when out of range.
pub fn dq_get[T](d: &Deque[T], i: usize) -> T
    if i < d.front.len()
        return copy(d.front[d.front.len() - 1 - i])
    return copy(d.back[i - d.front.len()])

pub fn dq_to_list[T](d: &Deque[T]) -> List[T]
    var o: List[T] = []
    var i = d.front.len()
    while i > 0 bound 16777216
        i -= 1
        o.push(copy(d.front[i]))
    for x in d.back
        o.push(copy(x))
    return o

# heap_pop returns the least element; among equal elements the order is
# fixed by the algorithm (deterministic, not stable).

pub fn heap_push[T: Ord](h: &mut List[T], x: T)

            h[i] = copy(h[p])
            h[p] = t
            i = p
        else
            i = 0

pub fn heap_pop[T: Ord](h: &mut List[T]) -> T?

        else

            h[i] = copy(h[m])
            h[m] = t
            i = m
    return some(top)

# Sorted vectors: lookup O(log n), insert/remove O(n), iteration in
# ascending key order (the canonical order the survey requires).

pub struct OrdMap[K, V]
    keys: List[K]
    vals: List[V]

pub fn lower_bound[K: Ord + Eq](xs: &[K], k: &K) -> usize

        xs[j] = copy(xs[j + 1])
        j += 1
    let _ = xs.pop()

    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, &k)
    if i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] == k
        m.vals[i] = v
    else
        insert_at(&mut m.keys, i, k)
        insert_at(&mut m.vals, i, v)

    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, k)

        return some(copy(m.vals[i]))
    return none

    let i = lower_bound(&m.keys, k)
    if i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] == k
        remove_at(&mut m.keys, i)
        remove_at(&mut m.vals, i)
        return true
    return false

# generic struct's field types on direct access outside generic code.)
pub fn om_keys[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &OrdMap[K, V]) -> List[K] = copy(m.keys)

pub fn om_range[K: Ord + Eq, V](m: &OrdMap[K, V], lo: &K, hi: &K) -> List[K]
    var o: List[K] = []
    var i = lower_bound(&m.keys, lo)
    while i < m.keys.len() and m.keys[i] < hi bound 16777216
        o.push(copy(m.keys[i]))
        i += 1
    return o

    let i = lower_bound(s, &k)
    if i < s.len() and s[i] == k
        return false
    insert_at(s, i, k)
    return true

pub fn set_contains[K: Ord + Eq](s: &[K], k: &K) -> text
    let i = lower_bound(s, k)
    return i < s.len() and s[i] == k

pub fn set_remove[K: Ord + Eq](s: &mut List[K], k: &K) -> bool
    let i = lower_bound(s, k)
    if i < s.len() and s[i] == k
        remove_at(s, i)
        return true
    return false

# unsigned of 1 to 7 bytes (a u64 does not fit i64: read 8 bytes as two u32).
# Decoding bytes into text needs a built-in (see needs-spec in SOURCE.md).

while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
o.push(s[i] as i64)
i += 1
return o

for _i in 0..n
o.push(0)

pub fn bytes_valid(b: &[i64]) -> bool
for x in b
if x < 0 or x > 255

return true

pub fn bytes_cat(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o = copy(a)
for x in b
o.push(x)
return o

let _ok = 1 / (if lo <= hi and hi <= (b.len() as i64) then 1 else 0)

module core.exact

# Exact arithmetic for Form a.mag[2] (survey M2): big integers, rationals,
# decimals and binary fixed-point, in pure RCE over List[i64] limbs.
# Big: sign and magnitude; mag is little-endian base 2^24 limbs with no
# high zero limbs (zero is neg false, mag []). Limb products stay below 2^48,
# so a column sum of up to 2^15 products fits i64.
# Division by zero traps (an integer division by zero in mag_divmod).
# Rounding is always an explicit argument; there is no ambient context.

return o

let t = mag_trim(m)
return Big(neg: neg and t.len() > 0, mag: t)

pub fn big_is_zero(a: Big) -> bool = a.mag.len() == 0

o.push(if r < 0 then 0 - r else r)
v = v / BASE

return false

module core.exact

# Exact arithmetic for Form bricks (survey M2): big integers, rationals,
# decimals and binary fixed-point, in pure RCE over List[i64] limbs.
# Big: sign and magnitude; mag is little-endian base 2^24 limbs with no
# high zero limbs (zero is neg false, mag []). Limb products stay below 2^48,
# so a column sum of up to 2^15 products fits i64.
# Division by zero traps (an integer division by zero in mag_divmod).
# Rounding is always an explicit argument; there is no ambient context.

const BASE: i64 = 16777216
const LMASK: i64 = 16777215
const LBITS: i64 = 24

pub struct Big
    neg: bool
    mag: List[i64]

pub fn mag_trim(m: List[i64]) -> List[i64]

    let t = mag_trim(m)
    return Big(neg: neg and t.len() > 0, mag: t)

pub fn big_zero() -> Big = Big(neg: false, mag: [])

pub fn big_is_zero(a: Big) -> bool = a.mag.len() == 0

pub fn big_from_int(n: i64) -> Big

    return o

        else
            br = 0

        i += 1

pub fn mag_mul(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    if a.len() == 0 or b.len() == 0

            c = t >> LBITS

# (quotient, remainder) of a magnitude by a small divisor 0 < d < 2^24,
# remainder appended as the last element.
pub fn mag_divsmall(a: &[i64], d: i64) -> List[i64]

        var t = a[i] >> b
        if i + 1 < a.len()

        i += 1
    return mag_trim(o)

        top = top >> 1

pub struct QR
    q: List[i64]

    let z = a.mag.len() == 0

    if a.mag.len() == 0

    return mk(a.neg != b.neg, qr.q)

    return mk(a.neg, qr.r)

    if a.neg != b.neg and r.mag.len() > 0

    return r

# Explicit rounding modes (General Decimal Arithmetic / IEEE 754 names).
const HALF_EVEN: i64 = 0

const DOWN: i64 = 3

pub fn big_round_div(n: Big, d: Big, mode: i64) -> Big
