        var j = idx.len()
        idx.push(i)
        while j > 0 and lex_cmp(&ks[idx[j - 1]], &ks[i]) > 0 bound 16777216
            idx[j] = idx[j - 1]
            j -= 1
        idx[j] = i
    for j in 1..idx.len()
        let _ok = 1 / (if lex_cmp(&ks[idx[j - 1]], &ks[idx[j]]) < 0 then 1 else 0)
    var o = cbor_head(5, ks.len() as i64)
    for i in idx
        o = enc_cat(o, &ks[i])
        o = enc_cat(o, &vs[i])
    return o

fn enc_text(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    let b = bytes_of(t)
    return enc_cat(cbor_head(3, b.len() as i64), &b)

fn enc_int(v: i64) -> List[i64] = if v >= 0 then cbor_head(0, v) else cbor_head(1, -1 - v)

fn enc_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = cbor_head(2, b.len() as i64)
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn enc_simple(v: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if v < 24
        o.push(224 | v)
    else
        o.push(248)
        o.push(v)
    return o

fn enc_tag(t: i64, inner: List[i64]) -> List[i64] = enc_cat(cbor_head(6, t), &inner)

# Nesting depth is bounded by 64.
pub fn cbor_encode(c: &Cbor) -> List[i64] bound 64
    match c
        CInt(v: v) -> return enc_int(v)
        CBytes(b: b) -> return enc_bytes(b)
        CText(t: t) -> return enc_text(t)
        CArr(items: items) -> return enc_arr(items.len(), items.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)))
        CMap(keys: keys, vals: vals) -> return enc_map(keys.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)), vals.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)))
        CTag(tag: tag, item: item) -> return enc_tag(tag, cbor_encode(item))
        CSimple(v: v) -> return enc_simple(v)

error BadCbor(at: i64)

pub struct CborOut
    v: Cbor
    next: i64

fn arg_of(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> VarOut ! BadCbor
    # argument of the head at off, shortest form enforced
    if off >= (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    let ai = b[off as usize] & 31
    if ai < 24
        return VarOut(v: ai, next: off + 1)
    if ai > 27
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    let n = if ai == 24 then 1 else (if ai == 25 then 2 else (if ai == 26 then 4 else 8))
    if off + n >= (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    var v: i64 = 0
    for k in 1..(n + 1)
        let x = b[(off + k) as usize]
        if k == 1 and n == 8 and x > 127
            fail BadCbor(at: off)
        v = (v << 8) | x
    let lo = if ai == 24 then 25 else (if ai == 25 then 256 else (if ai == 26 then 65536 else 4294967296))
    if v < lo
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    return VarOut(v: v, next: off + 1 + n)

fn ascii_table() -> List[text] = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~".chars()

# Decode one deterministic data item at off. Text must be ASCII here
# (needs spec: text from UTF-8 bytes); floats are refused.
pub fn cbor_decode_at(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> CborOut ! BadCbor bound 64
    let h = try arg_of(b, off)
    let m = b[off as usize] >> 5
    let n = h.v
    var p = h.next
    if m == 0
        return CborOut(v: CInt(v: n), next: p)
    if m == 1
        return CborOut(v: CInt(v: -1 - n), next: p)
    if m == 2 or m == 3
        if p + n > (b.len() as i64)
            fail BadCbor(at: off)
        var bs: List[i64] = []
        for k in 0..n
            bs.push(b[(p + k) as usize])
        if m == 2
            return CborOut(v: CBytes(b: bs), next: p + n)
        let tbl = ascii_table()
        var t = ""
        for k in 0..n
            let x = bs[k as usize]
            if x == 10
                t = t + "\n"
            elif x == 13
                t = t + "\r"
            elif x == 9
                t = t + "\t"
            elif x >= 32 and x < 127
                t = t + copy(tbl[(x - 32) as usize])
            else
                fail BadCbor(at: p + k)
        return CborOut(v: CText(t: t), next: p + n)
    if m == 4
        var items: List[Cbor] = []
        for _k in 0..n
            let r = try cbor_decode_at(b, p)
            p = r.next
            items.push(r.v)
        return CborOut(v: CArr(items: items), next: p)
    if m == 5
        var ks: List[Cbor] = []
        var vs: List[Cbor] = []
        var prev: List[i64] = []
        for k in 0..n
            let ks0 = p
            let rk = try cbor_decode_at(b, p)
            var kb: List[i64] = []
            for q in ks0..rk.next
                kb.push(b[q as usize])
            if k > 0 and lex_cmp(&prev, &kb) >= 0
                fail BadCbor(at: ks0)
            prev = kb
            let rv = try cbor_decode_at(b, rk.next)
            let _kn = rk.next
            p = rv.next
            ks.push(rk.v)
            vs.push(rv.v)
        return CborOut(v: CMap(keys: ks, vals: vs), next: p)
    if m == 6
        let r = try cbor_decode_at(b, p)
        let nx = r.next
        return CborOut(v: CTag(tag: n, item: Box(r.v)), next: nx)
    let ai = b[off as usize] & 31
    if ai > 24 or (ai == 24 and n < 32)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    return CborOut(v: CSimple(v: n), next: p)

# Decode a whole buffer holding exactly one deterministic item.
pub fn cbor_decode(b: &[i64]) -> Cbor ! BadCbor
    let r = try cbor_decode_at(b, 0)
    if r.next != (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: r.next)
    return r.v

# ---------------- JCS (RFC 8785) ----------------
# Json values with integer numbers only: an integer is printed the way
# ECMAScript prints the equal double, which for |v| <= 2^53 is its decimal
# form; larger magnitudes trap (I-JSON range). Non-integer numbers need
# spec (no f64 bit access for the shortest round-trip form).

pub kind JsonDoc
    JNull
    JBool(v: bool)
    JInt(v: i64)
    JStr(t: text)
    JArr(items: List[JsonDoc])
    JObj(keys: List[text], vals: List[JsonDoc])

fn hex4(v: i64) -> text
    let ds = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    return copy(ds[((v >> 12) & 15) as usize]) + copy(ds[((v >> 8) & 15) as usize]) + copy(ds[((v >> 4) & 15) as usize]) + copy(ds[(v & 15) as usize])

# JSON string per RFC 8785 3.2.2.2: escape " \ and U+0000..U+001F (short
# forms \b \t \n \f \r, else \u00xx lowercase); everything else verbatim.
pub fn jcs_string(t: &text) -> text
    var s = "\""
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if c == "\""
            s = s + "\\\""
        elif c == "\\"
            s = s + "\\\\"
        elif x == 8
            s = s + "\\b"
        elif x == 9
            s = s + "\\t"
        elif x == 10
            s = s + "\\n"
        elif x == 12
            s = s + "\\f"
        elif x == 13
            s = s + "\\r"
        elif x < 32
            s = s + "\\u" + hex4(x)
        else
            s = s + c
    return s + "\""

# UTF-16 code units of a UTF-8 text (sort key of RFC 8785 3.2.3).
pub fn utf16_units(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        let x = t[i] as i64
        var cp = x
        var n: usize = 1
        if x >= 240
            cp = ((x & 7) << 18) | (((t[i + 1] as i64) & 63) << 12) | (((t[i + 2] as i64) & 63) << 6) | ((t[i + 3] as i64) & 63)
            n = 4
        elif x >= 224
            cp = ((x & 15) << 12) | (((t[i + 1] as i64) & 63) << 6) | ((t[i + 2] as i64) & 63)
            n = 3
        elif x >= 192
            cp = ((x & 31) << 6) | ((t[i + 1] as i64) & 63)
            n = 2
        if cp >= 65536
            let u = cp - 65536
            o.push(55296 + (u >> 10))
            o.push(56320 + (u & 1023))
        else
            o.push(cp)
        i += n
    return o

fn jcs_int(v: i64) -> text
    let _ok = 1 / (if v <= 9007199254740992 and v >= -9007199254740992 then 1 else 0)
    return v.tostr()

fn jcs_arr(parts: List[text]) -> text = "[" + ",".join(parts) + "]"

# Members sorted by UTF-16 code units of the keys; duplicate keys trap.
fn jcs_obj(keys: &[text], vals: List[text]) -> text
    var us: List[List[i64]] = []
    for k in keys
        us.push(utf16_units(k))
    var idx: List[usize] = []
    for i in 0..keys.len()
        var j = idx.len()
        idx.push(i)
        while j > 0 and lex_cmp(&us[idx[j - 1]], &us[i]) > 0 bound 16777216
            idx[j] = idx[j - 1]
            j -= 1
        idx[j] = i
    for j in 1..idx.len()
        let _ok = 1 / (if lex_cmp(&us[idx[j - 1]], &us[idx[j]]) < 0 then 1 else 0)
    var parts: List[text] = []
    for i in idx
        parts.push(jcs_string(&keys[i]) + ":" + copy(vals[i]))
    return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"

pub fn jcs(j: &JsonDoc) -> text bound 64
    match j
        JNull -> return "null"
        JBool(v: v) -> return if v then "true" else "false"
        JInt(v: v) -> return jcs_int(v)
        JStr(t: t) -> return jcs_string(t)
        JArr(items: items) -> return jcs_arr(items.map(fn(x: JsonDoc) => jcs(&x)))
        JObj(keys: keys, vals: vals) -> return jcs_obj(keys, vals.map(fn(x: JsonDoc) => jcs(&x)))

module enc

# Encodings (survey M8): base64 (RFC 4648), LEB128 varints with zigzag,
# deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1, core deterministic encoding)
# and the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785). Bytes are List[i64]
# 0..255 (core.bytes). Decoders reject every non-canonical input: padding
# or trailing bits in base64, overlong varints, non-shortest CBOR heads,
# indefinite lengths, unsorted or duplicate map keys.
# Not covered (needs spec, see vectors/SOURCE.md): CBOR and JCS floats (no
# f64 bit access in 5.15), CBOR integers beyond i64, decoding non-ASCII
# CBOR text (no text-from-UTF-8 built-in).

fn enc_cat(a: List[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = a
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(s[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- base64 (RFC 4648 sections 4 and 5) ----------------

fn b64_alpha(url: bool) -> List[text] = if url then "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_".chars() else "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/".chars()

# url: the URL-safe alphabet; pad: emit '=' padding.
pub fn b64_encode(b: &[i64], url: bool, pad: bool) -> text
    let a = b64_alpha(url)
    var s = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < b.len() bound 16777216
        let n = b.len() - i
        let x0 = b[i]
        let x1 = if n > 1 then b[i + 1] else 0
        let x2 = if n > 2 then b[i + 2] else 0
        let v = (x0 << 16) | (x1 << 8) | x2
        s = s + copy(a[((v >> 18) & 63) as usize]) + copy(a[((v >> 12) & 63) as usize])
        if n > 1
            s = s + copy(a[((v >> 6) & 63) as usize])
        elif pad
            s = s + "="
        if n > 2
            s = s + copy(a[(v & 63) as usize])
        elif pad
            s = s + "="
        i += 3
    return s

error BadBase64(at: i64)

fn b64_val(c: i64, url: bool) -> i64
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 71
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c + 4
    if c == (if url then 45 else 43)
        return 62
    if c == (if url then 95 else 47)
        return 63
    return -1

# Strict decode: padding exactly as b64_encode(pad) would emit it, no
# whitespace, zero trailing bits (RFC 4648 section 3.5 canonical form).
pub fn b64_decode(s: &text, url: bool, pad: bool) -> List[i64] ! BadBase64
    var n = s.len_bytes()
    if pad
        if n % 4 != 0
            fail BadBase64(at: n as i64)
        if n > 0 and s[n - 1] == 61
            n -= 1
            if s[n - 1] == 61
                n -= 1
    elif n % 4 == 1
        fail BadBase64(at: n as i64)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var acc: i64 = 0
    var bits: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let v = b64_val(s[i] as i64, url)
        if v < 0
            fail BadBase64(at: i as i64)
        acc = ((acc << 6) | v) & 16777215
        bits += 6
        if bits >= 8
            bits -= 8
            o.push((acc >> bits) & 255)
        i += 1
    if bits > 0 and (acc & ((1 << bits) - 1)) != 0
        fail BadBase64(at: (n - 1) as i64)
    return o

# ---------------- LEB128 varints ----------------

pub fn uvarint(v: i64) -> List[i64]
    let _ok = 1 / (if v >= 0 then 1 else 0)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var x = v
    while x >= 128 bound 10
        o.push((x & 127) | 128)
        x = x >> 7
    o.push(x)
    return o

error BadVarint(at: i64)

pub struct VarOut
    v: i64
    next: i64

# Decode at off; rejects truncation, overlong forms (a final 0x00 byte after
# the first) and values above 2^63 - 1.
pub fn uvarint_decode(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> VarOut ! BadVarint
    var v: i64 = 0
    var sh: i64 = 0
    var i = off
    loop bound 10
        if i >= (b.len() as i64)
            fail BadVarint(at: i)
        let x = b[i as usize]
        if sh == 63 and x > 0
            fail BadVarint(at: i)
        v = v | ((x & 127) << sh)
        i += 1
        if x < 128
            if x == 0 and i - off > 1
                fail BadVarint(at: i - 1)
            return VarOut(v: v, next: i)
        sh += 7
    fail BadVarint(at: i)

pub fn zigzag(v: i64) -> i64 = if v >= 0 then 2 * v else 0 - 2 * (v + 1) - 1 + 2

pub fn unzigzag(z: i64) -> i64 = if z % 2 == 0 then z / 2 else 0 - (z - 1) / 2 - 1

# ---------------- Deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 4.2.1) ----------------

pub kind Cbor
    CInt(v: i64)
    CBytes(b: List[i64])
    CText(t: text)
    CArr(items: List[Cbor])
    CMap(keys: List[Cbor], vals: List[Cbor])
    CTag(tag: i64, item: Box[Cbor])
    CSimple(v: i64)

# Simple values: false 20, true 21, null 22, undefined 23.
pub const CBOR_FALSE: i64 = 20
pub const CBOR_TRUE: i64 = 21
pub const CBOR_NULL: i64 = 22
pub const CBOR_UNDEF: i64 = 23

# Shortest head for major type m and argument n >= 0.
pub fn cbor_head(m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
    let mt = m << 5
    if n < 24
        return [mt | n]
    if n < 256
        return [mt | 24, n]
    if n < 65536
        return [mt | 25, n >> 8, n & 255]
    if n < 4294967296
        return [mt | 26, (n >> 24) & 255, (n >> 16) & 255, (n >> 8) & 255, n & 255]
    var o: List[i64] = [mt | 27]
    for k in 0..8
        o.push((n >> (8 * (7 - k))) & 255)
    return o

fn lex_cmp(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> i64
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len() and i < b.len() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return if a[i] < b[i] then -1 else 1
        i += 1
    if a.len() == b.len()
        return 0
    return if a.len() < b.len() then -1 else 2

fn enc_arr(n: usize, parts: List[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o = cbor_head(4, n as i64)
    for p in parts
        o = enc_cat(o, &p)
    return o

# Map: sort entries by the bytes of their encoded keys; a duplicate key
# traps (RFC 8949 5.6: deterministic encoders must not emit duplicates).
fn enc_map(ks: List[List[i64]], vs: List[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var idx: List[usize] = []
    for i in 0..ks.len()
        var j = idx.len()
        idx.push(i)
        while j > 0 and lex_cmp(&ks[idx[j - 1]], &ks[i]) > 0 bound 16777216
            idx[j] = idx[j - 1]
            j -= 1
        idx[j] = i
    for j in 1..idx.len()
        let _ok = 1 / (if lex_cmp(&ks[idx[j - 1]], &ks[idx[j]]) < 0 then 1 else 0)
    var o = cbor_head(5, ks.len() as i64)
    for i in idx
        o = enc_cat(o, &ks[i])
        o = enc_cat(o, &vs[i])
    return o

fn enc_text(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    let b = bytes_of(t)
    return enc_cat(cbor_head(3, b.len() as i64), &b)

fn enc_int(v: i64) -> List[i64] = if v >= 0 then cbor_head(0, v) else cbor_head(1, -1 - v)

fn enc_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = cbor_head(2, b.len() as i64)
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn enc_simple(v: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if v < 24
        o.push(224 | v)
    else
        o.push(248)
        o.push(v)
    return o

fn enc_tag(t: i64, inner: List[i64]) -> List[i64] = enc_cat(cbor_head(6, t), &inner)

# Nesting depth is bounded by 64.
pub fn cbor_encode(c: &Cbor) -> List[i64] bound 64
    match c
        CInt(v: v) -> return enc_int(v)
        CBytes(b: b) -> return enc_bytes(b)
        CText(t: t) -> return enc_text(t)
        CArr(items: items) -> return enc_arr(items.len(), items.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)))
        CMap(keys: keys, vals: vals) -> return enc_map(keys.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)), vals.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)))
        CTag(tag: tag, item: item) -> return enc_tag(tag, cbor_encode(item))
        CSimple(v: v) -> return enc_simple(v)

error BadCbor(at: i64)

pub struct CborOut
    v: Cbor
    next: i64

fn arg_of(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> VarOut ! BadCbor
    # argument of the head at off, shortest form enforced
    if off >= (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    let ai = b[off as usize] & 31
    if ai < 24
        return VarOut(v: ai, next: off + 1)
    if ai > 27
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    let n = if ai == 24 then 1 else (if ai == 25 then 2 else (if ai == 26 then 4 else 8))
    if off + n >= (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    var v: i64 = 0
    for k in 1..(n + 1)
        let x = b[(off + k) as usize]
        if k == 1 and n == 8 and x > 127
            fail BadCbor(at: off)
        v = (v << 8) | x
    let lo = if ai == 24 then 24 else (if ai == 25 then 256 else (if ai == 26 then 65536 else 4294967296))
    if v < lo
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    return VarOut(v: v, next: off + 1 + n)

fn ascii_table() -> List[text] = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~".chars()

# Decode one deterministic data item at off. Text must be ASCII here
# (needs spec: text from UTF-8 bytes); floats are refused.
pub fn cbor_decode_at(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> CborOut ! BadCbor bound 64
    let h = try arg_of(b, off)
    let m = b[off as usize] >> 5
    let n = h.v
    var p = h.next
    if m == 0
        return CborOut(v: CInt(v: n), next: p)
    if m == 1
        return CborOut(v: CInt(v: -1 - n), next: p)
    if m == 2 or m == 3
        if p + n > (b.len() as i64)
            fail BadCbor(at: off)
        var bs: List[i64] = []
        for k in 0..n
            bs.push(b[(p + k) as usize])
        if m == 2
            return CborOut(v: CBytes(b: bs), next: p + n)
        let tbl = ascii_table()
        var t = ""
        for k in 0..n
            let x = bs[k as usize]
            if x == 10
                t = t + "\n"
            elif x == 13
                t = t + "\r"
            elif x == 9
                t = t + "\t"
            elif x >= 32 and x < 127
                t = t + copy(tbl[(x - 32) as usize])
            else
                fail BadCbor(at: p + k)
        return CborOut(v: CText(t: t), next: p + n)
    if m == 4
        var items: List[Cbor] = []
        for _k in 0..n
            let r = try cbor_decode_at(b, p)
            p = r.next
            items.push(r.v)
        return CborOut(v: CArr(items: items), next: p)
    if m == 5
        var ks: List[Cbor] = []
        var vs: List[Cbor] = []
        var prev: List[i64] = []
        for k in 0..n
            let ks0 = p
            let rk = try cbor_decode_at(b, p)
            var kb: List[i64] = []
            for q in ks0..rk.next
                kb.push(b[q as usize])
            if k > 0 and lex_cmp(&prev, &kb) >= 0
                fail BadCbor(at: ks0)
            prev = kb
            let rv = try cbor_decode_at(b, rk.next)
            let _kn = rk.next
            p = rv.next
            ks.push(rk.v)
            vs.push(rv.v)
        return CborOut(v: CMap(keys: ks, vals: vs), next: p)
    if m == 6
        let r = try cbor_decode_at(b, p)
        let nx = r.next
        return CborOut(v: CTag(tag: n, item: Box(r.v)), next: nx)
    let ai = b[off as usize] & 31
    if ai > 24 or (ai == 24 and n < 32)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    return CborOut(v: CSimple(v: n), next: p)

# Decode a whole buffer holding exactly one deterministic item.

# CBOR text (no text-from-UTF-8 built-in).

module enc

# Encodings (survey M8): base64 (RFC 4648), LEB128 varints with zigzag,
# deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1, core deterministic encoding)
# and the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785). Bytes are List[i64]
# 0..255 (core.bytes). Decoders reject every non-canonical input: padding
# or trailing bits in base64, overlong varints, non-shortest CBOR heads,
# indefinite lengths, unsorted or duplicate map keys.
# Not covered (needs spec, see vectors/SOURCE.md): CBOR and JCS floats (no
# f64 bit access in 5.15), CBOR integers beyond i64, decoding non-ASCII
# CBOR text (no text-from-UTF-8 built-in).

fn enc_cat(a: List[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = a
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(s[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- base64 (RFC 4648 sections 4 and 5) ----------------

fn b64_alpha(url: bool) -> List[text] = if url then "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_".chars() else "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/".chars()

# url: the URL-safe alphabet; pad: emit '=' padding.
pub fn b64_encode(b: &[i64], url: bool, pad: bool) -> text
    let a = b64_alpha(url)
    var s = ""
    var i: usize = 0

        let n = b.len() - i
        let x0 = b[i]
        let x1 = if n > 1 then b[i + 1] else 0
        let x2 = if n > 2 then b[i + 2] else 0
        let v = (x0 << 16) | (x1 << 8) | x2
        s = s + copy(a[((v >> 18) & 63) as usize]) + copy(a[((v >> 12) & 63) as usize])
        if n > 1
            s = s + copy(a[((v >> 6) & 63) as usize])
        elif pad
            s = s + "="
        if n > 2
            s = s + copy(a[(v & 63) as usize])
        elif pad
            s = s + "="
        i += 3
    return s

error BadBase64(at: i64)

fn b64_val(c: i64, url: bool) -> i64
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 71
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c + 4
    if c == (if url then 45 else 43)
        return 62
    if c == (if url then 95 else 47)
        return 63
    return -1

# whitespace, zero trailing bits (RFC 4648 section 3.5 canonical form).
pub fn b64_decode(s: &text, url: bool, pad: bool) -> List[i64] ! BadBase64

        if n % 4 != 0
            fail BadBase64(at: n as i64)
        if n > 0 and s[n - 1] == 61
            n -= 1
            if s[n - 1] == 61
                n -= 1
    elif n % 4 == 1
        fail BadBase64(at: n as i64)

    var acc: i64 = 0
    var bits: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let v = b64_val(s[i] as i64, url)
        if v < 0
            fail BadBase64(at: i as i64)

            bits -= 8

    v: i64

pub fn cbor_head(m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]

    if n < 256

# Decode a whole buffer holding exactly one deterministic item.
pub fn cbor_decode(b: &[i64]) -> Cbor ! BadCbor
    let r = try cbor_decode_at(b, 0)
    if r.next != (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: r.next)
    return r.v

# Json values with integer numbers only: an integer is printed the way
# ECMAScript prints the equal double, which for |v| <= 2^53 is its decimal
# form; larger magnitudes trap (I-JSON range). Non-integer numbers need
# spec (no f64 bit access for the shortest round-trip form).

pub kind JsonDoc
    JNull
    JBool(v: bool)
    JInt(v: i64)
    JStr(t: text)
    JArr(items: List[JsonDoc])
    JObj(keys: List[text], vals: List[JsonDoc])

fn hex4(v: i64) -> text

    return copy(ds[((v >> 12) & 15) as usize]) + copy(ds[((v >> 8) & 15) as usize]) + copy(ds[((v >> 4) & 15) as usize]) + copy(ds[(v & 15) as usize])

# forms \b \t \n \f \r, else \u00xx lowercase); everything else verbatim.
pub fn jcs_string(t: &text) -> text

        let x = c[0] as i64
        if c == "\""
            s = s + "\\\""
        elif c == "\\"
            s = s + "\\\\"
        elif x == 8
            s = s + "\\b"
        elif x == 9
            s = s + "\\t"
        elif x == 10
            s = s + "\\n"
        elif x == 12
            s = s + "\\f"
        elif x == 13
            s = s + "\\r"
        elif x < 32
            s = s + "\\u" + hex4(x)
        else
            s = s + c
    return s + "\""

pub fn utf16_units(t: &text) -> List[i64]

            n = 3
        elif x >= 192

            n = 2

            o.push(55296 + (u >> 10))
            o.push(56320 + (u & 1023))

            o.push(cp)
        i += n
    return o

    let _ok = 1 / (if v <= 9007199254740992 and v >= -9007199254740992 then 1 else 0)
    return v.tostr()

fn jcs_arr(parts: List[text]) -> text = "[" + ",".join(parts) + "]"

# Members sorted by UTF-16 code units of the keys; duplicate keys trap.
fn jcs_obj(keys: &[text], vals: List[text]) -> text
    var us: List[List[i64]] = []
    for k in keys
        us.push(utf16_units(k))
    var idx: List[usize] = []
    for i in 0..keys.len()
        var j = idx.len()
        idx.push(i)

            j -= 1
        idx[j] = i
    for j in 1..idx.len()
        let _ok = 1 / (if lex_cmp(&us[idx[j - 1]], &us[idx[j]]) < 0 then 1 else 0)
    var parts: List[text] = []
    for i in idx
        parts.push(jcs_string(&keys[i]) + ":" + copy(vals[i]))
    return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"

pub fn jcs(j: &JsonDoc) -> text bound 64
    match j
        JNull -> return "null"
        JBool(v: v) -> return if v then "true" else "false"
        JInt(v: v) -> return jcs_int(v)
        JStr(t: t) -> return jcs_string(t)
        JArr(items: items) -> return jcs_arr(items.map(fn(x: JsonDoc) => jcs(&x)))
        JObj(keys: keys, vals: vals) -> return jcs_obj(keys, vals.map(fn(x: JsonDoc) => jcs(&x)))

module fmt

# Locale-free formatting, parsing and a linear-time regex (survey M17,
# part 1). No locale, no host call: the same input gives the same text on
# every host.
# - Integers: any radix 2..36, sign, zero/space padding, digit grouping;
# strict parsing that refuses overflow, empty digits and stray bytes
# (like C++ from_chars: no whitespace, no "0x", lowercase or uppercase
# digits).
# - Templates: "{}" takes the next argument, "{N}" argument N, "{{" and
# "}}" are literal braces.
# - Regex: a Thompson NFA run as a Pike VM, so matching costs
# O(len(pattern) * len(input)) and never backtracks (RE2's guarantee).
# Syntax: literals, ".", [...] and [^...] with ranges, \d \w \s \D \W
# \S, \n \t \r, escapes of metacharacters, * + ? and {m}, {m,},
# {m,n} (m, n <= 1000), |, (...), (?:...), ^ and $ (the ends of the
# whole input, no multiline mode). It matches bytes of the UTF-8 text;
# "." takes one whole UTF-8 sequence except "\n". Class ranges are ASCII;
# a negated class or \D \W \S takes any whole non-ASCII sequence. No
# captures or backreferences (not regular).

const DIGITS: text = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

error BadInt(at: i64)
error BadFormat(at: i64)
error BadRegex(at: i64)

# ---------------- integers ----------------

# Digits of v in radix r (2..36), lowercase, "-" for negatives; the full
# i64 range (the most negative value is handled without negating it).
pub fn int_to(v: i64, r: i64) -> text
let ds = DIGITS.chars()
if v == 0
return "0"
var s = ""
var x = v
while x != 0 bound 64
let d = x % r
let a = if d < 0 then 0 - d else d
s = copy(ds[a as usize]) + s
x = x / r
return if v < 0 then "-" + s else s

pub fn int_dec(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 10)

pub fn int_hex(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 16)

fn digit_val(c: i64) -> i64
if c >= 48 and c <= 57
return c - 48
if c >= 97 and c <= 122
return c - 87
if c >= 65 and c <= 90
return c - 55
return 99

# Strict parse in radix r: optional "+" or "-", then one or more digits,
# nothing else. Overflow of i64 is refused (BadInt at the digit).
pub fn int_parse(s: &text, r: i64) -> i64 ! BadInt
let n = s.len_bytes()
if n == 0
fail BadInt(at: 0)
var i: usize = 0
var neg = false
let c0 = s[0] as i64
if c0 == 45 or c0 == 43
neg = c0 == 45
i = 1
if i >= n
fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
# accumulate as a negative number: -2^63 fits, 2^63 does not
var acc: i64 = 0
let lim = (0 - 9223372036854775807 - 1)
while i < n bound 1000000
let d = digit_val(s[i] as i64)
if d >= r
fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
if acc < (lim + d) / r
fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
let m = acc * r
if m < lim + d
fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
acc = m - d
i += 1
if not neg
if acc == lim
fail BadInt(at: (n - 1) as i64)
return 0 - acc
return acc

pub fn int_parse_dec(s: &text) -> i64 ! BadInt = int_parse(s, 10)

# Pad on the left to w code points with fill (one character).
pub fn pad_left(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
var o = copy(s)
var n = s.chars().len() as i64
while n < w bound 1000000
o = copy(fill) + o
n += 1
return o

pub fn pad_right(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
var o = copy(s)
var n = s.chars().len() as i64
while n < w bound 1000000
o = o + copy(fill)
n += 1
return o

# Zero padding after the sign: zero_pad(-42, 6) = "-00042".
pub fn zero_pad(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
let s = int_dec(v)
let z = "0"
if v < 0
let cs = s.chars()
var body = ""
for i in 1..cs.len()
body = body + copy(cs[i])
return "-" + pad_left(&body, w - 1, &z)
return pad_left(&s, w, &z)

# Group decimal digits by three with sep: group_dec(-1234567, ",") =
# "-1,234,567".
pub fn group_dec(v: i64, sep: &text) -> text
let cs = int_dec(v).chars()
let start: usize = if v < 0 then 1 else 0
let nd = cs.len() - start
var o = if v < 0 then "-" else ""
for k in 0..nd
if k > 0 and (nd - k) % 3 == 0
o = o + copy(sep)
o = o + copy(cs[start + k])
return o

# ---------------- templates ----------------

pub fn format(t: &text, args: &[text]) -> text ! BadFormat
let cs = t.chars()
let n = cs.len()
var o = ""
var next: usize = 0
var i: usize = 0
while i < n bound 1000000
let c = copy(cs[i])
if c == "{"
if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "{"
o = o + "{"
i += 2
else
var j = i + 1
var idx: i64 = -1
while j < n and cs[j] != "}" bound 1000000
let d = digit_val(cs[j][0] as i64)
if d > 9
fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
idx = (if idx < 0 then 0 else idx) * 10 + d
if idx > 1000000
fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
j += 1
if j >= n
fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
let k: usize = if idx < 0 then next else idx as usize
if k >= args.len()
fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
if idx < 0
next += 1
o = o + copy(args[k])
i = j + 1
continue
if c == "}"
if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "}"
o = o + "}"
i += 2
continue
fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
o = o + c
i += 1
return o

# ---------------- regex ----------------
# Program: instructions of 3 i64 [op, a, b]; jumps are relative to the
# instruction, so fragments can be concatenated and wrapped freely.
const OP_BYTE: i64 = 0
const OP_ANY: i64 = 1
const OP_CLASS: i64 = 2
const OP_SPLIT: i64 = 3
const OP_JMP: i64 = 4
const OP_MATCH: i64 = 5
const OP_BOL: i64 = 6
const OP_EOL: i64 = 7

pub struct Regex
code: List[i64]
classes: List[i64]

struct Parser
pat: List[i64]
pos: usize
classes: List[i64]
err: i64

fn ins(op: i64, a: i64, b: i64) -> List[i64] = [op, a, b]

fn cat(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o = a
for x in b
o.push(x)
return o

fn ilen(f: &[i64]) -> i64 = (f.len() / 3) as i64

fn star(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
let n = ilen(&f)
return cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 2), f), ins(OP_JMP, 0 - (n + 1), 0))

fn plus(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
let n = ilen(&f)
return cat(f, ins(OP_SPLIT, 0 - n, 1))

fn opt(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
let n n = ilen(&f)
return cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 1), f)

fn alt(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
let na = ilen(&a)
let nb = ilen(&b)
return cat(cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, na + 2), a), ins(OP_JMP, nb + 1, 0)), b)

fn peek(p: &Parser) -> i64 = if p.pos < p.pat.len() then p.pat[p.pos] else -1

# a class is stored at an offset: [negated, pairs, lo1, hi1, ...]
fn add_class(p: &mut Parser, neg: bool, rs: &[i64]) -> i64
let at = p.classes.len() as i64
p.classes.push(if neg then 1 else 0)
p.classes.push((rs.len() / 2) as i64)
for x in rs
p.classes.push(x)
return at

fn esc_ranges(c: i64) -> List[i64]
if c == 100 or c == 68
return [48, 57]
if c == 119 or c == 87
return [48, 57, 65, 90, 95, 95, 97, 122]
if c == 115 or c == 83
return [9, 13, 32, 32]
return []

fn esc_byte(c: i64) -> i64
if c == 110
return 10
if c == 116
return 9
if c == 114
return 13
return c

fn is_meta(c: i64) -> bool = c == 92 or c == 46 or c == 91 or c == 93 or c == 40 or c == 41 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 125 or c == 124 or c == 94 or c == 36 or c == 45 or c == 47

fn is_esc_letter(c: i64) -> bool = c == 110 or c == 116 or c == 114

fn parse_class(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64]
# after "["
var neg = false
if peek(p) == 94
neg = true
p.pos += 1
var rs: List[i64] = []
var first = true
while p.err < 0 bound 100000
let c = peek(p)
if c < 0
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
if c == 93 and not first
p.pos += 1
break
first = false
var lo = c
p.pos += 1
if c == 92
let e = peek(p)
p.pos += 1
let er = esc_ranges(e)
if er.len() > 0
if e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
for x in er
rs.push(x)
continue
if not is_meta(e) and not is_esc_letter(e)
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
lo = esc_byte(e)
var hi = lo
if peek(p) == 45 and p.pos + 1 < p.pat.len() and p.pat[p.pos + 1] != 93
p.pos += 1
hi = peek(p)
p.pos += 1
if hi == 92
let e2 = peek(p)
p.pos += 1
if not is_meta(e2) and not is_esc_letter(e2)
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
hi = esc_byte(e2)
if hi < lo
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
rs.push(lo)
rs.push(hi)
let at = add_class(p, neg, &rs)
return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)

fn parse_num(p: &mut Parser) -> i64
var v: i64 = -1
while peek(p) >= 48 and peek(p) <= 57 bound 10
v = (if v < 0 then 0 else v) * 10 + peek(p) - 48
p.pos += 1
return v

fn repeat(f: List[i64], m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
for _ in 0..m
o = cat(o, copy(f))
if n < 0
return cat(o, star(f))
for _ in 0..(n - m)
o = cat(o, opt(copy(f)))
return o

fn parse_atom(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
let c = peek(p)
p.pos += 1
if c == 40
if peek(p) == 63
p.pos += 1
if peek(p) != 58
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
p.pos += 1
let f = parse_alt(p)
if peek(p) != 41
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
p.pos += 1
return f
if c == 91
return parse_class(p)
if c == 46
return ins(OP_ANY, 0, 0)
if c == 94
return ins(OP_BOL, 0, 0)
if c == 36
return ins(OP_EOL, 0, 0)
if c == 92
let e = peek(p)
p.pos += 1
let er = esc_ranges(e)
if er.len() > 0
let at = add_class(p, e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83, &er)
return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)
if is_meta(e) or is_esc_letter(e)
return ins(OP_BYTE, esc_byte(e), 0)
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
if c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 41 or c == 93 or c == 125
p.err = (p.pos - 1) as i64
return []
return ins(OP_BYTE, c, 0)

fn parse_seq(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
var f: List[i64] = []
while p.err < 0 bound 100000
let c = peek(p)
if c < 0 or c == 124 or c == 41
break
var a = parse_atom(p)
while p.err < 0 bound 100
let q = peek(p)
if q == 42
a = star(a)
if q == 43
a = plus(a)
if q == 63
a = opt(a)
if q != 42 and q != 43 and q != 63 and q != 123
break
if q == 123
p.pos += 1
let m = parse_num(p)
var n = m
if peek(p) == 44
p.pos += 1
n = parse_num(p)
if m < 0 or peek(p) != 125 or (n >= 0 and n < m) or m > 1000 or n > 1000
p.err = p.pos as i64
return []
p.pos += 1
a = repeat(a, m, n)
if q != 123
p.pos += 1
f = cat(f, a)
return f

fn parse_alt(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
var f = parse_seq(p)
while peek(p) == 124 and p.err < 0 bound 100000
p.pos += 1
let g = parse_seq(p)
f = alt(f, g)
return f

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
o.push(s[i] as i64)
i += 1
return o

pub fn compile(pattern: &text) -> Regex ! BadRegex
var p = Parser(pat: bytes_of(pattern), pos: 0, classes: [], err: -1)
let f = parse_alt(&mut p)
if p.err < 0 and p.pos < p.pat.len()
p.err = p.pos as i64
if p.err >= 0
fail BadRegex(at: p.err)
return Regex(code: cat(f, ins(OP_MATCH, 0, 0)), classes: copy(p.classes))

fn in_class(cl: &[i64], at: usize, c: i64) -> bool
let n = cl[at + 1] as usize
var hit = false
for k in 0..n
hit = hit or (c >= cl[at + 2 + 2 * k] and c <= cl[at + 3 + 2 * k])
return hit != (cl[at] == 1)

fn seq_len(c: i64) -> i64
if c < 128
return 1
if c >= 240
return 4
if c >= 224
return 3
if c >= 192
return 2
return 1

fn spush(st: &mut List[i64], sp: usize, v: i64) -> usize
if sp < st.len()
st[sp] = v
else
st.push(v)
return sp + 1

# Add pc and its epsilon closure at input position i to list l (marking
# with stamp so each pc enters once per step).
fn add(re: &Regex, l: &mut List[i64], mark: &mut List[i64], stamp: i64, pc0: i64, i: usize, n: usize)
var st: List[i64] = [pc0]
var sp: usize = 1
while sp > 0 bound 1000000
sp -= 1
let pc = st[sp]
if mark[pc as usize] == stamp
continue
mark[pc as usize] = stamp
let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
if op == OP_JMP
sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
if op == OP_SPLIT
sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 2])
sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
if op == OP_BOL and i == 0
sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
if op == OP_EOL and i == n
sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
if op != OP_JMP and op != OP_SPLIT and op != OP_BOL and op != OP_EOL
l.push(pc)

# Pike VM. full: the match must span the input; else any substring.
fn run(re: &Regex, b: &[i64], full: bool) -> bool
let n = b.len()
let np = re.code.len() / 3
var mark: List[i64] = []
for _ in 0..np
mark.push(-1)
var cur: List[i64] = []
var stamp: i64 = 0
add(re, &mut cur, &mut mark, stamp, 0, 0, n)
# threads waiting for a multi-byte "." to finish: [pc, resume position]
var pend: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0
loop bound 16777216
for pc in cur
if re.code[3 * pc as usize] == OP_MATCH and (not full or i == n)
return true
if i >= n
break
stamp += 1
var nxt: List[i64] = []
var keep: List[i64] = []
var k: usize = 0
while k < pend.len() bound 1000000
if pend[k + 1] == (i + 1) as i64
add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pend[k], i + 1, n)
else
keep.push(pend[k])
keep.push(pend[k + 1])
k += 2
let c = b[i]
for pc in cur
let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
let a = re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1]
let sl = seq_len(c)
# a class tests a whole code point; non-ASCII ones lie outside
# every (ASCII) range
let cls = op == OP_CLASS and in_class(&re.classes, a as usize, if sl > 1 then -1 else c)
let one = (op == OP_BYTE and c == a) or (cls and sl == 1) or (op == OP_ANY and sl == 1 and c != 10)
if one
add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pc + 1, i + 1, n)
if (op == OP_ANY or cls) and sl > 1 and i + (sl as usize) <= n
keep.push(pc + 1)
keep.push((i as i64) + seq_len(c))
# a search restarts only at code point boundaries
if not full and (i + 1 >= n or b[i + 1] < 128 or b[i + 1] > 191)
add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, 0, i + 1, n)
cur = nxt
pend = keep
if cur.len() == 0 and pend.len() == 0 and full
return false
i += 1
return false

pub fn is_match(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
let b = bytes_of(s)
return run(re, &b, true)

pub fn search(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
let b = bytes_of(s)
return run(re, &b, false)

# - Templates: "{}" takes the next argument, "{N}" argument N, "{{" and
#   "}}" are literal braces.
# - Regex: a Thompson NFA run as a Pike VM, so matching costs
#   O(len(pattern) * len(input)) and never backtracks (RE2's guarantee).
#   Syntax: literals, ".", [...] and [^...] with ranges, \d \w \s \D \W
#   \S, \n \t \r, escapes of metacharacters, * + ? and {m}, {m,},
#   {m,n} (m, n <= 1000), |, (...), (?:...), ^ and $ (the ends of the
#   whole input, no multiline mode). It matches bytes of the UTF-8 text;
#   "." takes one whole UTF-8 sequence except "\n". Class ranges are ASCII;
#   a negated class or \D \W \S takes any whole non-ASCII sequence. No
#   captures or backreferences (not regular).

const DIGITS: text = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

error BadInt(at: i64)
error BadFormat(at: i64)
error BadRegex(at: i64)

# ---------------- integers ----------------

# Digits of v in radix r (2..36), lowercase, "-" for negatives; the full
# i64 range (the most negative value is handled without negating it).

pub fn int_hex(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 16)

fn digit_val(c: i64) -> i64

        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 55

# nothing else. Overflow of i64 is refused (BadInt at the digit).
pub fn int_parse(s: &text, r: i64) -> i64 ! BadInt

        fail BadInt(at: 0)

    var neg = false

        i = 1

            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)

        if m < lim + d

        acc = m - d
        i += 1
    if not neg
        if acc == lim
            fail BadInt(at: (n - 1) as i64)
        return 0 - acc
    return acc

pub fn pad_left(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text

    var n = s.chars().len() as i64

            let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
            let a = re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1]
            let sl = seq_len(c)
            # a class tests a whole code point; non-ASCII ones lie outside
            # every (ASCII) range
            let cls = op == OP_CLASS and in_class(&re.classes, a as usize, if sl > 1 then -1 else c)
            let one = (op == OP_BYTE and c == a) or (cls and sl == 1) or (op == OP_ANY and sl == 1 and c != 10)
            if one
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pc + 1, i + 1, n)
            if (op == OP_ANY or cls) and sl > 1 and i + (sl as usize) <= n
                keep.push(pc + 1)
                keep.push((i as i64) + seq_len(c))
        # a search restarts only at code point boundaries
        if not full and (i + 1 >= n or b[i + 1] < 128 or b[i + 1] > 191)
            add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, 0, i + 1, n)
        cur = nxt
        pend = keep
        if cur.len() == 0 and pend.len() == 0 and full
            return false
        i += 1
    return false

pub fn is_match(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, true)

pub fn search(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, false)

module fmt

# Locale-free formatting, parsing and a linear-time regex (survey M17,
# part 1). No locale, no host call: the same input gives the same text on
# every host.
# - Integers: any radix 2..36, sign, zero/space padding, digit grouping;
#   strict parsing that refuses overflow, empty digits and stray bytes
#   (like C++ from_chars: no whitespace, no "0x", lowercase or uppercase
#   digits).
# - Templates: "{}" takes the next argument, "{N}" argument N, "{{" and
#   "}}" are literal braces.
# - Regex: a Thompson NFA run as a Pike VM, so matching costs
#   O(len(pattern) * len(input)) and never backtracks (RE2's guarantee).
#   Syntax: literals, ".", [...] and [^...] with ranges, \d \w \s \D \W
#   \S, \n \t \r, escapes of metacharacters, * + ? and {m}, {m,},
#   {m,n} (m, n <= 1000), |, (...), (?:...), ^ and $ (the ends of the
#   whole input, no multiline mode). It matches bytes of the UTF-8 text;
#   "." takes one whole UTF-8 sequence except "\n". Class ranges are ASCII;
#   a negated class or \D \W \S takes any whole non-ASCII sequence. No

const DIGITS: text = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

error BadInt(at: i64)
error BadFormat(at: i64)
error BadRegex(at: i64)

# ---------------- integers ----------------

# Digits of v in radix r (2..36), lowercase, "-" for negatives; the full
# i64 range (the most negative value is handled without negating it).
pub fn int_to(v: i64, r: i64) -> text
    let ds = DIGITS.chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var s = ""
    var x = v
    while x != 0 bound 64
        let d = x % r
        let a = if d < 0 then 0 - d else d
        s = copy(ds[a as usize]) + s
        x = x / r
    return if v < 0 then "-" + s else s

pub fn int_dec(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 10)

pub fn int_hex(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 16)

fn digit_val(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 55
    return 99

# Strict parse in radix r: optional "+" or "-", then one or more digits,
# nothing else. Overflow of i64 is refused (BadInt at the digit).
pub fn int_parse(s: &text, r: i64) -> i64 ! BadInt
    let n = s.len_bytes()
    if n == 0
        fail BadInt(at: 0)
    var i: usize = 0
    var neg = false
    let c0 = s[0] as i64
    if c0 == 45 or c0 == 43
        neg = c0 == 45
        i = 1
    if i >= n
        fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
    # accumulate as a negative number: -2^63 fits, 2^63 does not
    var acc: i64 = 0
    let lim = (0 - 9223372036854775807 - 1)
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let d = digit_val(s[i] as i64)
        if d >= r
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        if acc < (lim + d) / r
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        let m = acc * r
        if m < lim + d
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        acc = m - d
        i += 1
    if not neg
        if acc == lim
            fail BadInt(at: (n - 1) as i64)
        return 0 - acc
    return acc

pub fn int_parse_dec(s: &text) -> i64 ! BadInt = int_parse(s, 10)

# Pad on the left to w code points with fill (one character).
pub fn pad_left(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = copy(fill) + o
        n += 1
    return o

pub fn pad_right(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = o + copy(fill)
        n += 1
    return o

# Zero padding after the sign: zero_pad(-42, 6) = "-00042".
pub fn zero_pad(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    let s = int_dec(v)
    let z = "0"
    if v < 0
        let cs = s.chars()
        var body = ""
        for i in 1..cs.len()
            body = body + copy(cs[i])
        return "-" + pad_left(&body, w - 1, &z)
    return pad_left(&s, w, &z)

# Group decimal digits by three with sep: group_dec(-1234567, ",") =
# "-1,234,567".
pub fn group_dec(v: i64, sep: &text) -> text
    let cs = int_dec(v).chars()
    let start: usize = if v < 0 then 1 else 0
    let nd = cs.len() - start
    var o = if v < 0 then "-" else ""
    for k in 0..nd
        if k > 0 and (nd - k) % 3 == 0
            o = o + copy(sep)
        o = o + copy(cs[start + k])
    return o

# ---------------- templates ----------------

pub fn format(t: &text, args: &[text]) -> text ! BadFormat
    let cs = t.chars()
    let n = cs.len()
    var o = ""
    var next: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        if c == "{"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "{"
                o = o + "{"
                i += 2
            else
                var j = i + 1
                var idx: i64 = -1
                while j < n and cs[j] != "}" bound 1000000
                    let d = digit_val(cs[j][0] as i64)
                    if d > 9
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    idx = (if idx < 0 then 0 else idx) * 10 + d
                    if idx > 1000000
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    j += 1
                if j >= n
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                let k: usize = if idx < 0 then next else idx as usize
                if k >= args.len()
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                if idx < 0
                    next += 1
                o = o + copy(args[k])
                i = j + 1
            continue
        if c == "}"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "}"
                o = o + "}"
                i += 2
                continue
            fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
        o = o + c
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- regex ----------------
# Program: instructions of 3 i64 [op, a, b]; jumps are relative to the
# instruction, so fragments can be concatenated and wrapped freely.
const OP_BYTE: i64 = 0
const OP_ANY: i64 = 1
const OP_CLASS: i64 = 2
const OP_SPLIT: i64 = 3
const OP_JMP: i64 = 4
const OP_MATCH: i64 = 5
const OP_BOL: i64 = 6
const OP_EOL: i64 = 7

pub struct Regex
    code: List[i64]
    classes: List[i64]

struct Parser
    pat: List[i64]
    pos: usize
    classes: List[i64]
    err: i64

fn ins(op: i64, a: i64, b: i64) -> List[i64] = [op, a, b]

fn cat(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = a
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn ilen(f: &[i64]) -> i64 = (f.len() / 3) as i64

fn star(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 2), f), ins(OP_JMP, 0 - (n + 1), 0))

fn plus(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(f, ins(OP_SPLIT, 0 - n, 1))

fn opt(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 1), f)

fn alt(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let na = ilen(&a)
    let nb = ilen(&b)
    return cat(cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, na + 2), a), ins(OP_JMP, nb + 1, 0)), b)

fn peek(p: &Parser) -> i64 = if p.pos < p.pat.len() then p.pat[p.pos] else -1

# a class is stored at an offset: [negated, pairs, lo1, hi1, ...]
fn add_class(p: &mut Parser, neg: bool, rs: &[i64]) -> i64
    let at = p.classes.len() as i64
    p.classes.push(if neg then 1 else 0)
    p.classes.push((rs.len() / 2) as i64)
    for x in rs
        p.classes.push(x)
    return at

fn esc_ranges(c: i64) -> List[i64]
    if c == 100 or c == 68
        return [48, 57]
    if c == 119 or c == 87
        return [48, 57, 65, 90, 95, 95, 97, 122]
    if c == 115 or c == 83
        return [9, 13, 32, 32]
    return []

fn esc_byte(c: i64) -> i64
    if c == 110
        return 10
    if c == 116
        return 9
    if c == 114
        return 13
    return c

fn is_meta(c: i64) -> bool = c == 92 or c == 46 or c == 91 and c == 93 or c == 40 or c == 41 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 125 or c == 124 or c == 94 or c == 36 or c == 45 or c == 47

fn is_esc_letter(c: i64) -> bool = c == 110 or c == 116 or c == 114

fn parse_class(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64]
    # after "["
    var neg = false
    if peek(p) == 94
        neg = true
        p.pos += 1
    var rs: List[i64] = []
    var first = true
    while p.err < 0 bound 100000
        let c = peek(p)
        if c < 0
            p.err = p.pos as i64
            return []
        if c == 93 and not first
            p.pos += 1
            break
        first = false
        var lo = c
        p.pos += 1
        if c == 92
            let e = peek(p)
            p.pos += 1
            let er = esc_ranges(e)
            if er.len() > 0
                if e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                for x in er
                    rs.push(x)
                continue
            if not is_meta(e) and not is_esc_letter(e)
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
            lo = esc_byte(e)
        var hi = lo
        if peek(p) == 45 and p.pos + 1 < p.pat.len() and p.pat[p.pos + 1] != 93
            p.pos += 1
            hi = peek(p)
            p.pos += 1
            if hi == 92
                let e2 = peek(p)
                p.pos += 1
                if not is_meta(e2) and not is_esc_letter(e2)
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                hi = esc_byte(e2)
            if hi < lo
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
        rs.push(lo)
        rs.push(hi)
    let at = add_class(p, neg, &rs)
    return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)

fn parse_num(p: &mut Parser) -> i64
    var v: i64 = -1
    while peek(p) >= 48 and peek(p) <= 57 bound 10
        v = (if v < 0 then 0 else v) * 10 + peek(p) - 48
        p.pos += 1
    return v

fn repeat(f: List[i64], m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..m
        o = cat(o, copy(f))
    if n < 0
        return cat(o, star(f))
    for _ in 0..(n - m)
        o = cat(o, opt(copy(f)))
    return o

fn parse_atom(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    let c = peek(p)
    p.pos += 1
    if c == 40
        if peek(p) == 63
            p.pos += 1
            if peek(p) != 58
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
            p.pos += 1
        let f = parse_alt(p)
        if peek(p) != 41
            p.err = p.pos as i64
            return []
        p.pos += 1
        return f
    if c == 91
        return parse_class(p)
    if c == 46
        return ins(OP_ANY, 0, 0)
    if c == 94
        return ins(OP_BOL, 0, 0)
    if c == 36
        return ins(OP_EOL, 0, 0)
    if c == 92
        let e = peek(p)
        p.pos += 1
        let er = esc_ranges(e)
        if er.len() > 0
            let at = add_class(p, e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83, &er)
            return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)
        if is_meta(e) or is_esc_letter(e)
            return ins(OP_BYTE, esc_byte(e), 0)
        p.err = p.pos as i64
        return []
    if c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 41 or c == 93 or c == 125
        p.err = (p.pos - 1) as i64
        return []
    return ins(OP_BYTE, c, 0)

fn parse_seq(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    var f: List[i64] = []
    while p.err < 0 bound 100000
        let c = peek(p)
        if c < 0 or c == 124 or c == 41
            break
        var a = parse_atom(p)
        while p.err < 0 bound 100
            let q = peek(p)
            if q == 42
                a = star(a)
            if q == 43
                a = plus(a)
            if q == 63
                a = opt(a)
            if q != 42 and q != 43 and q != 63 and q != 123
                break
            if q == 123
                p.pos += 1
                let m = parse_num(p)
                var n = m
                if peek(p) == 44
                    p.pos += 1
                    n = parse_num(p)
                if m < 0 or peek(p) != 125 or (n >= 0 and n < m) or m > 1000 or n > 1000
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                p.pos += 1
                a = repeat(a, m, n)
            if q != 123
                p.pos += 1
        f = cat(f, a)
    return f

fn parse_alt(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    var f = parse_seq(p)
    while peek(p) == 124 and p.err < 0 bound 100000
        p.pos += 1
        let g = parse_seq(p)
        f = alt(f, g)
    return f

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(s[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

pub fn compile(pattern: &text) -> Regex ! BadRegex
    var p = Parser(pat: bytes_of(pattern), pos: 0, classes: [], err: -1)
    let f = parse_alt(&mut p)
    if p.err < 0 and p.pos < p.pat.len()
        p.err = p.pos as i64
    if p.err >= 0
        fail BadRegex(at: p.err)
    return Regex(code: cat(f, ins(OP_MATCH, 0, 0)), classes: copy(p.classes))

fn in_class(cl: &[i64], at: usize, c: i64) -> bool
    let n = cl[at + 1] as usize
    var hit = false
    for k in 0..n
        hit = hit or (c >= cl[at + 2 + 2 * k] and c <= cl[at + 3 + 2 * k])
    return hit != (cl[at] == 1)

fn seq_len(c: i64) -> i64
    if c < 128
        return 1
    if c >= 240
        return 4
    if c >= 224
        return 3
    if c >= 192
        return 2
    return 1

fn spush(st: &mut List[i64], sp: usize, v: i64) -> usize
    if sp < st.len()
        st[sp] = v
    else
        st.push(v)
    return sp + 1

# Add pc and its epsilon closure at input position i to list l (marking
# with stamp so each pc enters once per step).
fn add(re: &Regex, l: &mut List[i64], mark: &mut List[i64], stamp: i64, pc0: i64, i: usize, n: usize)
    var st: List[i64] = [pc0]
    var sp: usize = 1
    while sp > 0 bound 1000000
        sp -= 1
        let pc = st[sp]
        if mark[pc as usize] == stamp
            continue
        mark[pc as usize] = stamp
        let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
        if op == OP_JMP
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
        if op == OP_SPLIT
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 2])
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
        if op == OP_BOL and i == 0
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
        if op == OP_EOL and i == n
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
        if op != OP_JMP and op != OP_SPLIT and op != OP_BOL and op != OP_EOL
            l.push(pc)

# Pike VM. full: the match must span the input; else any substring.
fn run(re: &Regex, b: &[i64], full: bool) -> bool
    let n = b.len()
    let np = re.code.len() / 3
    var mark: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..np
        mark.push(-1)
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    var stamp: i64 = 0
    add(re, &mut cur, &mut mark, stamp, 0, 0, n)
    # threads waiting for a multi-byte "." to finish: [pc, resume position]
    var pend: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        for pc in cur
            if re.code[3 * pc as usize] == OP_MATCH and (not full or i == n)
                return true
        if i >= n
            break
        stamp += 1
        var nxt: List[i64] = []
        var keep: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < pend.len() bound 1000000
            if pend[k + 1] == (i + 1) as i64
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pend[k], i + 1, n)
            else
                keep.push(pend[k])
                keep.push(pend[k + 1])
            k += 2
        let c = b[i]
        for pc in cur
            let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
            let a = re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1]
            let sl = seq_len(c)
            # a class tests a whole code point; non-ASCII ones lie outside
            # every (ASCII) range
            let cls = op == OP_CLASS and in_class(&re.classes, a as usize, if sl > 1 then -1 else c)
            let one = (op == OP_BYTE and c == a) or (cls and sl == 1) or (op == OP_ANY and sl == 1 and c != 10)
            if one
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pc + 1, i + 1, n)
            if (op == OP_ANY or cls) and sl > 1 and i + (sl as usize) <= n
                keep.push(pc + 1)
                keep.push((i as i64) + seq_len(c))
        # a search restarts only at code point boundaries
        if not full and (i + 1 >= n or b[i + 1] < 128 or b[i + 1] > 191)
            add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, 0, i + 1, n)
        cur = nxt
        pend = keep
        if cur.len() == 0 and pend.len() == 0 and full
            return false
        i += 1
    return false

pub fn is_match(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, true)

pub fn search(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, false)

        n += 1
    return o

pub fn pad_right(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = o + copy(fill)
        n += 1
    return o

# Zero padding after the sign: zero_pad(-42, 6) = "-00042".
pub fn zero_pad(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    let s = int_dec(v)
    let z = "0"
    if v < 0
        let cs = s.chars()
        var body = ""
        for i in 1..cs.len()
            body = body + copy(cs[i])
        return "-" + pad_left(&body, w - 1, &z)
    return pad_left(&s, w, &z)

# Group decimal digits by three with sep: group_dec(-1234567, ",") =
# "-1,234,567".
pub fn group_dec(v: i64, sep: &text) -> text
    let cs = int_dec(v).chars()
    let start: usize = if v < 0 then 1 else 0
    let nd = cs.len() - start
    var o = if v < 0 then "-" else ""
    for k in 0..nd
        if k > 0 and (nd - k) % 3 == 0
            o = o + copy(sep)
        o = o + copy(cs[start + k])
    return o

# ---------------- templates ----------------

pub fn format(t: &text, args: &[text]) -> text ! BadFormat
    let cs = t.chars()
    let n = cs.len()
    var o = ""
    var next: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        if c == "{"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "{"
                o = o + "{"
                i += 2
            else
                var j = i + 1
                var idx: i64 = -1
                while j < n and cs[j] != "}" bound 1000000
                    let d = digit_val(cs[j][0] as i64)
                    if d > 9
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    idx = (if idx < 0 then 0 else idx) * 10 + d
                    if idx > 1000000
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    j += 1
                if j >= n
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                let k: usize = if idx < 0 then next else idx as usize
                if k >= args.len()
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                if idx > 0
                    next += 1
                o = o + copy(args[k])
                i = j + 1
            continue
        if c == "}"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "}"
                o = o + "}"
                i += 2
                continue
            fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
        o = o + c
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- regex ----------------
# Program: instructions of 3 i64 [op, a, b]; jumps are relative to the
# instruction, so fragments can be concatenated and wrapped freely.
const OP_BYTE: i64 = 0
const OP_ANY: i64 = 1
const OP_CLASS: i64 = 2
const OP_SPLIT: i64 = 3
const OP_JMP: i64 = 4
const OP_MATCH: i64 = 5
const OP_BOL: i64 = 6
const OP_EOL: i64 = 7

pub struct Regex
    code: List[i64]
    classes: List[i64]

struct Parser
    pat: List[i64]
    pos: usize
    classes: List[i64]
    err: i64

fn ins(op: i64, a: i64, b: i64) -> List[i64] = [op, a, b]

fn cat(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = a
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn ilen(f: &[i64]) -> i64 = (f.len() / 3) as i64

fn star(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 2), f), ins(OP_JMP, 0 - (n + 1), 0))

fn plus(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(f, ins(OP_SPLIT, 0 - n, 1))

fn opt(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 1), f)

fn alt(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let na = ilen(&a)
    let nb = ilen(&b)
    return cat(cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, na + 2), a), ins(OP_JMP, nb + 1, 0)), b)

fn peek(p: &Parser) -> i64 = if p.pos < p.pat.len() then p.pat[p.pos] else -1

# a class is stored at an offset: [negated, pairs, lo1, hi1, ...]
fn add_class(p: &mut Parser, neg: bool, rs: &[i64]) -> i64
    let at = p.classes.len() as i64
    p.classes.push(if neg then 1 else 0)
    p.classes.push((rs.len() / 2) as i64)
    for x in rs
        p.classes.push(x)
    return at

fn esc_ranges(c: i64) -> List[i64]
    if c == 100 or c == 68
        return [48, 57]
    if c == 119 or c == 87
        return [48, 57, 65, 90, 95, 95, 97, 122]
    if c == 115 or c == 83
        return [9, 13, 32, 32]
    return []

fn esc_byte(c: i64) -> i64
    if c == 110
        return 10
    if c == 116
        return 9
    if c == 114
        return 13
    return c

fn is_meta(c: i64) -> bool = c == 92 or c == 46 or c == 91 or c == 93 or c == 40 or c == 41 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 125 or c == 124 or c == 94 or c == 36 or c == 45 or c == 47

fn is_esc_letter(c: i64) -> bool = c == 110 or c == 116 or c == 114

fn parse_class(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64]
    # after "["
    var neg = false
    if peek(p) == 94
        neg = true
        p.pos += 1
    var rs: List[i64] = []
    var first = true
    while p.err < 0 bound 100000
        let c = peek(p)
        if c < 0
            p.err = p.pos as i64
            return []
        if c == 93 and not first
            p.pos += 1
            break
        first = false
        var lo = c
        p.pos += 1
        if c == 92
            let e = peek(p)
            p.pos += 1
            let er = esc_ranges(e)
            if er.len() > 0
                if e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                for x in er
                    rs.push(x)
                continue
            if not is_meta(e) and not is_esc_letter(e)
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
            lo = esc_byte(e)
        var hi = lo
        if peek(p) == 45 and p.pos + 1 < p.pat.len() and p.pat[p.pos + 1] != 93
            p.pos += 1
            hi = peek(p)
            p.pos += 1
            if hi == 92
                let e2 = peek(p)
                p.pos += 1
                if not is_meta(e2) and not is_esc_letter(e2)
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                hi = esc_byte(e2)
            if hi < lo
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
        rs.push(lo)
        rs.push(hi)
    let at = add_class(p, neg, &rs)
    return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)

fn parse_num(p: &mut Parser) -> i64
    var v: i64 = -1
    while peek(p) >= 48 and peek(p) <= 57 bound 10
        v = (if v < 0 then 0 else v) * 10 + peek(p) - 48
        p.pos += 1
    return v

fn repeat(f: List[i64], m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..m
        o = cat(o, copy(f))
    if n < 0
        return cat(o, star(f))
    for _ in 0..(n - m)
        o = cat(o, opt(copy(f)))
    return o

fn parse_atom(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    let c = peek(p)
    p.pos += 1
    if c == 40
        if peek(p) == 63
            p.pos += 1
            if peek(p) != 58
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
            p.pos += 1
        let f = parse_alt(p)
        if peek(p) != 41
            p.err = p.pos as i64
            return []
        p.pos += 1
        return f
    if c == 91
        return parse_class(p)
    if c == 46
        return ins(OP_ANY, 0, 0)
    if c == 94
        return ins(OP_BOL, 0, 0)
    if c == 36
        return ins(OP_EOL, 0, 0)
    if c == 92
        let e = peek(p)
        p.pos += 1
        let er = esc_ranges(e)
        if er.len() > 0
            let at = add_class(p, e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83, &er)
            return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)
        if is_meta(e) or is_esc_letter(e)
            return ins(OP_BYTE, esc_byte(e), 0)
        p.err = p.pos as i64
        return []
    if c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 41 or c == 93 or c == 125
        p.err = (p.pos - 1) as i64
        return []
    return ins(OP_BYTE, c, 0)

fn parse_seq(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    var f: List[i64] = []
    while p.err < 0 bound 100000
        let c = peek(p)
        if c < 0 or c == 124 or c == 41
            break
        var a = parse_atom(p)
        while p.err < 0 bound 100
            let q = peek(p)
            if q == 42
                a = star(a)
            if q == 43
                a = plus(a)
            if q == 63
                a = opt(a)
            if q != 42 and q != 43 and q != 63 and q != 123
                break
            if q == 123
                p.pos += 1
                let m = parse_num(p)
                var n = m
                if peek(p) == 44
                    p.pos += 1
                    n = parse_num(p)
                if m < 0 or peek(p) != 125 or (n >= 0 and n < m) or m > 1000 or n > 1000
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                p.pos += 1
                a = repeat(a, m, n)
            if q != 123
                p.pos += 1
        f = cat(f, a)
    return f

fn parse_alt(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    var f = parse_seq(p)
    while peek(p) == 124 and p.err < 0 bound 100000
        p.pos += 1
        let g = parse_seq(p)
        f = alt(f, g)
    return f

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(s[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

pub fn compile(pattern: &text) -> Regex ! BadRegex
    var p = Parser(pat: bytes_of(pattern), pos: 0, classes: [], err: -1)
    let f = parse_alt(&mut p)
    if p.err < 0 and p.pos < p.pat.len()
        p.err = p.pos as i64
    if p.err >= 0
        fail BadRegex(at: p.err)
    return Regex(code: cat(f, ins(OP_MATCH, 0, 0)), classes: copy(p.classes))

fn in_class(cl: &[i64], at: usize, c: i64) -> bool
    let n = cl[at + 1] as usize
    var hit = false
    for k in 0..n
        hit = hit or (c >= cl[at + 2 + 2 * k] and c <= cl[at + 3 + 2 * k])
    return hit != (cl[at] == 1)

fn seq_len(c: i64) -> i64
    if c < 128
        return 1
    if c >= 240
        return 4
    if c >= 224
        return 3
    if c >= 192
        return 2
    return 1

fn spush(st: &mut List[i64], sp: usize, v: i64) -> usize
    if sp < st.len()
        st[sp] = v
    else
        st.push(v)
    return sp + 1

# Add pc and its epsilon closure at input position i to list l (marking
# with stamp so each pc enters once per step).
fn add(re: &Regex, l: &mut List[i64], mark: &mut List[i64], stamp: i64, pc0: i64, i: usize, n: usize)
    var st: List[i64] = [pc0]
    var sp: usize = 1
    while sp > 0 bound 1000000
        sp -= 1
        let pc = st[sp]
        if mark[pc as usize] == stamp
            continue
        mark[pc as usize] = stamp
        let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
        if op == OP_JMP
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
        if op == OP_SPLIT
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 2])
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
        if op == OP_BOL and i == 0
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
        if op == OP_EOL and i == n
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
        if op != OP_JMP and op != OP_SPLIT and op != OP_BOL and op != OP_EOL
            l.push(pc)

# Pike VM. full: the match must span the input; else any substring.
fn run(re: &Regex, b: &[i64], full: bool) -> bool
    let n = b.len()
    let np = re.code.len() / 3
    var mark: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..np
        mark.push(-1)
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    var stamp: i64 = 0
    add(re, &mut cur, &mut mark, stamp, 0, 0, n)
    # threads waiting for a multi-byte "." to finish: [pc, resume position]
    var pend: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        for pc in cur
            if re.code[3 * pc as usize] == OP_MATCH and (not full or i == n)
                return true
        if i >= n
            break
        stamp += 1
        var nxt: List[i64] = []
        var keep: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < pend.len() bound 1000000
            if pend[k + 1] == (i + 1) as i64
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pend[k], i + 1, n)
            else
                keep.push(pend[k])
                keep.push(pend[k + 1])
            k += 2
        let c = b[i]
        for pc in cur
            let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
            let a = re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1]
            let sl = seq_len(c)
            # a class tests a whole code point; non-ASCII ones lie outside
            # every (ASCII) range
            let cls = op == OP_CLASS and in_class(&re.classes, a as usize, if sl > 1 then -1 else c)
            let one = (op == OP_BYTE and c == a) or (cls and sl == 1) or (op == OP_ANY and sl == 1 and c != 10)
            if one
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pc + 1, i + 1, n)
            if (op == OP_ANY or cls) and sl > 1 and i + (sl as usize) <= n
                keep.push(pc + 1)
                keep.push((i as i64) + seq_len(c))
        # a search restarts only at code point boundaries
        if not full and (i + 1 >= n or b[i + 1] < 128 or b[i + 1] > 191)
            add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, 0, i + 1, n)
        cur = nxt
        pend = keep
        if cur.len() == 0 and pend.len() == 0 and full
            return false
        i += 1
    return false

pub fn is_match(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, true)

pub fn search(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, false)

module fmt

# Locale-free formatting, parsing and a linear-time regex (survey M17,
# part 1). No locale, no host call: the same input gives the same text on
# every host.
# - Integers: any radix 2..36, sign, zero/space padding, digit grouping;
#   strict parsing that refuses overflow, empty digits and stray bytes
#   (like C++ from_chars: no whitespace, no "0x", lowercase or uppercase
#   digits).
# - Templates: "{}" takes the next argument, "{N}" argument N, "{{" and
#   "}}" are literal braces.
# - Regex: a Thompson NFA run as a Pike VM, so matching costs
#   O(len(pattern) * len(input)) and never backtracks (RE2's guarantee).
#   Syntax: literals, ".", [...] and [^...] with ranges, \d \w \s \D \W
#   \S, \n \t \r, escapes of metacharacters, * + ? and {m}, {m,},
#   {m,n} (m, n <= 1000), |, (...), (?:...), ^ and $ (the ends of the
#   whole input, no multiline mode). It matches bytes of the UTF-8 text;
#   "." takes one whole UTF-8 sequence except "\n". Class ranges are ASCII;
#   a negated class or \D \W \S takes any whole non-ASCII sequence. No
#   captures or backreferences (not regular).

const DIGITS: text = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

error BadInt(at: i64)
error BadFormat(at: i64)
error BadRegex(at: i64)

# ---------------- integers ----------------

# Digits of v in radix r (2..36), lowercase, "-" for negatives; the full
# i64 range (the most negative value is handled without negating it).
pub fn int_to(v: i64, r: i64) -> text
    let ds = DIGITS.chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var s = ""
    var x = v
    while x != 0 bound 64
        let d = x % r
        let a = if d < 0 then 0 - d else d
        s = copy(ds[a as usize]) + s
        x = x / r
    return if v < 0 then "-" + s else s

pub fn int_dec(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 10)

pub fn int_hex(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 16)

fn digit_val(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 55
    return 99

# Strict parse in radix r: optional "+" or "-", then one or more digits,
# nothing else. Overflow of i64 is refused (BadInt at the digit).
pub fn int_parse(s: &text, r: i64) -> i64 ! BadInt
    let n = s.len_bytes()
    if n == 0
        fail BadInt(at: 0)
    var i: usize = 0
    var neg = false
    let c0 = s[0] as i64
    if c0 == 45 or c0 == 43
        neg = c0 == 45
        i = 1
    if i >= n
        fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
    # accumulate as a negative number: -2^63 fits, 2^63 does not
    var acc: i64 = 0
    let lim = (0 - 9223372036854775807 - 1)
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let d = digit_val(s[i] as i64)
        if d >= r
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        if acc < (lim + d) / r
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        let m = acc * r
        if m < lim + d
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        acc = m - d
        i += 1
    if not neg
        if acc == lim
            fail BadInt(at: (n - 1) as i64)
        return 0 - acc
    return acc

pub fn int_parse_dec(s: &text) -> i64 ! BadInt = int_parse(s, 10)

# Pad on the left to w code points with fill (one character).
pub fn pad_left(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = copy(fill) + o
        n += 1
    return o

pub fn pad_right(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = o + copy(fill)
        n += 1
    return o

# Zero padding after the sign: zero_pad(-42, 6) = "-00042".
pub fn zero_pad(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    let s = int_dec(v)
    let z = "0"
    if v < 0
        let cs = s.chars()
        var body = ""
        for i in 1..cs.len()
            body = body + copy(cs[i])
        return "-" + pad_left(&body, w - 1, &z)
    return pad_left(&s, w, &z)

# Group decimal digits by three with sep: group_dec(-1234567, ",") =
# "-1,234,567x".
pub fn group_dec(v: i64, sep: &text) -> text
    let cs = int_dec(v).chars()
    let start: usize = if v < 0 then 1 else 0
    let nd = cs.len() - start
    var o = if v < 0 then "-" else ""
    for k in 0..nd
        if k > 0 and (nd - k) % 3 == 0
            o = o + copy(sep)
        o = o + copy(cs[start + k])
    return o

# ---------------- templates ----------------

pub fn format(t: &text, args: &[text]) -> text ! BadFormat
    let cs = t.chars()
    let n = cs.len()
    var o = ""
    var next: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        if c == "{"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "{"
                o = o + "{"
                i += 2
            else
                var j = i + 1
                var idx: i64 = -1
                while j < n and cs[j] != "}" bound 1000000
                    let d = digit_val(cs[j][0] as i64)
                    if d > 9
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    idx = (if idx < 0 then 0 else idx) * 10 + d
                    if idx > 1000000
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    j += 1
                if j >= n
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                let k: usize = if idx < 0 then next else idx as usize
                if k >= args.len()
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                if idx < 0
                    next += 1
                o = o + copy(args[k])
                i = j + 1
            continue
        if c == "}"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "}"
                o = o + "}"
                i += 2
                continue
            fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
        o = o + c
        i += 1
    return o
