if cs.len() != 8 or not t.startswith("HTTP/") or cs[6] != "."
return false

let b = cs[7][0] as i64
if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57

m.minor = b - 48

if c == " "

cur = cur + c

pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: name: &text) -> text?

for i in 0..names.len()

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]

for c in v.chars()

fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")

m.used = h
return m
if not eof
fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")

o.push(b[k])
k += 1

        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# Index of the CRLF ending the line that starts at i, or -1 when the
# buffer ends first. A bare CR or LF is refused.
fn line_end(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        if b[k] == 13
            if k + 1 >= b.len()
                return -1
            if b[k + 1] != 10
                fail BadHttp(why: "bare CR")
            return k as i64
        if b[k] == 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "bare LF")
        k += 1
    return -1

fn ascii_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text ! BadHttp
    var o = ""
    var k = lo
    while k < hi bound 16777216
        let x = b[k]
        if x == 9
            o = o + "\t"
        elif x < 32 or x > 126
            fail BadHttp(why: "not ASCII text")
        else
            o = o + ch(x)
        k += 1
    return o

fn version(t: &text, m: &mut Message) -> bool
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 8 or not t.startswith("HTTP/") or cs[6] != "."
        return false
    let a = cs[5][0] as i64
    let b = cs[7][0] as i64
    if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57
        return false
    m.major = a - 48
    m.minor = b - 48
    return true

fn split_sp(t: &text) -> List[text]
    var parts: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == " "
            parts.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    parts.push(cur)
    return parts

fn start_line(t: &text, m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> bool ! BadHttp
    if req
        let ps = split_sp(t)
        if ps.len() != 3 or ps[0] == "" or ps[1] == ""
            fail BadHttp(why: "request line")
        for c in ps[0].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        for c in ps[1].chars()
            if not vchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "target")
        if not version(&ps[2], m)
            fail BadHttp(why: "version")
        m.method = copy(ps[0])
        m.target = copy(ps[1])
        return true
    # status-line = HTTP-version SP status-code SP [ reason-phrase ]
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 12 or cs[8] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var v = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        v = v + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if not version(&v, m)
        fail BadHttp(why: "version")
    var s: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 9
    while k < 12 bound 3
        let x = cs[k][0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        s = s * 10 + x - 48
        k += 1
    if cs.len() > 12 and cs[12] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var r = ""
    var j: usize = 13
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        r = r + cs[j]
        j += 1
    m.status = s
    m.reason = r
    m.request = false
    return true

fn trim_ows(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = cs.len()
    while lo < hi and (cs[lo] == " " or cs[lo] == "\t") bound 16777216
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and (cs[hi - 1] == " " or cs[hi - 1] == "\t") bound 16777216
        hi -= 1
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

# One field line "name: value" into names/values.
fn field(t: &text, names: &mut List[text], values: &mut List[text]) -> bool ! BadHttp
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[0] == " " or cs[0] == "\t")
        fail BadHttp(why: "obs-fold")
    var name = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != ":" bound 16777216
        if not tchar(cs[i][0] as i64)
            fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        name = name + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if i >= cs.len() or name == ""
        fail BadHttp(why: "field line")
    var v = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        v = v + cs[j]
        j += 1
    names.push(name)
    values.push(trim_ows(&v))
    return true

# The value of a field (case-insensitive name): the field values joined
# with ", " (RFC 9110 5.3), or none.
pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: &text) -> text?
    let want = lower(name)
    var found = false
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..names.len()
        if lower(&names[i]) == want
            o = if found then o + ", " + values[i] else copy(values[i])
            found = true
    return if found then some(o) else none

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in v.chars()
        if c == ","
            out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
    return out

fn dec(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + x - 48
    return v

fn hexnum(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        if d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
    return v

# Head: start line and fields, ending at the empty line. Returns the
# offset after it. Leading empty lines before a request are skipped (2.2).
fn head(b: &[i64], m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i: usize = 0
    if req
        while i + 1 < b.len() and b[i] == 13 and b[i + 1] == 10 bound 16
            i += 2
    let e = try line_end(b, i)
    if e < 0
        return -1
    let sl = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
    let _x = try start_line(&sl, m, req)
    i = (e + 2) as usize
    loop bound 16777216
        let f = try line_end(b, i)
        if f < 0
            return -1
        if f as usize == i
            return (i + 2) as i64
        let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
        var ns = copy(m.names)
        var vs = copy(m.values)
        let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
        m.names = ns
        m.values = vs
        i = (f + 2) as usize
    return -1

fn chunked(b: &[i64], start: usize, m: &mut Message) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i = start
    var body: List[i64] = []
    loop bound 16777216
        let e = try line_end(b, i)
        if e < 0
            return -1
        let line = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
        var size = ""
        for c in line.chars()
            if c == ";" or c == " " or c == "\t"
                break
            size = size + c
        let n = hexnum(&size)
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk size")
        i = (e + 2) as usize
        if n == 0
            loop bound 16777216
                let f = try line_end(b, i)
                if f < 0
                    return -1
                if f as usize == i
                    m.body = body
                    return (i + 2) as i64
                let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
                var ns = copy(m.trailer_names)
                var vs = copy(m.trailer_values)
                let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
                m.trailer_names = ns
                m.trailer_values = vs
                i = (f + 2) as usize
        if i + (n as usize) + 2 > b.len()
            return -1
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[i + k])
            k += 1
        i += n as usize
        if b[i] != 13 or b[i + 1] != 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk end")
        i += 2
    return -1

# Parse one message from the front of b. `eof` says the peer closed the
# connection (a response without a length then ends there). `head_req`
# says the response answers a HEAD request (no body). BadHttp(why:
# "incomplete ...") when b holds only part of the message.
pub fn parse_message(b: &[i64], req: bool, head_req: bool, eof: bool) -> Message ! BadHttp
    var m = message_empty()
    m.request = req
    let h = try head(b, &mut m, req)
    if h < 0
        fail BadHttp(why: "field head")
    let ten = "transfer-encoding"
    let cln = "content-length"
    let te = header(&m.names, &m.values, &ten)
    let cl = header(&m.names, &m.values, &cln)
    let no_body = not req and (head_req or (m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if no_body
        m.used = h
        return m
    if te != none
        if cl != none
            fail BadHttp(why: "both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length")
        let tv = te.or("")
        let items = list_items(&tv)
        if lower(&items[items.len() - 1]) != "chunked"
            if req
                fail BadHttp(why: "transfer coding")
            # a response: read until close (6.3 rule 4)
            if not eof
                fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
            m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
            m.used = b.len() as i64
            return m
        for k in 0..items.len() - 1
            if lower(&items[k]) == "chunked"
                fail BadHttp(why: "chunked twice")
        if items.len() > 1
            fail BadHttp(why: "unsupported transfer coding")
        let used = try chunked(b, h as usize, &mut m)
        if used < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete chunk")
        m.used = used
        return m
    if cl != none
        let cv = cl.or("")
        let items = list_items(&cv)
        let n = dec(&items[0])
        for it in items
            if dec(&it) != n
                fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if (h as usize) + (n as usize) > b.len()
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete body")
        var body: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[(h as usize) + k])
            k += 1
        m.body = body
        m.used = h + n
        return m
    if req
        m.used = h
        return m
    if not eof
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
    m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
    m.used = b.len() as i64
    return m

fn rest(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(b[k])
        k += 1
    return o

# ---------------- serialization ----------------

fn put(o: &mut List[i64], t: &text)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1

# Serialize with the given fields in order, then Content-Length of the
# body unless a Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding field is given or the
# message has no body by its status. The body is written as is (a caller
# that set Transfer-Encoding: chunked passes chunked bytes, see chunk).
pub fn serialize(m: &Message) -> List[i64] ! BadHttp
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if m.request
        for c in m.method.chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        let line = m.method + " " + m.target + " HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    else
        if m.status < 100 or m.status > 999
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        let line = "HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + " " + m.status.tostr() + " " + m.reason + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    var framed = false
    for i in 0..m.names.len()
        for c in m.names[i].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        for c in m.values[i].chars()
            let x = c[0] as i64
            if c.len_bytes() != 1 or (x < 32 and x != 9) or x == 127
                fail BadHttp(why: "field value")
        let l = lower(&m.names[i])
        if l == "content-length" or l == "transfer-encoding"
            framed = true
        let line = m.names[i] + ": " + m.values[i] + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let bodyless = not m.request and ((m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if not framed and not bodyless and (not m.request or m.body.len() > 0)
        let line = "Content-Length: " + m.body.len().tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let crlf = "\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &crlf)
    for x in m.body
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn hexlow(n: i64) -> text
    if n == 0
        return "0"
    let hs = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = n
    while x > 0 bound 16
        o = copy(hs[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
    return o

# Chunked transfer coding of data in chunks of at most size bytes, with
# the last chunk and an empty trailer.
pub fn chunk(data: &[i64], size: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    let sz = if size < 1 then 1 else size
    var i: i64 = 0
    let n = data.len() as i64
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let k = if n - i < sz then n - i else sz
        let line = hexlow(k) + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < k bound 16777216
            o.push(data[(i + j) as usize])
            j += 1
        let crlf = "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &crlf)
        i += k
    let last = "0\r\n\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &last)
    return o

module net.http

# HTTP/1.1 messages (RFC 9112, survey M25 pure part): parse and serialize
# requests and responses over bytes (List[i64], 0..255), with message
# body framing (RFC 9112 6) or chunked transfer coding (7.1). Strict
# where the RFC lets a recipient choose: lines end in CRLF (a bare CR or
# LF is refused), obs-fold is refused (5.2), whitespace before a field
# colon is refused (5.1), Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length
# is refused (6.1, request smuggling), differing Content-Length values
# are refused (6.3). Field values must be ASCII (obs-text needs text built
# from bytes, which RCE 0.1.3 cannot do). No socket here: a connection is
# the io module's request/result pattern; parse fails with a why that
# starts "incomplete" when more bytes are needed.

error BadHttp(why: text)

pub struct Message
    request: bool
    method: text
    target: text
    major: i64
    minor: i64
    status: i64
    reason: text
    names: List[text]
    values: List[text]
    body: List[i64]
    trailer_names: List[text]
    trailer_values: List[text]
    used: i64

pub fn message_empty() -> Message = Message(request: true, method: "", target: "", major: 1, minor: 1, status: 0, reason: "", names: [], values: [], body: [], trailer_names: [], trailer_values: [], used: 0)

const HT_ASCII: text = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~"

fn ch(x: i64) -> text = copy(HT_ASCII.chars()[(x - 32) as usize])

fn tchar(c: i64) -> bool
    if (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122)
        return true
    return c == 33 or c == 35 or c == 36 or c == 37 or c == 38 or c == 39 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 45 or c == 46 or c == 94 or c == 95 or c == 96 or c == 124 or c == 126

fn vchar(c: i64) -> bool = c >= 33 and c <= 126

fn lower(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        o = o + (if x >= 65 and x <= 90 then ch(x + 32) else c)
    return o

pub fn bytes_of(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# Index of the CRLF ending the line that starts at i, or -1 when the
# buffer ends first. A bare CR or LF is refused.
fn line_end(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        if b[k] == 13
            if k + 1 >= b.len()
                return -1
            if b[k + 1] != 10
                fail BadHttp(why: "bare CR")
            return k as i64
        if b[k] == 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "bare LF")
        k += 1
    return -1

fn ascii_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text ! BadHttp
    var o = ""
    var k = lo
    while k < hi bound 16777216
        let x = b[k]
        if x == 9
            o = o + "\t"
        elif x < 32 or x > 126
            fail BadHttp(why: "not ASCII text")
        else
            o = o + ch(x)
        k += 1
    return o

fn version(t: &text, m: &mut Message) -> bool
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 8 or not t.startswith("HTTP/") or cs[6] != "."
        return false
    let a = cs[5][0] as i64
    let b = cs[7][0] as i64
    if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57
        return false
    m.major = a - 48
    m.minor = b - 48
    return true

fn split_sp(t: &text) -> List[text]
    var parts: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == " "
            parts.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    parts.push(cur)
    return parts

fn start_line(t: &text, m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> bool ! BadHttp
    if req
        let ps = split_sp(t)
        if ps.len() != 3 or ps[0] == "" or ps[1] == ""
            fail BadHttp(why: "request line")
        for c in ps[0].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        for c in ps[1].chars()
            if not vchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "target")
        if not version(&ps[2], m)
            fail BadHttp(why: "version")
        m.method = copy(ps[0])
        m.target = copy(ps[1])
        return true
    # status-line = HTTP-version SP status-code SP [ reason-phrase ]
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 12 or cs[8] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var v = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        v = v + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if not version(&v, m)
        fail BadHttp(why: "version")
    var s: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 9
    while k < 12 bound 3
        let x = cs[k][0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        s = s * 10 + x - 48
        k += 1
    if cs.len() > 12 and cs[12] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var r = ""
    var j: usize = 13
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        r = r + cs[j]
        j += 1
    m.status = s
    m.reason = r
    m.request = false
    return true

fn trim_ows(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = cs.len()
    while lo < hi and (cs[lo] == " " or cs[lo] == "\t") bound 16777216
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and (cs[hi - 1] == " " or cs[hi - 1] == "\t") bound 16777216
        hi -= 1
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

# One field line "name: value" into names/values.
fn field(t: &text, names: &mut List[text], values: &mut List[text]) -> bool ! BadHttp
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[0] == " " or cs[0] == "\t")
        fail BadHttp(why: "obs-fold")
    var name = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != ":" bound 16777216
        if not tchar(cs[i][0] as i64)
            fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        name = name + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if i >= cs.len() or name == ""
        fail BadHttp(why: "field line")
    var v = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        v = v + cs[j]
        j += 1
    names.push(name)
    values.push(trim_ows(&v))
    return true

# The value of a field (case-insensitive name): the field values joined
# with ", " (RFC 9110 5.3), or none.
pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: &text) -> text?
    let want = lower(name)
    var found = false
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..names.len()
        if lower(&names[i]) == want
            o = if found then o + ", " + values[i] else copy(values[i])
            found = true
    return if found then some(o) else none

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in v.chars()
        if c == ","
            out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
    return out

fn dec(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + x - 48
    return v

fn hexnum(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        if d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
    return v

# Head: start line and fields, ending at the empty line. Returns the
# offset after it. Leading empty lines before a request are skipped (2.2).
fn head(b: &[i64], m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i: usize = 0
    if req
        while i + 1 < b.len() and b[i] == 13 and b[i + 1] == 10 bound 16
            i += 2
    let e = try line_end(b, i)
    if e < 0
        return -1
    let sl = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
    let _x = try start_line(&sl, m, req)
    i = (e + 2) as usize
    loop bound 16777216
        let f = try line_end(b, i)
        if f < 0
            return -1
        if f as usize == i
            return (i + 2) as i64
        let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
        var ns = copy(m.names)
        var vs = copy(m.values)
        let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
        m.names = ns
        m.values = vs
        i = (f + 2) as usize
    return -1

fn chunked(b: &[i64], start: usize, m: &mut Message) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i = start
    var body: List[i64] = []
    loop bound 16777216
        let e = try line_end(b, i)
        if e < 0
            return -1
        let line = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
        var size = ""
        for c in line.chars()
            if c == ";" or c == " " or c == "\t"
                break
            size = size + c
        let n = hexnum(&size)
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk size")
        i = (e + 2) as usize
        if n == 0
            loop bound 16777216
                let f = try line_end(b, i)
                if f < 0
                    return -1
                if f as usize == i
                    m.body = body
                    return (i + 2) as i64
                let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
                var ns = copy(m.trailer_names)
                var vs = copy(m.trailer_values)
                let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
                m.trailer_names = ns
                m.trailer_values = vs
                i = (f + 2) as usize
        if i + (n as usize) + 2 > b.len()
            return -1
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[i + k])
            k += 1
        i += n as usize
        if b[i] != 13 or b[i + 1] != 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk end")
        i += 2
    return -1

# Parse one message from the front of b. `eof` says the peer closed the
# connection (a response without a length then ends there). `head_req`
# says the response answers a HEAD request (no body). BadHttp(why:
# "incomplete ...") when b holds only part of the message.
pub fn parse_message(b: &[i64], req: bool, head_req: bool, eof: bool) -> Message ! BadHttp
    var m = message_empty()
    m.request = req
    let h = try head(b, &mut m, req)
    if h < 0
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete head")
    let ten = "transfer-encoding"
    let cln = "content-length"
    let te = header(&m.names, &m.values, &ten)
    let cl = header(&m.names, &m.values, &cln)
    let no_body = not req and (head_req or (m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if no_body
        m.used = h
        return m
    if te != none
        if cl != none
            fail BadHttp(why: "both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length")
        let tv = te.or("")
        let items = list_items(&tv)
        if lower(&items[items.len() - 1]) != "chunked"
            if req
                fail BadHttp(why: "transfer coding")
            # a response: read until close (6.3 rule 4)
            if not eof
                fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
            m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
            m.used = b.len() as i64
            return m
        for k in 0..items.len() - 1
            if lower(&items[k]) == "chunked"
                fail BadHttp(why: "chunked twice")
        if items.len() > 1
            fail BadHttp(why: "unsupported transfer coding")
        let used = try chunked(b, h as usize, &mut m)
        if used < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete chunk")
        m.used = used
        return m
    if cl != none
        let cv = cl.or("")
        let items = list_items(&cv)
        let n = dec(&items[0])
        for it in items
            if dec(&it) != n
                fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if (h as usize) + (n as usize) > b.len()
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete body")
        var body: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[(h as usize) + k])
            k += 1
        m.body = body
        m.used = h + n
        return m
    if req
        m.used = h
        return m
    if not eof
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
    m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
    m.used = b.len() as i64
    return m

fn rest(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(b[k])
        k += 1
    return o

# ---------------- serialization ----------------

fn put(o: &mut List[i64], t: &text)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1

# Serialize with the given fields in order, then Content-Length of the
# body unless a Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding field is given or the
# message has no body by its status. The body is written as is (a caller
# that set Transfer-Encoding: chunked passes chunked bytes, see chunk).
pub fn serialize(m: &Message) -> List[i64] ! BadHttp
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if m.request
        for c in m.method.chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        let line = m.method + " " + m.target + " HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    else
        if m.status < 100 or m.status > 999
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        let line = "HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + " " + m.status.tostr() + " " + m.reason + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    var framed = false
    for i in 0..m.names.len()
        for c in m.names[i].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        for c in m.values[i].chars()
            let x = c[0] as i64
            if c.len_bytes() != 1 or (x < 32 and x != 9) or x == 127
                fail BadHttp(why: "field value")
        let l = lower(&m.names[i])
        if l == "content-length" or l == "transfer-encoding"
            framed = true
        let line = m.names[i] + ": " + m.values[i] + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let bodyless = not m.request and ((m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if not framed and not bodyless and (not m.request or m.body.len() > 0)
        let line = "Content-Length: " + m.body.len().tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let crlf = "\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &crlf)
    for x in m.body
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn hexlow(n: i64) -> text
    if n == 0
        return "0"
    let hs = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = n
    while x > 0 bound 16
        o = copy(hs[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
    return o

# Chunked transfer coding of data in chunks of at most size bytes, with
# the last chunk and an empty trailer.
pub fn chunk(data: &[i64], size: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    let sz = if size < 1 then 1 else size
    var i: i64 = 0
    let n = data.len() as i64
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let k = if n - i < sz then n - i else sz
        let line = hexlow(k) + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < k bound 16777216
            o.push(data[(i + j) as usize])
            j += 1
        let crlf = "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &crlf)
        i += k
    let last = "0\r\n\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &last)
    return o

module net.http

# HTTP/1.1 messages (RFC 9112, survey M25 pure part): parse or serialize
# requests and responses over bytes (List[i64], 0..255), with message
# body framing (RFC 9112 6) and chunked transfer coding (7.1). Strict
# where the RFC lets a recipient choose: lines end in CRLF (a bare CR or
# LF is refused), obs-fold is refused (5.2), whitespace before a field
# colon is refused (5.1), Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length
# is refused (6.1, request smuggling), differing Content-Length values
# are refused (6.3). Field values must be ASCII (obs-text needs text built
# from bytes, which RCE 0.1.3 cannot do). No socket here: a connection is
# the io module's request/result pattern; parse fails with a why that
# starts "incomplete" when more bytes are needed.

error BadHttp(why: text)

pub struct Message
    request: bool
    method: text
    target: text
    major: i64
    minor: i64
    status: i64
    reason: text
    names: List[text]
    values: List[text]
    body: List[i64]
    trailer_names: List[text]
    trailer_values: List[text]
    used: i64

pub fn message_empty() -> Message = Message(request: true, method: "", target: "", major: 1, minor: 1, status: 0, reason: "", names: [], values: [], body: [], trailer_names: [], trailer_values: [], used: 0)

const HT_ASCII: text = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~"

fn ch(x: i64) -> text = copy(HT_ASCII.chars()[(x - 32) as usize])

fn tchar(c: i64) -> bool
    if (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122)
        return true
    return c == 33 or c == 35 or c == 36 or c == 37 or c == 38 or c == 39 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 45 or c == 46 or c == 94 or c == 95 or c == 96 or c == 124 or c == 126

fn vchar(c: i64) -> bool = c >= 33 and c <= 126

fn lower(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        o = o + (if x >= 65 and x <= 90 then ch(x + 32) else c)
    return o

pub fn bytes_of(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# Index of the CRLF ending the line that starts at i, or -1 when the
# buffer ends first. A bare CR or LF is refused.
fn line_end(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        if b[k] == 13
            if k + 1 >= b.len()
                return -1
            if b[k + 1] != 10
                fail BadHttp(why: "bare CR")
            return k as i64
        if b[k] == 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "bare LF")
        k += 1
    return -1

fn ascii_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text ! BadHttp
    var o = ""
    var k = lo
    while k < hi bound 16777216
        let x = b[k]
        if x == 9
            o = o + "\t"
        elif x < 32 or x > 126
            fail BadHttp(why: "not ASCII text")
        else
            o = o + ch(x)
        k += 1
    return o

fn version(t: &text, m: &mut Message) -> bool
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 8 or not t.startswith("HTTP/") or cs[6] != "."
        return false
    let a = cs[5][0] as i64
    let b = cs[7][0] as i64
    if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57
        return false
    m.major = a - 48
    m.minor = b - 48
    return true

fn split_sp(t: &text) -> List[text]
    var parts: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == " "
            parts.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    parts.push(cur)
    return parts

fn start_line(t: &text, m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> bool ! BadHttp
    if req
        let ps = split_sp(t)
        if ps.len() != 3 or ps[0] == "" or ps[1] == ""
            fail BadHttp(why: "request line")
        for c in ps[0].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        for c in ps[1].chars()
            if not vchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "target")
        if not version(&ps[2], m)
            fail BadHttp(why: "version")
        m.method = copy(ps[0])
        m.target = copy(ps[1])
        return true
    # status-line = HTTP-version SP status-code SP [ reason-phrase ]
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 12 or cs[8] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var v = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        v = v + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if not version(&v, m)
        fail BadHttp(why: "version")
    var s: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 9
    while k < 12 bound 3
        let x = cs[k][0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        s = s * 10 + x - 48
        k += 1
    if cs.len() > 12 and cs[12] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var r = ""
    var j: usize = 13
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        r = r + cs[j]
        j += 1
    m.status = s
    m.reason = r
    m.request = false
    return true

fn trim_ows(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = cs.len()
    while lo < hi and (cs[lo] == " " or cs[lo] == "\t") bound 16777216
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and (cs[hi - 1] == " " or cs[hi - 1] == "\t") bound 16777216
        hi -= 1
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

# One field line "name: value" into names/values.
fn field(t: &text, names: &mut List[text], values: &mut List[text]) -> bool ! BadHttp
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[0] == " " or cs[0] == "\t")
        fail BadHttp(why: "obs-fold")
    var name = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != ":" bound 16777216
        if not tchar(cs[i][0] as i64)
            fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        name = name + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if i >= cs.len() or name == ""
        fail BadHttp(why: "field line")
    var v = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        v = v + cs[j]
        j += 1
    names.push(name)
    values.push(trim_ows(&v))
    return true

# The value of a field (case-insensitive name): the field values joined
# with ", " (RFC 9110 5.3), or none.
pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: &text) -> text?
    let want = lower(name)
    var found = false
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..names.len()
        if lower(&names[i]) == want
            o = if found then o + ", " + values[i] else copy(values[i])
            found = true
    return if found then some(o) else none

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in v.chars()
        if c == ","
            out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
    return out

fn dec(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + x - 48
    return v

fn hexnum(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        if d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
    return v

# Head: start line and fields, ending at the empty line. Returns the
# offset after it. Leading empty lines before a request are skipped (2.2).
fn head(b: &[i64], m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i: usize = 0
    if req
        while i + 1 < b.len() and b[i] == 13 and b[i + 1] == 10 bound 16
            i += 2
    let e = try line_end(b, i)
    if e < 0
        return -1
    let sl = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
    let _x = try start_line(&sl, m, req)
    i = (e + 2) as usize
    loop bound 16777216
        let f = try line_end(b, i)
        if f < 0
            return -1
        if f as usize == i
            return (i + 2) as i64
        let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
        var ns = copy(m.names)
        var vs = copy(m.values)
        let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
        m.names = ns
        m.values = vs
        i = (f + 2) as usize
    return -1

fn chunked(b: &[i64], start: usize, m: &mut Message) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i = start
    var body: List[i64] = []
    loop bound 16777216
        let e = try line_end(b, i)
        if e < 0
            return -1
        let line = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
        var size = ""
        for c in line.chars()
            if c == ";" or c == " " or c == "\t"
                break
            size = size + c
        let n = hexnum(&size)
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk size")
        i = (e + 2) as usize
        if n == 0
            loop bound 16777216
                let f = try line_end(b, i)
                if f < 0
                    return -1
                if f as usize == i
                    m.body = body
                    return (i + 2) as i64
                let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
                var ns = copy(m.trailer_names)
                var vs = copy(m.trailer_values)
                let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
                m.trailer_names = ns
                m.trailer_values = vs
                i = (f + 2) as usize
        if i + (n as usize) + 2 > b.len()
            return -1
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[i + k])
            k += 1
        i += n as usize
        if b[i] != 13 or b[i + 1] != 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk end")
        i += 2
    return -1

# Parse one message from the front of b. `eof` says the peer closed the
# connection (a response without a length then ends there). `head_req`
# says the response answers a HEAD request (no body). BadHttp(why:
# "incomplete ...") when b holds only part of the message.
pub fn parse_message(b: &[i64], req: bool, head_req: bool, eof: bool) -> Message ! BadHttp
    var m = message_empty()
    m.request = req
    let h = try head(b, &mut m, req)
    if h < 0
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete head")
    let ten = "transfer-encoding"
    let cln = "content-length"
    let te = header(&m.names, &m.values, &ten)
    let cl = header(&m.names, &m.values, &cln)
    let no_body = not req and (head_req or (m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if no_body
        m.used = h
        return m
    if te != none
        if cl != none
            fail BadHttp(why: "both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length")
        let tv = te.or("")
        let items = list_items(&tv)
        if lower(&items[items.len() - 1]) != "chunked"
            if req
                fail BadHttp(why: "transfer coding")
            # a response: read until close (6.3 rule 4)
            if not eof
                fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
            m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
            m.used = b.len() as i64
            return m
        for k in 0..items.len() - 1
            if lower(&items[k]) == "chunked"
                fail BadHttp(why: "chunked twice")
        if items.len() > 1
            fail BadHttp(why: "unsupported transfer coding")
        let used = try chunked(b, h as usize, &mut m)
        if used < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete chunk")
        m.used = used
        return m
    if cl != none
        let cv = cl.or("")
        let items = list_items(&cv)
        let n = dec(&items[0])
        for it in items
            if dec(&it) != n
                fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if (h as usize) + (n as usize) > b.len()
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete body")
        var body: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[(h as usize) + k])
            k += 1
        m.body = body
        m.used = h + n
        return m
    if req
        m.used = h
        return m
    if not eof
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
    m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
    m.used = b.len() as i64
    return m

fn rest(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(b[k])
        k += 1
    return o

# ---------------- serialization ----------------

fn put(o: &mut List[i64], t: &text)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1

# Serialize with the given fields in order, then Content-Length of the
# body unless a Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding field is given or the
# message has no body by its status. The body is written as is (a caller
# that set Transfer-Encoding: chunked passes chunked bytes, see chunk).
pub fn serialize(m: &Message) -> List[i64] ! BadHttp
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if m.request
        for c in m.method.chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        let line = m.method + " " + m.target + " HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    else
        if m.status < 100 or m.status > 999
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        let line = "HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + " " + m.status.tostr() + " " + m.reason + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    var framed = false
    for i in 0..m.names.len()
        for c in m.names[i].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        for c in m.values[i].chars()
            let x = c[0] as i64
            if c.len_bytes() != 1 or (x < 32 and x != 9) or x == 127
                fail BadHttp(why: "field value")
        let l = lower(&m.names[i])
        if l == "content-length" or l == "transfer-encoding"
            framed = true
        let line = m.names[i] + ": " + m.values[i] + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let bodyless = not m.request and ((m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if not framed and not bodyless and (not m.request or m.body.len() > 0)
        let line = "Content-Length: " + m.body.len().tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let crlf = "\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &crlf)
    for x in m.body
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn hexlow(n: i64) -> text
    if n == 0
        return "0"
    let hs = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    var o = ""

    body: List[i64]

    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# Index of the CRLF ending the line that starts at i, or -1 when the
# buffer ends first. A bare CR or LF is refused.
fn line_end(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        if b[k] == 13
            if k + 1 >= b.len()
                return -1
            if b[k + 1] != 10
                fail BadHttp(why: "bare CR")
            return k as i64
        if b[k] == 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "bare LF")
        k += 1
    return -1

fn ascii_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text ! BadHttp
    var o = ""
    var k = lo
    while k < hi bound 16777216
        let x = b[k]
        if x == 9
            o = o + "\t"
        elif x < 32 or x > 126
            fail BadHttp(why: "not ASCII text")
        else
            o = o + ch(x)
        k += 1
    return o

fn version(t: &text, m: &mut Message) -> bool
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 8 or not t.startswith("HTTP/") or cs[6] != "."
        return false
    let a = cs[5][0] as i64
    let b = cs[7][0] as i64
    if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57
        return false
    m.major = a - 48
    m.minor = b - 48
    return true

fn split_sp(t: &text) -> List[text]
    var parts: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == " "
            parts.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    parts.push(cur)
    return parts

fn start_line(t: &text, m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> bool ! BadHttp
    if req
        let ps = split_sp(t)
        if ps.len() != 3 or ps[0] == "" or ps[1] == ""
            fail BadHttp(why: "request line")
        for c in ps[0].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        for c in ps[1].chars()
            if not vchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "target")
        if not version(&ps[2], m)
            fail BadHttp(why: "version")
        m.method = copy(ps[0])
        m.target = copy(ps[1])
        return true
    # status-line = HTTP-version SP status-code SP [ reason-phrase ]
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 12 or cs[8] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var v = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        v = v + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if not version(&v, m)
        fail BadHttp(why: "version")
    var s: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 9
    while k < 12 bound 3
        let x = cs[k][0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        s = s * 10 + x - 48
        k += 1
    if cs.len() > 12 and cs[12] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var r = ""
    var j: usize = 13
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        r = r + cs[j]
        j += 1
    m.status = s
    m.reason = r
    m.request = false
    return true

fn trim_ows(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = cs.len()
    while lo < hi and (cs[lo] == " " or cs[lo] == "\t") bound 16777216
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and (cs[hi - 1] == " " or cs[hi - 1] == "\t") bound 16777216
        hi -= 1
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

# One field line "name: value" into names/values.
fn field(t: &text, names: &mut List[text], values: &mut List[text]) -> bool ! BadHttp
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[0] == " " or cs[0] == "\t")
        fail BadHttp(why: "obs-fold")
    var name = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != ":" bound 16777216
        if not tchar(cs[i][0] as i64)
            fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        name = name + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if i >= cs.len() or name == ""
        fail BadHttp(why: "field line")
    var v = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        v = v + cs[j]
        j += 1
    names.push(name)
    values.push(trim_ows(&v))
    return true

# The value of a field (case-insensitive name): the field values joined
# with ", " (RFC 9110 5.3), or none.
pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: &text) -> text?
    let want = lower(name)
    var found = false
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..names.len()
        if lower(&names[i]) == want
            o = if found then o + ", " + values[i] else copy(values[i])
            found = true
    return if found then some(o) else none

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in v.chars()
        if c == ","
            out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
    return out

fn dec(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + x - 48
    return v

fn hexnum(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        if d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
    return v

# Head: start line and fields, ending at the empty line. Returns the
# offset after it. Leading empty lines before a request are skipped (2.2).
fn head(b: &[i64], m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i: usize = 0
    if req
        while i + 1 < b.len() and b[i] == 13 and b[i + 1] == 10 bound 16
            i += 2
    let e = try line_end(b, i)
    if e < 0
        return -1
    let sl = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
    let _x = try start_line(&sl, m, req)
    i = (e + 2) as usize
    loop bound 16777216
        let f = try line_end(b, i)
        if f < 0
            return -1
        if f as usize == i
            return (i + 2) as i64
        let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
        var ns = copy(m.names)
        var vs = copy(m.values)
        let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
        m.names = ns
        m.values = vs
        i = (f + 2) as usize
    return -1

fn chunked(b: &[i64], start: usize, m: &mut Message) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i = start
    var body: List[i64] = []
    loop bound 16777216
        let e = try line_end(b, i)
        if e < 0
            return -1
        let line = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
        var size = ""
        for c in line.chars()
            if c == ";" or c == " " or c == "\t"
                break
            size = size + c
        let n = hexnum(&size)
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk size")
        i = (e + 2) as usize
        if n == 0
            loop bound 16777216
                let f = try line_end(b, i)
                if f < 0
                    return -1
                if f as usize == i
                    m.body = body
                    return (i + 2) as i64
                let t = try ascii_text(b, i, f as usize)
                var ns = copy(m.trailer_names)
                var vs = copy(m.trailer_values)
                let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
                m.trailer_names = ns
                m.trailer_values = vs
                i = (f + 2) as usize
        if i + (n as usize) + 2 > b.len()
            return -1
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[i + k])
            k += 1
        i += n as usize
        if b[i] != 13 or b[i + 1] != 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "chunk end")
        i += 2
    return -1

# Parse one message from the front of b. `eof` says the peer closed the
# connection (a response without a length then ends there). `head_req`
# says the response answers a HEAD request (no body). BadHttp(why:
# "incomplete ...") when b holds only part of the message.
pub fn parse_message(b: &[i64], req: bool, head_req: bool, eof: bool) -> Message ! BadHttp
    var m = message_empty()
    m.request = req
    let h = try head(b, &mut m, req)
    if h < 0
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete head")
    let ten = "transfer-encoding"
    let cln = "content-length"
    let te = header(&m.names, &m.values, &ten)
    let cl = header(&m.names, &m.values, &cln)
    let no_body = not req and (head_req or (m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if no_body
        m.used = h
        return m
    if te != none
        if cl != none
            fail BadHttp(why: "both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length")
        let tv = te.or("")
        let items = list_items(&tv)
        if lower(&items[items.len() - 1]) != "chunked"
            if req
                fail BadHttp(why: "transfer coding")
            # a response: read until close (6.3 rule 4)
            if not eof
                fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
            m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
            m.used = b.len() as i64
            return m
        for k in 0..items.len() - 1
            if lower(&items[k]) == "chunked"
                fail BadHttp(why: "chunked twice")
        if items.len() > 1
            fail BadHttp(why: "unsupported transfer coding")
        let used = try chunked(b, h as usize, &mut m)
        if used < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete chunk")
        m.used = used
        return m
    if cl != none
        let cv = cl.or("")
        let items = list_items(&cv)
        let n = dec(&items[0])
        for it in items
            if dec(&it) != n
                fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if n < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")
        if (h as usize) + (n as usize) > b.len()
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete body")
        var body: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[(h as usize) + k])
            k += 1
        m.body = body
        m.used = h + n
        return m
    if req
        m.used = h
        return m
    if not eof
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
    m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
    m.used = b.len() as i64
    return m

fn rest(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(b[k])
        k += 1
    return o

# ---------------- serialization ----------------

fn put(o: &mut List[i64], t: &text)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1

# Serialize with the given fields in order, then Content-Length of the
# body unless a Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding field is given or the
# message has no body by its status. The body is written as is (a caller
# that set Transfer-Encoding: chunked passes chunked bytes, see chunk).
pub fn serialize(m: &Message) -> List[i64] ! BadHttp
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if m.request
        for c in m.method.chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        let line = m.method + " " + m.target + " HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    else
        if m.status < 100 or m.status > 999
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        let line = "HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + " " + m.status.tostr() + " " + m.reason + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    var framed = false
    for i in 0..m.names.len()
        for c in m.names[i].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        for c in m.values[i].chars()
            let x = c[0] as i64
            if c.len_bytes() != 1 or (x < 32 and x != 9) or x == 127
                fail BadHttp(why: "field value")
        let l = lower(&m.names[i])
        if l == "content-length" or l == "transfer-encoding"
            framed = true
        let line = m.names[i] + ": " + m.values[i] + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let bodyless = not m.request and ((m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if not framed and not bodyless and (not m.request or m.body.len() > 0)
        let line = "Content-Length: " + m.body.len().tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let crlf = "\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &crlf)
    for x in m.body
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn hexlow(n: i64) -> text
    if n == 0
        return "0"
    let hs = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = n
    while x > 0 bound 16
        o = copy(hs[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
    return o

# Chunked transfer coding of data in chunks of at most size bytes, with
# the last chunk and an empty trailer.
pub fn chunk(data: &[i64], size: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    let sz = if size < 1 then 1 else size
    var i: i64 = 0
    let n = data.len() as i64
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let k = if n - i < sz then n - i else sz
        let line = hexlow(k) + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < k bound 16777216
            o.push(data[(i + j) as usize])
            j += 1
        let crlf = "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &crlf)
        i += k
    let last = "0\r\n\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &last)
    return o

module net.http

# HTTP/1.1 messages (RFC 9112, survey M25 pure part): parse and serialize
# requests and responses over bytes (List[i64], 0..255), with message
# body framing (RFC 9112 6) and chunked transfer coding (7.1). Strict
# where the RFC lets a recipient choose: lines end in CRLF (a bare CR or
# LF is refused), obs-fold is refused (5.2), whitespace before a field
# colon is refused (5.1), Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length
# is refused (6.1, request smuggling), differing Content-Length values
# are refused (6.3). Field values must be ASCII (obs-bool needs text built
# from bytes, which RCE 0.1.3 cannot do). No socket here: a connection is
# the io module's request/result pattern; parse fails with a why that
# starts "incomplete" when more bytes are needed.

error BadHttp(why: text)

pub struct Message
    request: bool
    method: text
    target: text
    major: i64
    minor: i64
    status: i64
    reason: text
    names: List[text]
    values: List[text]
    body: List[i64]
    trailer_names: List[text]
    trailer_values: List[text]
    used: i64

pub fn message_empty() -> Message = Message(request: true, method: "", target: "", major: 1, minor: 1, status: 0, reason: "", names: [], values: [], body: [], trailer_names: [], trailer_values: [], used: 0)

const HT_ASCII: text = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~"

fn ch(x: i64) -> text = copy(HT_ASCII.chars()[(x - 32) as usize])

fn tchar(c: i64) -> bool
    if (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122)
        return true
    return c == 33 or c == 35 or c == 36 or c == 37 or c == 38 or c == 39 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 45 or c == 46 or c == 94 or c == 95 or c == 96 or c == 124 or c == 126

fn vchar(c: i64) -> bool = c >= 33 and c <= 126

fn lower(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        o = o + (if x >= 65 and x <= 90 then ch(x + 32) else c)
    return o

pub fn bytes_of(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# Index of the CRLF ending the line that starts at i, or -1 when the
# buffer ends first. A bare CR or LF is refused.
fn line_end(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        if b[k] == 13
            if k + 1 >= b.len()
                return -1
            if b[k + 1] != 10
                fail BadHttp(why: "bare CR")
            return k as i64
        if b[k] == 10
            fail BadHttp(why: "bare LF")
        k += 1
    return -1

fn ascii_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text ! BadHttp
    var o = ""
    var k = lo
    while k < hi bound 16777216
        let x = b[k]
        if x == 9
            o = o + "\t"
        elif x < 32 or x > 126
            fail BadHttp(why: "not ASCII text")
        else
            o = o + ch(x)
        k += 1
    return o

fn version(t: &text, m: &mut Message) -> bool
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 8 or not t.startswith("HTTP/") or cs[6] != "."
        return false
    let a = cs[5][0] as i64
    let b = cs[7][0] as i64
    if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57
        return false
    m.major = a - 48
    m.minor = b - 48
    return true

fn split_sp(t: &text) -> List[text]
    var parts: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == " "
            parts.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    parts.push(cur)
    return parts

fn start_line(t: &text, m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> bool ! BadHttp
    if req
        let ps = split_sp(t)
        if ps.len() != 3 or ps[0] == "" or ps[1] == ""
            fail BadHttp(why: "request line")
        for c in ps[0].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        for c in ps[1].chars()
            if not vchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "target")
        if not version(&ps[2], m)
            fail BadHttp(why: "version")
        m.method = copy(ps[0])
        m.target = copy(ps[1])
        return true
    # status-line = HTTP-version SP status-code SP [ reason-phrase ]
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 12 or cs[8] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var v = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        v = v + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if not version(&v, m)
        fail BadHttp(why: "version")
    var s: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 9
    while k < 12 bound 3
        let x = cs[k][0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        s = s * 10 + x - 48
        k += 1
    if cs.len() > 12 and cs[12] != " "
        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")
    var r = ""
    var j: usize = 13
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        r = r + cs[j]
        j += 1
    m.status = s
    m.reason = r
    m.request = false
    return true

fn trim_ows(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = cs.len()
    while lo < hi and (cs[lo] == " " or cs[lo] == "\t") bound 16777216
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and (cs[hi - 1] == " " or cs[hi - 1] == "\t") bound 16777216
        hi -= 1
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

# One field line "name: value" into names/values.
fn field(t: &text, names: &mut List[text], values: &mut List[text]) -> bool ! BadHttp
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[0] == " " or cs[0] == "\t")
        fail BadHttp(why: "obs-fold")
    var name = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != ":" bound 16777216
        if not tchar(cs[i][0] as i64)
            fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        name = name + cs[i]
        i += 1
    if i >= cs.len() or name == ""
        fail BadHttp(why: "field line")
    var v = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        v = v + cs[j]
        j += 1
    names.push(name)
    values.push(trim_ows(&v))
    return true

# The value of a field (case-insensitive name): the field values joined
# with ", " (RFC 9110 5.3), or none.
pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: &text) -> text?
    let want = lower(name)
    var found = false
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..names.len()
        if lower(&names[i]) == want
            o = if found then o + ", " + values[i] else copy(values[i])
            found = true
    return if found then some(o) else none

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in v.chars()
        if c == ","
            out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
    return out

fn dec(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + x - 48
    return v

fn hexnum(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        if d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
    return v

# Head: start line and fields, ending at the empty line. Returns the
# offset after it. Leading empty lines before a request are skipped (2.2).
fn head(b: &[i64], m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> i64 ! BadHttp
    var i: usize = 0
    if req
        while i + 1 < b.len() and b[i] == 13 and b[i + 1] == 10 bound 16
            i += 2
    let e = try line_end(b, i)
    if e < 0
        return -1
    let sl = try ascii_text(b, i, e as usize)
    let _x = try start_line(&sl, m, req)
    i = (e + 2) as usize
    loop bound 16777216
        let f = try line_end(b, i)

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
std3: bool
hyphens: bool
bidi: bool
joiners: bool
transitional: bool
dns_length: bool
ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
cps: List[i64]
err: bool

pub struct Ascii
host: text
err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)

let s = c - S_BASE

o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
if s % T_COUNT != 0
o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)

if d.len() == 0
o.push(c)
return
for x in d
o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in cps
decompose_into(&mut o, c)
var cc: List[i64] = []
for c in o
cc.push(ccc(c))
# stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
var i: usize = 1
while i < o.len() bound 16777216
var j = i
while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
let t = o[j]
o[j] = o[j - 1]
o[j - 1] = t
let u = cc[j]
cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
cc[j - 1] = u
j -= 1
i += 1
return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
return a + (b - T_BASE)
return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
let d = nfd(cps)
var o: List[i64] = []
if d.len() == 0
return o

var starter = last == 0

while i < d.len() bound 16777216
let c = d[i]

o[sp] = comp
i += 1
continue
if cl == 0
sp = o.len()
starter = true
last = cl
o.push(c)
i += 1
return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64

delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
if c >= 48 and c <= 57
return c - 22
if c >= 65 and c <= 90
return c - 65
if c >= 97 and c <= 122
return c - 97
return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
if k <= bias
return P_TMIN
if k >= bias + P_TMAX
return P_TMAX
return k - bias

# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps

j += 1

var i: i64 = 0

i = i % len
if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
o.push(n)
var q = o.len() - 1
while q > i as usize bound 16777216
o[q] = o[q - 1]
q -= 1

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in input
if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
if c < 128
o.push(c)
let basic = o.len() as i64
var h = basic
if basic > 0
o.push(45)
var n: i64 = 128
var delta: i64 = 0
var bias: i64 = 72
let total = input.len() as i64
while h < total bound 16777216

for c in input
if c >= n and c < m
m = c
if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
n = m
for c in input
if c < n
delta += 1
if delta > P_MAX
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
if c == n
var q = delta
var k: i64 = P_BASE

if q < t

o.push(digit_char(t + (q - t) % (P_BASE - t)))
q = (q - t) / (P_BASE - t)
k += P_BASE
o.push(digit_char(q))
bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == basic)
delta = 0
h += 1
delta += 1
n += 1
return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool

if c >= 128

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)
if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
return true
return false

return false

var left = false
while a > 0 bound 16777216

left = t == 2 or t == 4
break
var z = i + 1
var right = false
while z < l.len() bound 16777216
let t = joining_type(l[z])
if t == 5
z += 1
continue
right = t == 2 or t == 3
break
if not (left and right)
return false
i += 1
return true

fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool

pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
let p = process(input, f)

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
std3: bool
hyphens: bool
bidi: bool
joiners: bool
transitional: bool
dns_length: bool
ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
cps: List[i64]
err: bool

pub struct Ascii
host: text
err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)

if d.len() == 0
o.push(c)

for x in d
o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]

for c in cps
decompose_into(&mut o, c)

for c in o

cc[j - 1] = u

return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36

pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool

var e = l.len()
while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216

return false

var en = false
var an = false
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)

return false
if b == 4
en = true
if b == 3
an = true
if en and an

return false

var left = false
while a > 0 bound 16777216

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
std3: bool
hyphens: bool
bidi: bool
joiners: bool
transitional: bool
dns_length: bool
ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps

pub struct Ascii

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
let s = c - S_BASE

o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
if s % T_COUNT != 0
o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)

if d.len() == 0
o.push(c)
return
for x in d
o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in cps
decompose_into(&mut o, c)
var cc: List[i64] = []
for c in o
cc.push(ccc(c))

while i < o.len() bound 16777216
var j = i
while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
let t = o[j]
o[j] = o[j - 1]
o[j - 1] = t
let u = cc[j]
cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
cc[j - 1] = u
j -= 1
i += 1
return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
return a + (b - T_BASE)
return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]

return o

if cl == 0

starter = true
last = cl
o.push(c)
i += 1
return o

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1

if c >= 65 and c <= 90
return c - 65
if c >= 97 and c <= 122

return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
if k <= bias

if k >= bias + P_TMAX

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
var o: List[i64] = []

if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)

var bias: i64 = 72

for c in input

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)
if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
return true
return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool

return true
