# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
    std3: bool
    hyphens: bool
    bidi: bool
    joiners: bool
    transitional: bool
    dns_length: bool
    ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
    cps: List[i64]
    err: bool

pub struct Ascii
    host: text
    err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
    if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
        let s = c - S_BASE
        o.push(L_BASE + s / N_COUNT)
        o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
        if s % T_COUNT != 0
            o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)
        return
    let d = decomposition(c)
    if d.len() == 0
        o.push(c)
        return
    for x in d
        o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in cps
        decompose_into(&mut o, c)
    var cc: List[i64] = []
    for c in o
        cc.push(ccc(c))
    # stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < o.len() bound 16777216
        var j = i
        while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
            let t = o[j]
            o[j] = o[j - 1]
            o[j - 1] = t
            let u = cc[j]
            cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
            cc[j - 1] = u
            j -= 1
        i += 1
    return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
    if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
        return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
    if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
        return a + (b - T_BASE)
    return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let d = nfd(cps)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if d.len() == 0
        return o
    var sp: usize = 0
    var last = ccc(d[0])
    var starter = last == 0
    o.push(d[0])
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < d.len() bound 16777216
        let c = d[i]
        let cl = ccc(c)
        let comp = if starter then compose_pair(o[sp], c) else -1
        if starter and (last < cl or last == 0) and comp >= 0
            o[sp] = comp
            i += 1
            continue
        if cl == 0
            sp = o.len()
            starter = true
        last = cl
        o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
    var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
    delta += delta / numpoints
    var k: i64 = 0
    while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
        delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
        k += P_BASE
    return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 22
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 97
    return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
    if k <= bias
        return P_TMIN
    if k >= bias + P_TMAX
        return P_TMAX
    return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var b: usize = 0
    var j: usize = 0
    while j < input.len() bound 16777216
        if input[j] == 45
            b = j
        j += 1
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < b bound 16777216
        if input[k] >= 128
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(input[k])
        k += 1
    var p: usize = if b > 0 then b + 1 else 0
    var n: i64 = 128
    var i: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    while p < input.len() bound 16777216
        let oldi = i
        var w: i64 = 1
        var kk: i64 = P_BASE
        loop bound 64
            if p >= input.len()
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            let d = digit_value(input[p])
            p += 1
            if d < 0
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if d > (P_MAX - i) / w
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            i += d * w
            let t = thresh(kk, bias)
            if d < t
                break
            if w > P_MAX / (P_BASE - t)
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            w = w * (P_BASE - t)
            kk += P_BASE
        let len = o.len() as i64 + 1
        bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
        if i / len > P_MAX - n
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        n += i / len
        i = i % len
        if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(n)
        var q = o.len() - 1
        while q > i as usize bound 16777216
            o[q] = o[q - 1]
            q -= 1
        o[i as usize] = n
        i += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        if c < 128
            o.push(c)
    let basic = o.len() as i64
    var h = basic
    if basic > 0
        o.push(45)
    var n: i64 = 128
    var delta: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    let total = input.len() as i64
    while h < total bound 16777216
        var m: i64 = P_MAX
        for c in input
            if c >= n and c < m
                m = c
        if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
        n = m
        for c in input
            if c < n
                delta += 1
                if delta > P_MAX
                    return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if c == n
                var q = delta
                var k: i64 = P_BASE
                loop bound 64
                    let t = thresh(k, bias)
                    if q < t
                        break
                    o.push(digit_char(t + (q - t) % (P_BASE - t)))
                    q = (q - t) / (P_BASE - t)
                    k += P_BASE
                o.push(digit_char(q))
                bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == basic)
                delta = 0
                h += 1
        delta += 1
        n += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

# ---------------- UTS #46 processing ----------------

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        if c >= 128
            return false
    return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
            return true
    return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    let f = bidi_class(l[0])
    if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
        return false
    var e = l.len()
    while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216
        e -= 1
    if e == 0
        return false
    let last = bidi_class(l[e - 1])
    if f == 0
        for c in l
            let b = bidi_class(c)
            if b != 0 and b != 4 and b != 5 and b != 6 and b != 7 and b != 8 and b != 9 and b != 10
                return false
        return last == 0 or last == 4
    var en = false
    var an = false
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 0 or b > 10
            return false
        if b == 4
            en = true
        if b == 3
            an = true
    if en and an
        return false
    return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < l.len() bound 16777216
        let c = l[i]
        if c == 8204 or c == 8205
            let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
            if not virama
                if c == 8205
                    return false
                var a = i
                var left = false
                while a > 0 bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
                    if t == 5
                        a -= 1
                        continue
                    left = t == 2 or t == 4
                    break
                var z = i + 1
                var right = false
                while z < l.len() bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[z])
                    if t == 5
                        z += 1
                        continue
                    right = t == 2 or t == 3
                    break
                if not (left and right)
                    return false
        i += 1
    return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    if decoded
        let n = nfc(l)
        if n != copy(l)
            return false
    if f.hyphens
        if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
            return false
        if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
            return false
    elif is_xn(l)
        return false
    if is_mark(l[0])
        return false
    for c in l
        if c == 46
            return false
        let s = status(c)
        if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
            return false
        if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
            return false
    if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
        return false
    return true

pub struct Labels
    labels: List[List[i64]]
    err: bool

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels
    var m: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        let s = status(c)
        if s == 4
            continue
        if s == 1
            if f.transitional and c == 7838
                m.push(115)
                m.push(115)
            else
                for x in mapping(c)
                    m.push(x)
        elif s == 2 and f.transitional
            for x in mapping(c)
                m.push(x)
        else
            m.push(c)
    let n = nfc(&m)
    var raw: List[List[i64]] = []
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    for c in n
        if c == 46
            raw.push(cur)
            cur = []
        else
            cur.push(c)
    raw.push(cur)
    var err = false
    var out: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in raw
        if is_xn(&l)
            if not all_ascii(&l)
                err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var rest: List[i64] = []
            var k: usize = 4
            while k < l.len() bound 16777216
                rest.push(l[k])
                k += 1
            let d = puny_decode(&rest)
            if d.err
                if not f.ignore_bad_punycode
                    err = true
                    out.push(copy(l))
                    continue
                if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                    err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            if d.cps.len() == 0 or all_ascii(&d.cps)
                err = true
            if not valid_label(&d.cps, f, false, true)
                err = true
            out.push(d.cps)
        else
            if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                err = true
            out.push(copy(l))
    if f.bidi
        var rtl = false
        for l in out
            if is_rtl_label(&l)
                rtl = true
        if rtl
            for l in out
                if not bidi_ok(&l)
                    err = true
    return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o.push(46)
        for c in ls[i]
            o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# 4.3 ToUnicode.
pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    return Cps(cps: join_dots(&p.labels), err: p.err)

const ASCII_TAB: text = "\u{0}\u{1}\u{2}\u{3}\u{4}\u{5}\u{6}\u{7}\u{8}\t\n\u{b}\u{c}\r\u{e}\u{f}\u{10}\u{11}\u{12}\u{13}\u{14}\u{15}\u{16}\u{17}\u{18}\u{19}\u{1a}\u{1b}\u{1c}\u{1d}\u{1e}\u{1f} !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~\u{7f}"

# ASCII code points as text; any other code point is written U+FFFD
# (only reachable in an output that also carries err).
pub fn ascii_text(cps: &[i64]) -> text
    let t = ASCII_TAB.chars()
    var o = ""
    for c in cps
        o = o + (if c >= 0 and c < 128 then copy(t[c as usize]) else "\u{fffd}")
    return o

# 4.2 ToASCII.
pub fn to_ascii_cps(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    var err = p.err
    var ls: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in p.labels
        if all_ascii(&l)
            ls.push(copy(l))
        else
            let e = puny_encode(&l)
            if e.err
                err = true
                ls.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var x: List[i64] = [120, 110, 45, 45]
            for c in e.cps
                x.push(c)
            ls.push(x)
    let o = join_dots(&ls)
    if f.dns_length
        if o.len() < 1 or o.len() > 253
            err = true
        for l in ls
            if l.len() < 1 or l.len() > 63
                err = true
    return Cps(cps: o, err: err)

pub fn to_ascii(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Ascii
    let r = to_ascii_cps(input, f)
    return Ascii(host: ascii_text(&r.cps), err: r.err)

# Code points of UTF-8 text (text is always well formed).
pub fn text_cps(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        let b = t[i] as i64
        if b < 128
            o.push(b)
            i += 1
        elif b < 224
            o.push((b & 31) << 6 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63))
            i += 2
        elif b < 240
            o.push((b & 15) << 12 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[i + 2] as i64 & 63))
            i += 3
        else
            o.push((b & 7) << 18 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (t[i + 2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[i + 3] as i64 & 63))
            i += 4
    return o

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
    std3: bool
    hyphens: bool
    bidi: bool
    joiners: bool
    transitional: bool
    dns_length: bool
    ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
    cps: List[i64]
    err: bool

pub struct Ascii
    host: text
    err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
    if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
        let s = c - S_BASE
        o.push(L_BASE + s / N_COUNT)
        o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
        if s % T_COUNT != 0
            o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)
        return
    let d = decomposition(c)
    if d.len() == 0
        o.push(c)
        return
    for x in d
        o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in cps
        decompose_into(&mut o, c)
    var cc: List[i64] = []
    for c in o
        cc.push(ccc(c))
    # stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < o.len() bound 16777216
        var j = i
        while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
            let t = o[j]
            o[j] = o[j - 1]
            o[j - 1] = t
            let u = cc[j]
            cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
            cc[j - 1] = u
            j -= 1
        i += 1
    return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
    if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
        return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
    if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
        return a + (b - T_BASE)
    return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let d = nfd(cps)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if d.len() == 0
        return o
    var sp: usize = 0
    var last = ccc(d[0])
    var starter = last == 0
    o.push(d[0])
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < d.len() bound 16777216
        let c = d[i]
        let cl = ccc(c)
        let comp = if starter then compose_pair(o[sp], c) else -1
        if starter and (last < cl or last == 0) and comp >= 0
            o[sp] = comp
            i += 1
            continue
        if cl == 0
            sp = o.len()
            starter = true
        last = cl
        o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
    var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
    delta += delta / numpoints
    var k: i64 = 0
    while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
        delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
        k += P_BASE
    return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 22
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 97
    return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
    if k <= bias
        return P_TMIN
    if k >= bias + P_TMAX
        return P_TMAX
    return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps

    var b: usize = 0
    var j: usize = 0
    while j < input.len() bound 16777216
        if input[j] == 45
            b = j
        j += 1

        if input[k] >= 128
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(input[k])

    var n: i64 = 128
    var i: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72

        var kk: i64 = P_BASE

            if p >= input.len()

            p += 1

                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if d > (P_MAX - i) / w
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            i += d * w
            let t = thresh(kk, bias)
            if d < t
                break
            if w > P_MAX / (P_BASE - t)
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            w = w * (P_BASE - t)
            kk += P_BASE
        let len = o.len() as i64 + 1
        bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
        if i / len > P_MAX - n
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        n += i / len
        i = i % len
        if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(n)
        var q = o.len() - 1
        while q > i as usize bound 16777216
            o[q] = o[q - 1]
            q -= 1
        o[i as usize] = n
        i += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        if c < 128
            o.push(c)
    let basic = o.len() as i64
    var h = basic
    if basic > 0
        o.push(45)
    var n: i64 = 128
    var delta: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72

                    k += P_BASE

# ---------------- UTS #46 processing ----------------

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        if c >= 128
            return false
    return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
            return true
    return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    let f = bidi_class(l[0])
    if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
        return false
    var e = l.len()
    while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216
        e -= 1
    if e == 0
        return false
    let last = bidi_class(l[e - 1])
    if f == 0
        for c in l
            let b = bidi_class(c)
            if b != 0 and b != 4 and b != 5 and b != 6 and b != 7 and b != 8 and b != 9 and b != 10
                return false
        return last == 0 or last == 4
    var en = false
    var an = false
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 0 or b > 10
            return false
        if b == 4
            en = true
        if b == 3
            an = true
    if en and an
        return false
    return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < l.len() bound 16777216
        let c = l[i]
        if c == 8204 or c == 8205
            let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
            if not virama

                    return false

                var left = false
                while a > 0 bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
                    if t == 5
                        a -= 1

                    left = t == 2 or t == 4
                    break
                var z = i + 1
                var right = false
                while z < l.len() bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[z])
                    if t == 5
                        z += 1
                        continue
                    right = t == 2 or t == 3
                    break
                if not (left and right)
                    return false
        i += 1
    return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    if decoded
        let n = nfc(l)
        if n != copy(l)
            return false
    if f.hyphens
        if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
            return false
        if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
            return false
    elif is_xn(l)
        return false
    if is_mark(l[0])
        return false
    for c in l
        if c == 46
            return false
        let s = status(c)
        if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
            return false
        if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
            return false
    if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
        return false
    return true

pub struct Labels
    labels: List[List[i64]]
    err: bool

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels
    var m: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        let s = status(c)
        if s == 4
            continue
        if s == 1
            if f.transitional and c == 7838
                m.push(115)
                m.push(115)
            else

                    m.push(x)
        elif s == 2 and f.transitional
            for x in mapping(c)
                m.push(x)

    var cur: List[i64] = []

            cur = []

            var k: usize = 4
            while k < l.len() bound 16777216
                rest.push(l[k])

                    err = true

                    err = true

                continue

                err = true
            out.push(copy(l))

        for l in out
            if is_rtl_label(&l)
                rtl = true
        if rtl
            for l in out
                if not bidi_ok(&l)
                    err = true
    return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o.push(46)
        for c in ls[i]
            o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# 4.3 ToUnicode.
pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    return Cps(cps: join_dots(&p.labels), err: p.err)

pub fn ascii_text(cps: &[i64]) -> text

pub fn to_ascii_cps(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    var err = p.err

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
    std3: bool
    hyphens: bool
    bidi: bool
    joiners: bool
    transitional: bool
    dns_length: bool
    ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
    cps: List[i64]
    err: bool

pub struct Ascii
    host: text
    err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)

        o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)

            o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)

    if d.len() == 0
        o.push(c)
        return
    for x in d
        o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]

    for c in cps
        decompose_into(&mut o, c)

            o[j] = o[j - 1]
            o[j - 1] = t
            let u = cc[j]
            cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
            cc[j - 1] = u
            j -= 1
        i += 1
    return o

        return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT

fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    if decoded
        let n = nfc(l)
        if n != copy(l)
            return false
    if f.hyphens
        if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
            return false
        if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
            return false
    elif is_xn(l)
        return false
    if is_mark(l[0])
        return false
    for c in l
        if c == 46
            return false
        let s = status(c)
        if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
            return false
        if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
            return false
    if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
        return false
    return true

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels

    for c in input
        let s = status(c)
        if s == 4
            continue
        if s == 1
            if f.transitional and c == 7838

                m.push(115)
            else
                for x in mapping(c)
                    m.push(x)
        elif s == 2 and f.transitional
            for x in mapping(c)
                m.push(x)
        else
            m.push(c)
    let n = nfc(&m)
    var raw: List[List[i64]] = []
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    for c in n
        if c == 46
            raw.push(cur)
            cur = []
        else
            cur.push(c)
    raw.push(cur)
    var err = false
    var out: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in raw
        if is_xn(&l)
            if not all_ascii(&l)
                err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var rest: List[i64] = []
            var k: usize = 4
            while k < l.len() bound 16777216
                rest.push(l[k])
                k += 1
            let d = puny_decode(&rest)
            if d.err
                if not f.ignore_bad_punycode
                    err = true
                    out.push(copy(l))
                    continue
                if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                    err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            if d.cps.len() == 0 or all_ascii(&d.cps)
                err = true
            if not valid_label(&d.cps, f, false, true)
                err = true
            out.push(d.cps)
        else
            if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                err = true
            out.push(copy(l))
    if f.bidi
        var rtl = false
        for l in out
            if is_rtl_label(&l)
                rtl = true
        if rtl
            for l in out
                if not bidi_ok(&l)
                    err = true
    return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o.push(46)
        for c in ls[i]
            o.push(c)

    return o

pub fn to_ascii_cps(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    var err = p.err
    var ls: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in p.labels
        if all_ascii(&l)
            ls.push(copy(l))
        else
            let e = puny_encode(&l)
            if e.err
                err = true
                ls.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var x: List[i64] = [120, 110, 45, 45]
            for c in e.cps

    if f.dns_length

        for l in ls
            if l.len() < 1 or l.len() > 63

    return Cps(cps: o, err: err)

pub fn text_cps(t: &text) -> List[i64]

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        let b = t[i] as i64
        if b < 128

        elif b < 224

            i += 2
        elif b < 240

            i += 4

# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate

# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns

    hyphens: bool
    bidi: text

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
    var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
    delta += delta / numpoints
    var k: i64 = 0
    while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
        delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
        k += P_BASE
    return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 22
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 97
    return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
    if k <= bias
        return P_TMIN
    if k >= bias + P_TMAX
        return P_TMAX
    return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var b: usize = 0
    var j: usize = 0
    while j < input.len() bound 16777216
        if input[j] == 45
            b = j
        j += 1
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < b bound 16777216
        if input[k] >= 128
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(input[k])
        k += 1
    var p: usize = if b > 0 then b + 1 else 0
    var n: i64 = 128
    var i: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    while p < input.len() bound 16777216
        let oldi = i
        var w: i64 = 1
        var kk: i64 = P_BASE
        loop bound 64
            if p >= input.len()
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            let d = digit_value(input[p])
            p += 1
            if d < 0
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if d > (P_MAX - i) / w
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            i += d * w
            let t = thresh(kk, bias)
            if d < t
                break
            if w > P_MAX / (P_BASE - t)
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            w = w * (P_BASE - t)
            kk += P_BASE
        let len = o.len() as i64 + 1
        bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
        if i / len > P_MAX - n
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        n += i / len
        i = i % len
        if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(n)
        var q = o.len() - 1
        while q > i as usize bound 16777216
            o[q] = o[q - 1]
            q -= 1
        o[i as usize] = n
        i += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        if c < 128
            o.push(c)
    let basic = o.len() as i64
    var h = basic
    if basic > 0
        o.push(45)
    var n: i64 = 128
    var delta: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    let total = input.len() as i64
    while h < total bound 16777216
        var m: i64 = P_MAX
        for c in input
            if c >= n and c < m
                m = c
        if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
        n = m
        for c in input
            if c < n
                delta += 1
                if delta > P_MAX
                    return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if c == n
                var q = delta
                var k: i64 = P_BASE
                loop bound 64
                    let t = thresh(k, bias)
                    if q < t
                        break
                    o.push(digit_char(t + (q - t) % (P_BASE - t)))
                    q = (q - t) / (P_BASE - t)
                    k += P_BASE
                o.push(digit_char(q))
                bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == basic)
                delta = 0
                h += 1
        delta += 1
        n += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

# ---------------- UTS #46 processing ----------------

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        if c >= 128
            return false
    return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
            return true
    return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    let f = bidi_class(l[0])
    if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
        return false
    var e = l.len()
    while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216
        e -= 1
    if e == 0
        return false
    let last = bidi_class(l[e - 1])
    if f == 0
        for c in l
            let b = bidi_class(c)
            if b != 0 and b != 4 and b != 5 and b != 6 and b != 7 and b != 8 and b != 9 and b != 10
                return false
        return last == 0 or last == 4
    var en = false
    var an = false
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 0 or b > 10
            return false
        if b == 4
            en = true
        if b == 3
            an = true
    if en and an
        return false
    return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < l.len() bound 16777216
        let c = l[i]
        if c == 8204 or c == 8205
            let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
            if not virama
                if c == 8205
                    return false
                var a = i
                var left = false
                while a > 0 bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
                    if t == 5
                        a -= 1
                        continue
                    left = t == 2 or t == 4
                    break
                var z = i + 1
                var right = false
                while z < l.len() bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[z])
                    if t == 5
                        z += 1
                        continue
                    right = t == 2 or t == 3
                    break
                if not (left and right)
                    return false
        i += 1
    return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    if decoded
        let n = nfc(l)
        if n != copy(l)
            return false
    if f.hyphens
        if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
            return false
        if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
            return false
    elif is_xn(l)
        return false
    if is_mark(l[0])
        return false
    for c in l
        if c == 46
            return false
        let s = status(c)
        if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
            return false
        if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
            return false
    if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
        return false
    return true

pub struct Labels
    labels: List[List[i64]]
    err: bool

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels
    var m: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        let s = status(c)
        if s == 4
            continue
        if s == 1
            if f.transitional and c == 7838
                m.push(115)
                m.push(115)
            else
                for x in mapping(c)
                    m.push(x)
        elif s == 2 and f.transitional
            for x in mapping(c)
                m.push(x)
        else
            m.push(c)
    let n = nfc(&m)
    var raw: List[List[i64]] = []
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    for c in n
        if c == 46
            raw.push(cur)
            cur = []
        else
            cur.push(c)
    raw.push(cur)
    var err = false
    var out: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in raw
        if is_xn(&l)
            if not all_ascii(&l)
                err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var rest: List[i64] = []
            var k: usize = 4
            while k < l.len() bound 16777216
                rest.push(l[k])
                k += 1
            let d = puny_decode(&rest)
            if d.err
                if not f.ignore_bad_punycode
                    err = true
                    out.push(copy(l))
                    continue
                if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                    err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            if d.cps.len() == 0 or all_ascii(&d.cps)
                err = true
            if not valid_label(&d.cps, f, false, true)
                err = true
            out.push(d.cps)
        else
            if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                err = true
            out.push(copy(l))
    if f.bidi
        var rtl = false
        for l in out
            if is_rtl_label(&l)
                rtl = true
        if rtl
            for l in out
                if not bidi_ok(&l)
                    err = true
    return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o.push(46)
        for c in ls[i]
            o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# 4.3 ToUnicode.
pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    return Cps(cps: join_dots(&p.labels), err: p.err)

const ASCII_TAB: text = "\u{0}\u{1}\u{2}\u{3}\u{4}\u{5}\u{6}\u{7}\u{8}\t\n\u{b}\u{c}\r\u{e}\u{f}\u{10}\u{11}\u{12}\u{13}\u{14}\u{15}\u{16}\u{17}\u{18}\u{19}\u{1a}\u{1b}\u{1c}\u{1d}\u{1e}\u{1f} !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~\u{7f}"

# ASCII code points as text; any other code point is written U+FFFD
# (only reachable in an output that also carries err).
pub fn ascii_text(cps: &[i64]) -> text
    let t = ASCII_TAB.chars()
    var o = ""
    for c in cps
        o = o + (if c >= 0 and c < 128 then copy(t[c as usize]) else "\u{fffd}")
    return o

# 4.2 ToASCII.
pub fn to_ascii_cps(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    var err = p.err
    var ls: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in p.labels
        if all_ascii(&l)
            ls.push(copy(l))
        else
            let e = puny_encode(&l)
            if e.err
                err = true
                ls.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var x: List[i64] = [120, 110, 45, 45]
            for c in e.cps
                x.push(c)
            ls.push(x)
    let o = join_dots(&ls)
    if f.dns_length
        if o.len() < 1 or o.len() > 253
            err = true
        for l in ls
            if l.len() < 1 or l.len() > 63
                err = true
    return Cps(cps: o, err: err)

pub fn to_ascii(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Ascii
    let r = to_ascii_cps(input, f)
    return Ascii(host: ascii_text(&r.cps), err: r.err)

pub fn text_cps(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        let b = t[i] as i64
        if b < 128
            o.push(b)
            i += 1
        elif b < 224
            o.push((b & 31) << 6 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63))
            i += 2
        elif b < 240

        else
            o.push((b & 7) << 18 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (t[i + 2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[i + 3] as i64 & 63))
            i += 4
    return o

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
    std3: bool
    hyphens: bool
    bidi: bool
    joiners: bool
    transitional: bool
    dns_length: bool
    ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
    cps: List[i64]
    err: bool

pub struct Ascii
    host: text
    err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
    if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
        let s = c - S_BASE
        o.push(L_BASE + s / N_COUNT)
        o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
        if s % T_COUNT != 0
            o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)
        return
    let d = decomposition(c)
    if d.len() == 0
        o.push(c)
        return
    for x in d
        o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in cps
        decompose_into(&mut o, c)
    var cc: List[i64] = []
    for c in o
        cc.push(ccc(c))
    # stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < o.len() bound 16777216
        var j = i
        while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
            let t = o[j]
            o[j] = o[j - 1]
            o[j - 1] = t
            let u = cc[j]
            cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
            cc[j - 1] = u
            j -= 1
        i += 1
    return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
    if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
        return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
    if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
        return a + (b - T_BASE)
    return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let d = nfd(cps)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if d.len() == 0
        return o
    var sp: usize = 0
    var last = ccc(d[0])
    var starter = last == 0
    o.push(d[0])
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < d.len() bound 16777216
        let c = d[i]
        let cl = ccc(c)
        let comp = if starter then compose_pair(o[sp], c) else -1
        if starter and (last < cl or last == 0) and comp >= 0
            o[sp] = comp
            i += 1
            continue
        if cl == 0
            sp = o.len()
            starter = true
        last = cl
        o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
    var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
    delta += delta / numpoints
    var k: i64 = 0
    while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
        delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
        k += P_BASE
    return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 22
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 97
    return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
    if k <= bias
        return P_TMIN
    if k >= bias + P_TMAX
        return P_TMAX
    return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var b: usize = 0
    var j: usize = 0
    while j < input.len() bound 16777216
        if input[j] == 45
            b = j
        j += 1
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < b bound 16777216
        if input[k] >= 128
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(input[k])
        k += 1
    var p: usize = if b > 0 then b + 1 else 0
    var n: i64 = 128
    var i: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    while p < input.len() bound 16777216
        let oldi = i
        var w: i64 = 1
        var kk: i64 = P_BASE
        loop bound 64
            if p >= input.len()
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            let d = digit_value(input[p])
            p += 1
            if d < 0
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if d > (P_MAX - i) / w
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            i += d * w
            let t = thresh(kk, bias)
            if d < t
                break
            if w > P_MAX / (P_BASE - t)
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            w = w * (P_BASE - t)
            kk += P_BASE
        let len = o.len() as i64 + 1
        bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
        if i / len > P_MAX - n
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        n += i / len
        i = i % len
        if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(n)
        var q = o.len() - 1
        while q > i as usize bound 16777216
            o[q] = o[q - 1]
            q -= 1
        o[i as usize] = n
        i += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        if c < 128
            o.push(c)
    let basic = o.len() as i64
    var h = basic
    if basic > 0
        o.push(45)
    var n: i64 = 128
    var delta: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    let total = input.len() as i64
    while h < total bound 16777216
        var m: i64 = P_MAX
        for c in input
            if c >= n and c < m
                m = c
        if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
        n = m
        for c in input
            if c < n
                delta += 1
                if delta > P_MAX
                    return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if c == n
                var q = delta
                var k: i64 = P_BASE
                loop bound 64
                    let t = thresh(k, bias)
                    if q < t
                        break
                    o.push(digit_char(t + (q - t) % (P_BASE - t)))
                    q = (q - t) / (P_BASE - t)
                    k += P_BASE
                o.push(digit_char(q))
                bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == basic)
                delta = 0
                h += 1
        delta += 1
        n += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

# ---------------- UTS #46 processing ----------------

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        if c >= 128
            return false
    return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
            return true
    return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    let f = bidi_class(l[0])
    if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
        return false
    var e = l.len()
    while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216
        e -= 1
    if e == 0
        return false
    let last = bidi_class(l[e - 1])
    if f == 0
        for c in l
            let b = bidi_class(c)
            if b != 0 and b != 4 and b != 5 and b != 6 and b != 7 and b != 8 and b != 9 and b != 10
                return false
        return last == 0 or last == 4
    var en = false
    var an = false
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 0 or b > 10
            return false
        if b == 4
            en = true
        if b == 3
            an = true
    if en and an
        return false
    return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < l.len() bound 16777216
        let c = l[i]
        if c == 8204 or c == 8205
            let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
            if not virama
                if c == 8205
                    return false
                var a = i
                var left = false
                while a > 0 bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
                    if t == 5
                        a -= 1
                        continue
                    left = t == 2 or t == 4
                    break
                var z = i + 1
                var right = false
                while z < l.len() bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[z])
                    if t == 5
                        z += 1
                        continue
                    right = t == 2 or t == 3
                    break
                if not (left and right)
                    return false
        i += 1
    return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    if decoded
        let n = nfc(l)
        if n != copy(l)
            return false
    if f.hyphens
        if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
            return false
        if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
            return false
    elif is_xn(l)
        return false
    if is_mark(l[0])
        return false
    for c in l
        if c == 46
            return false
        let s = status(c)
        if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
            return false
        if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
            return false
    if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
        return false
    return true

pub struct Labels
    labels: List[List[i64]]
    err: bool

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels
    var m: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        let s = status(c)
        if s == 4
            continue
        if s == 1
            if f.transitional and c == 7838
                m.push(115)
                m.push(115)
            else
                for x in mapping(c)
                    m.push(x)
        elif s == 2 and f.transitional
            for x in mapping(c)
                m.push(x)
        else
            m.push(c)
    let n = nfc(&m)
    var raw: List[List[i64]] = []
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    for c in n
        if c == 46
            raw.push(cur)
            cur = []
        else
            cur.push(c)
    raw.push(cur)
    var err = false
    var out: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in raw
        if is_xn(&l)
            if not all_ascii(&l)
                err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var rest: List[i64] = []
            var k: usize = 4
            while k < l.len() bound 16777216
                rest.push(l[k])
                k += 1
            let d = puny_decode(&rest)
            if d.err
                if not f.ignore_bad_punycode
                    err = true
                    out.push(copy(l))
                    continue
                if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                    err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            if d.cps.len() == 0 or all_ascii(&d.cps)
                err = true
            if not valid_label(&d.cps, f, false, true)
                err = true
            out.push(d.cps)
        else
            if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                err = true
            out.push(copy(l))
    if f.bidi
        var rtl = false
        for l in out
            if is_rtl_label(&l)
                rtl = true
        if rtl
            for l in out
                if not bidi_ok(&l)
                    err = true
    return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o.push(46)
        for c in ls[i]
            o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# 4.3 ToUnicode.
pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    return Cps(cps: join_dots(&p.labels), err: p.err)

const ASCII_TAB: text = "\u{0}\u{1}\u{2}\u{3}\u{4}\u{5}\u{6}\u{7}\u{8}\t\n\u{b}\u{c}\r\u{e}\u{f}\u{10}\u{11}\u{12}\u{13}\u{14}\u{15}\u{16}\u{17}\u{18}\u{19}\u{1a}\u{1b}\u{1c}\u{1d}\u{1e}\u{1f} !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~\u{7f}"

# ASCII code points as text; any other code point is written U+FFFD
# (only reachable in an output that also carries err).
pub fn ascii_text(cps: &[i64]) -> text
    let t = ASCII_TAB.chars()
    var o = ""
    for c in cps
        o = o + (if c >= 0 and c < 128 then copy(t[c as usize]) else "\u{fffd}")
    return o

# 4.2 ToASCII.
pub fn to_ascii_cps(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    var err = p.err
    var ls: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in p.labels
        if all_ascii(&l)
            ls.push(copy(l))
        else
            let e = puny_encode(&l)
            if e.err
                err = true
                ls.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var x: List[i64] = [120, 110, 45, 45]
            for c in e.cps
                x.push(c)
            ls.push(x)
    let o = join_dots(&ls)
    if f.dns_length
        if o.len() < 1 or o.len() > 253
            err = true
        for l in ls
            if l.len() < 1 or l.len() > 63
                err = true
    return Cps(cps: o, err: err)

pub fn to_ascii(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Ascii
    let r = to_ascii_cps(input, f)
    return Ascii(host: ascii_text(&r.cps), err: r.err)

# Code points of UTF-8 text (text is always well formed).
pub fn text_cps(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        let b = t[i] as i64
        if b < 128

        elif b < 224

            i += 4
    return o

module num.linalg

# Dense real linear algebra over IEEE 754 binary64 (survey workstream A).
#
# Determinism. Every result is a fixed sequence of correctly rounded
# + - * / and sqrt (spec 6.3 N3: one result per operation on every
# target, no FMA contraction), so a call gives the same bits on every
# emit target. The order of every reduction is fixed and documented, and
# it is the order of the Reference BLAS and LAPACK 3.12.1 routine each
# function ports: a sum runs left to right in increasing index unless the
# routine says otherwise. Ported routines are checked bit for bit against
# Reference LAPACK 3.12.1 (tests/num/linalg_checks*.rce).
#
# Storage. A matrix is column major, element (i, j) of an m x n  at
# a[i + j * m] (0-based), like LAPACK with lda = m. Functions on raw
# storage take an offset and a leading dimension (or stride) so the
# LAPACK index arithmetic carries over unchanged.
#
# Non-finite values trap like every f64 operation (6.3 N3), so NaN and
# infinity never appear; the NaN branches of LAPACK are dead here.

pub struct Mat
m: usize
n: usize
a: List[f64]

# One error type: why is "shape", "singular" (at = 0-based column of the
# first zero pivot) or "not positive definite" (at = failing column).
error LaError(why: text, at: i64)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model
# Binary64 parameters (LAPACK DLAMCH): eps = 2^-53 ('E', round to
# nearest), safe minimum = 2^-1022 ('S'), overflow = (1 - 2^-53) 2^1024.

pub fn la_pow2(k: i64) -> f64
var r = 1.0
var i: i64 = 0
if k >= 0
while i < k bound 1100
r = r * 2.0
i += 1
else
while i > k bound 1100
r = r * 0.5
i -= 1
return r

pub const LA_EPS: f64 = 1.1102230246251565e-16
pub const LA_SFMIN: f64 = 2.2250738585072014e-308
pub const LA_HUGE: f64 = 1.7976931348623157e308

pub fn la_abs(x: f64) -> f64 = if x < 0.0 then 0.0 - x else x

# Fortran SIGN(a, b): |a| with the sign of b (b >= 0 counts as positive;
# there is no negative zero).
pub fn la_sign(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 = if b >= 0.0 then la_abs(a) else 0.0 - la_abs(a)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BLAS 1
# Vectors are (list, offset, stride); strides are positive.

# DDOT: sum of x[i] * y[i], i = 0..n-1 in order (the unrolled reference
# loop associates left to right, so it is the same order).
pub fn ddot(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, y: &[f64], oy: usize, iy: usize) -> f64
var t = 0.0
for i in 0..n
t = t + x[ox + i * ix] * y[oy + i * iy]
return t

# DAXPY: y := y + alpha * x (no-op when alpha == 0).
pub fn daxpy(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, y: &mut List[f64], oy: usize, iy: usize)
if alpha == 0.0
return
for i in 0..n
y[oy + i * iy] = y[oy + i * iy] + alpha * x[ox + i * ix]

# DSCAL: x := alpha * x.
pub fn dscal(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: &mut List[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize)
for i in 0..n
x[ox + i * ix] = alpha * x[ox + i * ix]

# DSWAP.
pub fn dswap(n: usize, x: &mut List[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, oy: usize, iy: usize)
for i in 0..n
let t = x[ox + i * ix]
x[ox + i * ix] = x[oy + i * iy]
x[oy + i * iy] = t

# DASUM: sum of |x[i]| in order.
pub fn dasum(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> f64
var t = 0.0
for i in 0..n
t = t + la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
return t

# IDAMAX: first index (0-based) of the largest |x[i]|; 0 for n == 0.
pub fn idamax(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> usize
var k: usize = 0
if n == 0
return 0
var mx = la_abs(x[ox])
for i in 1..n
let v = la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
if v > mx
k = i
mx = v
return k

# DNRM2 of Reference BLAS 3.10+ (Anderson 2017, Blue's three
# accumulators): no overflow or harmful underflow for any finite input.
# tsml = 2^-511, tbig = 2^486, ssml = 2^537, sbig = 2^-538.
pub fn dnrm2(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> f64
if n == 0
return 0.0
let tsml = la_pow2(-511)
let tbig = la_pow2(486)
let ssml = la_pow2(537)
let sbig = la_pow2(-538)
var notbig = true
var asml = 0.0
var amed = 0.0
var abig = 0.0
for i in 0..n
let ax = la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
if ax > tbig
let t = ax * sbig
abig = abig + t * t
notbig = false
elif ax < tsml
if notbig
let t = ax * ssml
asml = asml + t * t
else
amed = amed + ax * ax
var scl = 1.0
var sumsq = 0.0
if abig > 0.0
if amed > 0.0
abig = abig + (amed * sbig) * sbig
scl = 1.0 / sbig
sumsq = abig
elif asml > 0.0
if amed > 0.0
let am = amed.sqrt()
let asm = asml.sqrt() / ssml
var ymin = asm
var ymax = am
if asm > am
ymin = am
ymax = asm
let r = ymin / ymax
sumsq = ymax * ymax * (1.0 + r * r)
else
scl = 1.0 / ssml
sumsq = asml
else
sumsq = amed
return scl * sumsq.sqrt()

# DLAPY2: sqrt(x^2 + y^2) without needless overflow.
pub fn dlapy2(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64
let xa = la_abs(x)
let ya = la_abs(y)
let w = xa.max(ya)
let z = xa.min(ya)
if z == 0.0
return w
let r = z / w
return w * (1.0 + r * r).sqrt()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- kernels
# The BLAS 2/3 and LAPACK kernels below work in place on one buffer w, so
# the operand aliasing of the reference code (a routine updating part of
# A from another part of A) is expressed with offsets. Arguments follow
# the Fortran ones: o* offsets, ld* leading dimensions, inc* strides.

pub fn axpy_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: usize, alpha: f64, ox: usize, ix: usize, oy: usize, iy: usize)
if alpha == 0.0
return
for i in 0..n
w[oy + i * iy] = w[oy + i * iy] + alpha * w[ox + i * ix]

# DGEMV: y := alpha op(A) x + beta y, A m x n. trans false: y has m
# entries, columns j = 0.. in order add (alpha x[j]) A[:, j]. trans true:
# y[j] += alpha (sum over i in order of A[i, j] x[i]).
pub fn gemv_b(w: &mut List[f64], trans: bool, m: usize, n: usize, alpha: f64, oa: usize, lda: usize, ox: usize, incx: usize, beta: f64, oy: usize, incy: usize)
if m == 0 or n == 0 or (alpha == 0.0 and beta == 1.0)
return
let leny = if trans then n else m
if beta != 1.0
for i in 0..leny
if beta == 0.0
w[oy + i * incy] = 0.0
else
w[oy + i * incy] = beta * w[oy + i * incy]
if alpha == 0.0
return
if not trans
for j in 0..n
let t = alpha * w[ox + j * incx]
for i in 0..m
w[oy + i * incy] = w[oy + i * incy] + t * w[oa + i + j * lda]
else
for j in 0..n
var t = 0.0
for i in 0..m
t = t + w[oa + i + j * lda] * w[ox + i * incx]
w[oy + j * incy] = w[oy + j * incy] + alpha * t

# DGER: A := A + alpha x y^T, column by column, skipping y[j] == 0.
pub fn ger_b(w: &mut List[f64], m: usize, n: usize, alpha: f64, ox: usize, incx: usize, oy: usize, incy: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize)
if m == 0 or n == 0 or alpha == 0.0
return
for j in 0..n
if w[oy + j * incy] != 0.0
let t = alpha * w[oy + j * incy]
for i in 0..m
w[oa + i + j * lda] = w[oa + i + j * lda] + w[ox + i * incx] * t

# DTRSM, left side: B := alpha inv(op(A)) B, A m x m triangular, B m x n.
pub fn trsm_b(w: &mut List[f64], upper: bool, trans: bool, unit: bool, m: usize, n: usize, alpha: f64, oa: usize, lda: usize, ob: usize, ldb: usize)
if m == 0 or n == 0
return
if alpha == 0.0
for j in 0..n
for i in 0..m
w[ob + i + j * ldb] = 0.0
return
for j in 0..n
let c = ob + j * ldb
if not trans
if alpha != 1.0
for i in 0..m
w[c + i] = alpha * w[c + i]
if upper
var k = m
while k > 0 bound 1048576
k -= 1
if w[c + k] != 0.0
if not unit
w[c + k] = w[c + k] / w[oa + k + k * lda]
let bk = w[c + k]
for i in 0..k
w[c + i] = w[c + i] - bk * w[oa + i + k * lda]
else
for k in 0..m
if w[c + k] != 0.0
if not unit
w[c + k] = w[c + k] / w[oa + k + k * lda]
let bk = w[c + k]
for i in (k + 1)..m
w[c + i] = w[c + i] - bk * w[oa + i + k * lda]
else
if upper
for i in 0..m
var t = alpha * w[c + i]
for k in 0..i
t = t - w[oa + k + i * lda] * w[c + k]
if not unit
t = t / w[oa + i + i * lda]
w[c + i] = t
else
var i = m
while i > 0 bound 1048576
i -= 1
var t = alpha * w[c + i]
for k in (i + 1)..m
t = t - w[oa + k + i * lda] * w[c + k]
if not unit
t = t / w[oa + i + i * lda]
w[c + i] = t

# DGEMM: C := alpha op(A) op(B) + beta C, C m x n, inner dimension k.
# The four loop orders are those of the reference routine: for op(A) = A
# the update is column-oriented (C[:, j] += (alpha B[l, j]) A[:, l] for
# l = 0.. in order); for op(A) = A^T each C[i, j] is one dot product in
# increasing l, then alpha t + beta C[i, j].
pub fn gemm_b(w: &mut List[f64], ta: bool, tb: bool, m: usize, n: usize, k: usize, alpha: f64, oa: usize, lda: usize, ob: usize, ldb: usize, beta: f64, oc: usize, ldc: usize)
if m == 0 or n == 0 or ((alpha == 0.0 or k == 0) and beta == 1.0)
return
if alpha == 0.0
for j in 0..n
for i in 0..m
if beta == 0.0
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = 0.0
else
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = beta * w[oc + i + j * ldc]
return
for j in 0..n
if not ta
if beta == 0.0
for i in 0..m
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = 0.0
elif beta != 1.0
for i in 0..m
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = beta * w[oc + i + j * ldc]
for l in 0..k
let bl = if tb then w[ob + j + l * ldb] else w[ob + l + j * ldb]
let t = alpha * bl
for i in 0..m
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = w[oc + i + j * ldc] + t * w[oa + i + l * lda]
else
for i in 0..m
var t = 0.0
for l in 0..k
let bl = if tb then w[ob + j + l * ldb] else w[ob + l + j * ldb]
t = t + w[oa + l + i * lda] * bl
if beta == 0.0
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = alpha * t
else
w[oc + i + j * ldc] = alpha * t + beta * w[oc + i + j * ldc]

# DGETF2: unblocked LU with partial pivoting (first largest |a| wins),
# multipliers scaled by the reciprocal of the pivot when |pivot| >= SFMIN
# (as the reference does), else divided. piv[j] is the 0-based row
# swapped with row j. Returns LAPACK INFO: 0, or j + 1 for the first exact
# zero pivot (the factorization still completes).
pub fn getf2_b(w: &mut List[f64], m: usize, n: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize, piv: &mut List[i64]) -> i64

let mn = if m < n then m else n
for j in 0..mn
let jp = j + idamax(m - j, w, oa + j + j * lda, 1)
piv.push(jp as i64)
if w[oa + jp + j * lda] != 0.0
if jp != j

let p = w[oa + j + j * lda]

info = (j + 1) as i64

return info

# DLASWP over columns 0..n-1 of B, rows k1..k2-1, forward or backward.
pub fn laswp_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: usize, ob: usize, ldb: usize, k1: usize, k2: usize, piv: &[i64], forward: bool)
var s: usize = 0
while s < k2 - k1 bound 1048576
let i = if forward then k1 + s else k2 - 1 - s
let p = piv[i] as usize
