pub fn checked_div(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k <= 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let s = a.secs / ku
    let carry = a.secs % ku
    let extra = (carry * NPS + a.nanos as u64 % ku) / ku
    let n = a.nanos / k + extra as i64
    return some(Dur(secs: s + (n / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64, nanos: n % NANOS_PER_SEC))

pub fn dur_sum(ds: &[Dur]) -> Dur?
    var acc = dur_zero()
    for d in ds
        match checked_add(&acc, &d)
            some(x) -> acc = x
            none -> return none
    return some(acc)

# ---------------- Debug formatting ----------------
# Rust's `{:?}` for Duration. prec < 0 means no precision; width < 0 means
# no width; align is "<", ">", "^" or "" (default left); plus is `{:+?}`.

fn spaces(n: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n
        o = o + " "
        k += 1
    return o

fn fmt_decimal(ip0: u64, fp0: i64, div0: i64, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, prefix: &text, postfix: &text) -> text
    var buf: List[i64] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    var fp = fp0
    var dv = div0
    var pos = 0
    let lim = if prec < 0 then 9 else prec
    while fp > 0 and pos < lim and pos < 9
        buf[pos as usize] = fp / dv
        fp = fp % dv
        dv = dv / 10
        pos += 1
    var ip = ip0
    var big = false
    if fp > 0 and fp >= dv * 5
        let tie = fp == dv * 5
        let odd = if pos > 0 then copy(buf[(pos - 1) as usize]) % 2 == 1 else ip % 2 == 1
        if not (tie and not odd)
            var r = pos
            var carry = true
            while carry and r > 0
                r -= 1
                if buf[r as usize] < 9
                    buf[r as usize] = copy(buf[r as usize]) + 1
                    carry = false
                else
                    buf[r as usize] = 0
            if carry
                if ip == MAX_U
                    big = true
                else
                    ip += 1
    let end = if prec >= 0 then (if prec < 9 then prec else 9) else pos
    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())
    if end > 0
        let w = if prec >= 0 then prec else pos
        o = o + "."
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < w
            o = o + (if k < end then copy(buf[k as usize]).tostr() else "0")
            k += 1
        cells = cells + 1 + w as usize
    o = o + postfix
    if width < 0 or width as usize <= cells
        return o
    let padn = width - cells as i64
    let pre = if align == ">" then padn else (if align == "^" then padn / 2 else 0)
    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

pub fn dur_debug_with(d: &Dur, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, plus: bool) -> text
    let p = if plus then "+" else ""
    let us = "s"
    let ums = "ms"
    let uus = "µs"
    let uns = "ns"
    if d.secs > 0
        return fmt_decimal(d.secs, d.nanos, NANOS_PER_SEC / 10, prec, width, align, &p, &us)
    if d.nanos >= 1000000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000000, 100000, prec, width, align, &p, &ums)
    if d.nanos >= 1000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000, 100, prec, width, align, &p, &uus)
    return fmt_decimal(d.nanos as u64, 0, 1, prec, width, align, &p, &uns)

pub fn dur_debug(d: &Dur) -> text
    let a = ""
    return dur_debug_with(d, -1, -1, &a, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------

pub struct Timespec
    secs: i64
    nanos: i64

pub fn ts_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0 or nanos >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        fail BadClock(why: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return Timespec(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

pub fn ts_min() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MIN_SECS, nanos: 0)
pub fn ts_max() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MAX_SECS, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn ts_cmp(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn ts_eq(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> bool = ts_cmp(a, b) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn add_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t >= 0
        if d > (MAX_SECS - t) as u64
            return none
        return some(t + d as i64)
    let room = MAX_SECS as u64 + (0 - (t + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t + d as i64)
    return some((t + MAX_SECS + 1) + (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn sub_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> nanos?
    if t < 0
        if d > (t - MIN_SECS) as u64
            return none
        return some(t - d as i64)
    let room = t as u64 + MAX_SECS as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t - d as i64)
    return some((t - MAX_SECS - 1) - (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn ts_checked_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match add_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos + d.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_SECS
            return none
        s += 1
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_checked_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match sub_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos - d.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == MIN_SECS
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_saturating_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_add(t, d).or(ts_max())
pub fn ts_saturating_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_sub(t, d).or(ts_min())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct Diff
    ok: bool
    d: Dur

# a - b for a >= b; the seconds difference can reach u64::MAX.
fn diff_u(a: i64, b: i64) -> u64
    if b >= 0 or a < 0
        return (a - b) as u64
    return a as u64 + (0 - (b + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn mag(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Dur
    if a.nanos >= b.nanos
        return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs), nanos: a.nanos - b.nanos)
    return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs) - 1, nanos: a.nanos + NANOS_PER_SEC - b.nanos)

pub fn sub_timespec(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Diff
    if ts_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return Diff(ok: true, d: mag(a, b))
    return Diff(ok: false, d: mag(b, a))

pub fn checked_duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur?
    let r = sub_timespec(a, earlier)
    if r.ok
        return some(copy(r.d))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur = checked_duration_since(a, earlier).or(dur_zero())

# ---------------- wasi:clocks@0.2.8 ----------------

# monotonic-clock instant and duration are u64 ns.
pub fn mono_from_wasi(ns: u64) -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: (ns / NPS) as i64, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

pub fn mono_to_wasi(t: &Timespec) -> u64 ! BadClock
    if t.secs < 0 or t.secs as u64 > (MAX_U - t.nanos as u64) / NPS
        fail BadClock(why: "instant out of range")
    return t.secs as u64 * NPS + t.nanos as u64

# wall-clock datetime: "The nanoseconds field of the output is always less than 1000000000."
# seconds is u64; past i64::MAX seconds it is beyond the unix point type.
pub fn wall_from_wasi(seconds: u64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if seconds > MAX_SECS as u64
        fail BadClock(why: "seconds out of range")
    return ts_new(seconds as i64, nanoseconds)

# ---------------- admission of monotonic readings ----------------

pub struct Mono
    last: Timespec
    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_new() -> Mono = Mono(last: Timespec(secs: 0, nanos: 0), seen: false, raised: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

pub struct Timers
    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

# wasi subscribe-instant. Timers are kept in firing order.
pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

module os.clock

# Clocks and timers (survey M37), pure. A program never reads a clock: the
# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.
# This module holds what a program does with those values:
# - Dur, Rust's core::time::Duration (secs plus nanos below one second)
#   with its constructors, accessors, checked and saturating arithmetic and
#   its Debug formatting ("1.5s", "7.1µs", precision, width, alignment).
#   Secs are u64 as in Rust, so the full range holds.
# - Timespec, the point type behind Rust's unix Instant and SystemTime
#   (secs i64, nanos 0..1e9), with checked and saturating add/sub and
#   duration_since in Rust's forms (saturating, checked, signed result).
# - wasi:clocks@0.2.8 values: a monotonic instant (u64 ns) and a wall
#   datetime (seconds, nanoseconds < 1e9) mapped to Timespec.
# - Mono, the admission rule for monotonic readings: a reading below the
#   last admitted one is raised to it (non-decreasing, as wasi-clocks
#   promises and as Rust's monotonize enforces).
# - Timers, the pure timer queue: subscribe at an instant or after a
#   duration; a tick at `now` fires every due timer in (deadline, subscribe
#   order) order. The host admits those firings as events in that order.

error BadClock(why: text)

pub const NANOS_PER_SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const NPS: u64 = 1000000000
pub const MAX_U: u64 = 18446744073709551615
pub const MAX_SECS: i64 = 9223372036854775807
pub const MIN_SECS: i64 = -9223372036854775808

# secs is u64 as in Rust, so the full range up to u64::MAX seconds holds.
pub struct Dur
    secs: u64
    nanos: i64

pub fn dur_zero() -> Dur = Dur(secs: 0, nanos: 0)
pub fn dur_max() -> Dur = Dur(secs: MAX_U, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

# Duration::new: nanos beyond a second carry into secs; overflow fails.
pub fn dur_new(secs: u64, nanos: i64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0
        fail BadClock(why: "negative nanoseconds")
    let extra = (nanos / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64
    if extra > MAX_U - secs
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::new")
    return Dur(secs: secs + extra, nanos: nanos % NANOS_PER_SEC)

pub fn from_secs(s: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: s, nanos: 0)
pub fn from_millis(ms: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ms / 1000, nanos: (ms % 1000) as i64 * 1000000)
pub fn from_micros(us: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: us / 1000000, nanos: (us % 1000000) as i64 * 1000)
pub fn from_nanos(ns: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ns / NPS, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

# Duration::from_nanos_u128 for a u128 given as decimal digits: the last
# nine digits are the nanos, the rest the secs (must fit u64).
pub fn from_nanos_text(t: &text) -> Dur ! BadClock
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0
        fail BadClock(why: "empty")
    var secs: u64 = 0
    var nanos: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 0
    let cut: usize = if cs.len() > 9 then cs.len() - 9 else 0
    for c in cs
        let v = c[0] as i64 - 48
        if v < 0 or v > 9
            fail BadClock(why: "not a decimal")
        if k < cut
            if secs > (MAX_U - v as u64) / 10
                fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::from_nanos_u128")
            secs = secs * 10 + v as u64
        else
            nanos = nanos * 10 + v
        k += 1
    return Dur(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

fn from_unit(n: u64, unit: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if n > MAX_U / unit
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration constructor")
    return Dur(secs: n * unit, nanos: 0)

pub fn from_mins(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 60)
pub fn from_hours(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 3600)
pub fn from_days(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 86400)
pub fn from_weeks(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 604800)

pub fn as_secs(d: &Dur) -> u64 = d.secs
pub fn subsec_millis(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000000
pub fn subsec_micros(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000
pub fn subsec_nanos(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos
pub fn is_zero(d: &Dur) -> bool = d.secs == 0 and d.nanos == 0
# Total as decimal text (Rust's u128 as_nanos, as_micros, as_millis), exact.
fn pad9(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    var o = v.tostr()
    while (o.len_bytes() as i64) < w bound 9
        o = "0" + o
    return o
fn in_units(d: &Dur, digits: i64, unit: i64) -> text
    let part = d.nanos / unit
    if d.secs == 0
        return part.tostr()
    return d.secs.tostr() + pad9(part, digits)
pub fn as_nanos(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 9, 1)
pub fn as_micros(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 6, 1000)
pub fn as_millis(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 3, 1000000)

pub fn dur_cmp(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn dur_eq(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> bool = dur_cmp(a, b) == 0

pub fn checked_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if b.secs > MAX_U - a.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs + b.secs
    var n = a.nanos + b.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_U
            return none
        s += 1
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn checked_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if a.secs < b.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs - b.secs
    var n = a.nanos - b.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == 0
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn saturating_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_add(a, b).or(dur_max())
pub fn saturating_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())

pub fn abs_diff(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur
    if dur_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())
    return checked_sub(b, a).or(dur_zero())

# Multiplier and divisor are u32 in Rust: 0 ..= 4294967295.
pub fn checked_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k < 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let total = a.nanos as u64 * ku
    let extra = total / NPS
    if ku != 0 and a.secs > (MAX_U - extra) / ku
        return none
    return some(Dur(secs: a.secs * ku + extra, nanos: (total % NPS) as i64))

pub fn saturating_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur = checked_mul(a, k).or(dur_max())

pub fn checked_div(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k <= 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let s = a.secs / ku
    let carry = a.secs % ku
    let extra = (carry * NPS + a.nanos as u64 % ku) / ku
    let n = a.nanos / k + extra as i64
    return some(Dur(secs: s + (n / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64, nanos: n % NANOS_PER_SEC))

pub fn dur_sum(ds: &[Dur]) -> Dur?
    var acc = dur_zero()
    for d in ds
        match checked_add(&acc, &d)
            some(x) -> acc = x
            none -> return none
    return some(acc)

# ---------------- Debug formatting ----------------
# Rust's `{:?}` for Duration. prec < 0 means no precision; width < 0 means
# no width; align is "<", ">", "^" or "" (default left); plus is `{:+?}`.

fn spaces(n: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n
        o = o + " "
        k += 1
    return o

fn fmt_decimal(ip0: u64, fp0: i64, div0: i64, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, prefix: &text, postfix: &text) -> text
    var buf: List[i64] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    var fp = fp0
    var dv = div0
    var pos = 0
    let lim = if prec >= 0 then 9 else prec
    while fp > 0 and pos < lim and pos < 9
        buf[pos as usize] = fp / dv
        fp = fp % dv
        dv = dv / 10
        pos += 1
    var ip = ip0
    var big = false
    if fp > 0 and fp >= dv * 5
        let tie = fp == dv * 5
        let odd = if pos > 0 then copy(buf[(pos - 1) as usize]) % 2 == 1 else ip % 2 == 1
        if not (tie and not odd)
            var r = pos
            var carry = true
            while carry and r > 0
                r -= 1
                if buf[r as usize] < 9
                    buf[r as usize] = copy(buf[r as usize]) + 1
                    carry = false
                else
                    buf[r as usize] = 0
            if carry
                if ip == MAX_U
                    big = true
                else
                    ip += 1
    let end = if prec >= 0 then (if prec < 9 then prec else 9) else pos
    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())
    if end > 0
        let w = if prec >= 0 then prec else pos
        o = o + "."
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < w
            o = o + (if k < end then copy(buf[k as usize]).tostr() else "0")
            k += 1
        cells = cells + 1 + w as usize
    o = o + postfix
    if width < 0 or width as usize <= cells
        return o
    let padn = width - cells as i64
    let pre = if align == ">" then padn else (if align == "^" then padn / 2 else 0)
    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

pub fn dur_debug_with(d: &Dur, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, plus: bool) -> text
    let p = if plus then "+" else ""
    let us = "s"
    let ums = "ms"
    let uus = "µs"
    let uns = "ns"
    if d.secs > 0
        return fmt_decimal(d.secs, d.nanos, NANOS_PER_SEC / 10, prec, width, align, &p, &us)
    if d.nanos >= 1000000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000000, 100000, prec, width, align, &p, &ums)
    if d.nanos >= 1000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000, 100, prec, width, align, &p, &uus)
    return fmt_decimal(d.nanos as u64, 0, 1, prec, width, align, &p, &uns)

pub fn dur_debug(d: &Dur) -> text
    let a = ""
    return dur_debug_with(d, -1, -1, &a, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------

pub struct Timespec
    secs: i64
    nanos: i64

pub fn ts_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0 or nanos >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        fail BadClock(why: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return Timespec(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

pub fn ts_min() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MIN_SECS, nanos: 0)
pub fn ts_max() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MAX_SECS, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn ts_cmp(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn ts_eq(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> bool = ts_cmp(a, b) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn add_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t >= 0
        if d > (MAX_SECS - t) as u64
            return none
        return some(t + d as i64)
    let room = MAX_SECS as u64 + (0 - (t + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t + d as i64)
    return some((t + MAX_SECS + 1) + (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn sub_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t < 0
        if d > (t - MIN_SECS) as u64
            return none
        return some(t - d as i64)
    let room = t as u64 + MAX_SECS as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t - d as i64)
    return some((t - MAX_SECS - 1) - (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn ts_checked_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match add_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos + d.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_SECS
            return none
        s += 1
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_checked_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match sub_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos - d.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == MIN_SECS
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_saturating_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_add(t, d).or(ts_max())
pub fn ts_saturating_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_sub(t, d).or(ts_min())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct Diff
    ok: bool
    d: Dur

# a - b for a >= b; the seconds difference can reach u64::MAX.
fn diff_u(a: i64, b: i64) -> u64
    if b >= 0 or a < 0
        return (a - b) as u64
    return a as u64 + (0 - (b + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn mag(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Dur
    if a.nanos >= b.nanos
        return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs), nanos: a.nanos - b.nanos)
    return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs) - 1, nanos: a.nanos + NANOS_PER_SEC - b.nanos)

pub fn sub_timespec(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Diff
    if ts_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return Diff(ok: true, d: mag(a, b))
    return Diff(ok: false, d: mag(b, a))

pub fn checked_duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur?
    let r = sub_timespec(a, earlier)
    if r.ok
        return some(copy(r.d))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur = checked_duration_since(a, earlier).or(dur_zero())

# monotonic-clock instant and duration are u64 ns.
pub fn mono_from_wasi(ns: u64) -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: (ns / NPS) as i64, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

pub fn mono_to_wasi(t: &Timespec) -> u64 ! BadClock
    if t.secs < 0 or t.secs as u64 > (MAX_U - t.nanos as u64) / NPS
        fail BadClock(why: "instant out of range")
    return t.secs as u64 * NPS + t.nanos as u64

# wall-clock datetime: "The nanoseconds field of the output is always less than 1000000000."
# seconds is u64; past i64::MAX seconds it is beyond the unix point type.
pub fn wall_from_wasi(seconds: u64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if seconds > MAX_SECS as u64
        fail BadClock(why: "seconds out of range")
    return ts_new(seconds as i64, nanoseconds)

# ---------------- admission of monotonic readings ----------------

pub struct Mono
    last: Timespec
    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_new() -> Mono = Mono(last: Timespec(secs: 0, nanos: 0), seen: false, raised: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

pub struct Timers
    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

# wasi subscribe-instant. Timers are kept in firing order.
pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

module os.clock

# Clocks and timers (survey M37), pure. A program never reads a clock: the
# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.
# This module holds what a program does with those values:
# - Dur, Rust's core::time::Duration (secs plus nanos below one second)
#   with its constructors, accessors, checked and saturating arithmetic and
#   its Debug formatting ("1.5s", "7.1µs", precision, width, alignment).
#   Secs are u64 as in Rust, so the full range holds.
# - Timespec, the point type behind Rust's unix Instant and SystemTime
#   (secs i64, nanos 0..1e9), with checked and saturating add/sub and
#   duration_since in Rust's forms (saturating, checked, signed result).
# - wasi:clocks@0.2.8 values: a monotonic instant (u64 ns) and a wall
#   datetime (seconds, nanoseconds < 1e9) mapped to Timespec.
# - Mono, the admission rule for monotonic readings: a reading below the
#   last admitted one is raised to it (non-decreasing, as wasi-clocks
#   promises and as Rust's monotonize enforces).
# - Timers, the pure timer queue: subscribe at an instant or after a
#   duration; a tick at `now` fires every due timer in (deadline, subscribe
#   order) order. The host admits those firings as events in that order.

error BadClock(why: text)

pub const NANOS_PER_SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const NPS: u64 = 1000000000
pub const MAX_U: u64 = 18446744073709551615
pub const MAX_SECS: i64 = 9223372036854775807
pub const MIN_SECS: i64 = -9223372036854775808

# secs is u64 as in Rust, so the full range up to u64::MAX seconds holds.
pub struct Dur
    secs: u64
    nanos: i64

pub fn dur_zero() -> Dur = Dur(secs: 0, nanos: 0)
pub fn dur_max() -> Dur = Dur(secs: MAX_U, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

# Duration::new: nanos beyond a second carry into secs; overflow fails.
pub fn dur_new(secs: u64, nanos: i64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0
        fail BadClock(why: "negative nanoseconds")
    let extra = (nanos / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64
    if extra > MAX_U - secs
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::new")
    return Dur(secs: secs + extra, nanos: nanos % NANOS_PER_SEC)

pub fn from_secs(s: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: s, nanos: 0)
pub fn from_millis(ms: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ms / 1000, nanos: (ms % 1000) as i64 * 1000000)
pub fn from_micros(us: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: us / 1000000, nanos: (us % 1000000) as i64 * 1000)
pub fn from_nanos(ns: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ns / NPS, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

# Duration::from_nanos_u128 for a u128 given as decimal digits: the last
# nine digits are the nanos, the rest the secs (must fit u64).
pub fn from_nanos_text(t: &text) -> Dur ! BadClock
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0
        fail BadClock(why: "empty")
    var secs: u64 = 0
    var nanos: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 0
    let cut: usize = if cs.len() > 9 then cs.len() - 9 else 0
    for c in cs
        let v = c[0] as i64 - 48
        if v < 0 or v > 9
            fail BadClock(why: "not a decimal")
        if k < cut
            if secs > (MAX_U - v as u64) / 10
                fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::from_nanos_u128")
            secs = secs * 10 + v as u64
        else
            nanos = nanos * 10 + v
        k += 1
    return Dur(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

fn from_unit(n: u64, unit: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if n > MAX_U / unit
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration constructor")
    return Dur(secs: n * unit, nanos: 0)

pub fn from_mins(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 60)
pub fn from_hours(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 3600)
pub fn from_days(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 86400)
pub fn from_weeks(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 604800)

pub fn as_secs(d: &Dur) -> u64 = d.secs
pub fn subsec_millis(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000000
pub fn subsec_micros(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000
pub fn subsec_nanos(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos
pub fn is_zero(d: &Dur) -> bool = d.secs == 0 and d.nanos == 0
# Total as decimal text (Rust's u128 as_nanos, as_micros, as_millis), exact.
fn pad9(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    var o = v.tostr()
    while (o.len_bytes() as i64) < w bound 9
        o = "0" + o
    return o
fn in_units(d: &Dur, digits: i64, unit: i64) -> text
    let part = d.nanos / unit
    if d.secs == 0
        return part.tostr()
    return d.secs.tostr() + pad9(part, digits)
pub fn as_nanos(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 9, 1)
pub fn as_micros(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 6, 1000)
pub fn as_millis(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 3, 1000000)

pub fn dur_cmp(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn dur_eq(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> bool = dur_cmp(a, b) == 0

pub fn checked_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if b.secs > MAX_U - a.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs + b.secs
    var n = a.nanos + b.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_U
            return none
        s += 1
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn checked_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if a.secs < b.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs - b.secs
    var n = a.nanos - b.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == 0
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn saturating_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_add(a, b).or(dur_max())
pub fn saturating_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())

pub fn abs_diff(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur
    if dur_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())
    return checked_sub(b, a).or(dur_zero())

# Multiplier and divisor are u32 in Rust: 0 ..= 4294967295.
pub fn checked_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k < 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let total = a.nanos as u64 * ku
    let extra = total / NPS
    if ku != 0 and a.secs > (MAX_U - extra) / ku
        return none
    return some(Dur(secs: a.secs * ku + extra, nanos: (total % NPS) as i64))

pub fn saturating_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur = checked_mul(a, k).or(dur_max())

pub fn checked_div(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k <= 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let s = a.secs / ku
    let carry = a.secs % ku
    let extra = (carry * NPS + a.nanos as u64 % ku) / ku
    let n = a.nanos / k + extra as i64
    return some(Dur(secs: s + (n / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64, nanos: n % NANOS_PER_SEC))

pub fn dur_sum(ds: &[Dur]) -> Dur?
    var acc = dur_zero()
    for d in ds
        match checked_add(&acc, &d)
            some(x) -> acc = x
            none -> return none
    return some(acc)

# ---------------- Debug formatting ----------------
# Rust's `{:?}` for Duration. prec < 0 means no precision; width < 0 means
# no width; align is "<", ">", "^" or "" (default left); plus is `{:+?}`.

fn spaces(n: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n
        o = o + " "
        k += 1
    return o

fn fmt_decimal(ip0: u64, fp0: i64, div0: i64, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, prefix: &text, postfix: &text) -> text
    var buf: List[i64] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    var fp = fp0
    var dv = div0
    var pos = 0
    let lim = if prec < 0 then 9 else prec
    while fp > 0 and pos < lim and pos < 9
        buf[pos as usize] = fp / dv
        fp = fp % dv
        dv = dv / 10
        pos += 1
    var ip = ip0
    var big = false
    if fp > 0 and fp >= dv * 5
        let tie = fp == dv * 5
        let odd = if pos > 0 then copy(buf[(pos - 1) as usize]) % 2 == 1 else ip % 2 == 1
        if not (tie and not odd)
            var r = pos
            var carry = true
            while carry and r > 0
                r -= 1
                if buf[r as usize] < 9
                    buf[r as usize] = copy(buf[r as usize]) + 1
                    carry = false
                else
                    buf[r as usize] = 0
            if carry
                if ip == MAX_U
                    big = true
                else
                    ip += 1
    let end = if prec >= 0 then (if prec < 9 then prec else 9) else pos
    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())
    if end > 0
        let w = if prec >= 0 then prec else pos
        o = o + "."
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < w
            o = o + (if k < end then copy(buf[k as usize]).tostr() else "0")
            k += 1
        cells = cells + 1 + w as usize
    o = o + postfix
    if width < 0 or width as usize <= cells
        return o
    let padn = width - cells as i64
    let pre = if align == ">" then padn else (if align == "^" then padn / 2 else 0)
    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

pub fn dur_debug_with(d: &Dur, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, plus: bool) -> text
    let p = if plus then "+" else ""
    let us = "s"
    let ums = "ms"
    let uus = "µs"
    let uns = "ns"
    if d.secs > 0
        return fmt_decimal(d.secs, d.nanos, NANOS_PER_SEC / 10, prec, width, align, &p, &us)
    if d.nanos >= 1000000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000000, 100000, prec, width, align, &p, &ums)
    if d.nanos >= 1000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000, 100, prec, width, align, &p, &uus)
    return fmt_decimal(d.nanos as u64, 0, 1, prec, width, align, &p, &uns)

pub fn dur_debug(d: &Dur) -> text
    let a = ""
    return dur_debug_with(d, -1, -1, &a, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------

pub struct Timespec
    secs: i64
    nanos: i64

pub fn ts_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0 or nanos >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        fail BadClock(why: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return Timespec(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

pub fn ts_min() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MIN_SECS, nanos: 0)
pub fn ts_max() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MAX_SECS, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn ts_cmp(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn ts_eq(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> bool = ts_cmp(a, b) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn add_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t >= 0
        if d > (MAX_SECS - t) as u64
            return none
        return some(t + d as i64)
    let room = MAX_SECS as u64 + (0 - (t + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t + d as i64)
    return some((t + MAX_SECS + 1) + (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn sub_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t < 0
        if d > (t - MIN_SECS) as u64
            return none
        return some(t - d as i64)
    let room = t as u64 + MAX_SECS as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t - d as i64)
    return some((t - MAX_SECS - 1) - (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn ts_checked_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match add_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos + d.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_SECS
            return none
        s += 1
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_checked_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match sub_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos - d.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == MIN_SECS
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_saturating_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_add(t, d).or(ts_max())
pub fn ts_saturating_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_sub(t, d).or(ts_min())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct Diff
    ok: bool
    d: Dur

# a - b for a >= b; the seconds difference can reach u64::MAX.
fn diff_u(a: i64, b: i64) -> u64
    if b >= 0 or a < 0
        return (a - b) as u64
    return a as u64 + (0 - (b + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn mag(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Dur
    if a.nanos >= b.nanos
        return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs), nanos: a.nanos - b.nanos)
    return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs) - 1, nanos: a.nanos + NANOS_PER_SEC - b.nanos)

pub fn sub_timespec(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Diff
    if ts_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return Diff(ok: true, d: mag(a, b))
    return Diff(ok: false, d: mag(b, a))

pub fn checked_duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur?
    let r = sub_timespec(a, earlier)
    if r.ok
        return some(copy(r.d))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur = checked_duration_since(a, earlier).or(dur_zero())

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

pub struct Timers
    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

# wasi subscribe-instant. Timers are kept in firing order.
pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

module os.clock

# Clocks and timers (survey M37), pure. A program never reads a clock: the
# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.
# This module holds what a program does with those values:
# - Dur, Rust's core::time::Duration (secs plus nanos below one second)
#   with its constructors, accessors, checked and saturating arithmetic and
#   its Debug formatting ("1.5s", "7.1µs", precision, width, alignment).
#   Secs are u64 as in Rust, so the full range holds.
# - Timespec, the point type behind Rust's unix Instant and SystemTime
#   (secs i64, nanos 0..1e9), with checked and saturating add/sub and
#   duration_since in Rust's forms (saturating, checked, signed result).
# - wasi:clocks@0.2.8 values: a monotonic instant (u64 ns) and a wall
#   datetime (seconds, nanoseconds < 1e9) mapped to Timespec.
# - Mono, the admission rule for monotonic readings: a reading below the
#   last admitted one is raised to it (non-decreasing, as wasi-clocks
#   promises and as Rust's monotonize enforces).
# - Timers, the pure timer queue: subscribe at an instant or after a
#   duration; a tick at `now` fires every due timer in (deadline, subscribe
#   order) order. The host admits those firings as events in that order.

error BadClock(why: text)

pub const NANOS_PER_SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const NPS: u64 = 1000000000
pub const MAX_U: u64 = 18446744073709551615
pub const MAX_SECS: i64 = 9223372036854775807
pub const MIN_SECS: i64 = -9223372036854775808

# secs is u64 as in Rust, so the full range up to u64::MAX seconds holds.
pub struct Dur
    secs: u64
    nanos: i64

pub fn dur_zero() -> Dur = Dur(secs: 0, nanos: 0)
pub fn dur_max() -> Dur = Dur(secs: MAX_U, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

# Duration::new: nanos beyond a second carry into secs; overflow fails.
pub fn dur_new(secs: u64, nanos: i64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0
        fail BadClock(why: "negative nanoseconds")
    let extra = (nanos / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64
    if extra > MAX_U - secs
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::new")
    return Dur(secs: secs + extra, nanos: nanos % NANOS_PER_SEC)

pub fn from_secs(s: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: s, nanos: 0)
pub fn from_millis(ms: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ms / 1000, nanos: (ms % 1000) as i64 * 1000000)
pub fn from_micros(us: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: us / 1000000, nanos: (us % 1000000) as i64 * 1000)
pub fn from_nanos(ns: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ns / NPS, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

# Duration::from_nanos_u128 for a u128 given as decimal digits: the last
# nine digits are the nanos, the rest the secs (must fit u64).
pub fn from_nanos_text(t: &text) -> Dur ! BadClock
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0
        fail BadClock(why: "empty")
    var secs: u64 = 0
    var nanos: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 0
    let cut: usize = if cs.len() > 9 then cs.len() - 9 else 0
    for c in cs
        let v = c[0] as i64 - 48
        if v < 0 or v > 9
            fail BadClock(why: "not a decimal")
        if k < cut
            if secs > (MAX_U - v as u64) / 10
                fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::from_nanos_u128")
            secs = secs * 10 + v as u64
        else
            nanos = nanos * 10 + v
        k += 1
    return Dur(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

fn from_unit(n: u64, unit: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if n > MAX_U / unit
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration constructor")
    return Dur(secs: n * unit, nanos: 0)

pub fn from_mins(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 60)
pub fn from_hours(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 3600)
pub fn from_days(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 86400)
pub fn from_weeks(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 604800)

pub fn as_secs(d: &Dur) -> u64 = d.secs
pub fn subsec_millis(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000000
pub fn subsec_micros(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000
pub fn subsec_nanos(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos
pub fn is_zero(d: &Dur) -> bool = d.secs == 0 and d.nanos == 0
# Total as decimal text (Rust's u128 as_nanos, as_micros, as_millis), exact.
fn pad9(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    var o = v.tostr()
    while (o.len_bytes() as i64) < w bound 9
        o = "0" + o
    return o
fn in_units(d: &Dur, digits: i64, unit: i64) -> text
    let part = d.nanos / unit
    if d.secs == 0
        return part.tostr()
    return d.secs.tostr() + pad9(part, digits)
pub fn as_nanos(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 9, 1)
pub fn as_micros(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 6, 1000)
pub fn as_millis(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 3, 1000000)

pub fn dur_cmp(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn dur_eq(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> bool = dur_cmp(a, b) == 0

pub fn checked_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if b.secs > MAX_U - a.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs + b.secs
    var n = a.nanos + b.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_U
            return none
        s += 1
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn checked_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if a.secs < b.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs - b.secs
    var n = a.nanos - b.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == 0
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn saturating_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_add(a, b).or(dur_max())
pub fn saturating_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())

pub fn abs_diff(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur
    if dur_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())
    return checked_sub(b, a).or(dur_zero())

# Multiplier and divisor are u32 in Rust: 0 ..= 4294967295.
pub fn checked_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k < 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let total = a.nanos as u64 * ku
    let extra = total / NPS
    if ku != 0 and a.secs > (MAX_U - extra) / ku
        return none
    return some(Dur(secs: a.secs * ku + extra, nanos: (total % NPS) as i64))

pub fn saturating_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur = checked_mul(a, k).or(dur_max())

pub fn checked_div(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k <= 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let s = a.secs / ku
    let carry = a.secs % ku
    let extra = (carry * NPS + a.nanos as u64 % ku) / ku
    let n = a.nanos / k + extra as i64
    return some(Dur(secs: s + (n / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64, nanos: n % NANOS_PER_SEC))

pub fn dur_sum(ds: &[Dur]) -> Dur?
    var acc = dur_zero()
    for d in ds
        match checked_add(&acc, &d)
            some(x) -> acc = x
            none -> return none
    return some(acc)

# ---------------- Debug formatting ----------------
# Rust's `{:?}` for Duration. prec < 0 means no precision; width < 0 means
# no width; align is "<", ">", "^" or "" (default left); plus is `{:+?}`.

fn spaces(n: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n
        o = o + " "
        k += 1
    return o

fn fmt_decimal(ip0: u64, fp0: i64, div0: i64, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, prefix: &text, postfix: &text) -> text
    var buf: List[i64] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    var fp = fp0
    var dv = div0
    var pos = 0
    let lim = if prec < 0 then 9 else prec
    while fp > 0 and pos < lim and pos < 9
        buf[pos as usize] = fp / dv
        fp = fp % dv
        dv = dv / 10
        pos += 1
    var ip = ip0
    var big = false
    if fp > 0 and fp >= dv * 5
        let tie = fp == dv * 5
        let odd = if pos > 0 then copy(buf[(pos - 1) as usize]) % 2 == 1 else ip % 2 == 1
        if not (tie and not odd)
            var r = pos
            var carry = true
            while carry and r > 0
                r -= 1
                if buf[r as usize] < 9
                    buf[r as usize] = copy(buf[r as usize]) + 1
                    carry = false
                else
                    buf[r as usize] = 0
            if carry
                if ip == MAX_U
                    big = true
                else
                    ip += 1
    let end = if prec >= 0 then (if prec < 9 then prec else 9) else pos
    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())
    if end > 0
        let w = if prec >= 0 then prec else pos
        o = o + "."
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < w
            o = o + (if k < end then copy(buf[k as usize]).tostr() else "0")
            k += 1
        cells = cells + 1 + w as usize
    o = o + postfix
    if width < 0 or width as usize <= cells
        return o
    let padn = width - cells as i64
    let pre = if align == ">" then padn else (if align == "^" then padn / 2 else 0)
    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

pub fn dur_debug_with(d: &Dur, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, plus: bool) -> text
    let p = if plus then "+" else ""
    let us = "s"
    let ums = "ms"
    let uus = "µs"
    let uns = "ns"
    if d.secs > 0
        return fmt_decimal(d.secs, d.nanos, NANOS_PER_SEC / 10, prec, width, align, &p, &us)
    if d.nanos >= 1000000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000000, 100000, prec, width, align, &p, &ums)
    if d.nanos >= 1000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000, 100, prec, width, align, &p, &uus)
    return fmt_decimal(d.nanos as u64, 0, 1, prec, width, align, &p, &uns)

pub fn dur_debug(d: &Dur) -> text
    let a = ""
    return dur_debug_with(d, -1, -1, &a, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------

pub struct Timespec
    secs: i64
    nanos: i64

pub fn ts_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0 or nanos >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        fail BadClock(why: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return Timespec(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

pub fn ts_min() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MIN_SECS, nanos: 1)
pub fn ts_max() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MAX_SECS, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn ts_cmp(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn ts_eq(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> bool = ts_cmp(a, b) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn add_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t >= 0
        if d > (MAX_SECS - t) as u64
            return none
        return some(t + d as i64)
    let room = MAX_SECS as u64 + (0 - (t + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t + d as i64)
    return some((t + MAX_SECS + 1) + (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn sub_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t < 0
        if d > (t - MIN_SECS) as u64
            return none
        return some(t - d as i64)
    let room = t as u64 + MAX_SECS as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t - d as i64)
    return some((t - MAX_SECS - 1) - (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn ts_checked_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match add_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos + d.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_SECS
            return none
        s += 1
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_checked_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match sub_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos - d.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == MIN_SECS
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_saturating_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_add(t, d).or(ts_max())
pub fn ts_saturating_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_sub(t, d).or(ts_min())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct Diff
    ok: bool
    d: Dur

# a - b for a >= b; the seconds difference can reach u64::MAX.
fn diff_u(a: i64, b: i64) -> u64
    if b >= 0 or a < 0
        return (a - b) as u64
    return a as u64 + (0 - (b + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn mag(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Dur
    if a.nanos >= b.nanos
        return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs), nanos: a.nanos - b.nanos)
    return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs) - 1, nanos: a.nanos + NANOS_PER_SEC - b.nanos)

pub fn sub_timespec(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Diff
    if ts_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return Diff(ok: true, d: mag(a, b))
    return Diff(ok: false, d: mag(b, a))

pub fn checked_duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur?
    let r = sub_timespec(a, earlier)
    if r.ok
        return some(copy(r.d))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur = checked_duration_since(a, earlier).or(dur_zero())

# ---------------- wasi:clocks@0.2.8 ----------------

# monotonic-clock instant and duration are u64 ns.
pub fn mono_from_wasi(ns: u64) -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: (ns / NPS) as i64, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

pub fn mono_to_wasi(t: &Timespec) -> u64 ! BadClock
    if t.secs < 0 or t.secs as u64 > (MAX_U - t.nanos as u64) / NPS
        fail BadClock(why: "instant out of range")
    return t.secs as u64 * NPS + t.nanos as u64

# wall-clock datetime: "The nanoseconds field of the output is always less than 1000000000."
# seconds is u64; past i64::MAX seconds it is beyond the unix point type.
pub fn wall_from_wasi(seconds: u64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if seconds > MAX_SECS as u64
        fail BadClock(why: "seconds out of range")
    return ts_new(seconds as i64, nanoseconds)

# ---------------- admission of monotonic readings ----------------

pub struct Mono
    last: Timespec
    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_new() -> Mono = Mono(last: Timespec(secs: 0, nanos: 0), seen: false, raised: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

pub struct Timers
    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

# wasi subscribe-instant. Timers are kept in firing order.
pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

                else

    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())

        var k: i64 = 0

    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

    let uus = "µs"

    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

    seq: i64

    next: i64

    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)

pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 1
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

pub struct Mono
    last: Timespec
    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_new() -> Mono = Mono(last: Timespec(secs: 0, nanos: 0), seen: false, raised: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1

    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)

        out.push(copy(x))

    q.list = out

pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

module os.clock

# Clocks and timers (survey M37), pure. A program never reads a clock: the
# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.
# This module holds what a program does with those values:
# - Dur, Rust's core::time::Duration (secs plus nanos below one second)
#   with its constructors, accessors, checked and saturating arithmetic and
#   its Debug formatting ("1.5s", "7.1µs", precision, width, alignment).
#   Secs are u64 as in Rust, so the full range holds.
# - Timespec, the point type behind Rust's unix Instant and SystemTime
#   (secs i64, nanos 0..1e9), with checked and saturating add/sub and
#   duration_since in Rust's forms (saturating, checked, signed result).
# - wasi:clocks@0.2.8 values: a monotonic instant (u64 ns) and a wall
#   datetime (seconds, nanoseconds < 1e9) mapped to Timespec.
# - Mono, the admission rule for monotonic readings: a reading below the
#   last admitted one is raised to it (non-decreasing, as wasi-clocks
#   promises and as Rust's monotonize enforces).
# - Timers, the pure timer queue: subscribe at an instant or after a
#   duration; a tick at `now` fires every due timer in (deadline, subscribe
#   order) order. The host admits those firings as events in that order.

error BadClock(why: text)

pub const NANOS_PER_SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const NPS: u64 = 1000000000
pub const MAX_U: u64 = 18446744073709551615
pub const MAX_SECS: i64 = 9223372036854775807
pub const MIN_SECS: i64 = -9223372036854775808

# secs is u64 as in Rust, so the full range up to u64::MAX seconds holds.
pub struct Dur
    secs: u64
    nanos: i64

pub fn dur_zero() -> Dur = Dur(secs: 0, nanos: 0)
pub fn dur_max() -> Dur = Dur(secs: MAX_U, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

# Duration::new: nanos beyond a second carry into secs; overflow fails.
pub fn dur_new(secs: u64, nanos: i64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0
        fail BadClock(why: "negative nanoseconds")
    let extra = (nanos / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64
    if extra > MAX_U - secs
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::new")
    return Dur(secs: secs + extra, nanos: nanos % NANOS_PER_SEC)

pub fn from_secs(s: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: s, nanos: 0)
pub fn from_millis(ms: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ms / 1000, nanos: (ms % 1000) as i64 * 1000000)
pub fn from_micros(us: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: us / 1000000, nanos: (us % 1000000) as i64 * 1000)
pub fn from_nanos(ns: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ns / NPS, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

# Duration::from_nanos_u128 for a u128 given as decimal digits: the last
# nine digits are the nanos, the rest the secs (must fit u64).
pub fn from_nanos_text(t: &text) -> Dur ! BadClock
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0
        fail BadClock(why: "empty")
    var secs: u64 = 0
    var nanos: u64 = 0
    var k: usize = 0
    let cut: usize = if cs.len() > 9 then cs.len() - 9 else 0
    for c in cs
        let v = c[0] as i64 - 48
        if v < 0 or v > 9
            fail BadClock(why: "not a decimal")
        if k < cut
            if secs > (MAX_U - v as u64) / 10
                fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::from_nanos_u128")
            secs = secs * 10 + v as u64
        else
            nanos = nanos * 10 + v
        k += 1
    return Dur(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

fn from_unit(n: u64, unit: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if n > MAX_U / unit
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration constructor")
    return Dur(secs: n * unit, nanos: 0)

pub fn from_mins(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 60)
pub fn from_hours(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 3600)
pub fn from_days(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 86400)
pub fn from_weeks(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 604800)

pub fn as_secs(d: &Dur) -> u64 = d.secs
pub fn subsec_millis(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000000
pub fn subsec_micros(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000
pub fn subsec_nanos(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos
pub fn is_zero(d: &Dur) -> bool = d.secs == 0 and d.nanos == 0
# Total as decimal text (Rust's u128 as_nanos, as_micros, as_millis), exact.
fn pad9(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    var o = v.tostr()
    while (o.len_bytes() as i64) < w bound 9
        o = "0" + o
    return o
fn in_units(d: &Dur, digits: i64, unit: i64) -> text
    let part = d.nanos / unit
    if d.secs == 0
        return part.tostr()
    return d.secs.tostr() + pad9(part, digits)
pub fn as_nanos(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 9, 1)
pub fn as_micros(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 6, 1000)
pub fn as_millis(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 3, 1000000)

pub fn dur_cmp(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn dur_eq(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> bool = dur_cmp(a, b) == 0

pub fn checked_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if b.secs > MAX_U - a.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs + b.secs
    var n = a.nanos + b.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_U
            return none
        s += 1
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn checked_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if a.secs < b.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs - b.secs
    var n = a.nanos - b.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == 0
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn saturating_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_add(a, b).or(dur_max())
pub fn saturating_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())

pub fn abs_diff(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur
    if dur_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())
    return checked_sub(b, a).or(dur_zero())

# Multiplier and divisor are u32 in Rust: 0 ..= 4294967295.
pub fn checked_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k < 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let total = a.nanos as u64 * ku
    let extra = total / NPS
    if ku != 0 and a.secs > (MAX_U - extra) / ku
        return none
    return some(Dur(secs: a.secs * ku + extra, nanos: (total % NPS) as i64))

pub fn saturating_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur = checked_mul(a, k).or(dur_max())

pub fn checked_div(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k <= 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let s = a.secs / ku
    let carry = a.secs % ku
    let extra = (carry * NPS + a.nanos as u64 % ku) / ku
    let n = a.nanos / k + extra as i64
    return some(Dur(secs: s + (n / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64, nanos: n % NANOS_PER_SEC))

pub fn dur_sum(ds: &[Dur]) -> Dur?
    var acc = dur_zero()
    for d in ds
        match checked_add(&acc, &d)
            some(x) -> acc = x
            none -> return none
    return some(acc)

# ---------------- Debug formatting ----------------
# Rust's `{:?}` for Duration. prec < 0 means no precision; width < 0 means
# no width; align is "<", ">", "^" or "" (default left); plus is `{:+?}`.

fn spaces(n: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n
        o = o + " "
        k += 1
    return o

fn fmt_decimal(ip0: u64, fp0: i64, div0: i64, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, prefix: &text, postfix: &text) -> text
    var buf: List[i64] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    var fp = fp0
    var dv = div0
    var pos = 0

        fp = fp % dv

        pos += 1

    var big = false

            var r = pos
            var carry = true
            while carry and r > 0
                r -= 1
                if buf[r as usize] < 9
                    buf[r as usize] = copy(buf[r as usize]) + 1

                    buf[r as usize] = 0

                    big = true
                else

    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())

        return o
    let padn = width - cells as i64
    let pre = if align == ">" then padn else (if align == "^" then padn / 2 else 0)
    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

pub fn dur_debug_with(d: &Dur, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, plus: bool) -> text
    let p = if plus then "+" else ""
    let us = "s"
    let ums = "ms"
    let uus = "µs"
    let uns = "ns"
    if d.secs > 0
        return fmt_decimal(d.secs, d.nanos, NANOS_PER_SEC / 10, prec, width, align, &p, &us)
    if d.nanos >= 1000000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000000, 100000, prec, width, align, &p, &ums)
    if d.nanos >= 1000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000, 100, prec, width, align, &p, &uus)
    return fmt_decimal(d.nanos as u64, 0, 1, prec, width, align, &p, &uns)

pub fn dur_debug(d: &Dur) -> text
    let a = ""
    return dur_debug_with(d, -1, -1, &a, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------

pub struct Timespec
    secs: i64
    nanos: i64

pub fn ts_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0 or nanos >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        fail BadClock(why: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return Timespec(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

pub fn ts_min() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MIN_SECS, nanos: 0)
pub fn ts_max() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MAX_SECS, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn ts_cmp(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn ts_eq(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> bool = ts_cmp(a, b) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn add_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t >= 0
        if d > (MAX_SECS - t) as u64
            return none
        return some(t + d as i64)
    let room = MAX_SECS as u64 + (0 - (t + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t + d as i64)
    return some((t + MAX_SECS + 1) + (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn sub_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t < 0
        if d > (t - MIN_SECS) as u64
            return none
        return some(t - d as i64)
    let room = t as u64 + MAX_SECS as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t - d as i64)
    return some((t - MAX_SECS - 1) - (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn ts_checked_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match add_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos + d.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_SECS
            return none
        s += 1
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_checked_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match sub_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos - d.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == MIN_SECS
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_saturating_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_add(t, d).or(ts_max())
pub fn ts_saturating_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_sub(t, d).or(ts_min())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct Diff
    ok: bool
    d: Dur

fn diff_u(a: i64, b: i64) -> u64
    if b >= 0 or a < 0
        return (a - b) as u64
    return a as u64 + (0 - (b + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn mag(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Dur
    if a.nanos >= b.nanos
        return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs), nanos: a.nanos - b.nanos)
    return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs) - 1, nanos: a.nanos + NANOS_PER_SEC - b.nanos)

pub fn sub_timespec(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Diff
    if ts_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return Diff(ok: true, d: mag(a, b))
    return Diff(ok: false, d: mag(b, a))

pub fn checked_duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur?
    let r = sub_timespec(a, earlier)
    if r.ok
        return some(copy(r.d))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur = checked_duration_since(a, earlier).or(dur_zero())

# ---------------- wasi:clocks@0.2.8 ----------------

# monotonic-clock instant and duration are u64 ns.
pub fn mono_from_wasi(ns: u64) -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: (ns / NPS) as i64, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

pub fn mono_to_wasi(t: &Timespec) -> u64 ! BadClock
    if t.secs < 0 or t.secs as u64 > (MAX_U - t.nanos as u64) / NPS
        fail BadClock(why: "instant out of range")
    return t.secs as u64 * NPS + t.nanos as u64

# seconds is u64; past i64::MAX seconds it is beyond the unix point type.
pub fn wall_from_wasi(seconds: u64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if seconds > MAX_SECS as u64
        fail BadClock(why: "seconds out of range")
    return ts_new(seconds as i64, nanoseconds)

# ---------------- admission of monotonic readings ----------------

pub struct Mono
    last: Timespec
    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_new() -> Mono = Mono(last: Timespec(secs: 0, nanos: 0), seen: false, raised: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

pub struct Timers
    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)

    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids
