        if used & mask(&f) != 0
            return false

# Decode frames from line levels (idle 1 between frames): each value, or
# -1 for a framing error (a stop bit at 0) and -2 for a parity error.
pub fn uart_decode(line: &List[i64], c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    let flen = 1 + c.data + (if c.parity == "N" then 0 else 1) + c.stop
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < line.len() bound 16777216
        if line[i] == 1
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + flen as usize > line.len()
            break
        var v: i64 = 0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < c.data bound 8
            v = v | (line[i + 1 + k as usize] << k)
            k += 1
        var res = v
        var p = i + 1 + c.data as usize
        if c.parity != "N"
            if line[p] != parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity)
                res = -2
            p += 1
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < c.stop bound 2
            if line[p + s as usize] != 1
                res = -1
            s += 1
        out.push(res)
        i += flen as usize
    return out

# 16550 divisor latch for a baud rate from a 1.8432 MHz clock (115200
# base); -1 when the rate is not an exact divisor.
pub fn uart_divisor(baud: i64) -> i64
    if baud <= 0 or 115200 % baud != 0
        return -1
    return 115200 / baud

# ---------------- register maps ----------------

pub struct Field
    name: text
    lsb: i64
    width: i64
    access: text

fn mask(f: &Field) -> i64 = ((1 << f.width) - 1) << f.lsb

pub fn field_get(reg: i64, f: &Field) -> i64 = (reg >> f.lsb) & ((1 << f.width) - 1)

# The register value after a software write of v to field f, given the
# current value: read-only fields keep their bits; for a write-1-to-clear
# field ("w1c") the written ones clear bits and the others stay.
pub fn field_set(reg: i64, f: &Field, v: i64) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if v < 0 or v >= (1 << f.width)
        fail BadDevice(why: "value does not fit the field")
    if f.access == "ro"
        fail BadDevice(why: "read-only field")
    if f.access == "w1c"
        return reg & ~(v << f.lsb)
    return (reg & ~mask(f)) | (v << f.lsb)

# Fields must not overlap and must fit the register width.
pub fn fields_ok(fs: &List[Field], width: i64) -> bool
    var used: i64 = 0
    for f in fs
        if f.width < 1 or f.lsb < 0 or f.lsb + f.width > width
            return false
        if used & mask(&f) != 0
            return false
        used = used | mask(&f)
    return true

    var t: i64 = 0
    if class != "Cpu" and class != "Simd"

    if passthrough

#    values and names (EDK2 MdePkg Base.h), memory and reset types
#    (UefiMultiPhase.h), variable names (Boot####);

#    byte of a message, 10-bit addressing, SMBus PEC (CRC-8 as
#    i2c-core-smbus.c computes it) and embedded-hal style transactions;
#  - SPI: the spidev mode bits (uapi spi.h), clock idle level and edges
#    per mode, word bit order;
#  - UART: asynchronous frames (start, 5 to 8 data bits LSB first,
#    parity, 1 or 2 stop bits), decode with framing and parity errors,
#    the 16550 divisor;
#  - register maps: fields read and written by offset and width, with
#    read-only and write-1-to-clear fields;
#  - Sandbox v0.1 device classes and the least tier a grant needs.

error BadDevice(why: text)

const HEX: text = "0123456789abcdef"

fn hexv(c: &text) -> i64
    let d = HEX.chars()
    let l = c.lower()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if d[i as usize] == l
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

fn hex2(b: i64) -> text
    let d = HEX.chars()
    return d[((b >> 4) & 15) as usize] + d[(b & 15) as usize]

# ---------------- UEFI ----------------

# The 16 bytes of an EFI_GUID in memory from its registry text
# "aabbccdd-eeff-gghh-iijj-kkllmmnnoopp": Data1 (u32), Data2, Data3 (u16)
# little endian, Data4 as written.
pub fn guid_bytes(t: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDevice
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 36 or cs[8] != "-" or cs[13] != "-" or cs[18] != "-" or cs[23] != "-"
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    var v: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 36 bound 64
        if i == 8 or i == 13 or i == 18 or i == 23
            i += 1
            continue
        let a = hexv(&cs[i])
        let b = hexv(&cs[i + 1])
        if a < 0 or b < 0
            fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
        v.push(a * 16 + b)
        i += 2
    return [v[3], v[2], v[1], v[0], v[5], v[4], v[7], v[6], v[8], v[9], v[10], v[11], v[12], v[13], v[14], v[15]]

# Registry text (upper case, as UEFI writes GUIDs) of 16 GUID bytes.
pub fn guid_text(b: &List[i64]) -> text ! BadDevice
    if b.len() != 16
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    let o = [b[3], b[2], b[1], b[0], b[5], b[4], b[7], b[6], b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11], b[12], b[13], b[14], b[15]]
    var s = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if i == 4 or i == 6 or i == 8 or i == 10
            s = s + "-"
        s = s + hex2(o[i])
        i += 1
    return s.upper()

pub const EFI_GLOBAL_VARIABLE: text = "8BE4DF61-93CA-11D2-AA0D-00E098032B8C"

# MAX_BIT of a 64-bit UEFI target.
pub const MAX_BIT: i64 = -9223372036854775808

const STATUS_ERRORS: text = "LOAD_ERROR INVALID_PARAMETER UNSUPPORTED BAD_BUFFER_SIZE BUFFER_TOO_SMALL NOT_READY DEVICE_ERROR WRITE_PROTECTED OUT_OF_RESOURCES VOLUME_CORRUPTED VOLUME_FULL NO_MEDIA MEDIA_CHANGED NOT_FOUND ACCESS_DENIED NO_RESPONSE NO_MAPPING TIMEOUT NOT_STARTED ALREADY_STARTED ABORTED ICMP_ERROR TFTP_ERROR PROTOCOL_ERROR INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION SECURITY_VIOLATION CRC_ERROR END_OF_MEDIA - - END_OF_FILE INVALID_LANGUAGE COMPROMISED_DATA IP_ADDRESS_CONFLICT HTTP_ERROR"
const STATUS_WARNINGS: text = "WARN_UNKNOWN_GLYPH WARN_DELETE_FAILURE WARN_WRITE_FAILURE WARN_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL WARN_STALE_DATA WARN_FILE_SYSTEM WARN_RESET_REQUIRED"

# The EFI_STATUS of a name without its prefix ("NOT_FOUND"); fails for an unknown name.
pub fn status_value(name: &text) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if name == "SUCCESS"
        return 0
    var i: i64 = 1
    for e in STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if e == name and e != "-"
            return MAX_BIT | i
        i += 1
    i = 1
    for w in STATUS_WARNINGS.split(" ")
        if w == name
            return i
        i += 1
    fail BadDevice(why: "unknown status")

pub fn status_name(v: i64) -> text
    if v == 0
        return "SUCCESS"
    let code = v & 9223372036854775807
    if v < 0
        let es = STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if code >= 1 and code <= es.len() as i64 and es[(code - 1) as usize] != "-"
            return copy(es[(code - 1) as usize])
        return ""
    let ws = STATUS_WARNINGS.split(" ")
    if code <= ws.len() as i64
        return copy(ws[(code - 1) as usize])
    return ""

# RETURN_ERROR: the high bit is set.
pub fn status_is_error(v: i64) -> bool = v < 0

const MEMORY_TYPES: text = "EfiReservedMemoryType EfiLoaderCode EfiLoaderData EfiBootServicesCode EfiBootServicesData EfiRuntimeServicesCode EfiRuntimeServicesData EfiConventionalMemory EfiUnusableMemory EfiACPIReclaimMemory EfiACPIMemoryNVS EfiMemoryMappedIO EfiMemoryMappedIOPortSpace EfiPalCode EfiPersistentMemory EfiUnacceptedMemoryType EfiMaxMemoryType"
const RESET_TYPES: text = "EfiResetCold EfiResetWarm EfiResetShutdown EfiResetPlatformSpecific"

fn index_of(list: &text, name: &text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in list.split(" ")
        if x == name
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn memory_type(name: &text) -> i64 = index_of(&MEMORY_TYPES, name)
pub fn reset_type(name: &text) -> i64 = index_of(&RESET_TYPES, name)

# Boot#### / Driver#### / SysPrep#### variable names: four upper-case hex digits.
pub fn load_option_name(prefix: &text, n: i64) -> text ! BadDevice
    if n < 0 or n > 65535
        fail BadDevice(why: "option number out of range")
    return prefix + (hex2(n >> 8) + hex2(n & 255)).upper()

pub fn load_option_number(name: &text, prefix: &text) -> i64
    if not name.startswith(prefix) or name.len_bytes() != prefix.len_bytes() + 4
        return -1
    let cs = name.chars()
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = prefix.chars().len()
    while i < cs.len() bound 8
        let h = hexv(&cs[i])
        if h < 0 or cs[i] != cs[i].upper()
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + h
        i += 1
    return v

# ---------------- I2C ----------------

pub const I2C_M_RD: i64 = 1
pub const I2C_M_TEN: i64 = 16

# i2c_check_addr_validity: 10-bit addresses up to 0x3ff; a 7-bit address
# must not be the general call address 0 nor exceed 0x7f.
pub fn i2c_addr_valid(addr: i64, ten: bool) -> bool
    if ten
        return addr >= 0 and addr <= 1023
    return addr > 0 and addr <= 127

# i2c_check_7bit_addr_validity_strict (probing): 0x08 to 0x77.
pub fn i2c_addr_valid_strict(addr: i64) -> bool = addr >= 8 and addr <= 119

# i2c_8bit_addr_from_msg: the first byte on the wire for a 7-bit address.
pub fn i2c_addr_byte(addr: i64, flags: i64) -> i64 = ((addr << 1) | (flags & I2C_M_RD)) & 255

# A 10-bit address on the wire: 11110 A9 A8 R/W, then A7..A0.
pub fn i2c_ten_bit_bytes(addr: i64, read: bool) -> List[i64] = [240 | ((addr >> 7) & 6) | (if read then 1 else 0), addr & 255]

fn crc8_step(d: i64) -> i64
    var data = d & 65535
    var i = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        if data & 32768 != 0
            data = data ^ (4208 << 3)
        data = data << 1
        i += 1
    return (data >> 8) & 255

# i2c_smbus_pec: incremental CRC-8 (x^8 + x^2 + x + 1) over bytes.
pub fn smbus_pec(crc: i64, bytes: &List[i64]) -> i64
    var c = crc
    for b in bytes
        c = crc8_step(((c ^ b) & 255) << 8)
    return c

# The PEC of a message sequence as i2c_smbus_xfer_emulated computes it:
# each message adds its address byte, then its data.
pub struct I2cMsg
    addr: i64
    flags: i64
    data: List[i64]

pub fn smbus_msgs_pec(msgs: &List[I2cMsg]) -> i64
    var pec: i64 = 0
    for m in msgs
        let ab = [i2c_addr_byte(m.addr, m.flags)]
        pec = smbus_pec(pec, &ab)
        pec = smbus_pec(pec, &m.data)
    return pec

# embedded-hal style expectations: each transaction is checked against
# the next expected one (operation, address, bytes); the result is the index
# of the first mismatch or -1 when every transaction matched and none
# remains.
pub struct Txn
    op: text
    addr: i64
    bytes: List[i64]

pub fn txn_check(expected: &List[Txn], actual: &List[Txn]) -> i64
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < actual.len() bound 1048576
        if i >= expected.len()
            return i as i64
        let e = copy(expected[i])
        let a = copy(actual[i])
        if e.op != a.op or e.addr != a.addr or e.bytes != a.bytes
            return i as i64
        i += 1
    if i < expected.len()
        return i as i64
    return -1

# ---------------- SPI ----------------

pub const SPI_CPHA: i64 = 1
pub const SPI_CPOL: i64 = 2
pub const SPI_CS_HIGH: i64 = 4
pub const SPI_LSB_FIRST: i64 = 8
pub const SPI_3WIRE: i64 = 16
pub const SPI_LOOP: i64 = 32
pub const SPI_NO_CS: i64 = 64
pub const SPI_READY: i64 = 128
pub const SPI_MODE_USER_MASK: i64 = 524287

pub fn spi_mode_number(mode: i64) -> i64 = mode & 3

# The idle clock level (CPOL) and the edge that samples data: "leading"
# when CPHA is 0, else "trailing"; as a direction, the sampling edge rises
# for modes 0 and 3 and falls for modes 1 and 2.
pub fn spi_idle_high(mode: i64) -> bool = mode & SPI_CPOL != 0
pub fn spi_sample_rising(mode: i64) -> bool = (mode & SPI_CPOL != 0) == (mode & SPI_CPHA != 0)

# The bits of one word in wire order.
pub fn spi_word_bits(word: i64, bits: i64, mode: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < bits bound 64
        let k = if mode & SPI_LSB_FIRST != 0 then i else bits - 1 - i
        o.push((word >> k) & 1)
        i += 1
    return o

pub fn spi_bits_word(bs: &List[i64], mode: i64) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    let n = bs.len() as i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n bound 64
        let k = if mode & SPI_LSB_FIRST != 0 then i else n - 1 - i
        v = v | (bs[i as usize] << k)
        i += 1
    return v

# ---------------- UART ----------------

pub struct UartCfg
    data: i64
    parity: text
    stop: i64

fn parity_bit(v: i64, data: i64, pk: &text) -> i64
    var ones: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data bound 8
        ones += (v >> i) & 1
        i += 1
    if pk == "E"
        return ones & 1
    if pk == "O"
        return 1 - (ones & 1)
    if pk == "M"
        return 1
    return 0

# The line levels of one frame: 0 start bit, data LSB first, parity
# ("N" none, "E" even, "O" odd, "M" mark, "S" space), stop bits at 1.
pub fn uart_frame(v: i64, c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [0]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < c.data bound 8
        o.push((v >> i) & 1)
        i += 1
    if c.parity != "N"
        o.push(parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity))
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < c.stop bound 2
        o.push(1)
        s += 1
    return o

# Decode frames from line levels (idle 1 between frames): each value, or
# -1 for a framing error (a stop bit at 0) and -2 for a parity error.
pub fn uart_decode(line: &List[i64], c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    let flen = 1 + c.data + (if c.parity == "N" then 0 else 1) + c.stop
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < line.len() bound 16777216
        if line[i] == 1
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + flen as usize > line.len()
            break
        var v: i64 = 0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k >= c.data bound 8
            v = v | (line[i + 1 + k as usize] << k)
            k += 1
        var res = v
        var p = i + 1 + c.data as usize
        if c.parity != "N"
            if line[p] != parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity)
                res = -2
            p += 1
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < c.stop bound 2
            if line[p + s as usize] != 1
                res = -1
            s += 1
        out.push(res)
        i += flen as usize
    return out

# 16550 divisor latch for a baud rate from a 1.8432 MHz clock (115200
# base); -1 when the rate is not an exact divisor.
pub fn uart_divisor(baud: i64) -> i64
    if baud <= 0 or 115200 % baud != 0

    return 115200 / baud

    var data = d & 65535

# ---------------- UART ----------------

pub struct UartCfg
    data: i64
    parity: text
    stop: i64

fn parity_bit(v: i64, data: i64, pk: &text) -> i64
    var ones: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data bound 8
        ones += (v >> i) & 1
        i += 1
    if pk == "E"
        return ones & 1
    if pk == "O"
        return 1 - (ones & 1)
    if pk == "M"
        return 1
    return 0

# The line levels of one frame: 0 start bit, data LSB first, parity
# ("N" none, "E" even, "O" odd, "M" mark, "S" space), stop bits at 1.
pub fn uart_frame(v: i64, c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [0]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < c.data bound 8
        o.push((v >> i) & 1)
        i += 1
    if c.parity != "N"
        o.push(parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity))
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < c.stop bound 2
        o.push(1)
        s += 1
    return o

# Decode frames from line levels (idle 1 between frames): each value, or
# -1 for a framing error (a stop bit at 0) and -2 for a parity error.
pub fn uart_decode(line: &List[i64], c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    let flen = 1 + c.data + (if c.parity == "N" then 0 else 1) + c.stop
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < line.len() bound 16777216
        if line[i] == 1
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + flen as usize > line.len()
            break
        var v: i64 = 0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < c.data bound 8
            v = v | (line[i + 1 + k as usize] << k)
            k += 1
        var res = v
        var p = i + 1 + c.data as usize
        if c.parity != "N"
            if line[p] != parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity)
                res = -2
            p += 1
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < c.stop bound 2
            if line[p + s as usize] != 1
                res = -1
            s += 1
        out.push(res)
        i += flen as usize
    return out

# 16550 divisor latch for a baud rate from a 1.8432 MHz clock (115200
# base); -1 when the rate is not an exact divisor.
pub fn uart_divisor(baud: i64) -> i64
    if baud <= 0 or 115200 % baud != 0
        return -1
    return 115200 / baud

# ---------------- register maps ----------------

pub struct Field
    name: text
    lsb: i64
    width: i64
    access: text

fn mask(f: &Field) -> i64 = ((1 << f.width) - 1) << f.lsb

pub fn field_get(reg: i64, f: &Field) -> i64 = (reg >> f.lsb) & ((1 << f.width) - 1)

# The register value after a software write of v to field f, given the
# current value: read-only fields keep their bits; for a write-1-to-clear
# field ("w1c") the written ones clear bits and the others stay.
pub fn field_set(reg: i64, f: &Field, v: i64) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if v < 0 or v >= (1 << f.width)
        fail BadDevice(why: "value does not fit the field")
    if f.access == "ro"
        fail BadDevice(why: "read-only field")
    if f.access == "w1c"
        return reg & ~(v << f.lsb)
    return (reg & ~mask(f)) | (v << f.lsb)

# Fields must not overlap and must fit the register width.
pub fn fields_ok(fs: &List[Field], width: i64) -> bool
    var used: i64 = 0
    for f in fs
        if f.width < 1 or f.lsb < 0 or f.lsb + f.width > width
            return false
        if used & mask(&f) != 0
            return false
        used = used | mask(&f)
    return true

# keyword), pure. Device transactions are host capability
# effects (one cap per device class, every transaction logged); this
# module holds the models a Form reasons with:
#  - UEFI: EFI_GUID text and byte forms (mixed endian), EFI_STATUS

#    per mode, word bit order;

#    parity, 1 or 2 stop bits), decode with framing and parity errors,

#    read-only and write-1-to-clear fields;

error BadDevice(why: text)

const HEX: text = "0123456789abcdef"

fn hexv(c: &text) -> i64
    let d = HEX.chars()
    let l = c.lower()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if d[i as usize] == l
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

fn hex2(b: i64) -> text
    let d = HEX.chars()
    return d[((b >> 4) & 15) as usize] + d[(b & 15) as usize]

# The 16 bytes of an EFI_GUID in memory from its registry text
# "aabbccdd-eeff-gghh-iijj-kkllmmnnoopp": Data1 (u32), Data2, Data3 (u16)
# little endian, Data4 as written.
pub fn guid_bytes(t: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDevice
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 36 or cs[8] != "-" or cs[13] != "-" or cs[18] != "-" or cs[23] != "-"
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    var v: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 36 bound 64
        if i == 8 or i == 13 or i == 18 or i == 23
            i += 1
            continue
        let a = hexv(&cs[i])
        let b = hexv(&cs[i + 1])
        if a < 0 or b < 0
            fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
        v.push(a * 16 + b)
        i += 2
    return [v[3], v[2], v[1], v[0], v[5], v[4], v[7], v[6], v[8], v[9], v[10], v[11], v[12], v[13], v[14], v[15]]

# Registry text (upper case, as UEFI writes GUIDs) of 16 GUID bytes.
pub fn guid_text(b: &List[i64]) -> text ! BadDevice
    if b.len() != 16
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    let o = [b[3], b[2], b[1], b[0], b[5], b[4], b[7], b[6], b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11], b[12], b[13], b[14], b[15]]
    var s = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if i == 4 or i == 6 or i == 8 or i == 10
            s = s + "-"
        s = s + hex2(o[i])
        i += 1
    return s.upper()

pub struct UartCfg
    data: i64
    parity: text
    stop: i64

fn parity_bit(v: i64, data: i64, pk: &text) -> i64
    var ones: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data bound 8
        ones += (v >> i) & 1
        i += 1
    if pk == "E"
        return ones & 1
    if pk == "O"
        return 1 - (ones & 1)
    if pk == "M"
        return 1
    return 0

# The line levels of one frame: 0 start bit, data LSB first, parity
# ("N" none, "E" even, "O" odd, "M" mark, "S" space), stop bits at 1.
pub fn uart_frame(v: i64, c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [0]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < c.data bound 8
        o.push((v >> i) & 1)
        i += 1
    if c.parity != "N"
        o.push(parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity))
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < c.stop bound 2
        o.push(1)
        s += 1
    return o

# Decode frames from line levels (idle 1 between frames): each value, or
# -1 for a framing error (a stop bit at 0) and -2 for a parity error.
pub fn uart_decode(line: &List[i64], c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    let flen = 1 + c.data + (if c.parity == "N" then 0 else 1) + c.stop
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < line.len() bound 16777216
        if line[i] == 1
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + flen as usize > line.len()
            break
        var v: i64 = 0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < c.data bound 8
            v = v | (line[i + 1 + k as usize] << k)
            k += 1
        var res = v
        var p = i + 1 + c.data as usize
        if c.parity != "N"
            if line[p] != parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity)
                res = -2
            p += 1
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < c.stop bound 2
            if line[p + s as usize] != 1
                res = -1
            s += 1
        out.push(res)
        i += flen as usize
    return out

pub fn uart_divisor(baud: i64) -> i64
    if baud <= 0 or 115200 % baud != 0
        return -1
    return 115200 / baud

pub struct Field
    name: text
    lsb: i64
    width: i64
    access: text

fn mask(f: &Field) -> i64 = ((1 << f.width) - 1) << f.lsb

pub fn field_get(reg: i64, f: &Field) -> i64 = (reg >> f.lsb) & ((1 << f.width) - 1)

# The register value after a software write of v to field f, given the
# current value: read-only fields keep their bits; for a write-1-to-clear
# field ("w1c") the written ones clear bits and the others stay.
pub fn field_set(reg: i64, f: &Field, v: i64) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if v < 0 or v >= (1 << f.width)
        fail BadDevice(why: "value does not fit the field")
    if f.access == "ro"
        fail BadDevice(why: "read-only field")
    if f.access == "w1c"
        return reg & ~(v << f.lsb)
    return (reg & ~mask(f)) | (v << f.lsb)

# Fields must not overlap and must fit the register width.
pub fn fields_ok(fs: &List[Field], width: i64) -> bool
    var used: i64 = 0
    for f in fs
        if f.width < 1 or f.lsb < 0 or f.lsb + f.width > width
            return false
        if used & mask(&f) != 0
            return false
        used = used | mask(&f)
    return true

const HEX: text = "0123456789abcdef"

fn hexv(c: &text) -> i64
    let d = HEX.chars()
    let l = c.lower()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if d[i as usize] == l
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

fn hex2(b: i64) -> text
    let d = HEX.chars()
    return d[((b >> 4) & 15) as usize] + d[(b & 15) as usize]

# The 16 bytes of an EFI_GUID in memory from its registry text
# "aabbccdd-eeff-gghh-iijj-kkllmmnnoopp": Data1 (u32), Data2, Data3 (u16)
# little endian, Data4 as written.
pub fn guid_bytes(t: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDevice
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 36 or cs[8] != "-" or cs[13] != "-" or cs[18] != "-" or cs[23] != "-"
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    var v: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 36 bound 64
        if i == 8 or i == 13 or i == 18 or i == 23
            i += 1
            continue
        let a = hexv(&cs[i])
        let b = hexv(&cs[i + 1])
        if a < 0 or b < 0
            fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
        v.push(a * 16 + b)
        i += 2
    return [v[3], v[2], v[1], v[0], v[5], v[4], v[7], v[6], v[8], v[9], v[10], v[11], v[12], v[13], v[14], v[15]]

# Registry text (upper case, as UEFI writes GUIDs) of 16 GUID bytes.
pub fn guid_text(b: &List[i64]) -> text ! BadDevice
    if b.len() != 16
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    let o = [b[3], b[2], b[1], b[0], b[5], b[4], b[7], b[6], b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11], b[12], b[13], b[14], b[15]]
    var s = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if i == 4 or i == 6 or i == 8 or i == 10
            s = s + "-"
        s = s + hex2(o[i])
        i += 1
    return s.upper()

pub fn status_value(name: &text) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if name == "SUCCESS"
        return 0
    var i: i64 = 1
    for e in STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if e == name and e != "-"
            return MAX_BIT | i
        i += 1
    i = 1
    for w in STATUS_WARNINGS.split(" ")
        if w == name
            return i
        i += 1
    fail BadDevice(why: "unknown status")

    if v == 0

    let code = v & 9223372036854775807
    if v < 0
        let es = STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if code >= 1 and code <= es.len() as i64 and es[(code - 1) as usize] != "-"

        return ""
    let ws = STATUS_WARNINGS.split(" ")
    if code <= ws.len() as i64

    return ""

#    (UefiMultiPhase.h), variable names (Boot####);

#    byte of a message, 10-bit addressing, SMBus PEC (CRC-8 as
#    i2c-core-smbus.c computes it) and embedded-hal style transactions;
#  - SPI: the spidev mode bits (uapi spi.h), clock idle level and edges
#    per mode, word bit order;

#    parity, 1 or 2 stop bits), decode with framing and parity errors,

#  - register maps: fields read and written by offset and width, with
#    read-only and write-1-to-clear fields;
#  - Sandbox v0.1 device classes and the least tier a grant needs.

error BadDevice(why: text)

const HEX: text = "0123456789abcdef"

fn hexv(c: &text) -> i64
    let d = HEX.chars()
    let l = c.lower()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if d[i as usize] == l
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

fn hex2(b: i64) -> text
    let d = HEX.chars()
    return d[((b >> 4) & 15) as usize] + d[(b & 15) as usize]

# ---------------- UEFI ----------------

# "aabbccdd-eeff-gghh-iijj-kkllmmnnoopp": Data1 (u32), Data2, Data3 (u16)
# little endian, Data4 as written.
pub fn guid_bytes(t: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDevice
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 36 or cs[8] != "-" or cs[13] != "-" or cs[18] != "-" or cs[23] != "-"
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    var v: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 36 bound 64
        if i == 8 or i == 13 or i == 18 or i == 23
            i += 1
            continue

        let b = hexv(&cs[i + 1])

pub fn guid_text(b: &List[i64]) -> text ! BadDevice

    let o = [b[3], b[2], b[1], b[0], b[5], b[4], b[7], b[6], b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11], b[12], b[13], b[14], b[15]]

    var i: usize = 0

    for e in STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if e == name and e != "-"

    i = 1
    for w in STATUS_WARNINGS.split(" ")
        if w == name

        i += 1

        return ""

    return ""

const MEMORY_TYPES: text = "EfiReservedMemoryType EfiLoaderCode EfiLoaderData EfiBootServicesCode EfiBootServicesData EfiRuntimeServicesCode EfiRuntimeServicesData EfiConventionalMemory EfiUnusableMemory EfiACPIReclaimMemory EfiACPIMemoryNVS EfiMemoryMappedIO EfiMemoryMappedIOPortSpace EfiPalCode EfiPersistentMemory EfiUnacceptedMemoryType EfiMaxMemoryType"

    var i: i64 = 0

    return -1

pub fn i2c_addr_valid_strict(addr: i64) -> bool = addr >= 8 and addr <= 119

pub fn i2c_addr_byte(addr: i64, flags: i64) -> i64 = ((addr << 1) | (flags & I2C_M_RD)) & 255

pub fn i2c_ten_bit_bytes(addr: i64, read: bool) -> List[i64] = [240 | ((addr >> 7) & 6) | (if read then 1 else 0), addr & 255]

pub fn smbus_pec(crc: i64, bytes: &List[i64]) -> i64
    var c = crc

pub struct I2cMsg
    addr: i64
    flags: i64
    data: List[i64]

pub fn smbus_msgs_pec(msgs: &List[I2cMsg]) -> i64

pub struct UartCfg
    data: i64
    parity: text
    stop: i64

    var ones: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data bound 8
        ones += (v >> i) & 1
        i += 1
    if pk == "E"
        return ones & 1
    if pk == "O"
        return 1 - (ones & 1)
    if pk == "M"
        return 1
    return 0

# ("N" none, "E" even, "O" odd, "M" mark, "S" space), stop bits at 1.
pub fn uart_frame(v: i64, c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [0]
    var i: i64 = 0

        o.push((v >> i) & 1)
        i += 1
    if c.parity != "N"
        o.push(parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity))
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < c.stop bound 2
        o.push(1)
        s += 1
    return o

# -1 for a framing error (a stop bit at 0) and -2 for a parity error.
pub fn uart_decode(line: &List[i64], c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    let flen = 1 + c.data + (if c.parity == "N" then 0 else 1) + c.stop
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < line.len() bound 16777216
        if line[i] == 1
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + flen as usize > line.len()
            break

        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < c.data bound 8
            v = v | (line[i + 1 + k as usize] << k)
            k += 1

        var p = i + 1 + c.data as usize
        if c.parity != "N"
            if line[p] != parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity)
                res = -2
            p += 1
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < c.stop bound 2
            if line[p + s as usize] != 1
                res = -1
            s += 1
        out.push(res)
        i += flen as usize
    return out

# base); -1 when the rate is not an exact divisor.
pub fn uart_divisor(baud: i64) -> i64
    if baud <= 0 or 115200 % baud != 0
        return -1
    return 115200 / baud

pub struct Field
    name: text
    lsb: i64
    width: i64
    access: text

fn mask(f: &Field) -> i64 = ((1 << f.width) - 1) << f.lsb

pub fn field_get(reg: i64, f: &Field) -> i64 = (reg >> f.lsb) & ((1 << f.width) - 1)

# The register value after a software write of v to field f, given the
# current value: read-only fields keep their bits; for a write-1-to-clear
# field ("w1c") the written ones clear bits and the others stay.
pub fn field_set(reg: i64, f: &Field, v: i64) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if v < 0 or v >= (1 << f.width)
        fail BadDevice(why: "value does not fit the field")
    if f.access == "ro"
        fail BadDevice(why: "read-only field")
    if f.access == "w1c"
        return reg & ~(v << f.lsb)
    return (reg & ~mask(f)) | (v << f.lsb)

# Fields must not overlap and must fit the register width.
pub fn fields_ok(fs: &List[Field], width: i64) -> bool
    var used: i64 = 0
    for f in fs
        if f.width < 1 or f.lsb < 0 or f.lsb + f.width > width
            return false
        if used & mask(&f) != 0
            return false
        used = used | mask(&f)
    return true

pub const DEVICE_CLASSES: text = "Cpu Simd Gpu Npu Tpu Lpu Photonic Quantum"

# Sandbox v0.1 5.1: the least tier (0 for S0 .. 7) a grant of this class
# needs: Cpu and Simd none beyond S0, any other class S2, direct
# assignment (passthrough) S5, a confidential-compute device S6. -1 for
# an unknown class.
pub fn grant_tier(class: &text, passthrough: bool, confidential: bool) -> i64
    if index_of(&DEVICE_CLASSES, class) < 0
        return -1
    var t: i64 = 0
    if class != "Cpu" and class != "Simd"
        t = 2
    if passthrough
        t = 5
    if confidential
        t = 6
    return t

module os.env

# Arguments and environment (survey M35), pure. A program never reads the
# process environment directly: the host admits one snapshot (argv and
# the variables the grant makes visible) as a logged event, and replay
# reads that event. This module holds what a program does with it:
# entry parsing and lookup with POSIX and Windows rules, pure updates for
# a child's environment, the grant filter and canonical form of a
# snapshot, shell-style expansion as Go's os.Expand defines it, and the
# Windows command line codec (CommandLineToArgvW rules as Rust's std
# parses them, and Rust's quoting for CreateProcessW).

error BadEnv(why: text)

pub struct Var
key: text
value: text

pub struct Snapshot
argv: List[text]
vars: List[Var]

fn sub(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text
var o = ""
var i = lo
while i < hi and i < cs.len() bound 16777216
o = o + cs[i]
i += 1
return o

# One "KEY=VALUE" entry. POSIX splits at the first "="; Windows starts the
# search at the second character, so "=C:=C:\\x" has key "=C:" (the
# per-drive current directories). An entry without "=" is a key with an
# empty value.
pub fn parse_entry(e: &text, win: bool) -> Var
let cs = e.chars()
var i: usize = if win and cs.len() > 0 then 1 else 0
while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
if cs[i] == "="
return Var(key: sub(&cs, 0, i), value: sub(&cs, i + 1, cs.len()))
i += 1
return Var(key: copy(e), value: "")

pub fn parse_environ(es: &[text], win: bool) -> List[Var]
var o: List[Var] = []
for e in es
o.push(parse_entry(&e, win))
return o

pub fn entry(v: &Var) -> text = v.key + "=" + v.value

fn upper_ascii(t: &text) -> text = t.upper()

fn same_key(a: &text, b: &text, win: bool) -> bool = if win then upper_ascii(a) == upper_ascii(b) else a == b

# The first matching entry wins (glibc getenv, Go's syscall.Getenv,
# GetEnvironmentVariableW on a block). Windows keys compare without case
# (ASCII here; the host supplies the full Windows upper-case table).
pub fn lookup(vs: &[Var], key: &text, win: bool) -> text?
for v in vs
if same_key(&v.key, key, win)
return some(copy(v.value))
return none

pub fn getenv(vs: &[Var], key: &text, win: bool) -> text = lookup(vs, key, win).or("")

pub fn valid_key(key: &text, win: bool) -> bool
let cs = key.chars()
if cs.len() == 0
return false
var i: usize = if win then 1 else 0
while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
if cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "\u{0}"
return false
i += 1
return cs[0] != "\u{0}"

# and unset; a pure update for building a child's environment.
pub fn setenv(vs: &[Var], key: &text, value: &text, win: bool) -> List[Var] ! BadEnv

o.push(Var(key: copy(v.key), value: copy(value)))

else
o.push(copy(v))
if not done
o.push(Var(key: copy(key), value: copy(value)))
return o

var o: List[Var] = []
for v in vs
if not same_key(&v.key, key, win)
o.push(copy(v))
return o

# Canonical form of a snapshot for the log: only the granted keys
# (exact names; all keys when `all`), one entry per key (the first), sorted
# by key bytes. Two hosts with the same environment admit the same event.
pub fn snapshot(argv: &[text], es: &[text], granted: &[text], all: bool, win: bool) -> Snapshot

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
# - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
# preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
# position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
# with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
# renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
# preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
# not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
# holes and timestamps are not modelled.
# - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
# names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size usize]) no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
dir: bool
data: List[text]
parent: i64

pub struct Ent
dir: i64
name: text
nd: i64

pub struct Desc
nd: i64
pos: i64
rd: bool
wr: bool
app: bool
live: bool

pub struct Fs
nodes: List[Node]
ents: List[Ent]
descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64

if e.dir == d and e.name == name
return e.nd
return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
for e in fs.ents
if e.dir == d
return false
return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
dir: i64
last: text
nd: i64
slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]

for c in path.split("/")
if c != ""
o.push(c)
return o

let wr = flags.contains("w")
let cr = flags.contains("c")
let ex = flags.contains("x")

return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

if w.last == ".."

return true

return false

x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
return x

let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)

while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 4096

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where

    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")

    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64
            data[p as usize] = c
        else
            data.push(c)
        p += 1

    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
    return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr or len < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o: List[text] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len bound 16777216
        o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")
        i += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
    return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
    return true

    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")

        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)

    if w.last == ".."

    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")

    if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)

    while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return x

    let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)

pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64
            data[p as usize] = c
        else
            data.push(c)
        p += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = data
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
    return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr or len < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o: List[text] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len bound 16777216
        o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")
        i += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
    return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
    return true

pub fn unlink_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

pub fn rmdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if w.last == "."
        fail bad("invalid")
    if w.last == ".."
        fail bad("not-empty")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)
        fail bad("not-empty")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

# a is d or a directory above d.
fn above(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> bool
    var x = d
    while x >= 0 bound 4096
        if x == a
            return true
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return false

# The child of a on the way down to d (a strictly above d).
fn child_towards(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> i64
    var x = d
    while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return x

pub fn rename_at(fs: &mut Fs, src: &text, dst: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let o = try resolve(fs, src, false)
    let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)
    if not named(&o) or not named(&n)
        fail bad("busy")
    if o.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    let isdir = fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].dir
    if not isdir and (o.slash or n.slash)
        fail bad("not-directory")
    # lock_rename's trap: the entry under the common ancestor
    if o.dir != n.dir
        if above(fs, o.dir, n.dir) and child_towards(fs, o.dir, n.dir) == o.nd
            fail bad("invalid")
        if above(fs, n.dir, o.dir) and child_towards(fs, n.dir, o.dir) == n.nd
            fail bad("not-empty")
    if o.nd == n.nd
        return true
    if n.nd >= 0
        let tdir = fs.nodes[n.nd as usize].dir
        if isdir and not tdir
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if not isdir and tdir
            fail bad("is-directory")
        if tdir and not is_empty(fs, n.nd)
            fail bad("not-empty")
        drop_ent(fs, n.dir, &n.last)
    drop_ent(fs, o.dir, &o.last)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: n.dir, name: copy(n.last), nd: o.nd))
    if isdir
        fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].parent = n.dir
    return true

# stat: "d" for a directory, else "f" and the size.
pub fn stat_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> text ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        return "d"
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    return "f" + fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].data.len().tostr()

# UTF-8 byte order (Linux sorts names as bytes).
fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 4096
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# The entry names of a directory, sorted (without "." and "..").
pub fn list_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> List[text] ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    var o: List[text] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == w.nd
            var k = o.len()
            o.push(copy(e.name))
            while k > 0 and text_lt(&o[k], &o[k - 1]) bound 4096
                let t = copy(o[k])
                o[k] = copy(o[k - 1])
                o[k - 1] = t
                k -= 1
    return o

# ---------------- scripts ----------------

fn num(s: &text) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in s.chars()
        v = v * 10 + (c[0] as i64 - 48)
    return v

fn op1(fs: &mut Fs, a: &List[text]) -> text ! FsErr
    let k = copy(a[0])
    if k == "mkdir"
        let _ = try mkdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "open"
        let h = try open_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "h" + h.tostr()
    if k == "read"
        let s = try read(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "=" + s
    if k == "write"
        let _ = try write(fs, num(&a[1]), &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "seek"
        let _ = try seek(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "trunc"
        let _ = try truncate(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "close"
        let _ = try close(fs, num(&a[1]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "unlink"
        let _ = try unlink_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rmdir"
        let _ = try rmdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rename"
        let _ = try rename_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "stat"
        return try stat_at(fs, &a[1])
    if k == "list"
        let l = try list_at(fs, &a[1])
        return ":" + ",".join(l)
    fail bad("invalid")

# Run a script of ";"-separated operations on a fresh filesystem; the
# outcome of each (ok, hN, =data, d, fN, :names or an error-code), joined by ";".
pub fn script(s: text) -> text
    var fs = fs_new()
    var out: List[text] = []
    for line in s.split(";")
        let a = line.split(" ")
        out.push(op1(&mut fs, &a) catch |e| e.code)
    return ";".join(out)

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes or timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0

    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64
            data[p as usize] = c
        else
            data.push(c)
        p += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = data
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64
            data[p as usize] = c
        else
            data.push(c)
        p += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = data
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
    return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr or len < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o: List[text] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len bound 16777216
        o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")
        i += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
    return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
    return true

pub fn unlink_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

pub fn rmdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if w.last == "."
        fail bad("invalid")
    if w.last == ".."
        fail bad("not-empty")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)
        fail bad("not-empty")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

fn above(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> bool
    var x = d
    while x >= 0 bound 4096
        if x == a
            return true
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent

    var x = d
    while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return x

pub fn rename_at(fs: &mut Fs, src: &text, dst: &text) -> bool ! FsErr

    let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)

        fail bad("busy")

    return true

pub fn stat_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> text ! FsErr

    if w.nd < 0
