#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64
            data[p as usize] = c
        else
            data.push(c)
        p += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = data
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
    return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr or len < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o: List[text] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len bound 16777216
        o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")
        i += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
    return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
    return true

pub fn unlink_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

pub fn rmdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if w.last == "."
        fail bad("invalid")
    if w.last == ".."
        fail bad("not-empty")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)
        fail bad("not-empty")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

# a is d or a directory above d.
fn above(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> bool
    var x = d
    while x >= 0 bound 4096
        if x == a
            return true
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return false

# The child of a on the way down to d (a strictly above d).
fn child_towards(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> i64
    var x = d
    while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return x

pub fn rename_at(fs: &mut Fs, src: &text, dst: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let o = try resolve(fs, src, false)
    let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)
    if not named(&o) or not named(&n)
        fail bad("busy")
    if o.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    let isdir = fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].dir
    if not isdir and (o.slash or n.slash)
        fail bad("not-directory")
    # lock_rename's trap: the entry under the common ancestor
    if o.dir != n.dir
        if above(fs, o.dir, n.dir) and child_towards(fs, o.dir, n.dir) == o.nd
            fail bad("invalid")
        if above(fs, n.dir, o.dir) and child_towards(fs, n.dir, o.dir) == n.nd
            fail bad("not-empty")
    if o.nd == n.nd
        return true
    if n.nd >= 0
        let tdir = fs.nodes[n.nd as usize].dir
        if isdir and not tdir
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if not isdir and tdir
            fail bad("is-directory")
        if tdir and not is_empty(fs, n.nd)
            fail bad("not-empty")
        drop_ent(fs, n.dir, &n.last)
    drop_ent(fs, o.dir, &o.last)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: n.dir, name: copy(n.last), nd: o.nd))
    if isdir
        fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].parent = n.dir
    return true

# stat: "d" for a directory, else "f" and the size.
pub fn stat_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> text ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        return "d"
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    return "f" + fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].data.len().tostr()

# UTF-8 byte order (Linux sorts names as bytes).
fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 4096
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# The entry names of a directory, sorted (without "." and "..").
pub fn list_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> List[text] ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    var o: List[text] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == w.nd
            var k = o.len()
            o.push(copy(e.name))
            while k > 0 and text_lt(&o[k], &o[k - 1]) bound 4096
                let t = copy(o[k])
                o[k] = copy(o[k - 1])
                o[k - 2] = t
                k -= 1
    return o

# ---------------- scripts ----------------

fn num(s: &text) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in s.chars()
        v = v * 10 + (c[0] as i64 - 48)
    return v

fn op1(fs: &mut Fs, a: &List[text]) -> text ! FsErr
    let k = copy(a[0])
    if k == "mkdir"
        let _ = try mkdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "open"
        let h = try open_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "h" + h.tostr()
    if k == "read"
        let s = try read(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "=" + s
    if k == "write"
        let _ = try write(fs, num(&a[1]), &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "seek"
        let _ = try seek(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "trunc"
        let _ = try truncate(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "close"
        let _ = try close(fs, num(&a[1]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "unlink"
        let _ = try unlink_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rmdir"
        let _ = try rmdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rename"
        let _ = try rename_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "stat"
        return try stat_at(fs, &a[1])
    if k == "list"
        let l = try list_at(fs, &a[1])
        return ":" + ",".join(l)
    fail bad("invalid")

# Run a script of ";"-separated operations on a fresh filesystem; the
# outcome of each (ok, hN, =data, d, fN, :names or an error-code), joined by ";".
pub fn script(s: text) -> text
    var fs = fs_new()
    var out: List[text] = []
    for line in s.split(";")
        let a = line.split(" ")
        out.push(op1(&mut fs, &a) catch |e| e.code)
    return ";".join(out)

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")

#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.

#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64

        else

    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
    return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr or len < 0
        fail bad("invalid")

    var o: List[text] = []
    var i: i64 = 0

        o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")
        i += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
    return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
    return true

pub fn unlink_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

pub fn rmdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if w.last == "."
        fail bad("invalid")
    if w.last == ".."
        fail bad("not-empty")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)
        fail bad("not-empty")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

# a is d or a directory above d.
fn above(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> bool
    var x = d
    while x >= 0 bound 4096
        if x == a
            return true
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return false

fn child_towards(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> i64
    var x = d
    while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return x

    let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)

        fail bad("busy")

        fail bad("no-entry")

    if not isdir and (o.slash or n.slash)
        fail bad("not-directory")

    if o.dir != n.dir
        if above(fs, o.dir, n.dir) and child_towards(fs, o.dir, n.dir) == o.nd
            fail bad("invalid")
        if above(fs, n.dir, o.dir) and child_towards(fs, n.dir, o.dir) == n.nd
            fail bad("not-empty")

        return true

        let tdir = fs.nodes[n.nd as usize].dir

            fail bad("not-directory")
        if not isdir and tdir
            fail bad("is-directory")

            fail bad("not-empty")

    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: n.dir, name: copy(n.last), nd: o.nd))
    if isdir
        fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].parent = n.dir
    return true

pub fn stat_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> text ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        return "d"
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    return "f" + fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].data.len().tostr()

# UTF-8 byte order (Linux sorts names as bytes).
fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 4096
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# The entry names of a directory, sorted (without "." and "..").
pub fn list_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> List[text] ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    var o: List[text] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == w.nd
            var k = o.len()
            o.push(copy(e.name))

                let t = copy(o[k])
                o[k] = copy(o[k - 1])
                o[k - 1] = t
                k -= 1
    return o

# ---------------- scripts ----------------

fn num(s: &text) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in s.chars()
        v = v * 10 + (c[0] as i64 - 48)
    return v

fn op1(fs: &mut Fs, a: &List[text]) -> text ! FsErr
    let k = copy(a[0])
    if k == "mkdir"
        let _ = try mkdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "open"
        let h = try open_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "h" + h.tostr()
    if k == "read"
        let s = try read(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "=" + s
    if k == "write"
        let _ = try write(fs, num(&a[1]), &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "seek"
        let _ = try seek(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "trunc"
        let _ = try truncate(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "close"
        let _ = try close(fs, num(&a[1]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "unlink"
        let _ = try unlink_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rmdir"
        let _ = try rmdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rename"
        let _ = try rename_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "stat"
        return try stat_at(fs, &a[1])
    if k == "list"
        let l = try list_at(fs, &a[1])
        return ":" + ",".join(l)
    fail bad("invalid")

# Run a script of ";"-separated operations on a fresh filesystem; the
# outcome of each (ok, hN, =data, d, fN, :names or an error-code), joined by ";".
pub fn script(s: text) -> text
    var fs = fs_new()
    var out: List[text] = []
    for line in s.split(";")
        let a = line.split(" ")
        out.push(op1(&mut fs, &a) catch |e| e.code)
    return ";".join(out)

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64

    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")

    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")

    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash

        if tr

    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

var all = true
for c in head.chars()
if c != "/"
all = false
return if head != "" and not all then rstrip_seps(&head, false) else head

pub fn posix_splitext(p: &text) -> Pair = splitext_any(p, false)

pub fn posix_normpath(p: &text) -> text
if p == ""
return "."
let r = posix_splitroot(p)
let init = copy(r.root)
var out: List[text] = []
for c in split_on(&r.tail, "/")
if c == "" or c == "."
continue
if c != ".." or (init == "" and out.len() == 0) or (out.len() > 0 and out[out.len() - 1] == "..")
out.push(copy(c))
elif out.len() > 0
let _ = out.pop()
let o = init + join_with(&out, "/")
return if o == "" then "." else o

pub fn posix_abspath(p: &text, cwd: &text) -> text
if p.startswith("/")
return posix_normpath(p)
let ps: List[text] = [copy(cwd), copy(p)]
let j = posix_join(&ps)
return posix_normpath(&j)

# Relative path from start to path, with cwd standing for os.getcwd().
pub fn posix_relpath(path: &text, start: &text, cwd: &text) -> text ! BadPath

fail BadPath(why: "no path specified")
let sa = posix_abspath(start, cwd)
let pa = posix_abspath(path, cwd)

let t = strip_lead(&pa)
let sl = if s == "" then [] else split_on(&s, "/")
let tl = if t == "" then [] else split_on(&t, "/")
var i: usize = 0
while i < sl.len() and i < tl.len() and sl[i] == tl[i] bound 16777216
i += 1
var rel: List[text] = []
var k = i
while k < sl.len() bound 16777216
rel.push("..")
k += 1
k = i
while k < tl.len() bound 16777216
rel.push(copy(tl[k]))
k += 1
return if rel.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rel, "/")

fn strip_lead(t: &text) -> text
let cs = t.chars()
var i: usize = 0
while i < cs.len() and cs[i] == "/" bound 16777216
i += 1
return sub(&cs, i, cs.len())

fn comps_clean(t: &text, sep: text) -> List[text]
var o: List[text] = []
for c in split_on(t, sep)
if c != "" and c != "."
o.push(copy(c))
return o

fn list_lt(a: &[text], b: &[text]) -> bool
var i: usize = 0
while i < a.len() and i < b.len() bound 16777216
if a[i] != b[i]
return text_lt(&a[i], &b[i])
i += 1
return a.len() < b.len()

fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
let x = cps(a)
let y = cps(b)
var i: usize = 0
while i < x.len() and i < y.len() bound 16777216
if x[i] != y[i]
return x[i] < y[i]
i += 1
return x.len() < y.len()

# Code points of UTF-8 text (code point order is Python's string order).
fn cps(t: &text) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
let b = t[i] as i64
if b < 128
o.push(b)
i += 1
elif b < 224
o.push((b & 31) << 6 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63))
i += 2
elif b < 240
o.push((b & 15) << 12 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[i + 2] as i64 & 63))
i += 3
else
o.push((b & 7) << 18 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (t[i + 2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[i + 3] as i64 & 63))
i += 4
return o

# Longest common prefix of the clean component lists of min and max.
fn common_of(sp: &[List[text]]) -> List[text]
var lo: usize = 0
var hi: usize = 0
var i: usize = 1
while i < sp.len() bound 16777216
if list_lt(&sp[i], &sp[lo])
lo = i
if list_lt(&sp[hi], &sp[i])
hi = i
i += 1
let a = copy(sp[lo])
let b = copy(sp[hi])
var o: List[text] = []
var k: usize = 0
while k < a.len() bound 16777216
if k >= b.len() or a[k] != b[k]
break
o.push(copy(a[k]))
k += 1
return o

pub fn posix_commonpath(ps: &[text]) -> text ! BadPath
if ps.len() == 0
fail BadPath(why: "empty")
let abs = ps[0].startswith("/")
var sp: List[List[text]] = []
for p in ps
if p.startswith("/") != abs
fail BadPath(why: "mix of absolute and relative")
sp.push(comps_clean(&p, "/"))
let c = common_of(&sp)
return (if abs then "/" else "") + join_with(&c, "/")

pub fn win_splitroot(p: &text) -> Root
let cs = p.chars()
var n: List[text] = []
for c in cs
n.push(if c == "/" then "\\" else copy(c))
if n.len() > 0 and n[0] == "\\"
if n.len() > 1 and n[1] == "\\"
let up = sub(&n, 0, 8).upper()
let start: usize = if up == "\\\\?\\UNC\\" then 8 else 2
var a = start
while a < n.len() and n[a] != "\\" bound 16777216
a += 1
if a >= n.len()
return Root(drive: copy(p), root: "", tail: "")
var b = a + 1
while b < n.len() and n[b] != "\\" bound 16777216
b += 1
if b >= n.len()
return Root(drive: copy(p), root: "", tail: "")
return Root(drive: sub(&cs, 0, b), root: sub(&cs, b, b + 1), tail: sub(&cs, b + 1, cs.len()))
return Root(drive: "", root: sub(&cs, 0, 1), tail: sub(&cs, 1, cs.len()))
if n.len() > 1 and n[1] == ":"
if n.len() > 2 and n[2] == "\\"
return Root(drive: sub(&cs, 0, 2), root: sub(&cs, 2, 3), tail: sub(&cs, 3, cs.len()))
return Root(drive: sub(&cs, 0, 2), root: "", tail: sub(&cs, 2, cs.len()))
return Root(drive: "", root: "", tail: copy(p))

pub fn win_splitdrive(p: &text) -> Pair
let r = win_splitroot(p)
return Pair(head: copy(r.drive), tail: r.root + r.tail)

pub fn win_isabs(p: &text) -> bool
let cs = p.chars()
var s: List[text] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < 3 and i < cs.len() bound 3
s.push(if cs[i] == "/" then "\\" else copy(cs[i]))
i += 1
return (s.len() >= 3 and s[1] == ":" and s[2] == "\\") or (s.len() >= 2 and s[0] == "\\" and s[1] == "\\")

# Case folding of win_normcase is ASCII only (Windows folds with the
# invariant locale table; the host owns that table).
pub fn win_normcase(p: &text) -> text = slashes_to_back(p).lower()

pub fn win_join(parts: &[text]) -> text
if parts.len() == 0
return ""
let r0 = win_splitroot(&parts[0])
var rd = copy(r0.drive)
var rr = copy(r0.root)
var rp = copy(r0.tail)
var i: usize = 1
while i < parts.len() bound 16777216
let q = win_splitroot(&parts[i])
i += 1
if q.root != ""
if q.drive != "" or rd == ""
rd = copy(q.drive)
rr = copy(q.root)
rp = copy(q.tail)
continue
elif q.drive != "" and q.drive != rd
if q.drive.lower() != rd.lower()
rd = copy(q.drive)
rr = copy(q.root)
rp = copy(q.tail)
continue
rd = copy(q.drive)
let pc = rp.chars()
if pc.len() > 0 and not is_sep(&pc[pc.len() - 1], true)
rp = rp + "\\"
rp = rp + q.tail
let dc = rd.chars()
if rp != "" and rr == "" and dc.len() > 0 and not (dc[dc.len() - 1] == ":" or is_sep(&dc[dc.len() - 1], true))

return rd + rr + rp

pub fn win_split(p: &text) -> Pair
let r = win_splitroot(p)
let cs = r.tail.chars()
var i = cs.len()
while i > 0 and not is_sep(&cs[i - 1], true) bound 16777216
i -= 1
let head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
return Pair(head: r.drive + r.root + rstrip_seps(&head, true), tail: sub(&cs, i, cs.len()))

pub fn win_basename(p: &text) -> text = win_split(p).tail
pub fn win_dirname(p: &text) -> text = win_split(p).head
pub fn win_splitext(p: &text) -> Pair = splitext_any(p, true)

pub fn win_normpath(p: &text) -> text
let q = slashes_to_back(p)
let r = win_splitroot(&q)
let prefix = r.drive + r.root
var comps = split_on(&r.tail, "\\")
var i: usize = 0
while i < comps.len() bound 16777216
if comps[i] == "" or comps[i] == "."
comps = remove_at(&comps, i, 1)
elif comps[i] == ".."
if i > 0 and comps[i - 1] != ".."
comps = remove_at(&comps, i - 1, 2)
i -= 1
elif i == 0 and r.root != ""
comps = remove_at(&comps, i, 1)
else
i += 1
else else
i += 1
if prefix == "" and comps.len() == 0
comps.push(".")
return prefix + join_with(&comps, "\\")

fn remove_at(xs: &[text], at: usize, n: usize) -> List[text]
var o: List[text] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < xs.len() bound 16777216
if i < at or i >= at + n
o.push(copy(xs[i]))
i += 1
return o

pub fn win_abspath(p: &text, cwd: &text) -> text
if win_isabs(p)
return win_normpath(p)
let ps: List[text] = [copy(cwd), copy(p)]
let j = win_join(&ps)
return win_normpath(&j)

pub fn win_relpath(path: &text, start: &text, cwd: &text) -> text ! BadPath

let sx = win_abspath(start, cwd)
let px = win_abspath(path, cwd)

while i < sl.len() and i < tl.len() and win_normcase(&sl[i]) == win_normcase(&tl[i]) bound 16777216
i += 1
var rel: List[text] = []
var k = i
while k < sl.len() bound 16777216
rel.push("..")
k += 1
k = i
while k < tl.len() bound 16777216
rel.push(copy(tl[k]))
k += 1
return if rel.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rel, "\\")

pub fn win_commonpath(ps: &[text]) -> text ! BadPath
if ps.len() == 0
fail BadPath(why: "empty")
var sp: List[List[text]] = []
let l0 = slashes_to_back(&ps[0]).lower()
let r0 = win_splitroot(&l0)
for p in ps
let lp = slashes_to_back(&p).lower()
let r = win_splitroot(&lp)
if r.drive != r0.drive
fail BadPath(why: "different drives")
if r.root != r0.root
fail BadPath(why: "mix of rooted and not rooted")
sp.push(comps_clean(&r.tail, "\\"))

let f = win_splitroot(&b0)

var k: usize = 0
while k < c.len() and k < common.len() bound 16777216
o.push(copy(common[k]))
k += 1
return f.drive + f.root + join_with(&o, "\\")

const RESERVED: text = "CON PRN AUX NUL CONIN$ CONOUT$ COM1 COM2 COM3 COM4 COM5 COM6 COM7 COM8 COM9 COM\u{b9} COM\u{b2} COM\u{b3} LPT1 LPT2 LPT3 LPT4 LPT5 LPT6 LPT7 LPT8 LPT9 LPT\u{b9} LPT\u{b2} LPT\u{b3}"

fn reserved_name(n: &text) -> bool
let cs = n.chars()
if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[cs.len() - 1] == "." or cs[cs.len() - 1] == " ")
return n != "." and n != ".."
for c in cs
if c.len_bytes() == 1 and (c[0] < 32 or c == "\"" or c == "*" or c == ":" or c == "<" or c == ">" or c == "?" or c == "|" or c == "/" or c == "\\")
return true
var stem = ""
for c in cs
if c == "."
break
stem = stem + c
let s = rstrip_spaces(&stem).upper()
return RESERVED.split(" ").contains(s)

fn rstrip_spaces(t: &text) -> text
let cs = t.chars()
var n = cs.len()
while n > 0 and cs[n - 1] == " " bound 16777216
n -= 1
return sub(&cs, 0, n)

# dot or space, wildcards, colon, control characters).
pub fn win_isreserved(p: &text) -> bool
let r = win_splitroot(p)
let bt = slashes_to_back(&r.tail)
for n in split_on(&bt, "\\")
if reserved_name(&n)

return false

# ---------------- WASI ----------------

# The components of a path relative to a granted directory: "." and empty
# components dropped, ".." taken lexically; an absolute path, or one that
# climbs above the directory, is refused (WASI ENOTCAPABLE). Symbolic
# links met on the way are resolved by the host under the same rule.
pub fn wasi_resolve(p: &text) -> List[text] ! BadPath
if p.startswith("/")
fail BadPath(why: "absolute")
var out: List[text] = []
for c in split_on(p, "/")
if c == "" or c == "."
continue
if c == ".."
if out.len() == 0
fail BadPath(why: "escapes the directory")
let _ = out.pop()
else
out.push(copy(c))
return out

pub struct Preopen
index: i64
rel: text

# The granted directory for an absolute path, as wasi-libc's
# __wasilibc_find_relpath picks it: the preopen whose components are the
# longest prefix of the path's normalized components (the later one on a
# tie), and the rest of the path relative to it ("." when equal).
pub fn wasi_preopen(preopens: &[text], p: &text) -> Preopen ! BadPath
if not p.startswith("/")
fail BadPath(why: "not absolute")
let pn = posix_normpath(p)
let pc = comps_clean(&pn, "/")
var best: i64 = -1
var blen: i64 = -1
var i: usize = 0
while i < preopens.len() bound 16777216
let qn = posix_normpath(&preopens[i])
let qc = comps_clean(&qn, "/")
var ok = preopens[i].startswith("/") and qc.len() <= pc.len()
var k: usize = 0
while ok and k < qc.len() bound 16777216
if qc[k] != pc[k]
ok = false
k += 1
if ok and qc.len() as i64 >= blen
best = i as i64
blen = qc.len() as i64
i += 1
if best < 0
fail BadPath(why: "no preopen")
var rest: List[text] = []
var k = blen as usize
while k < pc.len() bound 16777216
rest.push(copy(pc[k]))
k += 1
return Preopen(index: best, rel: if rest.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rest, "/"))

module os.path

# Path algebra (survey M34), pure and lexical: POSIX paths, Windows paths
# and WASI preopen-relative paths. The POSIX and Windows functions follow
# CPython 3.13 posixpath and ntpath exactly (the reference behind Python's
# os.path and pathlib), including POSIX's implementation-defined "//"
# root and Windows drives, UNC shares and \\?\ device paths. Nothing here
# touches a file system: symbolic links, the current directory and case
# folding of the file system are the host's (relpath takes the current
# directory as an argument; Windows case folding is ASCII here, see
# win_normcase). WASI resolution (wasi_resolve) is the lexical part of the
# preview 1 and 2 rule that a path is relative to a granted directory
# descriptor and never leaves it.

error BadPath(why: text)

pub struct Root
    drive: text
    root: text
    tail: text

pub struct Pair
    head: text
    tail: text

fn sub(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi and i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

fn cat(cs: &[text]) -> text = sub(cs, 0, cs.len())

fn rstrip_seps(t: &text, win: bool) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var n = cs.len()
    while n > 0 and (cs[n - 1] == "/" or (win and cs[n - 1] == "\\")) bound 16777216
        n -= 1
    return sub(&cs, 0, n)

fn is_sep(c: &text, win: bool) -> bool = c == "/" or (win and c == "\\")

fn split_on(t: &text, sep: text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == sep
            o.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    o.push(cur)
    return o

fn join_with(ps: &[text], sep: text) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ps.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o = o + sep
        o = o + ps[i]
        i += 1
    return o

fn slashes_to_back(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        o = o + (if c == "/" then "\\" else c)
    return o

# Splitting the extension (genericpath._splitext): the last dot after the
# last separator, unless every character before it in the name is a dot.
fn splitext_any(p: &text, win: bool) -> Pair
    let cs = p.chars()
    var s: i64 = -1
    var d: i64 = -1
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if is_sep(&cs[i], win)
            s = i as i64
        if cs[i] == "."
            d = i as i64
        i += 1
    if d > s
        var k = (s + 1) as usize
        while (k as i64) < d bound 16777216
            if cs[k] != "."
                return Pair(head: sub(&cs, 0, d as usize), tail: sub(&cs, d as usize, cs.len()))
            k += 1
    return Pair(head: copy(p), tail: "")

# ---------------- POSIX ----------------

pub fn posix_splitroot(p: &text) -> Root
    let cs = p.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0 or cs[0] != "/"
        return Root(drive: "", root: "", tail: copy(p))
    if cs.len() < 2 or cs[1] != "/" or (cs.len() > 2 and cs[2] == "/")
        return Root(drive: "", root: "/", tail: sub(&cs, 1, cs.len()))
    return Root(drive: "", root: "//", tail: sub(&cs, 2, cs.len()))

pub fn posix_isabs(p: &text) -> bool = p.startswith("/")

pub fn posix_join(parts: &[text]) -> text
    var path = ""
    var first = true
    for b in parts
        if first
            path = copy(b)
            first = false
        elif b.startswith("/") or path == ""
            path = copy(b)
        elif path.endswith("/")
            path = path + b
        else
            path = path + "/" + b
    return path

pub fn posix_split(p: &text) -> Pair
    let cs = p.chars()
    var i = cs.len()
    while i > 0 and cs[i - 1] != "/" bound 16777216
        i -= 1
    var head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
    let tail = sub(&cs, i, cs.len())
    var all = true
    for c in head.chars()
        if c != "/"
            all = false
    if head != "" and not all
        head = rstrip_seps(&head, false)
    return Pair(head: head, tail: tail)

pub fn posix_basename(p: &text) -> text = posix_split(p).tail

pub fn posix_dirname(p: &text) -> text
    let cs = p.chars()
    var i = cs.len()
    while i > 0 and cs[i - 1] != "/" bound 16777216
        i -= 1
    let head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
    var all = true
    for c in head.chars()
        if c != "/"
            all = false
    return if head != "" and not all then rstrip_seps(&head, false) else head

pub fn posix_splitext(p: &text) -> Pair = splitext_any(p, false)

pub fn posix_normpath(p: &text) -> text
    if p == ""
        return "."
    let r = posix_splitroot(p)
    let init = copy(r.root)
    var out: List[text] = []
    for c in split_on(&r.tail, "/")
        if c == "" or c == "."
            continue
        if c != ".." or (init == "" and out.len() == 0) or (out.len() > 0 and out[out.len() - 1] == "..")
            out.push(copy(c))
        elif out.len() > 0
            let _ = out.pop()
    let o = init + join_with(&out, "/")
    return if o == "" then "." else o

pub fn posix_abspath(p: &text, cwd: &text) -> text
    if p.startswith("/")
        return posix_normpath(p)
    let ps: List[text] = [copy(cwd), copy(p)]
    let j = posix_join(&ps)
    return posix_normpath(&j)

# Relative path from start to path, with cwd standing for os.getcwd().
pub fn posix_relpath(path: &text, start: &text, cwd: &text) -> text ! BadPath

        fail BadPath(why: "no path specified")

    let pa = posix_abspath(path, cwd)

    let t = strip_lead(&pa)

    let tl = if t == "" then [] else split_on(&t, "/")

    while i < sl.len() and i < tl.len() and sl[i] == tl[i] bound 16777216
        i += 1

    var k = i
    while k < sl.len() bound 16777216
        rel.push("..")
        k += 1
    k = i
    while k < tl.len() bound 16777216
        rel.push(copy(tl[k]))
        k += 1
    return if rel.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rel, "/")

fn strip_lead(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] == "/" bound 16777216
        i += 1
    return sub(&cs, i, cs.len())

fn comps_clean(t: &text, sep: text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in split_on(t, sep)
        if c != "" and c != "."
            o.push(copy(c))

fn list_lt(a: &[text], b: &[text]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0

fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    let x = cps(a)
    let y = cps(b)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < x.len() and i < y.len() bound 16777216
        if x[i] != y[i]

# Code points of UTF-8 text (code point order is Python's string order).

        if b < 128

# Longest common prefix of the clean component lists of min and max.
fn common_of(sp: &[List[text]]) -> List[text]

pub fn win_join(parts: &[text]) -> text

        k += 1

    let cs = t.chars()

        n -= 1

    let r = win_splitroot(p)

# ---------------- WASI ----------------

# The components of a path relative to a granted directory: "." and empty

pub fn wasi_resolve(p: &text) -> List[text] ! BadPath
    if p.startswith("/")
        fail BadPath(why: "absolute")
    var out: List[text] = []
    for c in split_on(p, "/")
        if c == "" or c == "."
            continue
        if c == ".."
            if out.len() == 0
                fail BadPath(why: "escapes the directory")
            let _ = out.pop()
        else
            out.push(copy(c))
    return out

pub fn wasi_preopen(preopens: &[text], p: &text) -> Preopen ! BadPath

        fail BadPath(why: "not absolute")

    var blen: i64 = -1
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < preopens.len() bound 16777216
        let qn = posix_normpath(&preopens[i])
        let qc = comps_clean(&qn, "/")
        var ok = preopens[i].startswith("/") and qc.len() <= pc.len()
        var k: usize = 0
        while ok and k < qc.len() bound 16777216
            if qc[k] != pc[k]
                ok = false
            k += 1

            best = i as i64
            blen = qc.len() as i64
        i += 1
    if best < 0
        fail BadPath(why: "no preopen")
    var rest: List[text] = []
    var k = blen as usize
    while k < pc.len() bound 16777216
        rest.push(copy(pc[k]))
        k += 1
    return Preopen(index: best, rel: if rest.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rest, "/"))

module os.path

# Path algebra (survey M34), pure and lexical: POSIX paths, Windows paths
# and WASI preopen-relative paths. The POSIX and Windows functions follow
# CPython 3.13 posixpath and ntpath exactly (the reference behind Python's
# os.path and pathlib), including POSIX's implementation-defined "//"
# root and Windows drives, UNC shares and \\?\ device paths. Nothing here
# touches a file system: symbolic links, the current directory and case
# folding of the file system are the host's (relpath takes the current
# directory as an argument; Windows case folding is ASCII here, see
# win_normcase). WASI resolution (wasi_resolve) is the lexical part of the
# preview 1 and 2 rule that a path is relative to a granted directory
# descriptor and never leaves it.

error BadPath(why: text)

pub struct Root
    drive: text
    root: text
    tail: text

pub struct Pair
    head: text
    tail: text

fn sub(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi and i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

fn cat(cs: &[text]) -> text = sub(cs, 0, cs.len())

fn rstrip_seps(t: &text, win: bool) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var n = cs.len()
    while n > 0 and (cs[n - 1] == "/" or (win and cs[n - 1] == "\\")) bound 16777216
        n -= 1
    return sub(&cs, 0, n)

fn is_sep(c: &text, win: bool) -> bool = c == "/" or (win and c == "\\")

fn split_on(t: &text, sep: text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == sep
            o.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    o.push(cur)
    return o

fn join_with(ps: &[text], sep: text) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ps.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o = o + sep
        o = o + ps[i]
        i += 1
    return o

fn slashes_to_back(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        o = o + (if c == "/" then "\\" else c)
    return o

# Splitting the extension (genericpath._splitext): the last dot after the
# last separator, unless every character before it in the name is a dot.
fn splitext_any(p: &text, win: bool) -> Pair
    let cs = p.chars()
    var s: i64 = -1
    var d: i64 = -1
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if is_sep(&cs[i], win)
            s = i as i64
        if cs[i] == "."
            d = i as i64
        i += 1
    if d > s
        var k = (s + 1) as usize
        while (k as i64) < d bound 16777216
            if cs[k] != "."
                return Pair(head: sub(&cs, 0, d as usize), tail: sub(&cs, d as usize, cs.len()))
            k += 1
    return Pair(head: copy(p), tail: "")

# ---------------- POSIX ----------------

pub fn posix_splitroot(p: &text) -> Root
    let cs = p.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0 or cs[0] != "/"
        return Root(drive: "", root: "", tail: copy(p))
    if cs.len() < 2 or cs[1] != "/" or (cs.len() > 2 and cs[2] == "/")
        return Root(drive: "", root: "/", tail: sub(&cs, 1, cs.len()))
    return Root(drive: "", root: "//", tail: sub(&cs, 2, cs.len()))

pub fn posix_isabs(p: &text) -> bool = p.startswith("/")

pub fn posix_join(parts: &[text]) -> text
    var path = ""
    var first = true
    for b in parts
        if first
            path = copy(b)
            first = false
        elif b.startswith("/") or path == ""
            path = copy(b)
        elif path.endswith("/")
            path = path + b
        else
            path = path + "/" + b
    return path

pub fn posix_split(p: &text) -> Pair
    let cs = p.chars()
    var i = cs.len()
    while i > 0 and cs[i - 1] != "/" bound 16777216
        i -= 1
    var head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
    let tail = sub(&cs, i, cs.len())
    var all = true
    for c in head.chars()
        if c != "/"
            all = false
    if head != "" and not all
        head = rstrip_seps(&head, false)
    return Pair(head: head, tail: tail)

pub fn posix_basename(p: &text) -> text = posix_split(p).tail

pub fn posix_dirname(p: &text) -> text
    let cs = p.chars()
    var i = cs.len()
    while i > 0 and cs[i - 1] != "/" bound 16777216
        i -= 1
    let head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
    var all = true
    for c in head.chars()
        if c != "/"
            all = false
    return if head != "" and not all then rstrip_seps(&head, false) else head

pub fn posix_splitext(p: &text) -> Pair = splitext_any(p, false)

pub fn posix_normpath(p: &text) -> text
    if p == ""
        return "."
    let r = posix_splitroot(p)
    let init = copy(r.root)
    var out: List[text] = []
    for c in split_on(&r.tail, "/")
        if c == "" or c == "."
            continue
        if c != ".." or (init == "" and out.len() == 0) or (out.len() > 0 and out[out.len() - 1] == "..")
            out.push(copy(c))
        elif out.len() > 0
            let _ = out.pop()
    let o = init + join_with(&out, "/")
    return if o == "" then "." else o

pub fn posix_abspath(p: &text, cwd: &text) -> text
    if p.startswith("/")
        return posix_normpath(p)
    let ps: List[text] = [copy(cwd), copy(p)]
    let j = posix_join(&ps)
    return posix_normpath(&j)

# Relative path from start to path, with cwd standing for os.getcwd().
pub fn posix_relpath(path: &text, start: &text, cwd: &text) -> text ! BadPath
    if path == ""
        fail BadPath(why: "no path specified")
    let sa = posix_abspath(start, cwd)
    let pa = posix_abspath(path, cwd)
    let s = strip_lead(&sa)
    let t = strip_lead(&pa)
    let sl = if s == "" then [] else split_on(&s, "/")
    let tl = if t == "" then [] else split_on(&t, "/")
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < sl.len() and i < tl.len() and sl[i] == tl[i] bound 16777216
        i += 1
    var rel: List[text] = []
    var k = i
    while k < sl.len() bound 16777216
        rel.push("..")
        k += 1
    k = i
    while k < tl.len() bound 16777216
        rel.push(copy(tl[k]))
        k += 1
    return if rel.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rel, "/")

fn strip_lead(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] == "/" bound 16777216
        i += 1
    return sub(&cs, i, cs.len())

fn comps_clean(t: &text, sep: text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in split_on(t, sep)
        if c != "" and c != "."
            o.push(copy(c))
    return o

fn list_lt(a: &[text], b: &[text]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len() and i < b.len() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return text_lt(&a[i], &b[i])
        i += 1
    return a.len() < b.len()

fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    let x = cps(a)
    let y = cps(b)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < x.len() and i < y.len() bound 16777216
        if x[i] != y[i]
            return x[i] < y[i]
        i += 1
    return x.len() < y.len()

# Code points of UTF-8 text (code point order is Python's string order).
fn cps(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        let b = t[i] as i64
        if b < 128
            o.push(b)
            i += 1
        elif b < 224
            o.push((b & 31) << 6 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63))
            i += 2
        elif b < 240
            o.push((b & 15) << 12 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[met + 2] as i64 & 63))
            i += 3
        else
            o.push((b & 7) << 18 | (t[i + 1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (t[i + 2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (t[i + 3] as i64 & 63))
            i += 4
    return o

# Longest common prefix of the clean component lists of min and max.
fn common_of(sp: &[List[text]]) -> List[text]
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < sp.len() bound 16777216
        if list_lt(&sp[i], &sp[lo])
            lo = i
        if list_lt(&sp[hi], &sp[i])
            hi = i
        i += 1
    let a = copy(sp[lo])
    let b = copy(sp[hi])
    var o: List[text] = []
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < a.len() bound 16777216
        if k >= b.len() or a[k] != b[k]
            break
        o.push(copy(a[k]))
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn posix_commonpath(ps: &[text]) -> text ! BadPath
    if ps.len() == 0
        fail BadPath(why: "empty")
    let abs = ps[0].startswith("/")
    var sp: List[List[text]] = []
    for p in ps
        if p.startswith("/") != abs
            fail BadPath(why: "mix of absolute and relative")
        sp.push(comps_clean(&p, "/"))
    let c = common_of(&sp)
    return (if abs then "/" else "") + join_with(&c, "/")

# ---------------- Windows ----------------

pub fn win_splitroot(p: &text) -> Root

    var n: List[text] = []
    for c in cs
        n.push(if c == "/" then "\\" else copy(c))
