pub fn win_relpath(path: &text, start: &text, cwd: &bool) -> text ! BadPath
    if path == ""
        fail BadPath(why: "no path specified")
    let sx = win_abspath(start, cwd)
    let px = win_abspath(path, cwd)
    let sa = win_splitroot(&sx)
    let pa = win_splitroot(&px)
    if win_normcase(&sa.drive) != win_normcase(&pa.drive)
        fail BadPath(why: "different mounts")
    let sl = if sa.tail == "" then [] else split_on(&sa.tail, "\\")
    let tl = if pa.tail == "" then [] else split_on(&pa.tail, "\\")
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < sl.len() and i < tl.len() and win_normcase(&sl[i]) == win_normcase(&tl[i]) bound 16777216
        i += 1
    var rel: List[text] = []
    var k = i
    while k < sl.len() bound 16777216
        rel.push("..")
        k += 1
    k = i
    while k < tl.len() bound 16777216
        rel.push(copy(tl[k]))
        k += 1
    return if rel.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rel, "\\")

pub fn win_commonpath(ps: &[text]) -> text ! BadPath
    if ps.len() == 0
        fail BadPath(why: "empty")
    var sp: List[List[text]] = []
    let l0 = slashes_to_back(&ps[0]).lower()
    let r0 = win_splitroot(&l0)
    for p in ps
        let lp = slashes_to_back(&p).lower()
        let r = win_splitroot(&lp)
        if r.drive != r0.drive
            fail BadPath(why: "different drives")
        if r.root != r0.root
            fail BadPath(why: "mix of rooted and not rooted")
        sp.push(comps_clean(&r.tail, "\\"))
    let b0 = slashes_to_back(&ps[0])
    let f = win_splitroot(&b0)
    var common = comps_clean(&f.tail, "\\")
    let c = common_of(&sp)
    var o: List[text] = []
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < c.len() and k < common.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(copy(common[k]))
        k += 1
    return f.drive + f.root + join_with(&o, "\\")

const RESERVED: text = "CON PRN AUX NUL CONIN$ CONOUT$ COM1 COM2 COM3 COM4 COM5 COM6 COM7 COM8 COM9 COM\u{b9} COM\u{b2} COM\u{b3} LPT1 LPT2 LPT3 LPT4 LPT5 LPT6 LPT7 LPT8 LPT9 LPT\u{b9} LPT\u{b2} LPT\u{b3}"

fn reserved_name(n: &text) -> bool
    let cs = n.chars()
    if cs.len() > 0 and (cs[cs.len() - 1] == "." or cs[cs.len() - 1] == " ")
        return n != "." and n != ".."
    for c in cs
        if c.len_bytes() == 1 and (c[0] < 32 or c == "\"" or c == "*" or c == ":" or c == "<" or c == ">" or c == "?" or c == "|" or c == "/" or c == "\\")
            return true
    var stem = ""
    for c in cs
        if c == "."
            break
        stem = stem + c
    let s = rstrip_spaces(&stem).upper()
    return RESERVED.split(" ").contains(s)

fn rstrip_spaces(t: &text) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var n = cs.len()
    while n > 0 and cs[n - 1] == " " bound 16777216
        n -= 1
    return sub(&cs, 0, n)

# A name Windows reserves anywhere in the path (DOS devices, trailing
# dot or space, wildcards, colon, control characters).
pub fn win_isreserved(p: &text) -> bool
    let r = win_splitroot(p)
    let bt = slashes_to_back(&r.tail)
    for n in split_on(&bt, "\\")
        if reserved_name(&n)
            return true
    return false

# ---------------- WASI ----------------

# The components of a path relative to a granted directory: "." and empty
# components dropped, ".." taken lexically; an absolute path, or one that
# climbs above the directory, is refused (WASI ENOTCAPABLE). Symbolic
# links met on the way are resolved by the host under the same rule.
pub fn wasi_resolve(p: &text) -> List[text] ! BadPath
    if p.startswith("/")
        fail BadPath(why: "absolute")
    var out: List[text] = []
    for c in split_on(p, "/")
        if c == "" or c == "."
            continue
        if c == ".."
            if out.len() == 0
                fail BadPath(why: "escapes the directory")
            let _ = out.pop()
        else
            out.push(copy(c))
    return out

pub struct Preopen
    index: i64
    rel: text

# The granted directory for an absolute path, as wasi-libc's
# __wasilibc_find_relpath picks it: the preopen whose components are the
# longest prefix of the path's normalized components (the later one on a
# tie), and the rest of the path relative to it ("." when equal).
pub fn wasi_preopen(preopens: &[text], p: &text) -> Preopen ! BadPath
    if not p.startswith("/")
        fail BadPath(why: "not absolute")
    let pn = posix_normpath(p)
    let pc = comps_clean(&pn, "/")
    var best: i64 = -1
    var blen: i64 = -1
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < preopens.len() bound 16777216
        let qn = posix_normpath(&preopens[i])
        let qc = comps_clean(&qn, "/")
        var ok = preopens[i].startswith("/") and qc.len() <= pc.len()
        var k: usize = 0
        while ok and k < qc.len() bound 16777216
            if qc[k] != pc[k]
                ok = false
            k += 1
        if ok and qc.len() as i64 >= blen
            best = i as i64
            blen = qc.len() as i64
        i += 1
    if best < 0
        fail BadPath(why: "no preopen")
    var rest: List[text] = []
    var k = blen as usize
    while k < pc.len() bound 16777216
        rest.push(copy(pc[k]))
        k += 1
    return Preopen(index: best, rel: if rest.len() == 0 then "." else join_with(&rest, "/"))

module os.perm

# Permission models (survey M36), pure, for reading and reporting: a
# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never
# raises privilege, so nothing here changes a permission on a system.
# - POSIX mode bits: file type and permission bits, the ls -l string
# (CPython stat.filemode), octal, symbolic modes as POSIX chmod defines
# them (with GNU coreutils' umask and X rules), and the access check
# of POSIX.1 section 4.5 for an unprivileged process.
# - Windows: SIDs (MS-DTYP 2.4.2: string and binary forms) and the
# discretionary access check over an ordered ACE list (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2,
# allow and deny ACEs, no inheritance or object ACEs).
# - Linux Landlock: the access-right bits of include/uapi/linux/landlock.h,
# the rights each ABI version knows, and a ruleset check (path-beneath
# rules, every layer must allow).
# - The proposed mapping of a Sandbox fs grant (r, w, x on a subtree) to
# POSIX bits and Landlock rights (spec item: grant names table).

error BadPerm(why: text)

# ---------------- POSIX mode bits ----------------

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub < S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const S_IFIFO: i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
let t = m & S_IFMT
if t == S_IFREG
return "-"
if t == S_IFDIR
return "d"
if t == S_IFLNK
return "l"
if t == S_IFCHR
return "c"
if t == S_IFBLK
return "b"
if t == S_IFIFO
return "p"
if t == S_IFSOCK
return "s"
return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

pub fn octal(m: i64) -> text
var o = ""
var v = m & 4095
var k: i64 = 0
while k < 4 bound 4
o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
v = v / 8
k += 1
return o

pub struct Chmod
mode: i64
naive: i64

pub struct Change
op: text
flag: i64
affected: i64
value: i64
mentioned: i64

const ORDINARY: i64 = 0
const COPY: i64 = 1
const X_IF_X: i64 = 2

fn octal_run(cs: &[text], i: usize) -> i64
var v: i64 = 0

while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
if v > 4095
return -1
k += 1
return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm

elif c == "u"

i += 1

elif d == "w"

elif d == "x"
value = value | 73
elif d == "X"

elif d == "s"

elif d == "t"

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
var nm = old & 4095
for c in ch
let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
var value = c.value
if c.flag == COPY
value = value & nm

if value & 292 != 0
spread = spread | 292
if value & 146 != 0
spread = spread | 146
if value & 73 != 0
spread = spread | 73
value = value | spread
elif c.flag == X_IF_X
if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
value = value | 73
value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit

let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
nm = (nm & preserved) | value
elif c.op == "+"
nm = nm | value
else
nm = nm & ~value

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
uid: i64
gid: i64
groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool

if c.uid == owner
cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
else
var in_group = c.gid == grp
for g in c.groups
if g == grp

if in_group
cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
return cls & want == want

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------

pub struct Sid
authority: i64
subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
return -1

var i = lo
while i < hi bound 16
let x = cs[i][0] as i64
if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57

v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
i += 1
return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64

return -1
var v: i64 = 0
var i = lo
while i < hi bound 16
let x = cs[i][0] as i64

d = x - 48
elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
d = x - 55
elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
d = x - 87
if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
return -1
v = v * 16 + d
i += 1
return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
let cs = t.chars()
if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
var parts: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 4
var first = true
var auth: i64 = 0
while i <= cs.len() bound 64
var j = i
while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
j += 1
var v: i64 = -1
if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
else
v = digits(&cs, i, j)
if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
if first
auth = v
first = false
else
parts.push(v)
i = j + 1
if parts.len() > 15
fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
var o = ""
var x = v
var k: i64 = 0
while k < 12 bound 12
o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
x = x >> 4
k += 1
return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text
var o = "S-1-" + (if s.authority < 4294967296 then s.authority.tostr() else "0x" + hex12(s.authority))
for x in s.subs
o = o + "-" + x.tostr()
return o

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn sid_bytes(s: &Sid) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = [1, s.subs.len() as i64]
var k: i64 = 5
while k >= 0 bound 6
o.push((s.authority >> (k * 8)) & 255)
k -= 1
for x in s.subs
o.push(x & 255)
o.push((x >> 8) & 255)
o.push((x >> 16) & 255)
o.push((x >> 24) & 255)
return o

pub fn sid_from_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> Sid ! BadPerm
if b.len() < 8 or b[0] != 1 or b[1] > 15 or b.len() != 8 + 4 * b[1] as usize
fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID bytes")
var a: i64 = 0
for k in 2..8
a = a * 256 + b[k]
var subs: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 8
while i < b.len() bound 64
subs.push(b[i] | b[i + 1] << 8 | b[i + 2] << 16 | b[i + 3] << 24)
i += 4
return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

pub struct Ace
allow: bool
sid: text
mask: i64

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
if not has_dacl
return true
var left = want
for a in dacl
var mine = false
for s in token
if s == a.sid
mine = true
if not mine
continue
if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
return false
if a.allow
left = left & ~a.mask
if left == 0
return true
return left == 0

# ---------------- Landlock ----------------

module os.perm

# Permission models (survey M36), pure, for reading and reporting: a
# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never
# raises privilege, so nothing here changes a permission on a system.
# - POSIX mode bits: file type and permission bits, the ls -l string
# (CPython stat.filemode), octal, symbolic modes as POSIX chmod defines
# them (with GNU coreutils' umask and X rules), and the access check
# of POSIX.1 section 4.5 for an unprivileged process.
# - Windows: SIDs (MS-DTYP 2.4.2: string and binary forms) and the
# discretionary access check over an ordered ACE list (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2,
# allow and deny ACEs, no inheritance or object ACEs).
# - Linux Landlock: the access-right bits of include/uapi/linux/landlock.h,
# the rights each ABI version knows, and a ruleset check (path-beneath
# rules, every layer must allow).
# - The proposed mapping of a Sandbox fs grant (r, w, x on a subtree) to
# POSIX bits and Landlock rights (spec item: grant names table).

error BadPerm(why: text)

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub const S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const BadPerm i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
let t = m & S_IFMT
if t == S_IFREG
return "-"
if t == S_IFDIR
return "d"
if t == S_IFLNK
return "l"
if t == S_IFCHR
return "c"
if t == S_IFBLK
return "b"
if t == S_IFIFO
return "p"
if t == S_IFSOCK
return "s"
return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

var v = m & 4095
var k: i64 = 0
while k < 4 bound 4
o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
v = v / 8
k += 1
return o

pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
var nm = old & 4095

let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned

# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask

# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool

cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
else
var in_group = c.gid == grp

if g == grp

if in_group

return cls & want == want

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64

i += 4
return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

if s == a.sid
mine = true
if not mine
continue
if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
return false
if a.allow
left = left & ~a.mask
if left == 0
return true
return left == 0

            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER

    let gw = grant_ll(&w)

    if rights & gw == gw
        o = o + "w"
    if rights & LL_EXECUTE != 0
        o = o + "x"
    return o

# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool

        return true
    var left = want
    for a in dacl
        var mine = false
        for s in token

        if not mine
            continue

            return false

# only); a sandbox handles only what the running kernel knows.
pub fn ll_fs_rights(abi: i64) -> i64
    if abi < 1
        return 0
    var r: i64 = 8191
    if abi >= 2
        r = r | LL_REFER
    if abi >= 3
        r = r | LL_TRUNCATE

fn beneath(rule: &[text], p: &[text]) -> bool
    if rule.len() > p.len()

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < rule.len() bound 16777216
        if rule[i] != p[i]
            return false
        i += 1
    return true

# layer must allow it; a layer allows the rights it does not handle, and
# a handled right only if a rule on p or an ancestor grants it.

# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.

    var r: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"

            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub const S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const S_IFIFO: i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
    let t = m & S_IFMT
    if t == S_IFREG
        return "-"
    if t == S_IFDIR
        return "d"
    if t == S_IFLNK
        return "l"
    if t == S_IFCHR
        return "c"
    if t == S_IFBLK
        return "b"
    if t == S_IFIFO
        return "p"
    if t == S_IFSOCK
        return "s"
    return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
    let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
    let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
    let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
    let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
    return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
    return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

pub fn octal(m: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var v = m & 4095
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 4 bound 4
        o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
        v = v / 8
        k += 1
    return o

pub struct Chmod
    mode: i64
    naive: i64

pub struct Change
    op: text
    flag: i64
    affected: i64
    value: i64
    mentioned: i64

const ORDINARY: i64 = 0
const COPY: i64 = 1
const X_IF_X: i64 = 2

fn octal_run(cs: &[text], i: usize) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    var k = i
    while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
        v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
        if v > 4095
            return -1
        k += 1
    return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm
    let cs = spec.chars()
    var out: List[Change] = []
    if cs.len() > 0 and is_oct(&cs[0])
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
            k += 1
        let v = octal_run(&cs, 0)
        if v < 0 or k != cs.len()
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        let men = if k < 5 then (v & (S_ISUID | S_ISGID)) | S_ISVTX | 511 else 4095
        out.push(Change(op: "=", flag: ORDINARY, affected: 4095, value: v, mentioned: men))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        var affected: i64 = 0
        loop bound 16777216
            if i >= cs.len()
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            let c = copy(cs[i])
            if c == "u"
                affected = affected | 2496
            elif c == "g"
                affected = affected | 1080
            elif c == "o"
                affected = affected | 519
            elif c == "a"
                affected = affected | 4095
            elif c == "=" or c == "+" or c == "-"
                break
            else
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            i += 1
        while i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-") bound 16777216
            let op = copy(cs[i])
            i += 1
            var value: i64 = 0
            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""
            if is_oct(&c)
                var k = i
                while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
                    k += 1
                let v = octal_run(&cs, i)
                if v < 0 or affected != 0 or (k < cs.len() and cs[k] != ",")
                    fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
                i = k
                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"
                value = 448
                i += 1
            elif c == "g"
                value = 56
                i += 1
            elif c == "o"
                value = 7
                i += 1
            else
                flag = ORDINARY
                while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "w"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i < cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

pub struct Sid
    authority: i64
    subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
        i += 1
    return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 12
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
        i += 1
    return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
    var parts: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 4
    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
            v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
        else
            v = digits(&cs, i, j)
        if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
            fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
        if first
            auth = v
            first = false
        else
            parts.push(v)
        i = j + 1
    if parts.len() > 15
        fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
    return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
    let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = v
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 12 bound 12
        o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text
    var o = "S-1-" + (if s.authority < 4294967296 then s.authority.tostr() else "0x" + hex12(s.authority))
    for x in s.subs
        o = o + "-" + x.tostr()
    return o

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn sid_bytes(s: &Sid) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [1, s.subs.len() as i64]
    var k: i64 = 5
    while k >= 0 bound 6
        o.push((s.authority >> (k * 8)) & 255)
        k -= 1
    for x in s.subs
        o.push(x & 255)
        o.push((x >> 8) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 16) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 24) & 255)
    return o

pub fn sid_from_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    if b.len() < 8 or b[0] != 1 or b[1] > 15 or b.len() != 8 + 4 * b[1] as usize
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID bytes")
    var a: i64 = 0
    for k in 2..8
        a = a * 256 + b[k]
    var subs: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 8
    while i < b.len() bound 64
        subs.push(b[i] | b[i + 1] << 8 | b[i + 2] << 16 | b[i + 3] << 24)
        i += 4
    return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

    allow: bool

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    if not has_dacl
        return true
    var left = want
    for a in dacl
        var mine = false
        for s in token
            if s == a.sid
                mine = true
        if not mine
            continue
        if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
            return false
        if a.allow
            left = left & ~a.mask
        if left == 0
            return true
    return left == 0

# ---------------- POSIX mode bits ----------------

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub const S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const S_IFIFO: i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
    let t = m & S_IFMT
    if t == S_IFREG
        return "-"
    if t == S_IFDIR
        return "d"
    if t == S_IFLNK
        return "l"
    if t == S_IFCHR
        return "c"
    if t == S_IFBLK
        return "b"
    if t == S_IFIFO
        return "p"
    if t == S_IFSOCK
        return "s"
    return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
    let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
    let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
    let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
    let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
    return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
    return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

pub fn octal(m: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var v = m & 4095
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 4 bound 4
        o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
        v = v / 8
        k += 1
    return o

pub struct Chmod
    mode: i64
    naive: i64

pub struct Change
    op: text
    flag: i64
    affected: i64
    value: i64
    mentioned: i64

const ORDINARY: i64 = 0
const COPY: i64 = 1
const X_IF_X: i64 = 2

fn octal_run(cs: &[text], i: usize) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    var k = i
    while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
        v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
        if v > 4095
            return -1
        k += 1
    return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm
    let cs = spec.chars()
    var out: List[Change] = []
    if cs.len() > 0 and is_oct(&cs[0])
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
            k += 1
        let v = octal_run(&cs, 0)
        if v < 0 or k != cs.len()
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        let men = if k < 5 then (v & (S_ISUID | S_ISGID)) | S_ISVTX | 511 else 4095
        out.push(Change(op: "=", flag: ORDINARY, affected: 4095, value: v, mentioned: men))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        var affected: i64 = 0
        loop bound 16777216
            if i >= cs.len()
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            let c = copy(cs[i])
            if c == "u"
                affected = affected | 2496
            elif c == "g"
                affected = affected | 1080
            elif c == "o"
                affected = affected | 519
            elif c == "a"
                affected = affected | 4095
            elif c == "=" or c == "+" or c == "-"
                break
            else
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            i += 1
        while i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-") bound 16777216
            let op = copy(cs[i])
            i += 1
            var value: i64 = 0
            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""
            if is_oct(&c)
                var k = i
                while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
                    k += 1
                let v = octal_run(&cs, i)
                if v < 0 or affected != 0 or (k < cs.len() and cs[k] != ",")
                    fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
                i = k
                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"
                value = 448
                i += 1
            elif c == "g"
                value = 56
                i += 1
            elif c == "o"
                value = 7
                i += 1
            else
                flag = ORDINARY
                while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "w"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i >= cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------

pub struct Sid
    authority: i64
    subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
        i += 1
    return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 12
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
        i += 1
    return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
    var parts: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 4
    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
            v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
        else
            v = digits(&cs, i, j)
        if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
            fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
        if first
            auth = v
            first = false
        else
            parts.push(v)
        i = j + 1
    if parts.len() > 15
        fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
    return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
    let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = v
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 12 bound 12
        o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text
    var o = "S-1-" + (if s.authority < 4294967296 then s.authority.tostr() else "0x" + hex12(s.authority))
    for x in s.subs
        o = o + "-" + x.tostr()
    return o

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn sid_bytes(s: &Sid) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [1, s.subs.len() as i64]
    var k: i64 = 5
    while k >= 0 bound 6
        o.push((s.authority >> (k * 8)) & 255)
        k -= 1
    for x in s.subs
        o.push(x & 255)
        o.push((x >> 8) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 16) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 24) & 255)
    return o

pub fn sid_from_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    if b.len() < 8 or b[0] != 1 or b[1] > 15 or b.len() != 8 + 4 * b[1] as usize
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID bytes")
    var a: i64 = 0
    for k in 2..8
        a = a * 256 + b[k]
    var subs: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 8
    while i < b.len() bound 64
        subs.push(b[i] | b[i + 1] << 8 | b[i + 2] << 16 | b[i + 3] << 24)
        i += 4
    return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

pub struct Ace
    allow: bool
    sid: text
    mask: i64

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    if not has_dacl
        return true
    var left = want
    for a in dacl
        var mine = false
        for s in token
            if s == a.sid
                mine = true
        if not mine
            continue
        if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
            return false
        if a.allow
            left = left & ~a.mask
        if left == 0
            return true
    return left == 0

# ---------------- Landlock ----------------

pub const LL_EXECUTE: i64 = 1
pub const LL_WRITE_FILE: i64 = 2
pub const LL_READ_FILE: i64 = 4
pub const LL_READ_DIR: i64 = 8
pub const LL_REMOVE_DIR: i64 = 16
pub const LL_REMOVE_FILE: i64 = 32
pub const LL_MAKE_CHAR: i64 = 64
pub const LL_MAKE_DIR: i64 = 128
pub const LL_MAKE_REG: i64 = 256
pub const LL_MAKE_SOCK: i64 = 512
pub const LL_MAKE_FIFO: i64 = 1024
pub const LL_MAKE_BLOCK: i64 = 2048
pub const LL_MAKE_SYM: i64 = 4096
pub const LL_REFER: i64 = 8192
pub const LL_TRUNCATE: i64 = 16384
pub const LL_IOCTL_DEV: i64 = 32768
pub const LL_NET_BIND_TCP: i64 = 1
pub const LL_NET_CONNECT_TCP: i64 = 2
pub const LL_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET: i64 = 1
pub const LL_SCOPE_SIGNAL: i64 = 2

# Filesystem rights known to a Landlock ABI version (1: EXECUTE to
# MAKE_SYM, 2: REFER, 3: TRUNCATE, 5: IOCTL_DEV; 4 added network rights
# only); a sandbox handles only what the running kernel knows.
pub fn ll_fs_rights(abi: i64) -> i64
    if abi < 1
        return 0
    var r: i64 = 8191
    if abi >= 2
        r = r | LL_REFER
    if abi >= 3
        r = r | LL_TRUNCATE
    if abi >= 5
        r = r | LL_IOCTL_DEV
    return r

pub fn ll_net_rights(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 4 then 3 else 0
pub fn ll_scopes(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 6 then 3 else 0

pub struct Rule
    path: List[text]
    rights: i64

pub struct Layer
    handled: i64
    rules: List[Rule]

fn beneath(rule: &[text], p: &[text]) -> bool
    if rule.len() > p.len()
        return false
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < rule.len() bound 16777216
        if rule[i] != p[i]
            return false
        i += 1
    return true

# A filesystem access `want` on path p (components from the root): each
# layer must allow it; a layer allows the rights it does not handle, and
# a handled right only if a rule on p or an ancestor grants it.
pub fn ll_allowed(layers: &[Layer], p: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    for l in layers
        let need = want & l.handled
        var got: i64 = 0
        for r in l.rules
            if beneath(&r.path, p)
                got = got | r.rights
        if need & ~got != 0
            return false
    return true

# ---------------- Sandbox grant mapping (proposal) ----------------

# fs grant modes as letters "r", "w", "x" (any subset). Proposed rights:
# r: read files and list directories; w: write, truncate, create and
# remove files, directories and symlinks, and rename within (REFER); x:
# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.
pub fn grant_ll(modes: &text) -> i64
    var r: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            r = r | LL_READ_FILE | LL_READ_DIR
        elif c == "w"
            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER
        elif c == "x"
            r = r | LL_EXECUTE
    return r

# The POSIX bits an fs grant needs on the files it covers, for reporting
# (owner class: the sandboxed program runs as the file's owner or not at
# all).
pub fn grant_mode(modes: &text) -> i64
    var m: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            m = m | 256
        elif c == "w"
            m = m | 128
        elif c == "x"
            m = m | 64
    return m

# The fs grant modes a Landlock right set fully contains.
pub fn ll_grant(rights: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    let r = "r"
    let w = "w"
    let gr = grant_ll(&r)
    let gw = grant_ll(&w)
    if rights & gr == gr
        o = o + "r"
    if rights & gw == gw
        o = o + "w"
    if rights & LL_EXECUTE != 0
        o = o + "x"
    return o

# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never
# raises privilege, so nothing here changes a permission on a system.

#    the rights each ABI version knows, and a ruleset check (path-beneath

                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "w"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i >= cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------

pub struct Sid
    authority: i64
    subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
        i += 1
    return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 12
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
        i += 1
    return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
    var parts: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 4
    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
            v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
        else
            v = digits(&cs, i, j)
        if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
            fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
        if first
            auth = v
            first = false
        else
            parts.push(v)
        i = j + 1
    if parts.len() > 15
        fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
    return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
    let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = v
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 12 bound 12
        o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text
    var o = "S-1-" + (if s.authority < 4294967296 then s.authority.tostr() else "0x" + hex12(s.authority))
    for x in s.subs
        o = o + "-" + x.tostr()
    return o

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn sid_bytes(s: &Sid) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [1, s.subs.len() as i64]
    var k: i64 = 5
    while k >= 0 bound 6
        o.push((s.authority >> (k * 8)) & 255)
        k -= 1
    for x in s.subs
        o.push(x & 255)
        o.push((x >> 8) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 16) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 24) & 255)
    return o

pub fn sid_from_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    if b.len() < 8 or b[0] != 1 or b[1] > 15 or b.len() != 8 + 4 * b[1] as usize
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID bytes")
    var a: i64 = 0
    for k in 2..8
        a = a * 256 + b[k]
    var subs: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 8
    while i < b.len() bound 64
        subs.push(b[i] | b[i + 1] << 8 | b[i + 2] << 16 | b[i + 3] << 24)
        i += 4
    return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

pub struct Ace
    allow: bool
    sid: text
    mask: i64

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    if not has_dacl
        return true
    var left = want
    for a in dacl
        var mine = false
        for s in token
            if s == a.sid
                mine = true
        if not mine
            continue
        if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
            return false
        if a.allow
            left = left & ~a.mask
        if left == 0
            return true
    return left == 0

# ---------------- Landlock ----------------

pub const LL_EXECUTE: i64 = 1
pub const LL_WRITE_FILE: i64 = 2
pub const LL_READ_FILE: i64 = 4
pub const LL_READ_DIR: i64 = 8
pub const LL_REMOVE_DIR: i64 = 16
pub const LL_REMOVE_FILE: i64 = 32
pub const LL_MAKE_CHAR: i64 = 64
pub const LL_MAKE_DIR: i64 = 128
pub const LL_MAKE_REG: i64 = 256
pub const LL_MAKE_SOCK: i64 = 512
pub const LL_MAKE_FIFO: i64 = 1024
pub const LL_MAKE_BLOCK: i64 = 2048
pub const LL_MAKE_SYM: i64 = 4096
pub const LL_REFER: i64 = 8192
pub const LL_TRUNCATE: i64 = 16384
pub const LL_IOCTL_DEV: i64 = 32768
pub const LL_NET_BIND_TCP: i64 = 1
pub const LL_NET_CONNECT_TCP: i64 = 2
pub const LL_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET: i64 = 1
pub const LL_SCOPE_SIGNAL: i64 = 2

# Filesystem rights known to a Landlock ABI version (1: EXECUTE to
# MAKE_SYM, 2: REFER, 3: TRUNCATE, 5: IOCTL_DEV; 4 added network rights
# only); a sandbox handles only what the running kernel knows.
pub fn ll_fs_rights(abi: i64) -> i64
    if abi < 1
        return 0
    var r: i64 = 8191
    if abi >= 2
        r = r | LL_REFER
    if abi >= 3
        r = r | LL_TRUNCATE
    if abi >= 5
        r = r | LL_IOCTL_DEV
    return r

pub fn ll_net_rights(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 4 then 3 else 0
pub fn ll_scopes(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 6 then 3 else 0

pub struct Rule
    path: List[text]
    rights: i64

pub struct Layer
    handled: i64
    rules: List[Rule]

fn beneath(rule: &[text], p: &[text]) -> bool
    if rule.len() > p.len()
        return false
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < rule.len() bound 16777216
        if rule[i] != p[i]
            return false
        i += 1
    return true

# A filesystem access `want` on path p (components from the root): each
# layer must allow it; a layer allows the rights it does not handle, and
# a handled right only if a rule on p or an ancestor grants it.
pub fn ll_allowed(layers: &[Layer], p: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    for l in layers
        let need = want & l.handled
        var got: i64 = 0
        for r in l.rules
            if beneath(&r.path, p)
                got = got | r.rights
        if need & ~got != 0
            return false
    return true

# ---------------- Sandbox grant mapping (proposal) ----------------

# fs grant modes as letters "r", "w", "xx" (any subset). Proposed rights:
# r: read files and list directories; w: write, truncate, create and
# remove files, directories and symlinks, and rename within (REFER); x:
# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.
pub fn grant_ll(modes: &text) -> i64
    var r: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            r = r | LL_READ_FILE | LL_READ_DIR
        elif c == "w"
            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER
        elif c == "x"
            r = r | LL_EXECUTE
    return r

# The POSIX bits an fs grant needs on the files it covers, for reporting
# (owner class: the sandboxed program runs as the file's owner or not at
# all).
pub fn grant_mode(modes: &text) -> i64
    var m: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            m = m | 256
        elif c == "w"
            m = m | 128
        elif c == "x"
            m = m | 64
    return m

# The fs grant modes a Landlock right set fully contains.
pub fn ll_grant(rights: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    let r = "r"
    let w = "w"
    let gr = grant_ll(&r)
    let gw = grant_ll(&w)
    if rights & gr == gr
        o = o + "r"
    if rights & gw == gw
        o = o + "w"
    if rights & LL_EXECUTE != 0
        o = o + "x"
    return o

module os.perm

# Permission models (survey M36), pure, for reading and reporting: a
# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never
# raises privilege, so nothing here changes a permission on a system.
#  - POSIX mode bits: file type and permission bits, the ls -l string
#    (CPython stat.filemode), octal, symbolic modes as POSIX chmod defines
#    them (with GNU coreutils' umask and X rules), and the access check
#    of POSIX.1 section 4.5 for an unprivileged process.
#  - Windows: SIDs (MS-DTYP 2.4.2: string and binary forms) and the
#    discretionary access check over an ordered ACE list (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2,
#    allow and deny ACEs, no inheritance or object ACEs).
#  - Linux Landlock: the access-right bits of include/uapi/linux/landlock.h,
#    the rights each ABI version knows, and a ruleset check (path-beneath
#    rules, every layer must allow).
#  - The proposed mapping of a Sandbox fs grant (r, w, x on a subtree) to
#    POSIX bits and Landlock rights (spec item: grant names table).

error BadPerm(why: text)

# ---------------- POSIX mode bits ----------------

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub const S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const S_IFIFO: i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
    let t = m & S_IFMT
    if t == S_IFREG
        return "-"
    if t == S_IFDIR
        return "d"
    if t == S_IFLNK
        return "l"
    if t == S_IFCHR
        return "c"
    if t == S_IFBLK
        return "b"
    if t == S_IFIFO
        return "p"
    if t == S_IFSOCK
        return "s"
    return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
    let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
    let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
    let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
    let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
    return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
    return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

pub fn octal(m: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var v = m & 4095
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 4 bound 4
        o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
        v = v / 8
        k += 1
    return o

pub struct Chmod
    mode: i64
    naive: i64

pub struct Change
    op: text
    flag: i64
    affected: i64
    value: i64
    mentioned: i64

const ORDINARY: i64 = 0
const COPY: i64 = 1
const X_IF_X: i64 = 2

fn octal_run(cs: &[text], i: usize) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    var k = i
    while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
        v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
        if v > 4095
            return -1
        k += 1
    return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm
    let cs = spec.chars()
    var out: List[Change] = []
    if cs.len() > 0 and is_oct(&cs[0])
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
            k += 1
        let v = octal_run(&cs, 0)
        if v < 0 or k != cs.len()
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        let men = if k < 5 then (v & (S_ISUID | S_ISGID)) | S_ISVTX | 511 else 4095
        out.push(Change(op: "=", flag: ORDINARY, affected: 4095, value: v, mentioned: men))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        var affected: i64 = 0
        loop bound 16777216
            if i >= cs.len()
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            let c = copy(cs[i])
            if c == "u"
                affected = affected | 2496
            elif c == "g"
                affected = affected | 1080
            elif c == "o"
                affected = affected | 519
            elif c == "a"
                affected = affected | 4095
            elif c == "=" or c == "+" or c == "-"
                break
            else
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            i += 1
        while i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-") bound 16777216
            let op = copy(cs[i])
            i += 1
            var value: i64 = 0
            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""
            if is_oct(&c)
                var k = i
                while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
                    k += 1
                let v = octal_run(&cs, i)
                if v < 0 or affected != 0 or (k < cs.len() and cs[k] != ",")
                    fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
                i = k
                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"
                value = 448
                i += 1
            elif c == "g"
                value = 56
                i += 1
            elif c == "o"
                value = 7
                i += 1
            else
                flag = ORDINARY
                while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "wx"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i >= cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")

# ---------------- Sandbox grant mapping (proposal) ----------------

# fs grant modes as letters "r", "w", "x" (any subset). Proposed rights:
# r: read files and list directories; w: write, truncate, create and
# remove files, directories and symlinks, and rename within (REFER); x:
# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.
pub fn grant_ll(modes: &text) -> i64
    var r: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            r = r | LL_READ_FILE | LL_READ_DIR
        elif c == "w"
            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER
        elif c == "x"
            r = r | LL_EXECUTE
    return r

# (owner class: the sandboxed program runs as the file's owner or not at
# all).
pub fn grant_mode(modes: &text) -> i64
    var m: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            m = m | 256
        elif c == "w"
            m = m | 128
        elif c == "x"
            m = m | 64
    return m

pub fn ll_grant(rights: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    let r = "r"
    let w = "w"
    let gr = grant_ll(&r)
    let gw = grant_ll(&w)
    if rights & gr == gr
        o = o + "r"
    if rights & gw == gw
        o = o + "w"
    if rights & LL_EXECUTE != 0
        o = o + "x"
    return o

pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text

    if t == S_IFDIR
        return "d"
    if t == S_IFLNK

    if t == S_IFCHR

    if t == S_IFBLK
        return "b"
    if t == S_IFIFO
        return "p"
    if t == S_IFSOCK
        return "s"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
    let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
    let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
    let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1

    return r + w + e

        v = v / 8

            i += 1

            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""

                    k += 1

                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"

            elif c == "g"

                i += 1
            elif c == "o"

                    elif d == "s"

                    elif d == "t"

pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"

        else

# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm

# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7

        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7

        for g in c.groups
