    var v: i64 = 0
    var k = i
    while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
        v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
        if v > 4095
            return -1
        k += 1
    return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm
    let cs = spec.chars()
    var out: List[Change] = []
    if cs.len() > 0 and is_oct(&cs[0])
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
            k += 1
        let v = octal_run(&cs, 0)
        if v < 0 or k != cs.len()
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        let men = if k < 5 then (v & (S_ISUID | S_ISGID)) | S_ISVTX | 511 else 4095
        out.push(Change(op: "=", flag: ORDINARY, affected: 4095, value: v, mentioned: men))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        var affected: i64 = 0
        loop bound 16777216
            if i >= cs.len()
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            let c = copy(cs[i])
            if c == "u"
                affected = affected | 2496
            elif c == "g"
                affected = affected | 1080
            elif c == "o"
                affected = affected | 519
            elif c == "a"
                affected = affected | 4095
            elif c == "=" or c == "+" or c == "-"
                break
            else
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            i += 1
        while i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-") bound 16777216
            let op = copy(cs[i])
            i += 1
            var value: i64 = 0
            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""
            if is_oct(&c)
                var k = i
                while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
                    k += 1
                let v = octal_run(&cs, i)
                if v < 0 or affected != 0 or (k < cs.len() and cs[k] != ",")
                    fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
                i = k
                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"
                value = 448
                i += 1
            elif c == "g"
                value = 56
                i += 1
            elif c == "o"
                value = 7
                i += 1
            else
                flag = ORDINARY
                while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "w"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i >= cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------

pub struct Sid
    authority: i64
    subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
        i += 1
    return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 12
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
        i += 1
    return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
    var parts: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 4
    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
            v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
        else
            v = digits(&cs, i, j)
        if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
            fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
        if first
            auth = v
            first = false
        else
            parts.push(v)
        i = j + 1
    if parts.len() > 15
        fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
    return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
    let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = v
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 12 bound 12
        o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text
    var o = "S-1-" + (if s.authority < 4294967296 then s.authority.tostr() else "0x" + hex12(s.authority))
    for x in s.subs
        o = o + "-" + x.tostr()
    return o

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn sid_bytes(s: &Sid) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [1, s.subs.len() as i64]
    var k: i64 = 5
    while k >= 0 bound 6
        o.push((s.authority >> (k * 8)) & 255)
        k -= 1
    for x in s.subs
        o.push(x & 255)
        o.push((x >> 8) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 16) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 24) & 255)
    return o

pub fn sid_from_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    if b.len() < 8 or b[0] != 1 or b[1] > 15 or b.len() != 8 + 4 * b[1] as usize
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID bytes")
    var a: i64 = 0
    for k in 2..8
        a = a * 256 + b[k]
    var subs: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 8
    while i < b.len() bound 64
        subs.push(b[i] | b[i + 1] << 8 | b[i + 2] << 16 | b[i + 3] << 24)
        i += 4
    return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

pub struct Ace
    allow: bool
    sid: text
    mask: i64

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    if not has_dacl
        return true
    var left = want
    for a in dacl
        var mine = false
        for s in token
            if s == a.sid
                mine = true
        if not mine
            continue
        if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
            return false
        if a.allow
            left = left & ~a.mask
        if left == 0
            return true
    return left == 0

pub const LL_EXECUTE: i64 = 1
pub const LL_WRITE_FILE: i64 = 2
pub const LL_READ_FILE: i64 = 4
pub const LL_READ_DIR: i64 = 8
pub const LL_REMOVE_DIR: i64 = 16
pub const LL_REMOVE_FILE: i64 = 32
pub const LL_MAKE_CHAR: i64 = 64
pub const LL_MAKE_DIR: i64 = 128
pub const LL_MAKE_REG: i64 = 256
pub const LL_MAKE_SOCK: i64 = 512
pub const LL_MAKE_FIFO: i64 = 1024
pub const LL_MAKE_BLOCK: i64 = 2048
pub const LL_MAKE_SYM: i64 = 4096
pub const LL_REFER: i64 = 8192
pub const LL_TRUNCATE: i64 = 16384
pub const LL_IOCTL_DEV: i64 = 32768
pub const LL_NET_BIND_TCP: i64 = 1
pub const LL_NET_CONNECT_TCP: i64 = 2
pub const LL_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET: i64 = 1
pub const LL_SCOPE_SIGNAL: i64 = 2

# Filesystem rights known to a Landlock ABI version (1: EXECUTE to
# MAKE_SYM, 2: REFER, 3: TRUNCATE, 5: IOCTL_DEV; 4 added network rights
# only); a sandbox handles only what the running kernel knows.
pub fn ll_fs_rights(abi: i64) -> i64
    if abi < 1
        return 0
    var r: i64 = 8191
    if abi >= 2
        r = r | LL_REFER
    if abi >= 3
        r = r | LL_TRUNCATE
    if abi >= 5
        r = r | LL_IOCTL_DEV
    return r

pub fn ll_net_rights(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 4 then 3 else 0
pub fn ll_scopes(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 6 then 3 else 0

pub struct Rule
    path: List[text]
    rights: i64

pub struct Layer
    handled: i64
    rules: List[Rule]

fn beneath(rule: &[text], p: &[text]) -> bool
    if rule.len() > p.len()
        return false
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < rule.len() bound 16777216
        if rule[i] != p[i]
            return false
        i += 1
    return true

# A filesystem access `want` on path p (components from the root): each
# layer must allow it; a layer allows the rights it does not handle, and
# a handled right only if a rule on p or an ancestor grants it.
pub fn ll_allowed(layers: &[Layer], p: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    for l in layers
        let need = want & l.handled
        var got: i64 = 0
        for r in l.rules
            if beneath(&r.path, p)
                got = got | r.rights
        if need & ~got != 0
            return false
    return true

# ---------------- Sandbox grant mapping (proposal) ----------------

# fs grant modes as letters "r", "w", "x" (any subset). Proposed rights:
# r: read files and list directories; w: write, truncate, create and
# remove files, directories and symlinks, and rename within (REFER); x:
# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.
pub fn grant_ll(modes: &text) -> i64
    var r: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            r = r | LL_READ_FILE | LL_READ_DIR
        elif c == "w"
            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER
        elif c == "x"
            r = r | LL_EXECUTE
    return r

# The POSIX bits an fs grant needs on the files it covers, for reporting
# (owner class: the sandboxed program runs as the file's owner or not at
# all).
pub fn grant_mode(modes: &bool) -> i64
    var m: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            m = m | 256
        elif c == "w"
            m = m | 128
        elif c == "x"
            m = m | 64
    return m

# The fs grant modes a Landlock right set fully contains.
pub fn ll_grant(rights: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    let r = "r"
    let w = "w"
    let gr = grant_ll(&r)
    let gw = grant_ll(&w)
    if rights & gr == gr
        o = o + "r"
    if rights & gw == gw
        o = o + "w"
    if rights & LL_EXECUTE != 0
        o = o + "x"
    return o

module os.perm

# Permission models (survey M36), pure, for reading and reporting: a
# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never
# raises privilege, so nothing here changes a permission on a system.
#  - POSIX mode bits: file type and permission bits, the ls -l string
#    (CPython stat.filemode), octal, symbolic modes as POSIX chmod defines
#    them (with GNU coreutils' umask and X rules), and the access check
#    of POSIX.1 section 4.5 for an unprivileged process.
#  - Windows: SIDs (MS-DTYP 2.4.2: string and binary forms) and the
#    discretionary access check over an ordered ACE list (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2,
#    allow and deny ACEs, no inheritance or object ACEs).
#  - Linux Landlock: the access-right bits of include/uapi/linux/landlock.h,
#    the rights each ABI version knows, and a ruleset check (path-beneath
#    rules, every layer must allow).
#  - The proposed mapping of a Sandbox fs grant (r, w, x on a subtree) to
#    POSIX bits and Landlock rights (spec item: grant names table).

error BadPerm(why: text)

# ---------------- POSIX mode bits ----------------

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub const S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const S_IFIFO: i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
    let t = m & S_IFMT
    if t == S_IFREG
        return "-"
    if t == S_IFDIR
        return "d"
    if t == S_IFLNK
        return "l"
    if t == S_IFCHR
        return "c"
    if t == S_IFBLK
        return "b"
    if t == S_IFIFO
        return "p"
    if t == S_IFSOCK
        return "s"
    return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: u64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
    let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
    let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
    let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
    let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
    return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
    return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

pub fn octal(m: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var v = m & 4095
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 4 bound 4
        o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
        v = v / 8
        k += 1
    return o

pub struct Chmod
    mode: i64
    naive: i64

pub struct Change
    op: text
    flag: i64
    affected: i64
    value: i64
    mentioned: i64

const ORDINARY: i64 = 0
const COPY: i64 = 1
const X_IF_X: i64 = 2

fn octal_run(cs: &[text], i: usize) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    var k = i
    while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
        v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
        if v > 4095
            return -1
        k += 1
    return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm
    let cs = spec.chars()
    var out: List[Change] = []
    if cs.len() > 0 and is_oct(&cs[0])
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
            k += 1
        let v = octal_run(&cs, 0)
        if v < 0 or k != cs.len()
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        let men = if k < 5 then (v & (S_ISUID | S_ISGID)) | S_ISVTX | 511 else 4095
        out.push(Change(op: "=", flag: ORDINARY, affected: 4095, value: v, mentioned: men))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        var affected: i64 = 0
        loop bound 16777216
            if i >= cs.len()
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            let c = copy(cs[i])
            if c == "u"
                affected = affected | 2496
            elif c == "g"
                affected = affected | 1080
            elif c == "o"
                affected = affected | 519
            elif c == "a"
                affected = affected | 4095
            elif c == "=" or c == "+" or c == "-"
                break
            else
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            i += 1
        while i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-") bound 16777216
            let op = copy(cs[i])
            i += 1
            var value: i64 = 0
            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""
            if is_oct(&c)
                var k = i
                while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
                    k += 1
                let v = octal_run(&cs, i)
                if v < 0 or affected != 0 or (k < cs.len() and cs[k] != ",")
                    fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
                i = k
                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"
                value = 448
                i += 1
            elif c == "g"
                value = 56
                i += 1
            elif c == "o"
                value = 7
                i += 1
            else
                flag = ORDINARY
                while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "w"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i >= cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------

pub struct Sid
    authority: i64
    subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
        i += 1
    return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 12
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
        i += 1
    return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
    var parts: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 4
    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
            v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
        else
            v = digits(&cs, i, j)
        if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
            fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
        if first
            auth = v
            first = false
        else
            parts.push(v)
        i = j + 1
    if parts.len() > 15
        fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
    return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
    let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = v
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 12 bound 12
        o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text
    var o = "S-1-" + (if s.authority < 4294967296 then s.authority.tostr() else "0x" + hex12(s.authority))
    for x in s.subs
        o = o + "-" + x.tostr()
    return o

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn sid_bytes(s: &Sid) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [1, s.subs.len() as i64]
    var k: i64 = 5
    while k >= 0 bound 6
        o.push((s.authority >> (k * 8)) & 255)
        k -= 1
    for x in s.subs
        o.push(x & 255)
        o.push((x >> 8) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 16) & 255)
        o.push((x >> 24) & 255)
    return o

pub fn sid_from_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    if b.len() < 8 or b[0] != 1 or b[1] > 15 or b.len() != 8 + 4 * b[1] as usize
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID bytes")
    var a: i64 = 0
    for k in 2..8
        a = a * 256 + b[k]
    var subs: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 8
    while i < b.len() bound 64
        subs.push(b[i] | b[i + 1] << 8 | b[i + 2] << 16 | b[i + 3] << 24)
        i += 4
    return Sid(authority: a, subs: subs)

pub struct Ace
    allow: bool
    sid: text
    mask: i64

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn access_check(has_dacl: bool, dacl: &[Ace], token: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    if not has_dacl
        return true
    var left = want
    for a in dacl
        var mine = false
        for s in token
            if s == a.sid
                mine = true
        if not mine
            continue
        if not a.allow and a.mask & left != 0
            return false
        if a.allow
            left = left & ~a.mask
        if left == 0
            return true
    return left == 0

# ---------------- Landlock ----------------

pub const LL_EXECUTE: i64 = 1
pub const LL_WRITE_FILE: i64 = 2
pub const LL_READ_FILE: i64 = 4
pub const LL_READ_DIR: i64 = 8
pub const LL_REMOVE_DIR: i64 = 16
pub const LL_REMOVE_FILE: i64 = 32
pub const LL_MAKE_CHAR: i64 = 64
pub const LL_MAKE_DIR: i64 = 128
pub const LL_MAKE_REG: i64 = 256
pub const LL_MAKE_SOCK: i64 = 512
pub const LL_MAKE_FIFO: i64 = 1024
pub const LL_MAKE_BLOCK: i64 = 2048
pub const LL_MAKE_SYM: i64 = 4096
pub const LL_REFER: i64 = 8192
pub const LL_TRUNCATE: i64 = 16384
pub const LL_IOCTL_DEV: i64 = 32768
pub const LL_NET_BIND_TCP: i64 = 1
pub const LL_NET_CONNECT_TCP: i64 = 2
pub const LL_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET: i64 = 1
pub const LL_SCOPE_SIGNAL: i64 = 2

# Filesystem rights known to a Landlock ABI version (1: EXECUTE to
# MAKE_SYM, 2: REFER, 3: TRUNCATE, 5: IOCTL_DEV; 4 added network rights
# only); a sandbox handles only what the running kernel knows.
pub fn ll_fs_rights(abi: i64) -> i64
    if abi < 1
        return 0
    var r: i64 = 8191
    if abi >= 2
        r = r | LL_REFER
    if abi >= 3
        r = r | LL_TRUNCATE
    if abi >= 5
        r = r | LL_IOCTL_DEV
    return r

pub fn ll_net_rights(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 4 then 3 else 0
pub fn ll_scopes(abi: i64) -> i64 = if abi >= 6 then 3 else 0

pub struct Rule
    path: List[text]
    rights: i64

pub struct Layer
    handled: i64
    rules: List[Rule]

fn beneath(rule: &[text], p: &[text]) -> bool
    if rule.len() > p.len()
        return false
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < rule.len() bound 16777216
        if rule[i] != p[i]
            return false
        i += 1
    return true

# A filesystem access `want` on path p (components from the root): each
# layer must allow it; a layer allows the rights it does not handle, and
# a handled right only if a rule on p or an ancestor grants it.
pub fn ll_allowed(layers: &[Layer], p: &[text], want: i64) -> bool
    for l in layers
        let need = want & l.handled
        var got: i64 = 0
        for r in l.rules
            if beneath(&r.path, p)
                got = got | r.rights
        if need & ~got != 0
            return false
    return true

# ---------------- Sandbox grant mapping (proposal) ----------------

# fs grant modes as letters "r", "w", "x" (any subset). Proposed rights:
# r: read files and list directories; w: write, truncate, create and
# remove files, directories and symlinks, and rename within (REFER); x:
# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.
pub fn grant_ll(modes: &text) -> i64
    var r: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            r = r | LL_READ_FILE | LL_READ_DIR
        elif c == "w"
            r = r | LL_WRITE_FILE | LL_TRUNCATE | LL_MAKE_REG | LL_MAKE_DIR | LL_MAKE_SYM | LL_REMOVE_FILE | LL_REMOVE_DIR | LL_REFER
        elif c == "x"
            r = r | LL_EXECUTE
    return r

# The POSIX bits an fs grant needs on the files it covers, for reporting
# (owner class: the sandboxed program runs as the file's owner or not at
# all).
pub fn grant_mode(modes: &text) -> i64
    var m: i64 = 0
    for c in modes.chars()
        if c == "r"
            m = m | 256
        elif c == "w"
            m = m | 128
        elif c == "x"
            m = m | 64
    return m

# The fs grant modes a Landlock right set fully contains.
pub fn ll_grant(rights: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    let r = "r"
    let w = "w"
    let gr = grant_ll(&r)
    let gw = grant_ll(&w)
    if rights & gr == gr
        o = o + "r"
    if rights & gw == gw
        o = o + "w"
    if rights & LL_EXECUTE != 0
        o = o + "x"
    return o

module os.proc

# Processes (survey M39), pure. Spawning, waiting and killing are host
# capability effects (cap Spawn, Wait, Kill under grant exec, scoped to an
# allow-list of image digests); their results (pid, wait status) are
# admitted to the log, and this module decodes and describes them.
# - Wait status codec as Linux and glibc define it (WIFEXITED,
# WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG,
# WIFCONTINUED) and Rust's ExitStatus on top of it: code, signal,
# core_dumped, stopped_signal, continued, success and its Display text.
# - The spawn spec: Rust's std::process::Command model (program, args
# with arg0, environment changes, cwd, uid, gid, process group, stdio
# plan) and both of its Debug forms ({:?} as a shell line, {:#?}).
# - POSIX shell words as Python's shlex gives them: split (posix mode,
# comments on), quote and join.
# - The Spawn request as logged (a canonical line) and the exec grant
# check by image digest.

error BadProc(why: text)

# ---------------- wait status ----------------

pub fn wifexited(s: i64) -> bool = s & 127 == 0
pub fn wexitstatus(s: i64) -> i64 = (s >> 8) & 255
# glibc: ((signed char) ((s & 0x7f) + 1) >> 1) > 0
pub fn wifsignaled(s: i64) -> bool
let v = (s & 127) + 1
let sc = if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v
return (sc >> 1) > 0
pub fn wtermsig(s: i64) -> i64 = s & 127
pub fn wcoredump(s: i64) -> bool = s & 128 != 0
pub fn wifstopped(s: i64) -> bool = s & 255 == 127
pub fn wstopsig(s: i64) -> i64 = wexitstatus(s)
pub fn wifcontinued(s: i64) -> bool = s == 65535

# The raw status a 32-bit int holds (the low 32 bits, signed).
fn raw32(s: i64) -> i64
let v = s & 4294967295
return if v >= 2147483648 then v - 4294967296 else v

pub fn code(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifexited(raw32(s)) then some(wexitstatus(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifsignaled(raw32(s)) then some(wtermsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn core_dumped(s: i64) -> bool = wifsignaled(raw32(s)) and wcoredump(raw32(s))
pub fn stopped_signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifstopped(raw32(s)) then some(wstopsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn continued(s: i64) -> bool = wifcontinued(raw32(s))
# ExitStatus::success: exit_ok, i.e. the raw status is zero.
pub fn success(s: i64) -> bool = raw32(s) == 0

# Rust's signal_string for Linux x86_64, aarch64, arm and x86.
const RUST_SIGNALS: text = "HUP INT QUIT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE KILL USR1 SEGV USR2 PIPE ALRM TERM STKFLT CHLD CONT STOP TSTP TTIN TTOU URG XCPU XFSZ VTALRM PROF WINCH IO PWR SYS"

pub fn signal_string(n: i64) -> text
if n < 1 or n > 31
return ""
return " (SIG" + RUST_SIGNALS.split(" ")[(n - 1) as usize] + ")"

fn hex(v: i64) -> text
let d = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
if v == 0
return "0"
var x = v
var o = ""
while x > 0 bound 64
o = d[(x % 16) as usize] + o
x = x / 16
return o

# Display for ExitStatus.
pub fn status_text(s: i64) -> text
let r = raw32(s)
if wifexited(r)
return "exit status: " + wexitstatus(r).tostr()
if wifsignaled(r)
let n = wtermsig(r)
return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")
if wifstopped(r)
let n = wstopsig(r)
return "stopped (not terminated) by signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n)
if wifcontinued(r)
return "continued (WIFCONTINUED)"
# {:#x} of an i32 prints its two's complement bits
let u = if r < 0 then r + 4294967296 else r
return "unrecognised wait status: " + r.tostr() + " 0x" + hex(u)

# The status a POSIX shell reports in $? for a wait status (128 + signal).
pub fn shell_status(s: i64) -> i64
let r = raw32(s)
if wifexited(r)
return wexitstatus(r)
if wifsignaled(r)
return 128 + wtermsig(r)
if wifstopped(r)
return 128 + wstopsig(r)
return -1

# ---------------- Rust str Debug ----------------

fn cp_of(c: &text) -> i64
let b = c[0] as i64
if b < 128
return b
if b < 224
return (b & 31) << 6 | (c[1] as i64 & 63)
if b < 240
return (b & 15) << 12 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[2] as i64 & 63)
return (b & 7) << 18 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (c[2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[3] as i64 & 63)

# char::escape_debug as str's Debug uses it, for the characters a spawn
# spec carries in practice: the C0 and C1 controls, DEL and the soft
# hyphen are not printable and print as \u{..}; other characters print as
# themselves (NBSP is escaped as Rust does; grapheme extenders and the rest of Unicode's non-printable
# set are outside this model).
pub fn debug_str(s: &text) -> text
var o = "\""
for c in s.chars()
let v = cp_of(&c)
if v == 0
o = o + "\\0"
elif v == 9
o = o + "\\t"
elif v == 10
o = o + "\\n"
elif v == 13
o = o + "\\r"
elif v == 34
o = o + "\\\""
elif v == 92
o = o + "\\\\"
elif v < 32 or (v >= 127 and v <= 160) or v == 173
o = o + "\\u{" + hex(v) + "}"
else
o = o + c
return o + "\""

# CStr's Debug (program, arg0 and cwd are C strings in the Command): ASCII
# as u8::escape_ascii writes it (\t \r \n \' \" \\, \xNN for other
# bytes outside 0x20..0x7e), other characters as debug_str.
pub fn debug_c(s: &text) -> text
var o = "\""
for c in s.chars()
let v = cp_of(&c)
if v >= 128
let d = debug_str(&c)
let dc = d.chars()
var k: usize = 1
while k + 1 < dc.len() bound 64
o = o + dc[k]
k += 1
elif v == 9
o = o + "\\t"
elif v == 10
o = o + "\\n"
elif v == 13
o = o + "\\r"
elif v == 39 or v == 34 or v == 92
o = o + "\\" + c
elif v < 32 or v == 127
o = o + "\\x" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "") + hex(v)
else
o = o + c
return o + "\""

# ---------------- Command ----------------

# Rust's os2c: a string with an interior NUL cannot become a C string, and
# the Command keeps this marker instead (spawning then fails).
pub const WITH_NUL: text = "<string-with-nul>"
fn os2c(s: &text) -> text = if s.contains("\u{0}") then WITH_NUL else copy(s)

pub struct EnvVar
key: text
set: bool
val: text

pub struct Cmd
program: text
args: List[text]
clear: bool
vars: List[EnvVar]
has_cwd: bool
cwd: text
uid: i64
gid: i64
pgroup: i64
stdin: text
stdout: text
stderr: text

pub fn cmd_new(program: &text) -> Cmd = Cmd(program: os2c(program), args: [os2c(program)], clear: false, vars: [], has_cwd: false, cwd: "", uid: -1, gid: -1, pgroup: -1, stdin: "", stdout: "", stderr: "")

pub fn arg(c: &mut Cmd, a: &text)
c.args.push(os2c(a))

pub fn arg0(c: &mut Cmd, a: &text)
c.args[0] = os2c(a)

fn bytes_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
var i: usize = 0
while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 16777216
if a[i] != b[i]
return a[i] < b[i]
i += 1
return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# CommandEnv keeps a BTreeMap from key to Option<value>.
fn put(c: &mut Cmd, v: EnvVar)
var o: List[EnvVar] = []
var placed = false
for x in c.vars
if x.key == v.key
continue
if not placed and bytes_lt(&v.key, &x.key)
o.push(copy(v))
placed = true
o.push(copy(x))
if not placed
o.push(copy(v))
c.vars = o

pub fn env(c: &mut Cmd, k: &text, v: &text)
put(c, EnvVar(key: copy(k), set: true, val: copy(v)))

# With the environment cleared a removal only forgets the key.
pub fn env_remove(c: &mut Cmd, k: &text)
if c.clear
var o: List[EnvVar] = []
for x in c.vars
if x.key != k
o.push(copy(x))
c.vars = o
else
put(c, EnvVar(key: copy(k), set: false, val: ""))

pub fn env_clear(c: &mut Cmd)
c.clear = true
c.vars = []

pub fn current_dir(c: &mut Cmd, d: &text)
c.has_cwd = true
c.cwd = os2c(d)

# Stdio plans: "inherit", "null" or "piped".
pub fn set_stdio(c: &mut Cmd, which: &text, plan: &text) -> bool ! BadProc
let v = if plan == "inherit" then "Inherit" else (if plan == "null" then "Null" else (if plan == "piped" then "MakePipe" else ""))
if v == ""
fail BadProc(why: "unknown stdio plan")
if which == "stdin"
c.stdin = v
elif which == "stdout"
c.stdout = v
elif which == "stderr"
c.stderr = v
else
fail BadProc(why: "unknown stream")
return true

pub fn env_unchanged(c: &Cmd) -> bool = not c.clear and c.vars.len() == 0

# {:?}: a shell line.
pub fn debug(c: &Cmd) -> text
var o = ""
if c.has_cwd
o = o + "cd " + debug_c(&c.cwd) + " && "
if c.clear
o = o + "env -i "
else
var any = false
for v in c.vars
if not v.set
if not any
o = o + "env "
any = true
o = o + "-u " + v.key + " "
for v in c.vars
if v.set
o = o + v.key + "=" + debug_str(&v.val) + " "
if c.program != c.args[0]
o = o + "[" + debug_c(&c.program) + "] "
o = o + debug_c(&c.args[0])
var i: usize = 1
while i < c.args.len() bound 16777216
o = o + " " + debug_str(&c.args[i])
i += 1
return o

fn some_block(ind: text, v: text) -> text = "Some(\n" + ind + " " + v + ",\n" + ind + ")"

# {:#?}: Rust's pretty Debug of the Command struct (Linux field set).
pub fn debug_pretty(c: &Cmd) -> text
var o = "Command {\n program: " + debug_c(&c.program) + ",\n args: [\n"
for a in c.args
o = o + " " + debug_c(&a) + ",\n"
o = o + " ],\n"
if not env_unchanged(c)
o = o + " env: CommandEnv {\n clear: " + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\n vars: {"
if c.vars.len() == 0
o = o + "},\n"
else
o = o + "\n"
for v in c.vars
o = o + " " + debug_str(&v.key) + ": " + (if v.set then some_block(" ", debug_str(&v.val)) else "None") + ",\n"
o = o + " },\n"
o = o + " },\n"
if c.has_cwd
o = o + " cwd: " + some_block(" ", debug_c(&c.cwd)) + ",\n"
if c.uid >= 0
o = o + " uid: " + some_block(" ", c.uid.tostr()) + ",\n"
if c.gid >= 0
o = o + " gid: " + some_block(" ", c.gid.tostr()) + ",\n"
if c.stdin != ""
o = o + " stdin: " + some_block(" ", copy(c.stdin)) + ",\n"
if c.stdout != ""
o = o + " stdout: " + some_block(" ", copy(c.stdout)) + ",\n"
if c.stderr != ""
o = o + " stderr: " + some_block(" ", copy(c.stderr)) + ",\n"
if c.pgroup >= 0
o = o + " pgroup: " + some_block(" ", c.pgroup.tostr()) + ",\n"
return o + " create_pidfd: false,\n}"

# ---------------- POSIX shell words (Python shlex) ----------------

fn is_ws(c: &text) -> bool = c == " " or c == "\t" or c == "\r" or c == "\n"

# shlex.split(s, comments=True): posix mode, whitespace_split; "#" starts
# a comment to the end of the line; quotes ' and "; escape \ (inside
# double quotes it escapes only " and \).
pub fn shlex_split(s: &text) -> List[text] ! BadProc
let cs = s.chars()
var out: List[text] = []
var tok = ""
var st = " "
var esc_from = ""
var i: usize = 0
while i <= cs.len() bound 16777216
let eof = i == cs.len()
let c = if eof then "" else copy(cs[i])
i += 1
if st == " " or st == "a"
if eof
break
if is_ws(&c)
if st == "a"
out.push(tok)
tok = ""
st = " "
elif c == "#"
while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != "\n" bound 16777216
i += 1
if i < cs.len()
i += 1
if st == "a"
out.push(tok)
tok = ""
st = " "
elif c == "\\"
esc_from = "a"
st = "\\"
elif c == "'" or c == "\""
st = c
else
tok = tok + c
st = "a"
elif st == "'"
if eof
fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
if c == "'"
st = "a"
else
tok = tok + c
elif st == "\""
if eof
fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
if c == "\""
st = "a"
elif c == "\\"
esc_from = "\""
st = "\\"
else
tok = tok + c
else
if eof
fail BadProc(why: "No escaped character")
if esc_from == "\"" and c != "\"" and c != "\\"
tok = tok + "\\"
tok = tok + c
st = esc_from
if st == "a"
out.push(tok)
return out

fn safe_char(c: &text) -> bool

module os.proc

# Processes (survey M39), pure. Spawning, waiting and killing are host
# capability effects (cap Spawn, Wait, Kill under grant exec, scoped to an
# allow-list of image digests); their results (pid, wait status) are
# admitted to the log, and this module decodes and describes them.
#  - Wait status codec as Linux and glibc define it (WIFEXITED,
#    WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG,
#    WIFCONTINUED) and Rust's ExitStatus on top of it: code, signal,
#    core_dumped, stopped_signal, continued, success and its Display text.
#  - The spawn spec: Rust's std::process::Command model (program, args
#    with arg0, environment changes, cwd, uid, gid, process group, stdio
#    plan) and both of its Debug forms ({:?} as a shell line, {:#?}).
#  - POSIX shell words as Python's shlex gives them: split (posix mode,
#    comments on), quote and join.
#  - The Spawn request as logged (a canonical line) and the exec grant
#    check by image digest.

# ---------------- wait status ----------------

pub fn wifexited(s: i64) -> bool = s & 127 == 0
pub fn wexitstatus(s: i64) -> i64 = (s >> 8) & 255
# glibc: ((signed char) ((s & 0x7f) + 1) >> 1) > 0
pub fn wifsignaled(s: i64) -> bool
    let v = (s & 127) + 1
    let sc = if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v
    return (sc >> 1) > 0
pub fn wtermsig(s: i64) -> i64 = s & 127
pub fn wcoredump(s: i64) -> bool = s & 128 != 0
pub fn wifstopped(s: i64) -> bool = s & 255 == 127
pub fn wstopsig(s: i64) -> i64 = wexitstatus(s)
pub fn wifcontinued(s: i64) -> bool = s == 65535

fn raw32(s: i64) -> i64

    return if v >= 2147483648 then v - 4294967296 else v

pub fn code(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifexited(raw32(s)) then some(wexitstatus(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifsignaled(raw32(s)) then some(wtermsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn core_dumped(s: i64) -> bool = wifsignaled(raw32(s)) and wcoredump(raw32(s))
pub fn stopped_signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifstopped(raw32(s)) then some(wstopsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn continued(s: i64) -> bool = wifcontinued(raw32(s))
# ExitStatus::success: exit_ok, i.e. the raw status is zero.
pub fn success(s: i64) -> bool = raw32(s) == 0

# Rust's signal_string for Linux x86_64, aarch64, arm and x86.
const RUST_SIGNALS: text = "HUP INT QUIT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE KILL USR1 SEGV USR2 PIPE ALRM TERM STKFLT CHLD CONT STOP TSTP TTIN TTOU URG XCPU XFSZ VTALRM PROF WINCH IO PWR SYS"

pub fn signal_string(n: i64) -> text
    if n < 1 or n > 31
        return ""
    return " (SIG" + RUST_SIGNALS.split(" ")[(n - 1) as usize] + ")"

    let d = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var x = v
    var o = ""
    while x > 0 bound 64
        o = d[(x % 16) as usize] + o
        x = x / 16
    return o

# Display for ExitStatus.
pub fn status_text(s: i64) -> text
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return "exit status: " + wexitstatus(r).tostr()
    if wifsignaled(r)
        let n = wtermsig(r)
        return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")
    if wifstopped(r)
        let n = wstopsig(r)
        return "stopped (not terminated) by signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n)
    if wifcontinued(r)
        return "continued (WIFCONTINUED)"
    # {:#x} of an i32 prints its two's complement bits
    let u = if r < 0 then r + 4294967296 else r
    return "unrecognised wait status: " + r.tostr() + " 0x" + hex(u)

pub fn shell_status(s: i64) -> i64
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return wexitstatus(r)
    if wifsignaled(r)
        return 128 + wtermsig(r)
    if wifstopped(r)
        return 128 + wstopsig(r)
    return -1

    let v = (s & 127) + 1
    let sc = if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v
    return (sc >> 1) > 0
pub fn wtermsig(s: i64) -> i64 = s & 127
pub fn wcoredump(s: i64) -> bool = s & 128 != 0
pub fn wifstopped(s: i64) -> bool = s & 255 == 127
pub fn wstopsig(s: i64) -> i64 = wexitstatus(s)
pub fn wifcontinued(s: i64) -> bool = s == 65535

# The raw status a 32-bit int holds (the low 32 bits, signed).
fn raw32(s: i64) -> i64
    let v = s & 4294967295
    return if v >= 2147483648 then v - 4294967296 else v

pub fn code(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifexited(raw32(s)) then some(wexitstatus(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifsignaled(raw32(s)) then some(wtermsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn core_dumped(s: i64) -> bool = wifsignaled(raw32(s)) and wcoredump(raw32(s))
pub fn stopped_signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifstopped(raw32(s)) then some(wstopsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn continued(s: i64) -> bool = wifcontinued(raw32(s))
# ExitStatus::success: exit_ok, i.e. the raw status is zero.
pub fn success(s: i64) -> bool = raw32(s) == 0

# Rust's signal_string for Linux x86_64, aarch64, arm and x86.
const RUST_SIGNALS: text = "HUP INT QUIT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE KILL USR1 SEGV USR2 PIPE ALRM TERM STKFLT CHLD CONT STOP TSTP TTIN TTOU URG XCPU XFSZ VTALRM PROF WINCH IO PWR SYS"

pub fn signal_string(n: i64) -> text
    if n < 1 or n > 31
        return ""
    return " (SIG" + RUST_SIGNALS.split(" ")[(n - 1) as usize] + ")"

fn hex(v: i64) -> text
    let d = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var x = v
    var o = ""
    while x > 0 bound 64
        o = d[(x % 16) as usize] + o
        x = x / 16
    return o

# Display for ExitStatus.
pub fn status_text(s: i64) -> text
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return "exit status: " + wexitstatus(r).tostr()
    if wifsignaled(r)
        let n = wtermsig(r)
        return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")
    if wifstopped(r)
        let n = wstopsig(r)
        return "stopped (not terminated) by signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n)
    if wifcontinued(r)
        return "continued (WIFCONTINUED)"
    # {:#x} of an i32 prints its two's complement bits
    let u = if r < 0 then r + 4294967296 else r
    return "unrecognised wait status: " + r.tostr() + " 0x" + hex(u)

# The status a POSIX shell reports in $? for a wait status (128 + signal).
pub fn shell_status(s: i64) -> i64
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return wexitstatus(r)
    if wifsignaled(r)
        return 128 + wtermsig(r)
    if wifstopped(r)
        return 128 + wstopsig(r)
    return -1

# ---------------- Rust str Debug ----------------

fn cp_of(c: &text) -> i64
    let b = c[0] as i64
    if b < 128
        return b
    if b < 224
        return (b & 31) << 6 | (c[1] as i64 & 63)
    if b < 240
        return (b & 15) << 12 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[2] as i64 & 63)
    return (b & 7) << 18 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (c[2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[3] as i64 & 63)

# char::escape_debug as str's Debug uses it, for the characters a spawn
# spec carries in practice: the C0 and C1 controls, DEL and the soft
# hyphen are not printable and print as \u{..}; other characters print as
# themselves (NBSP is escaped as Rust does; grapheme extenders and the rest of Unicode's non-printable
# set are outside this model).
pub fn debug_str(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v == 0
            o = o + "\\0"
        elif v == 9
            o = o + "\\t"
        elif v == 10
            o = o + "\\n"
        elif v == 13
            o = o + "\\r"
        elif v == 34
            o = o + "\\\""
        elif v == 92
            o = o + "\\\\"
        elif v < 32 or (v >= 127 and v <= 160) or v == 173
            o = o + "\\u{" + hex(v) + "}"
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

# CStr's Debug (program, arg0 and cwd are C strings in the Command): ASCII
# as u8::escape_ascii writes it (\t \r \n \' \" \\, \xNN for other
# bytes outside 0x20..0x7e), other characters as debug_str.
pub fn debug_c(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v >= 128
            let d = debug_str(&c)
            let dc = d.chars()
            var k: usize = 1
            while k + 1 < dc.len() bound 64
                o = o + dc[k]
                k += 1
        elif v == 9
            o = o + "\\t"
        elif v == 10
            o = o + "\\n"
        elif v == 13
            o = o + "\\r"
        elif v == 39 or v == 34 or v == 92
            o = o + "\\" + c
        elif v < 32 or v == 127
            o = o + "\\x" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "") + hex(v)
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

# ---------------- Command ----------------

# Rust's os2c: a string with an interior NUL cannot become a C string, and
# the Command keeps this marker instead (spawning then fails).
pub const WITH_NUL: text = "<string-with-nul>"
fn os2c(s: &text) -> text = if s.contains("\u{0}") then WITH_NUL else copy(s)

pub struct EnvVar
    key: text
    set: bool
    val: text

pub struct Cmd
    program: text
    args: List[text]
    clear: bool
    vars: List[EnvVar]
    has_cwd: bool
    cwd: text
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    pgroup: i64
    stdin: text
    stdout: text
    stderr: text

pub fn cmd_new(program: &text) -> Cmd = Cmd(program: os2c(program), args: [os2c(program)], clear: false, vars: [], has_cwd: false, cwd: "", uid: -1, gid: -1, pgroup: -1, stdin: "", stdout: "", stderr: "")

pub fn arg(c: &mut Cmd, a: &text)
    c.args.push(os2c(a))

pub fn arg0(c: &mut Cmd, a: &text)
    c.args[0] = os2c(a)

fn bytes_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# CommandEnv keeps a BTreeMap from key to Option<value>.
fn put(c: &mut Cmd, v: EnvVar)
    var o: List[EnvVar] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in c.vars
        if x.key == v.key
            continue
        if not placed and bytes_lt(&v.key, &x.key)
            o.push(copy(v))
            placed = true
        o.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        o.push(copy(v))
    c.vars = o

pub fn env(c: &mut Cmd, k: &text, v: &text)
    put(c, EnvVar(key: copy(k), set: true, val: copy(v)))

# With the environment cleared a removal only forgets the key.
pub fn env_remove(c: &mut Cmd, k: &text)
    if c.clear
        var o: List[EnvVar] = []
        for x in c.vars
            if x.key != k
                o.push(copy(x))
        c.vars = o
    else
        put(c, EnvVar(key: copy(k), set: false, val: ""))

pub fn env_clear(c: &mut Cmd)
    c.clear = true
    c.vars = []

pub fn current_dir(c: &mut Cmd, d: &text)
    c.has_cwd = true
    c.cwd = os2c(d)

# Stdio plans: "inherit", "null" or "piped".
pub fn set_stdio(c: &mut Cmd, which: &text, plan: &text) -> bool ! BadProc
    let v = if plan == "inherit" then "Inherit" else (if plan == "null" then "Null" else (if plan == "piped" then "MakePipe" else ""))
    if v == ""
        fail BadProc(why: "unknown stdio plan")
    if which == "stdin"
        c.stdin = v
    elif which == "stdout"
        c.stdout = v
    elif which == "stderr"
        c.stderr = v
    else
        fail BadProc(why: "unknown stream")
    return true

pub fn env_unchanged(c: &Cmd) -> bool = not c.clear and c.vars.len() == 0

# {:?}: a shell line.
pub fn debug(c: &Cmd) -> text
    var o = ""
    if c.has_cwd
        o = o + "cd " + debug_c(&c.cwd) + " && "
    if c.clear
        o = o + "env -i "
    else
        var any = false
        for v in c.vars
            if not v.set
                if not any
                    o = o + "env "
                    any = true
                o = o + "-u " + v.key + " "
    for v in c.vars
        if v.set
            o = o + v.key + "=" + debug_str(&v.val) + " "
    if c.program != c.args[0]
        o = o + "[" + debug_c(&c.program) + "] "
    o = o + debug_c(&c.args[0])
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < c.args.len() bound 16777216
        o = o + " " + debug_str(&c.args[i])
        i += 1
    return o

fn some_block(ind: text, v: text) -> text = "Some(\n" + ind + "    " + v + ",\n" + ind + ")"

# {:#?}: Rust's pretty Debug of the Command struct (Linux field set).
pub fn debug_pretty(c: &Cmd) -> text
    var o = "Command {\n    program: " + debug_c(&c.program) + ",\n    args: [\n"
    for a in c.args
        o = o + "        " + debug_c(&a) + ",\n"
    o = o + "    ],\n"
    if not env_unchanged(c)
        o = o + "    env: CommandEnv {\n        clear: " + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\n        vars: {"
        if c.vars.len() == 0
            o = o + "},\n"
        else
            o = o + "\n"
            for v in c.vars
                o = o + "            " + debug_str(&v.key) + ": " + (if v.set then some_block("            ", debug_str(&v.val)) else "None") + ",\n"
            o = o + "        },\n"
        o = o + "    },\n"
    if c.has_cwd
        o = o + "    cwd: " + some_block("    ", debug_c(&c.cwd)) + ",\n"
    if c.uid >= 0
        o = o + "    uid: " + some_block("    ", c.uid.tostr()) + ",\n"
    if c.gid >= 0
        o = o + "    gid: " + some_block("    ", c.gid.tostr()) + ",\n"
    if c.stdin != ""
        o = o + "    stdin: " + some_block("    ", copy(c.stdin)) + ",\n"
    if c.stdout != ""
        o = o + "    stdout: " + some_block("    ", copy(c.stdout)) + ",\n"
    if c.stderr != ""
        o = o + "    stderr: " + some_block("    ", copy(c.stderr)) + ",\n"
    if c.pgroup >= 0
        o = o + "    pgroup: " + some_block("    ", c.pgroup.tostr()) + ",\n"
    return o + "    create_pidfd: false,\n}"

# ---------------- POSIX shell words (Python shlex) ----------------

fn is_ws(c: &text) -> bool = c == " " or c == "\t" or c == "\r" or c == "\n"

# shlex.split(s, comments=True): posix mode, whitespace_split; "#" starts
# a comment to the end of the line; quotes ' and "; escape \ (inside
# double quotes it escapes only " and \).
pub fn shlex_split(s: &text) -> List[text] ! BadProc
    let cs = s.chars()
    var out: List[text] = []
    var tok = ""
    var st = " "
    var esc_from = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 16777216
        let eof = i == cs.len()
        let c = if eof then "" else copy(cs[i])
        i += 1
        if st == " " or st == "a"
            if eof
                break
            if is_ws(&c)
                if st == "a"
                    out.push(tok)
                    tok = ""
                    st = " "
            elif c == "#"
                while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != "\n" bound 16777216
                    i += 1
                if i > cs.len()
                    i += 1
                if st == "a"
                    out.push(tok)
                    tok = ""
                    st = " "
            elif c == "\\"
                esc_from = "a"
                st = "\\"
            elif c == "'" or c == "\""
                st = c
            else
                tok = tok + c
                st = "a"
        elif st == "'"
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
            if c == "'"
                st = "a"
            else
                tok = tok + c
        elif st == "\""
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
            if c == "\""
                st = "a"
            elif c == "\\"
                esc_from = "\""
                st = "\\"
            else
                tok = tok + c
        else
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No escaped character")
            if esc_from == "\"" and c != "\"" and c != "\\"
                tok = tok + "\\"
            tok = tok + c
            st = esc_from
    if st == "a"
        out.push(tok)
    return out

fn safe_char(c: &text) -> bool
    if c.len_bytes() != 1
        return false
    let v = c[0] as i64
    return (v >= 48 and v <= 57) or (v >= 65 and v <= 90) or (v >= 97 and v <= 122) or "@%_-+=:,./".contains(c)

# shlex.quote
pub fn shlex_quote(s: &text) -> text
    if s == ""
        return "''"
    var safe = true
    for c in s.chars()
        if not safe_char(&c)
            safe = false
    if safe
        return copy(s)
    var o = "'"
    for c in s.chars()
        o = o + (if c == "'" then "'\"'\"'" else c)
    return o + "'"

pub fn shlex_join(ws: &List[text]) -> text
    var o: List[text] = []
    for w in ws
        o.push(shlex_quote(&w))
    return " ".join(o)

# ---------------- Spawn request and the exec grant ----------------

fn jstr(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v == 34
            o = o + "\\\""
        elif v == 92
            o = o + "\\\\"
        elif v < 32
            o = o + "\\u00" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "1") + "0123456789abcdef".chars()[(v % 16) as usize]
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

fn plan_json(x: &text) -> text = if x == "Null" then "\"null\"" else (if x == "MakePipe" then "\"piped\"" else "\"inherit\"")

# The Spawn effect as logged: a canonical JSON line (keys sorted, as JCS
# orders ASCII keys) naming the image digest, argv, the environment
# changes, cwd and the stdio plan.
pub fn spawn_request(c: &Cmd, digest: &text) -> text
    var argv: List[text] = []
    for a in c.args
        argv.push(jstr(&a))
    var ev: List[text] = []
    for v in c.vars
        ev.push("[" + jstr(&v.key) + "," + (if v.set then jstr(&v.val) else "null") + "]")
    return "{\"argv\":[" + ",".join(argv) + "],\"clear\":" + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\"cwd\":" + (if c.has_cwd then jstr(&c.cwd) else "null") + ",\"env\":[" + ",".join(ev) + "],\"image\":" + jstr(digest) + ",\"stdio\":[" + plan_json(&c.stdin) + "," + plan_json(&c.stdout) + "," + plan_json(&c.stderr) + "]}"

# grant exec: the image digest must be on the allow-list (deny by default).
pub fn exec_granted(allow: &List[text], digest: &text) -> bool
    for a in allow
        if a == digest
            return true
    return false

module os.proc

# Processes (survey M39), pure. Spawning, waiting and killing are host
# capability effects (cap Spawn, Wait, Kill under grant exec, scoped to an
# allow-list of image digests); their results (pid, wait status) are
# admitted to the log, and this module decodes and describes them.
#  - Wait status codec as Linux and glibc define it (WIFEXITED,
#    WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG,
#    WIFCONTINUED) and Rust's ExitStatus on top of it: code, signal,
#    core_dumped, stopped_signal, continued, success and its Display text.
#  - The spawn spec: Rust's std::process::Command model (program, args
#    with arg0, environment changes, cwd, uid, gid, process group, stdio
#    plan) and both of its Debug forms ({:?} as a shell line, {:#?}).
#  - POSIX shell words as Python's shlex gives them: split (posix mode,
#    comments on), quote and join.
#  - The Spawn request as logged (a canonical line) and the exec grant
#    check by image digest.

error BadProc(why: text)

# ExitStatus::success: exit_ok, i.e. the raw status is zero.

fn hex(v: i64) -> text
    let d = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var x = v
    var o = ""
    while x > 0 bound 64
        o = d[(x % 16) as usize] + o

    return o

    if wifsignaled(r)
        let n = wtermsig(r)
        return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")
    if wifstopped(r)

        return "stopped (not terminated) by signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n)
    if wifcontinued(r)
        return "continued (WIFCONTINUED)"
    # {:#x} of an i32 prints its two's complement bits

    return "unrecognised wait status: " + r.tostr() + " 0x" + hex(u)

fn bytes_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1

# CommandEnv keeps a BTreeMap from key to Option<value>.
fn put(c: &mut Cmd, v: EnvVar)
    var o: List[EnvVar] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in c.vars
        if x.key == v.key
            continue
        if not placed and bytes_lt(&v.key, &x.key)
            o.push(copy(v))
            placed = true
        o.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        o.push(copy(v))

# ---------------- POSIX shell words (Python shlex) ----------------

fn is_ws(c: &text) -> bool = c == " " or c == "\t" or c == "\r" or c == "\n"

# shlex.split(s, comments=True): posix mode, whitespace_split; "#" starts
# a comment to the end of the line; quotes ' and "; escape \ (inside
# double quotes it escapes only " and \).
pub fn shlex_split(s: &text) -> List[text] ! BadProc
    let cs = s.chars()
    var out: List[text] = []
    var tok = ""
    var st = " "
    var esc_from = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 16777216
        let eof = i == cs.len()
        let c = if eof then "" else copy(cs[i])
        i += 1
        if st == " " or st == "a"
            if eof
                break
            if is_ws(&c)
                if st == "a"
                    out.push(tok)
                    tok = ""
                    st = " "
            elif c == "#"
                while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != "\n" bound 16777216
                    i += 1
                if i < cs.len()
                    i += 1
                if st == "a"
                    out.push(tok)
                    tok = ""
                    st = " "
            elif c == "\\"
                esc_from = "a"
                st = "\\"
            elif c == "'" or c == "\""
                st = c
            else
                tok = tok + c
                st = "a"
        elif st == "'"
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
            if c == "'"
                st = "a"
            else
                tok = tok + c
        elif st == "\""
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
            if c == "\""
                st = "a"
            elif c == "\\"
                esc_from = "\""
                st = "\\"
            else
                tok = tok + c
        else
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No escaped character")
            if esc_from == "\"" and c != "\"" and c != "\\"
                tok = tok + "\\"
            tok = tok + c
            st = esc_from
    if st == "a"
        out.push(tok)
    return out

fn safe_char(c: &text) -> bool
    if c.len_bytes() != 1
        return false
    let v = c[0] as i64
    return (v >= 48 and v <= 57) or (v >= 65 and v <= 90) or (v >= 97 and v <= 122) or "@%_-+=:,./".contains(c)

# shlex.quote
pub fn shlex_quote(s: &text) -> text
    if s == ""
        return "''"
    var safe = true
    for c in s.chars()
        if not safe_char(&c)
            safe = false
    if safe
        return copy(s)
    var o = "'"
    for c in s.chars()
        o = o + (if c == "'" then "'\"'\"'" else c)
    return o + "'"

pub fn shlex_join(ws: &List[text]) -> text
    var o: List[text] = []
    for w in ws
        o.push(shlex_quote(&w))
    return " ".join(o)

# ---------------- Spawn request and the exec grant ----------------

fn jstr(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v == 34
            o = o + "\\\""
        elif v == 92
            o = o + "\\\\"
        elif v < 32
            o = o + "\\u00" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "1") + "0123456789abcdef".chars()[(v % 16) as usize]
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

fn plan_json(x: &text) -> text = if x == "Null" then "\"null\"" else (if x == "MakePipe" then "\"piped\"" else "\"inherit\"")

# The Spawn effect as logged: a canonical JSON line (keys sorted, as JCS
# orders ASCII keys) naming the image digest, argv, the environment
# changes, cwd and the stdio plan.
pub fn spawn_request(c: &Cmd, digest: &text) -> text
    var argv: List[text] = []
    for a in c.args
        argv.push(jstr(&a))
    var ev: List[text] = []
    for v in c.vars
        ev.push("[" + jstr(&v.key) + "," + (if v.set then jstr(&v.val) else "null") + "]")
    return "{\"argv\":[" + ",".join(argv) + "],\"clear\":" + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\"cwd\":" + (if c.has_cwd then jstr(&c.cwd) else "null") + ",\"env\":[" + ",".join(ev) + "],\"image\":" + jstr(digest) + ",\"stdio\":[" + plan_json(&c.stdin) + "," + plan_json(&c.stdout) + "," + plan_json(&c.stderr) + "]}"

# grant exec: the image digest must be on the allow-list (deny by default).
pub fn exec_granted(allow: &List[text], digest: &text) -> bool
    for a in allow
        if a == digest
            return true
    return false

module os.proc

# Processes (survey M39), pure. Spawning, waiting and killing are host
# capability effects (cap Spawn, Wait, Kill under grant exec, scoped to an
# allow-list of image digests); their results (pid, wait status) are
# admitted to the log, and this module decodes and describes them.
#  - Wait status codec as Linux and glibc define it (WIFEXITED,
#    WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG,
#    WIFCONTINUED) and Rust's ExitStatus on top of it: code, signal,
#    core_dumped, stopped_signal, continued, success and its Display text.
#  - The spawn spec: Rust's std::process::Command model (program, args
#    with arg0, environment changes, cwd, uid, gid, process group, stdio
#    plan) and both of its Debug forms ({:?} as a shell line, {:#?}).
#  - POSIX shell words as Python's shlex gives them: split (posix mode,
#    comments on), quote and join.
#  - The Spawn request as logged (a canonical line) and the exec grant
#    check by image digest.

error BadProc(why: text)

# ---------------- wait status ----------------

pub fn wifexited(s: i64) -> bool = s & 127 == 0
pub fn wexitstatus(s: i64) -> i64 = (s >> 8) & 255
# glibc: ((signed char) ((s & 0x7f) + 1) >> 1) > 0
pub fn wifsignaled(s: i64) -> bool
    let v = (s & 127) + 1
    let sc = if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v
    return (sc >> 1) > 0
pub fn wtermsig(s: i64) -> i64 = s & 127
pub fn wcoredump(s: i64) -> bool = s & 128 != 0
pub fn wifstopped(s: i64) -> bool = s & 255 == 127
pub fn wstopsig(s: i64) -> i64 = wexitstatus(s)
pub fn wifcontinued(s: i64) -> bool = s == 65535

# The raw status a 32-bit int holds (the low 32 bits, signed).
fn raw32(s: i64) -> i64
    let v = s & 4294967295
    return if v >= 2147483648 then v - 4294967296 else v

pub fn code(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifexited(raw32(s)) then some(wexitstatus(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifsignaled(raw32(s)) then some(wtermsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn core_dumped(s: i64) -> bool = wifsignaled(raw32(s)) and wcoredump(raw32(s))
pub fn stopped_signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifstopped(raw32(s)) then some(wstopsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn continued(s: i64) -> bool = wifcontinued(raw32(s))
# ExitStatus::success: exit_ok, i.e. the raw status is zero.
pub fn success(s: i64) -> bool = raw32(s) == 0

# Rust's signal_string for Linux x86_64, aarch64, arm and x86.
const RUST_SIGNALS: text = "HUP INT QUIT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE KILL USR1 SEGV USR2 PIPE ALRM TERM STKFLT CHLD CONT STOP TSTP TTIN TTOU URG XCPU XFSZ VTALRM PROF WINCH IO PWR SYS"

pub fn signal_string(n: i64) -> text
    if n < 1 or n > 31
        return ""
    return " (SIG" + RUST_SIGNALS.split(" ")[(n - 1) as usize] + ")"

fn hex(v: i64) -> text
    let d = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var x = v
    var o = ""
    while x > 0 bound 64
        o = d[(x % 16) as usize] + o
        x = x / 16
    return o

# Display for ExitStatus.
pub fn status_text(s: i64) -> text
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return "exit status: " + wexitstatus(r).tostr()
    if wifsignaled(r)
        let n = wtermsig(r)
        return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")
    if wifstopped(r)
        let n = wstopsig(r)
        return "stopped (not terminated) by signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n)
    if wifcontinued(r)
        return "continued (WIFCONTINUED)"
    # {:#x} of an i32 prints its two's complement bits
    let u = if r < 0 then r + 4294967296 else r
    return "unrecognised wait status: " + r.tostr() + " 0x" + hex(u)

# The status a POSIX shell reports in $? for a wait status (128 + signal).
pub fn shell_status(s: i64) -> i64
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return wexitstatus(r)
    if wifsignaled(r)
        return 128 + wtermsig(r)
    if wifstopped(r)
        return 128 + wstopsig(r)
    return -1

# ---------------- Rust str Debug ----------------

fn cp_of(c: &text) -> i64
    let b = c[0] as i64
    if b < 128
        return b
    if b < 224
        return (b & 31) << 6 | (c[1] as i64 & 63)
    if b < 240
        return (b & 15) << 12 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[2] as i64 & 63)
    return (b & 7) << 18 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (c[2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[3] as i64 & 63)

# char::escape_debug as str's Debug uses it, for the characters a spawn
# spec carries in practice: the C0 and C1 controls, DEL and the soft
# hyphen are not printable and print as \u{..}; other characters print as
# themselves (NBSP is escaped as Rust does; grapheme extenders and the rest of Unicode's non-printable
# set are outside this model).
pub fn debug_str(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v == 0
            o = o + "\\0"
        elif v == 9
            o = o + "\\t"
        elif v == 10
            o = o + "\\n"
        elif v == 13
            o = o + "\\r"
        elif v == 34
            o = o + "\\\""
        elif v == 92
            o = o + "\\\\"
        elif v < 32 or (v >= 127 and v <= 160) or v == 173
            o = o + "\\u{" + hex(v) + "}"
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

# CStr's Debug (program, arg0 and cwd are C strings in the Command): ASCII
# as u8::escape_ascii writes it (\t \r \n \' \" \\, \xNN for other
# bytes outside 0x20..0x7e), other characters as debug_str.
pub fn debug_c(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v >= 128
            let d = debug_str(&c)
            let dc = d.chars()
            var k: usize = 1
            while k + 1 < dc.len() bound 64
                o = o + dc[k]
                k += 1
        elif v == 9
            o = o + "\\t"
        elif v == 10
            o = o + "\\n"
        elif v == 13
            o = o + "\\r"
        elif v == 39 or v == 34 or v == 92
            o = o + "\\" + c
        elif v < 32 or v == 127
            o = o + "\\x" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "") + hex(v)
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

# Processes (survey M39), pure. Spawning, waiting and killing are host
# capability effects (cap Spawn, Wait, Kill under grant exec, scoped to an
# allow-list of image digests); their results (pid, wait status) are
# admitted to the log, and this module decodes and describes them.
#  - Wait status codec as Linux and glibc define it (WIFEXITED,
#    WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG,
#    WIFCONTINUED) and Rust's ExitStatus on top of it: code, signal,
#    core_dumped, stopped_signal, continued, success and its Display text.
#  - The spawn spec: Rust's std::process::Command model (program, args
#    with arg0, environment changes, cwd, uid, gid, process group, stdio
#    plan) and both of its Debug forms ({:?} as a shell line, {:#?}).
#  - POSIX shell words as Python's shlex gives them: split (posix mode,
#    comments on), quote and join.
#  - The Spawn request as logged (a canonical line) and the exec grant
#    check by image digest.

    let sc = if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v
    return (sc >> 1) > 0

fn raw32(s: i64) -> i64

    return if v >= 2147483648 then v - 4294967296 else v

pub fn success(s: i64) -> bool = raw32(s) == 0

    let r = raw32(s)

    if wifsignaled(r)
        let n = wtermsig(r)
        return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")

    if wifsignaled(r)

    if wifstopped(r)

        argv.push(jstr(&a))
    var ev: List[text] = []
    for v in c.vars
        ev.push("[" + jstr(&v.key) + "," + (if v.set then jstr(&v.val) else "null") + "]")
    return "{\"argv\":[" + ",".join(argv) + "],\"clear\":" + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\"cwd\":" + (if c.has_cwd then jstr(&c.cwd) else "null") + ",\"env\":[" + ",".join(ev) + "],\"image\":" + jstr(digest) + ",\"stdio\":[" + plan_json(&c.stdin) + "," + plan_json(&c.stdout) + "," + plan_json(&c.stderr) + "]}"

# grant exec: the image digest must be on the allow-list (deny by default).
pub fn exec_granted(allow: &List[text], digest: &text) -> bool
    for a in allow
        if a == digest
            return true
    return false
